{"parentUuid":"6bce1455-5d2f-4e58-bc85-e9d6ed8e72f2","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CexKQow7uDxCTVGfFpqMG","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01EUQY8WAcLqbM6M1yDcs6pM","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\003-check-deps-script.md","content":"# 003 — `check:deps` script to gate dependency vulnerabilities in CI\n\n**Status:** draft\n\n## Context\n\nPlans 001 and 002 cleared all current advisories (`npm audit` → 0 vulnerabilities). To keep it that way, the user wants a `check:deps` npm script that runs on every new PR in the pipeline:\n\n- **Critical** vulnerability → error, pipeline fails.\n- **Moderate / low** vulnerability → warning, pipeline continues.\n\nCurrent state of the repo:\n- There is **no CI pipeline yet** (no `.github/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, etc.). The remote is GitHub (`github.com/carlossas/recruiting-challenge`).\n- `npm audit --audit-level=<level>` alone is not enough: it can set the exit code by threshold, but it can't emit *warnings* for lower severities while passing, and its text output isn't annotated for CI.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Script: `src/scripts/check-deps.ts`\n\nA small TypeScript script, run with `tsx`, placed next to the existing `src/scripts/seed.ts` (same convention; covered by `tsc` type-checking since `tsconfig.json` only includes `src/**`).\n\nSplit into two parts so the logic is testable without the network:\n\n- **`evaluateAudit(report)`** — pure function. Input: parsed `npm audit --json` report. Output: `{ errors, warnings, exitCode }`.\n- **`main()`** — runs `npm audit --json`, parses stdout, calls `evaluateAudit`, prints results, sets `process.exitCode`.\n\nBehavior:\n\n| Severity | Output | Exit code |\n|---|---|---|\n| `critical` | error line per package | `1` (fails pipeline) |\n| `high` | **see open question Q1** | — |\n| `moderate`, `low` | warning line per package | `0` |\n| `info` | ignored | `0` |\n| none | `✔ No known vulnerabilities` | `0` |\n| `npm audit` could not run (network/registry error, invalid JSON) | **see open question Q2** | — |\n\nEach reported line includes: package name, severity, advisory title + URL, whether it's direct or transitive, and whether a fix is available. A summary line with counts per severity is printed at the end.\n\n**CI annotations:** when `GITHUB_ACTIONS === 'true'`, lines are emitted as `::error title=…::…` / `::warning title=…::…` so they show up in the PR's checks UI. Outside GitHub Actions, plain `console.error` / `console.warn` with an `ERROR` / `WARN` prefix. No dependency on any CI provider.\n\nImplementation notes:\n- `npm audit` exits non-zero whenever it finds anything, so the exit code of `npm audit` is **ignored**; the decision comes only from the parsed JSON.\n- Spawned via `child_process.spawnSync('npm', ['audit', '--json'], { shell: process.platform === 'win32' })` — on Windows `npm` is `npm.cmd`, which Node 20+ refuses to spawn without a shell.\n- Scans **all** dependencies (prod + dev), matching \"the repository's vulnerabilities\". Dev-only packages are still flagged but labeled as such in the output.\n- No new dependencies.\n- Docstrings (TSDoc) on every exported function and the module, per CLAUDE.md.\n\n### 2. `package.json`\n\n```json\n\"check:deps\": \"tsx src/scripts/check-deps.ts\"\n```\n\n### 3. Tests: `test/check-deps.test.ts`\n\nUnit tests for `evaluateAudit` using inline fixtures shaped like real `npm audit --json` output (the report captured in plan 001 is a real sample):\n\n- No vulnerabilities → exit 0, no errors/warnings.\n- Only `low` + `moderate` → exit 0, one warning per package.\n- One `critical` among moderates → exit 1, one error + the warnings.\n- `high` → according to Q1.\n- Audit error payload → according to Q2.\n\n## Open questions (need your call before approval)\n\n- **Q1 — What about `high`?** You specified critical → fail and moderate/low → warn, but not `high`. Options:\n  - (a) **Fail on `high` too** — *recommended*. High advisories are usually remotely exploitable; letting them through as a warning is easy to ignore in a PR.\n  - (b) Warn on `high` (literal reading of the requirement).\n- **Q2 — What if `npm audit` itself fails** (registry down, no network)?\n  - (a) **Fail closed** (exit 1 with a clear \"audit could not run\" message) — *recommended*. A silent pass would hide the fact that nothing was checked.\n  - (b) Fail open (warn and exit 0) — avoids blocking PRs during npm registry outages.\n- **Q3 — Pipeline file.** There's no CI yet. Options:\n  - (a) Script only in this plan; the workflow goes in a separate plan — *recommended*, keeps this change small.\n  - (b) Also add `.github/workflows/check-deps.yml` here (trigger `pull_request`, `npm ci`, `npm run check:deps`).\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/scripts/check-deps.ts` (new)\n- `test/check-deps.test.ts` (new)\n- `package.json` — `scripts.check:deps`\n- `.github/workflows/check-deps.yml` only if Q3 = (b)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Fixing any vulnerability.\n- Other CI checks (tests, type-check) — can be added to the same workflow later.\n- `docs/` — after validation, Claude will ask for authorization to document the script (per CLAUDE.md §6).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` → existing + new `check-deps` tests pass.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `npm run check:deps` on the current repo → `✔ No known vulnerabilities`, exit 0.\n4. Real-world warning case: in a scratchpad copy of the repo **without** the plan 002 override (qs 6.15.3), `npm run check:deps` → 2 warnings (`qs`, `express`), exit 0.\n5. Critical case: covered by the unit test fixture (no real critical advisory available to reproduce).\n6. Annotation format: run with `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` in the scratchpad copy → lines start with `::warning`.\n\n## Rollback\n\nDelete the new files and remove the `check:deps` entry from `package.json`.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2258,"cache_read_input_tokens":157867,"output_tokens":2425,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":133},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2258,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":32,"output_tokens":2425,"cache_read_input_tokens":157867,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2258,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2258},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01EUQY8WAcLqbM6M1yDcs6pM":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\003-check-deps-script.md","content":"# 003 — `check:deps` script to gate dependency vulnerabilities in CI\n\n**Status:** draft\n\n## Context\n\nPlans 001 and 002 cleared all current advisories (`npm audit` → 0 vulnerabilities). To keep it that way, the user wants a `check:deps` npm script that runs on every new PR in the pipeline:\n\n- **Critical** vulnerability → error, pipeline fails.\n- **Moderate / low** vulnerability → warning, pipeline continues.\n\nCurrent state of the repo:\n- There is **no CI pipeline yet** (no `.github/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, etc.). The remote is GitHub (`github.com/carlossas/recruiting-challenge`).\n- `npm audit --audit-level=<level>` alone is not enough: it can set the exit code by threshold, but it can't emit *warnings* for lower severities while passing, and its text output isn't annotated for CI.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Script: `src/scripts/check-deps.ts`\n\nA small TypeScript script, run with `tsx`, placed next to the existing `src/scripts/seed.ts` (same convention; covered by `tsc` type-checking since `tsconfig.json` only includes `src/**`).\n\nSplit into two parts so the logic is testable without the network:\n\n- **`evaluateAudit(report)`** — pure function. Input: parsed `npm audit --json` report. Output: `{ errors, warnings, exitCode }`.\n- **`main()`** — runs `npm audit --json`, parses stdout, calls `evaluateAudit`, prints results, sets `process.exitCode`.\n\nBehavior:\n\n| Severity | Output | Exit code |\n|---|---|---|\n| `critical` | error line per package | `1` (fails pipeline) |\n| `high` | **see open question Q1** | — |\n| `moderate`, `low` | warning line per package | `0` |\n| `info` | ignored | `0` |\n| none | `✔ No known vulnerabilities` | `0` |\n| `npm audit` could not run (network/registry error, invalid JSON) | **see open question Q2** | — |\n\nEach reported line includes: package name, severity, advisory title + URL, whether it's direct or transitive, and whether a fix is available. A summary line with counts per severity is printed at the end.\n\n**CI annotations:** when `GITHUB_ACTIONS === 'true'`, lines are emitted as `::error title=…::…` / `::warning title=…::…` so they show up in the PR's checks UI. Outside GitHub Actions, plain `console.error` / `console.warn` with an `ERROR` / `WARN` prefix. No dependency on any CI provider.\n\nImplementation notes:\n- `npm audit` exits non-zero whenever it finds anything, so the exit code of `npm audit` is **ignored**; the decision comes only from the parsed JSON.\n- Spawned via `child_process.spawnSync('npm', ['audit', '--json'], { shell: process.platform === 'win32' })` — on Windows `npm` is `npm.cmd`, which Node 20+ refuses to spawn without a shell.\n- Scans **all** dependencies (prod + dev), matching \"the repository's vulnerabilities\". Dev-only packages are still flagged but labeled as such in the output.\n- No new dependencies.\n- Docstrings (TSDoc) on every exported function and the module, per CLAUDE.md.\n\n### 2. `package.json`\n\n```json\n\"check:deps\": \"tsx src/scripts/check-deps.ts\"\n```\n\n### 3. Tests: `test/check-deps.test.ts`\n\nUnit tests for `evaluateAudit` using inline fixtures shaped like real `npm audit --json` output (the report captured in plan 001 is a real sample):\n\n- No vulnerabilities → exit 0, no errors/warnings.\n- Only `low` + `moderate` → exit 0, one warning per package.\n- One `critical` among moderates → exit 1, one error + the warnings.\n- `high` → according to Q1.\n- Audit error payload → according to Q2.\n\n## Open questions (need your call before approval)\n\n- **Q1 — What about `high`?** You specified critical → fail and moderate/low → warn, but not `high`. Options:\n  - (a) **Fail on `high` too** — *recommended*. High advisories are usually remotely exploitable; letting them through as a warning is easy to ignore in a PR.\n  - (b) Warn on `high` (literal reading of the requirement).\n- **Q2 — What if `npm audit` itself fails** (registry down, no network)?\n  - (a) **Fail closed** (exit 1 with a clear \"audit could not run\" message) — *recommended*. A silent pass would hide the fact that nothing was checked.\n  - (b) Fail open (warn and exit 0) — avoids blocking PRs during npm registry outages.\n- **Q3 — Pipeline file.** There's no CI yet. Options:\n  - (a) Script only in this plan; the workflow goes in a separate plan — *recommended*, keeps this change small.\n  - (b) Also add `.github/workflows/check-deps.yml` here (trigger `pull_request`, `npm ci`, `npm run check:deps`).\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/scripts/check-deps.ts` (new)\n- `test/check-deps.test.ts` (new)\n- `package.json` — `scripts.check:deps`\n- `.github/workflows/check-deps.yml` only if Q3 = (b)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Fixing any vulnerability.\n- Other CI checks (tests, type-check) — can be added to the same workflow later.\n- `docs/` — after validation, Claude will ask for authorization to document the script (per CLAUDE.md §6).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` → existing + new `check-deps` tests pass.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `npm run check:deps` on the current repo → `✔ No known vulnerabilities`, exit 0.\n4. Critical case: covered by the unit test fixture (no real critical advisory available to reproduce).\n6. {"parentUuid":"16a6a29a-9372-47a3-8725-216a77f8e614","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CexLBPooMVwFqmEz4JiGb","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01STPHifrhRvc6wZaWUgAKZj","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\003-check-deps-script.md","content":"# 003 — `check:deps` script + CI workflow to gate dependency vulnerabilities\n\n**Status:** draft (rev 2 — open questions answered by the user)\n\n## Context\n\nPlans 001 and 002 cleared all current advisories (`npm audit` → 0 vulnerabilities). To keep it that way, the user wants a `check:deps` npm script that runs in a GitHub Actions pipeline on every PR.\n\nCurrent state of the repo:\n- **No CI pipeline yet** (no `.github/`). The remote is a public GitHub fork (`carlossas/recruiting-challenge`, parent `PlataformaT1/recruiting-challenge`).\n- `npm audit --audit-level=<level>` alone is not enough: it can set the exit code by threshold, but it can't emit *warnings* for lower severities while passing, and its output isn't annotated for CI.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Severity policy (answered by the user)\n\n| Severity | Output | Exit code |\n|---|---|---|\n| `critical` | error per package | `1` — **blocks the PR** |\n| `high` | error per package | `1` — **blocks the PR** |\n| `moderate`, `low` | warning per package | `0` |\n| `info` | ignored | `0` |\n| none | `✔ No known vulnerabilities` | `0` |\n| `npm audit` could not run (registry/network error, non-JSON output, JSON `error` payload) | explicit error: `npm audit could not run: <reason>` — makes clear that **nothing was checked** | `1` — **blocks the PR** (fail closed) |\n\n### 2. Script: `src/scripts/check-deps.ts`\n\nTypeScript, run with `tsx`, next to the existing `src/scripts/seed.ts` (same convention; covered by `tsc`, since `tsconfig.json` only includes `src/**`). It must **not** import `src/db.ts` or anything that opens SQLite.\n\nSplit so the logic is testable without the network:\n\n- **`evaluateAudit(report)`** — pure function. Input: parsed `npm audit --json` report. Output: `{ errors, warnings, exitCode }`.\n- **`runAudit()`** — spawns `npm audit --json` and returns either the parsed report or an \"audit could not run\" failure with the reason.\n- **`main()`** — wires both, prints results, sets `process.exitCode`.\n\nOutput per package: name, severity, advisory title + URL, direct vs transitive, prod vs dev, fix available. A summary line with counts per severity at the end.\n\n**CI annotations:** when `GITHUB_ACTIONS === 'true'`, lines are emitted as `::error title=…::…` / `::warning title=…::…` so they show up on the PR's checks. Otherwise plain `console.error` / `console.warn` with an `ERROR` / `WARN` prefix.\n\nImplementation notes:\n- `npm audit` exits non-zero whenever it finds anything, so its exit code is **not** used for the decision; only the parsed JSON is. Its exit code is used only to help classify \"could not run\" when stdout isn't valid JSON.\n- Spawned via `child_process.spawnSync('npm', ['audit', '--json'], { shell: process.platform === 'win32' })` — on Windows `npm` is `npm.cmd`, which Node 20+ refuses to spawn without a shell.\n- Scans **all** dependencies (prod + dev).\n- No new dependencies. TSDoc on the module and every exported function (CLAUDE.md §1).\n\n### 3. `package.json`\n\n```json\n\"check:deps\": \"tsx src/scripts/check-deps.ts\"\n```\n\n### 4. Tests: `test/check-deps.test.ts`\n\nUnit tests for `evaluateAudit` with inline fixtures shaped like real `npm audit --json` output (the report captured during plan 001 is a real sample):\n\n- No vulnerabilities → exit 0, nothing reported.\n- Only `low` + `moderate` → exit 0, one warning per package.\n- One `high` → exit 1, one error.\n- One `critical` among moderates → exit 1, one error + the warnings.\n- `info` only → exit 0, nothing reported.\n- Audit \"could not run\" failure → exit 1, explicit message.\n\n### 5. Workflow: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`\n\n```yaml\nname: CI\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n    branches: [develop, main]\n  workflow_dispatch:\n\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n\nconcurrency:\n  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}\n  cancel-in-progress: true\n\njobs:\n  check-deps:\n    name: check-deps\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7\n        with:\n          node-version: 24\n          cache: npm\n      - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n      - run: npm run check:deps\n```\n\n- Triggers on PRs into `develop` and `main` (branch model defined in plan 004).\n- Job name `check-deps` is the status-check name that branch protection will require (plan 004).\n- **Node 24**: matches local dev; Node 20 reached end-of-life in April 2026 (`engines: >=20` is left unchanged — out of scope).\n- `npm ci --ignore-scripts`: a security check job shouldn't run third-party install scripts, and the script doesn't need `better-sqlite3`'s native build. If `tsx`/esbuild fails without scripts on the runner, fall back to plain `npm ci` (to be confirmed in the first real run).\n- `permissions: contents: read` — least privilege.\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/scripts/check-deps.ts` (new)\n- `test/check-deps.test.ts` (new)\n- `package.json` — `scripts.check:deps`\n- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (new)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Fixing any vulnerability.\n- Other CI jobs (tests, type-check) — easy to add to the same workflow later.\n- Branch model, branch protection, and its docs — plan 004.\n- `docs/` for this script — covered by the plan 004 doc, written after validation (CLAUDE.md §6).\n\n## Validation\n\nLocal (Claude):\n1. `npm test` → existing + new `check-deps` tests pass.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `npm run check:deps` on the current repo → `✔ No known vulnerabilities`, exit 0.\n4. Warning case: scratchpad copy **without** the plan 002 override (`qs@6.15.3`) → 2 warnings (`qs`, `express`), exit 0.\n5. Annotation format: same copy with `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` → lines start with `::warning`.\n6. \"Could not run\" case: run with an unreachable registry (`npm_config_registry=http://127.0.0.1:9`) → explicit error message, exit 1.\n7. `critical` / `high`: covered by unit-test fixtures (no real advisory available to reproduce).\n\nOn GitHub (user, after the first PR — see plan 004):\n8. The `check-deps` check appears on the PR and passes.\n\n## Rollback\n\nDelete the new files and remove the `check:deps` entry from `package.json`.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1543,"cache_read_input_tokens":167145,"output_tokens":9416,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":3749},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1543,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":32,"output_tokens":9416,"cache_read_input_tokens":167145,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1543,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1543},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01STPHifrhRvc6wZaWUgAKZj":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\003-check-deps-script.md","content":"# 003 — `check:deps` script + CI workflow to gate dependency vulnerabilities\n\n**Status:** draft (rev 2 — open questions answered by the user)\n\n## Context\n\nPlans 001 and 002 cleared all current advisories (`npm audit` → 0 vulnerabilities). Severity policy (answered by the user)\n\n| Severity | Output | Exit code |\n|---|---|---|\n| `critical` | error per package | `1` — **blocks the PR** |\n| `high` | error per package | `1` — **blocks the PR** |\n| `moderate`, `low` | warning per package | `0` |\n| `info` | ignored | `0` |\n| none | `✔ No known vulnerabilities` | `0` |\n| `npm audit` could not run (registry/network error, non-JSON output, JSON `error` payload) | explicit error: `npm audit could not run: <reason>` — makes clear that **nothing was checked** | `1` — **blocks the PR** (fail closed) |\n\n### 2. Script: `src/scripts/check-deps.ts`\n\nTypeScript, run with `tsx`, next to the existing `src/scripts/seed.ts` (same convention; covered by `tsc`, since `tsconfig.json` only includes `src/**`). It must **not** import `src/db.ts` or anything that opens SQLite.\n\nSplit so the logic is testable without the network:\n\n- **`evaluateAudit(report)`** — pure function. Input: parsed `npm audit --json` report. Output: `{ errors, warnings, exitCode }`.\n- **`runAudit()`** — spawns `npm audit --json` and returns either the parsed report or an \"audit could not run\" failure with the reason.\n- **`main()`** — wires both, prints results, sets `process.exitCode`.\n\nOutput per package: name, severity, advisory title + URL, direct vs transitive, prod vs dev, fix available. A summary line with counts per severity at the end.\n\n**CI annotations:** when `GITHUB_ACTIONS === 'true'`, lines are emitted as `::error title=…::…` / `::warning title=…::…` so they show up on the PR's checks. Otherwise plain `console.error` / `console.warn` with an `ERROR` / `WARN` prefix.\n\nImplementation notes:\n- `npm audit` exits non-zero whenever it finds anything, so its exit code is **not** used for the decision; only the parsed JSON is. Its exit code is used only to help classify \"could not run\" when stdout isn't valid JSON.\n- Spawned via `child_process.spawnSync('npm', ['audit', '--json'], { shell: process.platform === 'win32' })` — on Windows `npm` is `npm.cmd`, which Node 20+ refuses to spawn without a shell.\n- Scans **all** dependencies (prod + dev).\n- No new dependencies. TSDoc on the module and every exported function (CLAUDE.md §1).\n\n### 3. `package.json`\n\n```json\n\"check:deps\": \"tsx src/scripts/check-deps.ts\"\n```\n\n### 4. Tests: `test/check-deps.test.ts`\n\nUnit tests for `evaluateAudit` with inline fixtures shaped like real `npm audit --json` output (the report captured during plan 001 is a real sample):\n\n- No vulnerabilities → exit 0, nothing reported.\n- Only `low` + `moderate` → exit 0, one warning per package.\n- One `high` → exit 1, one error.\n- One `critical` among moderates → exit 1, one error + the warnings.\n- `info` only → exit 0, nothing reported.\n- Audit \"could not run\" failure → exit 1, explicit message.\n\n### 5. Workflow: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`\n\n```yaml\nname: CI\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n    branches: [develop, main]\n  workflow_dispatch:\n\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n\nconcurrency:\n  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}\n  cancel-in-progress: true\n\njobs:\n  check-deps:\n    name: check-deps\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7\n        with:\n          node-version: 24\n          cache: npm\n      - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n      - run: npm run check:deps\n```\n\n- Triggers on PRs into `develop` and `main` (branch model defined in plan 004).\n- Job name `check-deps` is the status-check name that branch protection will require (plan 004).\n- **Node 24**: matches local dev; Node 20 reached end-of-life in April 2026 (`engines: >=20` is left unchanged — out of scope).\n- `npm ci --ignore-scripts`: a security check job shouldn't run third-party install scripts, and the script doesn't need `better-sqlite3`'s native build. If `tsx`/esbuild fails without scripts on the runner, fall back to plain `npm ci` (to be confirmed in the first real run).\n- `permissions: contents: read` — least privilege.\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/scripts/check-deps.ts` (new)\n- `test/check-deps.test.ts` (new)\n- `package.json` — `scripts.check:deps`\n- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (new)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Fixing any vulnerability.\n- Other CI jobs (tests, type-check) — easy to add to the same workflow later.\n- Branch model, branch protection, and its docs — plan 004.\n- `docs/` for this script — covered by the plan 004 doc, written after validation (CLAUDE.md §6).\n\n## Validation\n\nLocal (Claude):\n1. `npm test` → existing + new `check-deps` tests pass.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `npm run check:deps` on the current repo → `✔ No known vulnerabilities`, exit 0.\n4. Warning case: scratchpad copy **without** the plan 002 override (`qs@6.15.3`) → 2 warnings (`qs`, `express`), exit 0.\n5. Annotation format: same copy with `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` → lines start with `::warning`.\n6. \"Could not run\" case: run with an unreachable registry (`npm_config_registry=http://127.0.0.1:9`) → explicit error message, exit 1.\n7. `critical` / `high`: covered by unit-test fixtures (no real advisory available to reproduce).\n\nOn GitHub (user, after the first PR — see plan 004):\n8. The `check-deps` check appears on the PR and passes.\n\n## Rollback\n\nDelete the new files and remove the `check:deps` entry from `package.json`.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":101,"newStart":1,"newLines":130,"lines":["-# 003 — `check:deps` script to gate dependency vulnerabilities in CI","+# 003 — `check:deps` script + CI workflow to gate dependency vulnerabilities"," ","-**Status:** draft","+**Status:** draft (rev 2 — open questions answered by the user)"," "," ## Context"," ","-Plans 001 and 002 cleared all current advisories (`npm audit` → 0 vulnerabilities). To keep it that way, the user wants a `check:deps` npm script that runs on every new PR in the pipeline:\n\n- **Critical** vulnerability → error, pipeline fails.\n- **Moderate / low** vulnerability → warning, pipeline continues.\n\nCurrent state of the repo:\n- There is **no CI pipeline yet** (no `.github/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, etc.). The remote is GitHub (`github.com/carlossas/recruiting-challenge`).\n- `npm audit --audit-level=<level>` alone is not enough: it can set the exit code by threshold, but it can't emit *warnings* for lower severities while passing, and its text output isn't annotated for CI.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Script: `src/scripts/check-deps.ts`\n\nA small TypeScript script, run with `tsx`, placed next to the existing `src/scripts/seed.ts` (same convention; covered by `tsc` type-checking since `tsconfig.json` only includes `src/**`).\n\nSplit into two parts so the logic is testable without the network:\n\n- **`evaluateAudit(report)`** — pure function. Input: parsed `npm audit --json` report. Output: `{ errors, warnings, exitCode }`.\n- **`main()`** — runs `npm audit --json`, parses stdout, calls `evaluateAudit`, prints results, sets `process.exitCode`.\n\nBehavior:\n\n| Severity | Output | Exit code |\n|---|---|---|\n| `critical` | error line per package | `1` (fails pipeline) |\n| `high` | **see open question Q1** | — |\n| `moderate`, `low` | warning line per package | `0` |\n| `info` | ignored | `0` |\n| none | `✔ No known vulnerabilities` | `0` |\n| `npm audit` could not run (network/registry error, invalid JSON) | **see open question Q2** | — |\n\nEach reported line includes: package name, severity, advisory title + URL, whether it's direct or transitive, and whether a fix is available. A summary line with counts per severity is printed at the end.\n\n**CI annotations:** when `GITHUB_ACTIONS === 'true'`, lines are emitted as `::error title=…::…` / `::warning title=…::…` so they show up in the PR's checks UI. Outside GitHub Actions, plain `console.error` / `console.warn` with an `ERROR` / `WARN` prefix. No dependency on any CI provider.\n\nImplementation notes:\n- `npm audit` exits non-zero whenever it finds anything, so the exit code of `npm audit` is **ignored**; the decision comes only from the parsed JSON.\n- Spawned via `child_process.spawnSync('npm', ['audit', '--json'], { shell: process.platform === 'win32' })` — on Windows `npm` is `npm.cmd`, which Node 20+ refuses to spawn without a shell.\n- Scans **all** dependencies (prod + dev), matching \"the repository's vulnerabilities\". Dev-only packages are still flagged but labeled as such in the output.\n- No new dependencies.\n- Docstrings (TSDoc) on every exported function and the module, per CLAUDE.md.\n\n### 2. `package.json`\n\n```json\n\"check:deps\": \"tsx src/scripts/check-deps.ts\"\n```\n\n### 3. Tests: `test/check-deps.test.ts`\n\nUnit tests for `evaluateAudit` using inline fixtures shaped like real `npm audit --json` output (the report captured in plan 001 is a real sample):\n\n- No vulnerabilities → exit 0, no errors/warnings.\n- Only `low` + `moderate` → exit 0, one warning per package.\n- One `critical` among moderates → exit 1, one error + the warnings.\n- `high` → according to Q1.\n- Audit error payload → according to Q2.\n\n## Open questions (need your call before approval)\n\n- **Q1 — What about `high`?** You specified critical → fail and moderate/low → warn, but not `high`. Options:\n  - (a) **Fail on `high` too** — *recommended*. High advisories are usually remotely exploitable; letting them through as a warning is easy to ignore in a PR.\n  - (b) Warn on `high` (literal reading of the requirement).\n- **Q2 — What if `npm audit` itself fails** (registry down, no network)?\n  - (a) **Fail closed** (exit 1 with a clear \"audit could not run\" message) — *recommended*. A silent pass would hide the fact that nothing was checked.\n  - (b) Fail open (warn and exit 0) — avoids blocking PRs during npm registry outages.\n- **Q3 — Pipeline file.** There's no CI yet. Options:\n  - (a) Script only in this plan; the workflow goes in a separate plan — *recommended*, keeps this change small.\n  - (b) Also add `.github/workflows/check-deps.yml` here (trigger `pull_request`, `npm ci`, `npm run check:deps`).\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/scripts/check-deps.ts` (new)\n- `test/check-deps.test.ts` (new)\n- `package.json` — `scripts.check:deps`\n- `.github/workflows/check-deps.yml` only if Q3 = (b)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Fixing any vulnerability.\n- Other CI checks (tests, type-check) — can be added to the same workflow later.\n- `docs/` — after validation, Claude will ask for authorization to document the script (per CLAUDE.md §6).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` → existing + new `check-deps` tests pass.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `npm run check:deps` on the current repo → `✔ No known vulnerabilities`, exit 0.\n4. Real-world warning case: in a scratchpad copy of the repo **without** the plan 002 override (qs 6.15.3), `npm run check:deps` → 2 warnings (`qs`, `express`), exit 0.\n5. Critical case: covered by the unit test fixture (no real critical advisory available to reproduce).\n6. Annotation format: run with `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` in the scratchpad copy → lines start with `::warning`.\n\n## Rollback\n\nDelete the new files and remove the `check:deps` entry from `package.json`.\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"636b4297-0172-44da-a904-06e8398bafd3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"5bdfe50e-386d-4b74-aa33-2f33ba98fab4","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CexLBPooMVwFqmEz4JiGb","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01B2uxk8wPZ5vX2z9Xno2mLM","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\004-branching-model-and-protection.md","content":"# 004 — Branching model (`develop` → `main`), branch protection, and workflow docs\n\n**Status:** draft\n\n## Context\n\nThe user wants:\n- A `develop` branch. **All PRs target `develop`** (protected).\n- Releases go from `develop` to `main` (also protected).\n- The process documented in `docs/` as \"GitHub workflow — Releases and branches\".\n\nCurrent state:\n- Remote `origin` = `github.com/carlossas/recruiting-challenge` — public fork of `PlataformaT1/recruiting-challenge`, default branch `main`. Only `main` exists remotely (`cbf80ec`, same as local `HEAD`).\n- **`gh` CLI is not installed**, so Claude cannot configure GitHub settings (branch protection, default branch, Actions enablement). Those require the user's GitHub authentication → manual steps for the user (or: user installs `gh` + runs `gh auth login`, then Claude can apply them via the API with per-action approval).\n- **GitHub Actions is disabled by default on forks** until enabled in the repo's *Actions* tab.\n- The submission is scored partly on commit history (\"multiple commits, not one giant squash\" — EVALUATION.md), so merges must preserve individual commits.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Branch model\n\n```\nfeature/*, fix/*, chore/*  ──PR──▶  develop  ──release PR──▶  main\n```\n\n| Branch | Purpose | Created from | Merges into | Direct pushes |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `main` | Released state | — | — | ❌ |\n| `develop` | Integration | `main` | `main` (release PR) | ❌ |\n| `feature/<slug>`, `fix/<slug>`, `chore/<slug>` | One topic each (ideally one plan) | `develop` | `develop` | ✅ (owner's branch) |\n\n- **Merge method: \"Create a merge commit\"** for both feature → `develop` and `develop` → `main`. No squash — keeps every human-written commit visible.\n- A release = a PR from `develop` into `main`.\n\n### 2. Enforce \"only `develop` can merge into `main`\"\n\nGitHub has no native \"allowed source branch\" setting, so a second job is added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (from plan 003) and required on `main`:\n\n```yaml\n  release-source:\n    name: release-source\n    if: github.base_ref == 'main'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - name: Only develop from this repo can be merged into main\n        env:\n          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}\n          HEAD_REPO: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}\n          BASE_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}\n        run: |\n          if [ \"$HEAD_REF\" != \"develop\" ] || [ \"$HEAD_REPO\" != \"$BASE_REPO\" ]; then\n            echo \"::error::PRs into main must come from 'develop' in $BASE_REPO (got '$HEAD_REPO:$HEAD_REF')\"\n            exit 1\n          fi\n```\n\n- Values go through `env`, never interpolated into the shell script, to avoid script injection via branch names.\n- Checks the head **repo** too, so a fork's branch named `develop` can't pass.\n- On PRs into `develop` the job is skipped, which GitHub treats as passing — it's only *required* on `main`.\n\n### 3. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"cca99321-0c9e-4f10-88ee-b39aa94d7336","timestamp":"2026-09-11T21:09:27.714Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\003-check-deps-script.md","oldString":"**Status:** draft (rev 2 — open questions answered by the user)","newString":"**Status:** approved (rev 2 — open questions answered and plan approved by the user)","originalFile":"# 003 — `check:deps` script + CI workflow to gate dependency vulnerabilities\n\n**Status:** draft (rev 2 — open questions answered by the user)\n\n## Context\n\nPlans 001 and 002 cleared all current advisories (`npm audit` → 0 vulnerabilities). To keep it that way, the user wants a `check:deps` npm script that runs in a GitHub Actions pipeline on every PR.\n\nCurrent state of the repo:\n- **No CI pipeline yet** (no `.github/`). The remote is a public GitHub fork (`carlossas/recruiting-challenge`, parent `PlataformaT1/recruiting-challenge`).\n- `npm audit --audit-level=<level>` alone is not enough: it can set the exit code by threshold, but it can't emit *warnings* for lower severities while passing, and its output isn't annotated for CI.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Severity policy (answered by the user)\n\n| Severity | Output | Exit code |\n|---|---|---|\n| `critical` | error per package | `1` — **blocks the PR** |\n| `high` | error per package | `1` — **blocks the PR** |\n| `moderate`, `low` | warning per package | `0` |\n| `info` | ignored | `0` |\n| none | `✔ No known vulnerabilities` | `0` |\n| `npm audit` could not run (registry/network error, non-JSON output, JSON `error` payload) | explicit error: `npm audit could not run: <reason>` — makes clear that **nothing was checked** | `1` — **blocks the PR** (fail closed) |\n\n### 2. Script: `src/scripts/check-deps.ts`\n\nTypeScript, run with `tsx`, next to the existing `src/scripts/seed.ts` (same convention; covered by `tsc`, since `tsconfig.json` only includes `src/**`). It must **not** import `src/db.ts` or anything that opens SQLite.\n\nSplit so the logic is testable without the network:\n\n- **`evaluateAudit(report)`** — pure function. Input: parsed `npm audit --json` report. Output: `{ errors, warnings, exitCode }`.\n- **`runAudit()`** — spawns `npm audit --json` and returns either the parsed report or an \"audit could not run\" failure with the reason.\n- **`main()`** — wires both, prints results, sets `process.exitCode`.\n\nOutput per package: name, severity, advisory title + URL, direct vs transitive, prod vs dev, fix available. A summary line with counts per severity at the end.\n\n**CI annotations:** when `GITHUB_ACTIONS === 'true'`, lines are emitted as `::error title=…::…` / `::warning title=…::…` so they show up on the PR's checks. Otherwise plain `console.error` / `console.warn` with an `ERROR` / `WARN` prefix.\n\nImplementation notes:\n- `npm audit` exits non-zero whenever it finds anything, so its exit code is **not** used for the decision; only the parsed JSON is. Its exit code is used only to help classify \"could not run\" when stdout isn't valid JSON.\n- Spawned via `child_process.spawnSync('npm', ['audit', '--json'], { shell: process.platform === 'win32' })` — on Windows `npm` is `npm.cmd`, which Node 20+ refuses to spawn without a shell.\n- Scans **all** dependencies (prod + dev).\n- No new dependencies. TSDoc on the module and every exported function (CLAUDE.md §1).\n\n### 3. `package.json`\n\n```json\n\"check:deps\": \"tsx src/scripts/check-deps.ts\"\n```\n\n### 4. Tests: `test/check-deps.test.ts`\n\nUnit tests for `evaluateAudit` with inline fixtures shaped like real `npm audit --json` output (the report captured during plan 001 is a real sample):\n\n- No vulnerabilities → exit 0, nothing reported.\n- Only `low` + `moderate` → exit 0, one warning per package.\n- One `high` → exit 1, one error.\n- One `critical` among moderates → exit 1, one error + the warnings.\n- `info` only → exit 0, nothing reported.\n- Audit \"could not run\" failure → exit 1, explicit message.\n\n### 5. Workflow: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`\n\n```yaml\nname: CI\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n    branches: [develop, main]\n  workflow_dispatch:\n\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n\nconcurrency:\n  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}\n  cancel-in-progress: true\n\njobs:\n  check-deps:\n    name: check-deps\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7\n        with:\n          node-version: 24\n          cache: npm\n      - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n      - run: npm run check:deps\n```\n\n- Triggers on PRs into `develop` and `main` (branch model defined in plan 004).\n- Job name `check-deps` is the status-check name that branch protection will require (plan 004).\n- **Node 24**: matches local dev; Node 20 reached end-of-life in April 2026 (`engines: >=20` is left unchanged — out of scope).\n- `npm ci --ignore-scripts`: a security check job shouldn't run third-party install scripts, and the script doesn't need `better-sqlite3`'s native build. report: AuditReport } | { ok: false; reason: string };\n\n/**\n * Tells whether a lockfile node (e.g. `node_modules/qs`) is a dev-only dependency.\n * Returns `undefined` when the node is unknown.\n */\nexport type DevOnlyLookup = (node: string) => boolean | undefined;\n\n/**\n * Applies the severity policy to a parsed `npm audit --json` report.\n *\n * @param report - Parsed audit report.\n * @param isDevOnly - Optional lookup used to label findings as `prod` or `dev`.\n * @returns Errors, warnings, per-severity counts and the gate's exit code.\n */\nexport function evaluateAudit(report: AuditReport, isDevOnly?: DevOnlyLookup): Evaluation {\n  const counts: Record<Severity, number> = { info: 0, low: 0, moderate: 0, high: 0, critical: 0 };\n  const errors: Finding[] = [];\n  const warnings: Finding[] = [];\n\n  for (const vuln of Object.values(report.vulnerabilities)) {\n    if (!(vuln.severity in counts)) continue;\n    counts[vuln.severity] += 1;\n\n    const level = BLOCKING_SEVERITIES.has(vuln.severity)\n      ? 'error'\n      : WARNING_SEVERITIES.has(vuln.severity)\n        ? 'warning'\n        : undefined;\n    if (!level) continue;\n\n    const finding: Finding = {\n      level,\n      packageName: vuln.name,\n      severity: vuln.severity,\n      message: describeVulnerability(vuln, isDevOnly),\n    };\n    (level === 'error' ? errors : warnings).push(finding);\n  }\n\n  return { errors, warnings, counts, exitCode: errors.length > 0 ? 1 : 0 };\n}\n\n/**\n * Parses the raw output of `npm audit --json`.\n *\n * The exit code of `npm audit` is not used to decide pass/fail (it is non-zero\n * whenever anything is found); it only enriches the reason when the output is unusable.\n *\n * @param stdout - Standard output of `npm audit --json`.\n * @param stderr - Standard error, used as extra detail when the audit could not run.\n * @param status - Exit code of `npm audit`, if any.\n * @returns The parsed report, or the reason the audit could not be evaluated.\n */\nexport function parseAuditOutput(stdout: string, stderr = '', status: number | null = null): AuditOutcome {\n  const detail = stderr.trim().split(/\\r?\\n/).slice(-3).join(' | ');\n  const fail = (reason: string): AuditOutcome => ({ ok: false, reason: detail ? `${reason} — ${detail}` : reason });\n\n  if (!stdout.trim()) return fail(`npm audit produced no output (exit code ${status ?? 'unknown'})`);\n\n  let parsed: unknown;\n  try {\n    parsed = JSON.parse(stdout);\n  } catch {\n    return fail('npm audit output is not valid JSON');\n  }\n\n  if (!isRecord(parsed)) return fail('unexpected npm audit report format');\n\n  if (isRecord(parsed.error)) {\n    const parts = [parsed.error.code, parsed.error.summary]\n      .filter((part): part is string => typeof part === 'string' && part.length > 0)\n      .map((part) => part.replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim());\n    return fail(parts.join(': ') || 'npm audit reported an error');\n  }\n\n  if (!isRecord(parsed.vulnerabilities)) return fail('unexpected npm audit report format (missing \"vulnerabilities\")');\n\n  return { ok: true, report: parsed as unknown as AuditReport };\n}\n\n/**\n * Runs `npm audit --json` in the given directory and parses its output.\n *\n * @param cwd - Directory containing `package.json` and `package-lock.json`.\n * @returns The parsed report, or the reason the audit could not run.\n */\nexport function runAudit(cwd: string = process.cwd()): AuditOutcome {\n  const result = spawnSync('npm', ['audit', '--json'], {\n    cwd,\n    encoding: 'utf8',\n    maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,\n    // On Windows `npm` is `npm.cmd`, which Node refuses to spawn without a shell.\n    shell: process.platform === 'win32',\n  });\n  if (result.error) return { ok: false, reason: `failed to start npm: ${result.error.message}` };\n  return parseAuditOutput(result.stdout ?? '', result.stderr ?? '', result.status);\n}\n\n/**\n * Builds a {@link DevOnlyLookup} from `package-lock.json` (lockfile v2/v3 `packages` map).\n *\n * @param lockfilePath - Path to the lockfile.\n * @returns The lookup, or `undefined` if the lockfile can't be read.\n */\nexport function loadDevOnlyLookup(lockfilePath = 'package-lock.json'): DevOnlyLookup | undefined {\n  try {\n    const lock: unknown = JSON.parse(readFileSync(lockfilePath, 'utf8'));\n    if (!isRecord(lock) || !isRecord(lock.packages)) return undefined;\n    const packages = lock.packages;\n    return (node) => {\n      const entry = packages[node];\n      return isRecord(entry) ? entry.dev === true : undefined;\n    };\n  } catch {\n    return undefined;\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Formats a finding for the console or as a GitHub Actions annotation.\n *\n * @param finding - Finding to format.\n * @param githubActions - Emit a `::error` / `::warning` workflow command instead of plain text.\n */\nexport function formatFinding(finding: Finding, githubActions: boolean): string {\n  if (githubActions) {\n    const title = `${finding.severity} vulnerability: ${finding.packageName}`;\n    return `::${finding.level} title=${escapeProperty(title)}::${escapeData(finding.message)}`;\n  }\n  return `${finding.level === 'error' ? 'ERROR' : 'WARN '} ${finding.message}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Formats the message shown when `npm audit` could not run.\n *\n * @param reason - Why the audit could not run.\n * @param githubActions - Emit a `::error` workflow command instead of plain text.\n */\nexport function formatAuditFailure(reason: string, githubActions: boolean): string {\n  const message = `npm audit could not run: ${reason}. No dependencies were checked, so the gate fails closed.`;\n  return githubActions\n    ? `::error title=${escapeProperty('npm audit could not run')}::${escapeData(message)}`\n    : `ERROR ${message}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Formats the one-line summary printed at the end of a run.\n *\n * @param evaluation - Result of {@link evaluateAudit}.\n */\nexport function formatSummary(evaluation: Evaluation): string {\n  const { counts, errors, warnings } = evaluation;\n  const totals = `critical: ${counts.critical}, high: ${counts.high}, moderate: ${counts.moderate}, low: ${counts.low}, info: ${counts.info}`;\n  if (errors.length > 0) return `✖ check:deps FAILED — ${errors.length} blocking vulnerable package(s) (${totals})`;\n  if (warnings.length > 0) return `⚠ check:deps PASSED with ${warnings.length} warning(s) (${totals})`;\n  return '✔ No known vulnerabilities';\n}\n\n/**\n * Entry point: runs the audit, prints findings and a summary, and sets `process.exitCode`.\n */\nexport function main(): void {\n  const githubActions = process.env.GITHUB_ACTIONS === 'true';\n  // Workflow commands must go to stdout to be picked up by the runner.\n  const printError = githubActions ? console.log : console.error;\n  const printWarning = githubActions ? console.log : console.warn;\n\n  const outcome = runAudit();\n  if (!outcome.ok) {\n    printError(formatAuditFailure(outcome.reason, githubActions));\n    process.exitCode = 1;\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const evaluation = evaluateAudit(outcome.report, loadDevOnlyLookup());\n  for (const finding of evaluation.errors) printError(formatFinding(finding, githubActions));\n  for (const finding of evaluation.warnings) printWarning(formatFinding(finding, githubActions));\n  console.log(formatSummary(evaluation));\n  process.exitCode = evaluation.exitCode;\n}\n\n/**\n * Builds the human-readable description of a vulnerable package.\n */\nfunction describeVulnerability(vuln: AuditVulnerability, isDevOnly?: DevOnlyLookup): string {\n  const scope = [vuln.isDirect ? 'direct' : 'transitive'];\n  const dependencyType = classifyDependencyType(vuln.nodes, isDevOnly);\n  if (dependencyType) scope.push(dependencyType);\n\n  const advisories = vuln.via\n    .filter((entry): entry is AuditAdvisory => typeof entry === 'object' && entry !== null)\n    .map((advisory) => `${advisory.title} (${advisory.url})`);\n  const parents = vuln.via.filter((entry): entry is string => typeof entry === 'string');\n  const causes = parents.length > 0 ? [...advisories, `via ${parents.join(', ')}`] : advisories;\n\n  return `${vuln.name} ${vuln.range} [${vuln.severity}] (${scope.join(', ')}) — ${causes.join('; ')} — ${describeFix(vuln.fixAvailable)}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Labels a package as `dev` when every installed node is dev-only, `prod` otherwise,\n * or `undefined` when that can't be determined.\n */\nfunction classifyDependencyType(nodes: string[], isDevOnly?: DevOnlyLookup): 'prod' | 'dev' | undefined {\n  if (!isDevOnly || nodes.length === 0) return undefined;\n  const flags = nodes.map(isDevOnly);\n  if (flags.some((flag) => flag === undefined)) return undefined;\n  return flags.every(Boolean) ? 'dev' : 'prod';\n}\n\n/**\n * Describes the `fixAvailable` field of a vulnerability.\n */\nfunction describeFix(fix: AuditFix): string {\n  if (fix === true) return 'fix available';\n  if (fix === false) return 'no fix available';\n  return `fix available: ${fix.name}@${fix.version}${fix.isSemVerMajor ? ' (semver-major)' : ''}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Narrows an unknown value to a plain object.\n */\nfunction isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {\n  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);\n}\n\n/**\n * Escapes the message part of a GitHub Actions workflow command.\n */\nfunction escapeData(value: string): string {\n  return value.replace(/%/g, {\n  return escapeData(value).replace(/:/g, '%3A').replace(/,/g, '%2C');\n}\n\nif (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) {\n { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport {\n  evaluateAudit,\n  formatAuditFailure,\n  formatFinding,\n  parseAuditOutput,\n  type AuditReport,\n  type AuditVulnerability,\n  type Severity,\n} from '../src/scripts/check-deps.js';\n\n/**\n * Builds a vulnerability entry shaped like `npm audit --json` (report v2).\n */\nfunction vuln(name: string, severity: Severity, overrides: Partial<AuditVulnerability> = {}): AuditVulnerability {\n  return {\n    name,\n    severity,\n    isDirect: false,\n    via: [{ name, title: `${name} advisory`, url: `https://github.com/advisories/${name}`, severity }],\n    range: '<1.0.0',\n    nodes: [`node_modules/${name}`],\n    fixAvailable: true,\n    ...overrides,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Builds an audit report from a list of vulnerabilities.\n */\nfunction report(...vulns: AuditVulnerability[]): AuditReport {\n  return { vulnerabilities: Object.fromEntries(vulns.map((v) => [v.name, v])) };\n}\n\n/** Real report captured during plan 001 (esbuild low, qs + express moderate). */\nconst PLAN_001_REPORT: AuditReport = report(\n  vuln('esbuild', 'low', {\n    via: [{ name: 'esbuild', title: 'esbuild allows arbitrary file read when running the development server on Windows', url: 'https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr', severity: 'low' }],\n    range: '0.27.3 - 0.28.0',\n  }),\n  vuln('express', 'moderate', { isDirect: true, via: ['qs'], range: '4.22.2' }),\n  vuln('qs', 'moderate', {\n    via: [\n      { name: 'qs', title: 'qs array-limit bypass via bracket-key comma parsing', url: 'https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx', severity: 'moderate' },\n      { name: 'qs', title: 'qs: Denial of Service via Attacker Controlled isBuffer', url: 'https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g', severity: 'moderate' },\n    ],\n    range: '2.2.5 - 6.15.3',\n  }),\n);\n\ntest('check-deps: no vulnerabilities passes with nothing reported', () => {\n  const result = evaluateAudit(report());\n  assert.equal(result.exitCode, 0);\n  assert.equal(result.errors.length, 0);\n  assert.equal(result.warnings.length, 0);\n});\n\ntest('check-deps: low and moderate only produce warnings and pass', () => {\n  const result = evaluateAudit(PLAN_001_REPORT);\n  assert.equal(result.exitCode, 0);\n  assert.equal(result.errors.length, 0);\n  assert.deepEqual(result.warnings.map((w) => w.packageName).sort(), ['esbuild', 'express', 'qs']);\n  assert.deepEqual(result.counts, { info: 0, low: 1, moderate: 2, high: 0, critical: 0 });\n});\n\ntest('check-deps: high blocks', () => {\n  const result = evaluateAudit(report(vuln('lodash', 'high')));\n  assert.equal(result.exitCode, 1);\n  assert.equal(result.errors.length, 1);\n  assert.equal(result.errors[0]!.severity, 'high');\n});\n\ntest('check-deps: critical blocks and moderates are still reported as warnings', () => {\n  const result = evaluateAudit(report(vuln('minimist', 'critical'), vuln('qs', 'moderate'), vuln('debug', 'low')));\n  assert.equal(result.exitCode, 1);\n  assert.deepEqual(result.errors.map((e) => e.packageName), ['minimist']);\n  assert.deepEqual(result.warnings.map((w) => w.packageName).sort(), ['debug', 'qs']);\n});\n\ntest('check-deps: info is ignored', () => {\n  const result = evaluateAudit(report(vuln('left-pad', 'info')));\n  assert.equal(result.exitCode, 0);\n  assert.equal(result.errors.length + result.warnings.length, 0);\n  assert.equal(result.counts.info, 1);\n});\n\ntest('check-deps: message includes advisory, direct/transitive, prod/dev and fix info', () => {\n  const result = evaluateAudit(\n    report(\n      vuln('esbuild', 'low', { fixAvailable: { name: 'tsx', version: '4.23.13', isSemVerMajor: false } }),\n      vuln('express', 'moderate', { isDirect: true, via: ['qs'], fixAvailable: false }),\n    ),\n    (node) => node === 'node_modules/esbuild',\n  );\n  const byName = Object.fromEntries(result.warnings.map((w) => [w.packageName, w.message]));\n  assert.match(byName.esbuild!, /\\(transitive, dev\\)/);\n  assert.match(byName.esbuild!, /esbuild advisory \\(https:\\/\\/github\\.com\\/advisories\\/esbuild\\)/);\n  assert.match(byName.esbuild!, /fix available: tsx@4\\.23\\.13$/);\n  assert.match(byName.express!, /\\(direct, prod\\)/);\n  assert.match(byName.express!, /via qs/);\n  assert.match(byName.express!, /no fix available$/);\n});\n\ntest('check-deps: parseAuditOutput accepts a valid report', () => {\n  const outcome = parseAuditOutput(JSON.stringify({ auditReportVersion: 2, vulnerabilities: {} }), '', 0);\n  assert.equal(outcome.ok, log/);\n});\n\ntest('check-deps: parseAuditOutput fails closed on an unexpected shape', () => {","originalFile":"import { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport {\n  evaluateAudit,\n  formatAuditFailure,\n  formatFinding,\n  parseAuditOutput,\n  type AuditReport,\n  type AuditVulnerability,\n  type Severity,\n} from '../src/scripts/check-deps.js';\n\n/**\n * Builds a vulnerability entry shaped like `npm audit --json` (report v2).\n */\nfunction vuln(name: string, severity: Severity, overrides: Partial<AuditVulnerability> = {}): AuditVulnerability {\n  return {\n    name,\n    severity,\n    isDirect: false,\n    via: [{ name, title: `${name} advisory`, url: `https://github.com/advisories/${name}`, severity }],\n    range: '<1.0.0',\n    nodes: [`node_modules/${name}`],\n    fixAvailable: true,\n    ...overrides,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Builds an audit report from a list of vulnerabilities.\n */\nfunction report(...vulns: AuditVulnerability[]): AuditReport {\n  return { vulnerabilities: Object.fromEntries(vulns.map((v) => [v.name, v])) };\n}\n\n/** Real report captured during plan 001 (esbuild low, qs + express moderate). */\nconst PLAN_001_REPORT: AuditReport = report(\n  vuln('esbuild', 'low', {\n    via: [{ name: 'esbuild', title: 'esbuild allows arbitrary file read when running the development server on Windows', url: 'https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr', severity: 'low' }],\n    range: '0.27.3 - 0.28.0',\n  }),\n  vuln('express', 'moderate', { isDirect: true, via: ['qs'], range: '4.22.2' }),\n  vuln('qs', 'moderate', {\n    via: [\n      { name: 'qs', title: 'qs array-limit bypass via bracket-key comma parsing', url: 'https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx', severity: 'moderate' },\n      { name: 'qs', title: 'qs: Denial of Service via Attacker Controlled isBuffer', url: 'https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g', severity: 'moderate' },\n    ],\n    range: '2.2.5 - 6.15.3',\n  }),\n);\n\ntest('check-deps: no vulnerabilities passes with nothing reported', () => {\n  const result = evaluateAudit(report());\n  assert.equal(result.exitCode, 0);\n  assert.equal(result.errors.length, 0);\n  assert.equal(result.warnings.length, 0);\n});\n\ntest('check-deps: low and moderate only produce warnings and pass', () => {\n  const result = evaluateAudit(PLAN_001_REPORT);\n  assert.equal(result.exitCode, 0);\n  assert.equal(result.errors.length, 0);\n  assert.deepEqual(result.warnings.map((w) => w.packageName).sort(), ['esbuild', 'express', 'qs']);\n  assert.deepEqual(result.counts, { info: 0, low: 1, moderate: 2, high: 0, critical: 0 });\n});\n\ntest('check-deps: high blocks', () => {\n  const result = evaluateAudit(report(vuln('lodash', 'high')));\n  assert.equal(result.exitCode, 1);\n  assert.equal(result.errors.length, 1);\n  assert.equal(result.errors[0]!.severity, 'high');\n});\n\ntest('check-deps: critical blocks and moderates are still reported as warnings', () => {\n  const result = evaluateAudit(report(vuln('minimist', 'critical'), vuln('qs', 'moderate'), vuln('debug', 'low')));\n  assert.equal(result.exitCode, 1);\n  assert.deepEqual(result.errors.map((e) => e.packageName), ['minimist']);\n  assert.deepEqual(result.warnings.map((w) => w.packageName).sort(), ['debug', 'qs']);\n});\n\ntest('check-deps: info is ignored', () => {\n  const result = evaluateAudit(report(vuln('left-pad', 'info')));\n  assert.equal(result.exitCode, 0);\n  assert.equal(result.errors.length + result.warnings.length, 0);\n  assert.equal(result.counts.info, 1);\n});\n\ntest('check-deps: message includes advisory, direct/transitive, prod/dev and fix info', () => {\n  const result = evaluateAudit(\n    report(\n      vuln('esbuild', 'low', { fixAvailable: { name: 'tsx', version: '4.23.13', isSemVerMajor: false } }),\n      vuln('express', 'moderate', { isDirect: true, via: ['qs'], fixAvailable: false }),\n    ),\n    (node) => node === 'node_modules/esbuild',\n  );\n  const byName = Object.fromEntries(result.warnings.map((w) => [w.packageName, w.message]));\n  assert.match(byName.esbuild!, /\\(transitive, dev\\)/);\n  assert.match(byName.esbuild!, /esbuild advisory \\(https:\\/\\/github\\.com\\/advisories\\/esbuild\\)/);\n  assert.match(byName.esbuild!, /fix available: tsx@4\\.23\\.13$/);\n  assert.match(byName.express!, /\\(direct, prod\\)/);\n  assert.match(byName.express!, /via qs/);\n  assert.match(byName.express!, /no fix available$/);\n});\n\ntest('check-deps: parseAuditOutput accepts a valid report', () => {\n  const outcome = parseAuditOutput(JSON.stringify({ auditReportVersion: 2, vulnerabilities: {} }), '', 0);\n  assert.equal(outcome.ok, true);\n});\n\ntest('check-deps: parseAuditOutput fails closed on empty output', () => {\n  const outcome = parseAuditOutput('', 'npm ERR! network', 1);\n  assert.equal(outcome.ok, false);\n  assert.match(!outcome.ok ? outcome.reason : '', /no output \\(exit code 1\\).*network/);\n});\n\ntest('check-deps: parseAuditOutput fails closed on invalid JSON', To keep it that way, the user wants a `check:deps` npm script that runs in a GitHub Actions pipeline on every PR.\n\nCurrent state of the repo:\n- **No CI pipeline yet** (no `.github/`). The remote is a public GitHub fork (`carlossas/recruiting-challenge`, parent `PlataformaT1/recruiting-challenge`).\n- `npm audit --audit-level=<level>` alone is not enough: it can set the exit code by threshold, but it can't emit *warnings* for lower severities while passing, and its output isn't annotated for CI.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Severity policy (answered by the user)\n\n| Severity | Output | Exit code |\n|---|---|---|\n| `critical` | error per package | `1` — **blocks the PR** |\n| `high` | error per package | `1` — **blocks the PR** |\n| `moderate`, `low` | warning per package | `0` |\n| `info` | ignored | `0` |\n| none | `✔ No known vulnerabilities` | `0` |\n| `npm audit` could not run (registry/network error, non-JSON output, JSON `error` payload) | explicit error: `npm audit could not run: <reason>` — makes clear that **nothing was checked** | `1` — **blocks the PR** (fail closed) |\n\n### 2. Script: `src/scripts/check-deps.ts`\n\nTypeScript, run with `tsx`, next to the existing `src/scripts/seed.ts` (same convention; covered by `tsc`, since `tsconfig.json` only includes `src/**`). It must **not** import `src/db.ts` or anything that opens SQLite.\n\nSplit so the logic is testable without the network:\n\n- **`evaluateAudit(report)`** — pure function. Input: parsed `npm audit --json` report. Output: `{ errors, warnings, exitCode }`.\n- **`runAudit()`** — spawns `npm audit --json` and returns either the parsed report or an \"audit could not run\" failure with the reason.\n- **`main()`** — wires both, prints results, sets `process.exitCode`.\n\nOutput per package: name, severity, advisory title + URL, direct vs transitive, prod vs dev, fix available. A summary line with counts per severity at the end.\n\n**CI annotations:** when `GITHUB_ACTIONS === 'true'`, lines are emitted as `::error title=…::…` / `::warning title=…::…` so they show up on the PR's checks. Otherwise plain `console.error` / `console.warn` with an `ERROR` / `WARN` prefix.\n\nImplementation notes:\n- `npm audit` exits non-zero whenever it finds anything, so its exit code is **not** used for the decision; only the parsed JSON is. Its exit code is used only to help classify \"could not run\" when stdout isn't valid JSON.\n- Spawned via `child_process.spawnSync('npm', ['audit', '--json'], { shell: process.platform === 'win32' })` — on Windows `npm` is `npm.cmd`, which Node 20+ refuses to spawn without a shell.\n- Scans **all** dependencies (prod + dev).\n- No new dependencies. TSDoc on the module and every exported function (CLAUDE.md §1).\n\n### 3. `package.json`\n\n```json\n\"check:deps\": \"tsx src/scripts/check-deps.ts\"\n```\n\n### 4. Tests: `test/check-deps.test.ts`\n\nUnit tests for `evaluateAudit` with inline fixtures shaped like real `npm audit --json` output (the report captured during plan 001 is a real sample):\n\n- No vulnerabilities → exit 0, nothing reported.\n- Only `low` + `moderate` → exit 0, one warning per package.\n- One `high` → exit 1, one error.\n- One `critical` among moderates → exit 1, one error + the warnings.\n- `info` only → exit 0, nothing reported.\n- Audit \"could not run\" failure → exit 1, explicit message.\n\n### 5. Workflow: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`\n\n```yaml\nname: CI\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n    branches: [develop, main]\n  workflow_dispatch:\n\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n\nconcurrency:\n  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}\n  cancel-in-progress: true\n\njobs:\n  check-deps:\n    name: check-deps\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7\n        with:\n          node-version: 24\n          cache: npm\n      - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n      - run: npm run check:deps\n```\n\n- Triggers on PRs into `develop` and `main` (branch model defined in plan 004).\n- Job name `check-deps` is the status-check name that branch protection will require (plan 004).\n- **Node 24**: matches local dev; Node 20 reached end-of-life in April 2026 (`engines: >=20` is left unchanged — out of scope).\n- `npm ci --ignore-scripts`: a security check job shouldn't run third-party install scripts, and the script doesn't need `better-sqlite3`'s native build. If `tsx`/esbuild fails without scripts on the runner, fall back to plain `npm ci` (to be confirmed in the first real run).\n- `permissions: contents: read` — least privilege.\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/scripts/check-deps.ts` (new)\n- `test/check-deps.test.ts` (new)\n- `package.json` — `scripts.check:deps`\n- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (new)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Fixing any vulnerability.\n- Other CI jobs (tests, type-check) — easy to add to the same workflow later.\n- Branch model, branch protection, and its docs — plan 004.\n- `docs/` for this script — covered by the plan 004 doc, written after validation (CLAUDE.md §6).\n\n## Validation\n\nLocal (Claude):\n1. `npm test` → existing + new `check-deps` tests pass.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `npm run check:deps` on the current repo → `✔ No known vulnerabilities`, exit 0.\n4. Warning case: scratchpad copy **without** the plan 002 override (`qs@6.15.3`) → 2 warnings (`qs`, `express`), exit 0.\n5. Annotation format: same copy with `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` → lines start with `::warning`.\n6. \"Could not run\" case: run with an unreachable registry (`npm_config_registry=http://127.0.0.1:9`) → explicit error message, exit 1.\n7. `critical` / `high`: covered by unit-test fixtures (no real advisory available to reproduce).\n\nOn GitHub (user, after the first PR — see plan 004):\n8. The `check-deps` check appears on the PR and passes.\n\n## Rollback\n\nDelete the new files and remove the `check:deps` entry from `package.json`.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":6,"newStart":1,"newLines":6,"lines":[" # 003 — `check:deps` script + CI workflow to gate dependency vulnerabilities"," ","-**Status:** approved (rev 2 — open questions answered and plan approved by the user)","+**Status:** done locally (2026-09-11) — GitHub run pending (validation step 8, after plan 004 bootstrap)"," "," ## Context"," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"d83a58f5-b071-4615-b814-9ef5a2d1cf38","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"main"}

Fallback: plain `npm ci`.\n","originalFile":"# 003 — `check:deps` script + CI workflow to gate dependency vulnerabilities\n\n**Status:** done locally (2026-09-11) — GitHub run pending (validation step 8, after plan 004 bootstrap)\n\n## Context\n\nPlans 001 and 002 cleared all current advisories (`npm audit` → 0 vulnerabilities). To keep it that way, the user wants a `check:deps` npm script that runs in a GitHub Actions pipeline on every PR.\n\nCurrent state of the repo:\n- **No CI pipeline yet** (no `.github/`). The remote is a public GitHub fork (`carlossas/recruiting-challenge`, parent `PlataformaT1/recruiting-challenge`).\n- `npm audit --audit-level=<level>` alone is not enough: it can set the exit code by threshold, but it can't emit *warnings* for lower severities while passing, and its output isn't annotated for CI.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Severity policy (answered by the user)\n\n| Severity | Output | Exit code |\n|---|---|---|\n| `critical` | error per package | `1` — **blocks the PR** |\n| `high` | error per package | `1` — **blocks the PR** |\n| `moderate`, `low` | warning per package | `0` |\n| `info` | ignored | `0` |\n| none | `✔ No known vulnerabilities` | `0` |\n| `npm audit` could not run (registry/network error, non-JSON output, JSON `error` payload) | explicit error: `npm audit could not run: <reason>` — makes clear that **nothing was checked** | `1` — **blocks the PR** (fail closed) |\n\n### 2. Script: `src/scripts/check-deps.ts`\n\nTypeScript, run with `tsx`, next to the existing `src/scripts/seed.ts` (same convention; covered by `tsc`, since `tsconfig.json` only includes `src/**`). It must **not** import `src/db.ts` or anything that opens SQLite.\n\nSplit so the logic is testable without the network:\n\n- **`evaluateAudit(report)`** — pure function. Input: parsed `npm audit --json` report. Output: `{ errors, warnings, exitCode }`.\n- **`runAudit()`** — spawns `npm audit --json` and returns either the parsed report or an \"audit could not run\" failure with the reason.\n- **`main()`** — wires both, prints results, sets `process.exitCode`.\n\nOutput per package: name, severity, advisory title + URL, direct vs transitive, prod vs dev, fix available. A summary line with counts per severity at the end.\n\n**CI annotations:** when `GITHUB_ACTIONS === 'true'`, lines are emitted as `::error title=…::…` / `::warning title=…::…` so they show up on the PR's checks. Otherwise plain `console.error` / `console.warn` with an `ERROR` / `WARN` prefix.\n\nImplementation notes:\n- `npm audit` exits non-zero whenever it finds anything, so its exit code is **not** used for the decision; only the parsed JSON is. Its exit code is used only to help classify \"could not run\" when stdout isn't valid JSON.\n- Spawned via `child_process.spawnSync('npm', ['audit', '--json'], { shell: process.platform === 'win32' })` — on Windows `npm` is `npm.cmd`, which Node 20+ refuses to spawn without a shell.\n- Scans **all** dependencies (prod + dev).\n- No new dependencies. TSDoc on the module and every exported function (CLAUDE.md §1).\n\n### 3. `package.json`\n\n```json\n\"check:deps\": \"tsx src/scripts/check-deps.ts\"\n```\n\n### 4. Tests: `test/check-deps.test.ts`\n\nUnit tests for `evaluateAudit` with inline fixtures shaped like real `npm audit --json` output (the report captured during plan 001 is a real sample):\n\n- No vulnerabilities → exit 0, nothing reported.\n- Only `low` + `moderate` → exit 0, one warning per package.\n- One `high` → exit 1, one error.\n- One `critical` among moderates → exit 1, one error + the warnings.\n- `info` only → exit 0, nothing reported.\n- Audit \"could not run\" failure → exit 1, explicit message.\n\n### 5. Workflow: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`\n\n```yaml\nname: CI\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n    branches: [develop, main]\n  workflow_dispatch:\n\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n\nconcurrency:\n  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}\n  cancel-in-progress: true\n\njobs:\n  check-deps:\n    name: check-deps\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7\n        with:\n          node-version: 24\n          cache: npm\n      - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n      - run: npm run check:deps\n```\n\n- Triggers on PRs into `develop` and `main` (branch model defined in plan 004).\n- Job name `check-deps` is the status-check name that branch protection will require (plan 004).\n- **Node 24**: matches local dev; Node 20 reached end-of-life in April 2026 (`engines: >=20` is left unchanged — out of scope).\n- `npm ci --ignore-scripts`: a security check job shouldn't run third-party install scripts, and the script doesn't need `better-sqlite3`'s native build. If `tsx`/esbuild fails without scripts on the runner, fall back to plain `npm ci` (to be confirmed in the first real run).\n- `permissions: contents: read` — least privilege.\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/scripts/check-deps.ts` (new)\n- `test/check-deps.test.ts` (new)\n- `package.json` — `scripts.check:deps`\n- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (new)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Fixing any vulnerability.\n- Other CI jobs (tests, type-check) — easy to add to the same workflow later.\n- Branch model, branch protection, and its docs — plan 004.\n- `docs/` for this script — covered by the plan 004 doc, written after validation (CLAUDE.md §6).\n\n## Validation\n\nLocal (Claude):\n1. `npm test` → existing + new `check-deps` tests pass.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `npm run check:deps` on the current repo → `✔ No known vulnerabilities`, exit 0.\n4. Warning case: scratchpad copy **without** the plan 002 override (`qs@6.15.3`) → 2 warnings (`qs`, `express`), exit 0.\n5. Annotation format: same copy with `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` → lines start with `::warning`.\n6. \"Could not run\" case: run with an unreachable registry (`npm_config_registry=http://127.0.0.1:9`) → explicit error message, exit 1.\n7. `critical` / `high`: covered by unit-test fixtures (no real advisory available to reproduce).\n\nOn GitHub (user, after the first PR — see plan 004):\n8. {"parentUuid":"6b7f4ef0-3ab1-4f6a-aaac-2d3db8e406e4","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CexLor2tCS2puEyzwS1tP","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01P4CoDLh9QNUQfvYeRwg2B5","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\004-branching-model-and-protection.md","content":"# 004 — Branching model (`develop` → `main`), branch protection, and workflow docs\n\n**Status:** draft (rev 2 — `gh` available, open questions answered by the user)\n\n## Context\n\nThe user wants:\n- A `develop` branch as the **default branch**. **All PRs target `develop`** (protected).\n- `main` is **only for production deployments**: it receives releases from `develop` (also protected).\n- The process documented in `docs/` as \"GitHub workflow — Releases and branches\".\n\nCurrent state (checked with `gh`, read-only):\n- Remote `origin` = `github.com/carlossas/recruiting-challenge` — public fork of `PlataformaT1/recruiting-challenge`. Default branch `main`. Only `main` exists remotely (`cbf80ec`, same as local `HEAD`).\n- `gh` 2.100.0 installed at `C:\\Program Files\\GitHub CLI\\gh.exe` (not on this session's `PATH`; called by full path). Logged in as `carlossas`, permission `ADMIN`, token scopes `repo`, `workflow`.\n- No rulesets and no classic branch protection yet.\n- Actions: `enabled: true`, `allowed_actions: all` at the repo level.\n- Merge methods allowed: merge, squash, rebase.\n- The submission is scored partly on commit history (\"multiple commits, not one giant squash\" — EVALUATION.md), so merges must preserve individual commits.\n\n## Answers to the open questions (user)\n\n- **Q1 — Required approvals: 0.** It's a single-maintainer challenge; GitHub doesn't allow approving your own PR.\n- **Q2 — Rules apply to administrators: yes.** No bypass actors, so the owner can't push directly either.\n- **Q3 — Default branch: `develop`.** `main` is only for production deployments.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Branch model\n\n```\nfeature/*, fix/*, chore/*  ──PR──▶  develop (default)  ──release PR──▶  main (production)\n```\n\n| Branch | Purpose | Created from | Merges into | Direct pushes |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `main` | Production — only what's deployed | — | — | ❌ |\n| `develop` | Default + integration branch | `main` | `main` (release PR) | ❌ |\n| `feature/<slug>`, `fix/<slug>`, `chore/<slug>` | One topic each (ideally one plan) | `develop` | `develop` | ✅ (owner's branch) |\n\n- **Merge method: merge commit only** (enforced by the rulesets) for both feature → `develop` and `develop` → `main`. Keeps every human-written commit visible.\n- A release = a PR from `develop` into `main`.\n\n### 2. Enforce \"only `develop` can merge into `main`\"\n\nGitHub has no native \"allowed source branch\" rule, so a second job is added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and required on `main`:\n\n```yaml\n  release-source:\n    name: release-source\n    if: github.base_ref == 'main'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - name: Only develop from this repo can be merged into main\n        env:\n          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}\n          HEAD_REPO: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}\n          BASE_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}\n        run: |\n          if [ \"$HEAD_REF\" != \"develop\" ] || [ \"$HEAD_REPO\" != \"$BASE_REPO\" ]; then\n            echo \"::error::PRs into main must come from 'develop' in $BASE_REPO (got '$HEAD_REPO:$HEAD_REF')\"\n            exit 1\n          fi\n```\n\n- Values go through `env`, never interpolated into the shell script (no script injection via branch names).\n- Checks the head **repo** too, so a fork's branch named `develop` can't pass.\n- On PRs into `develop` the job is skipped, which GitHub treats as passing — it's only *required* on `main`.\n\n### 3. Branch protection via repository rulesets (`gh api`)\n\nRulesets instead of classic branch protection: they are the current GitHub mechanism, can restrict merge methods, and accept required checks by name **before they have ever run** (so protection can be applied before the first PR).\n\nThe ruleset definitions are versioned in the repo so they're reviewable and reproducible:\n\n- `.github/rulesets/develop.json`\n- `.github/rulesets/main.json`\n\n(GitHub does not read this folder automatically; it's only storage. They're applied with `gh`.)\n\n| Rule | `develop` | `main` |\n|---|---|---|\n| Restrict deletions | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Block force pushes (`non_fast_forward`) | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Require a pull request | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Required approvals | 0 (Q1) | 0 (Q1) |\n| Allowed merge methods | `merge` only | `merge` only |\n| Required status checks | `check-deps` | `check-deps`, `release-source` |\n| Require branch up to date (`strict`) | ✅ | ❌ — see note |\n| Checks must come from GitHub Actions (`integration_id: 15368`) | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Bypass actors | none (Q2 — applies to admins) | none (Q2) |\n\n**Why `strict` is off on `main`:** each release merge creates a merge commit on `main` that `develop` doesn't have. With `strict` on, the next release PR would require updating `develop` from `main`, which means pushing a merge commit directly to `develop` — blocked by `develop`'s own ruleset. Leaving it off avoids that deadlock; `check-deps` still runs on the release PR.\n\n**`integration_id: 15368`** (the GitHub Actions app) means the required checks only count when reported by Actions, so a manually posted commit status with the same name can't satisfy them.\n\nExample (`develop.json`):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"name\": \"develop\",\n  \"target\": \"branch\",\n  \"enforcement\": \"active\",\n  \"bypass_actors\": [],\n  \"conditions\": { \"ref_name\": { \"include\": [\"refs/heads/develop\"], \"exclude\": [] } },\n  \"rules\": [\n    { \"type\": \"deletion\" },\n    { \"type\": \"non_fast_forward\" },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"pull_request\",\n      \"parameters\": {\n        \"required_approving_review_count\": 0,\n        \"dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push\": false,\n        \"require_code_owner_review\": false,\n        \"require_last_push_approval\": false,\n        \"required_review_thread_resolution\": false,\n        \"allowed_merge_methods\": [\"merge\"]\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"required_status_checks\",\n      \"parameters\": {\n        \"strict_required_status_checks_policy\": true,\n        \"do_not_enforce_on_create\": false,\n        \"required_status_checks\": [{ \"context\": \"check-deps\", \"integration_id\": 15368 }]\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n`main.json` is the same with `refs/heads/main`, `strict_required_status_checks_policy: false`, and both `check-deps` and `release-source`.\n\n### 4. Repository settings (`gh`)\n\n```sh\ngh repo edit carlossas/recruiting-challenge --default-branch develop\ngh repo edit carlossas/recruiting-challenge --enable-merge-commit --enable-squash-merge=false --enable-rebase-merge=false\n```\n\nThe second command mirrors the rulesets at repo level so the PR UI only offers \"Create a merge commit\".\n\n### 5. CLAUDE.md\n\nAdd to §2 (Git): the branch model; `develop` is the default branch and `main` is production-only; Claude never pushes to `main` or `develop`; work happens on `feature/*`/`fix/*`/`chore/*` branches merged via PR.\n\n### 6. Docs: `docs/github-workflow.md` — \"GitHub workflow — Releases and branches\"\n\nWritten **after** the change is validated (CLAUDE.md §6; the user has already authorized this doc). Contents:\n- Branch model diagram (mermaid) and naming conventions.\n- **`develop` is the default branch; `main` is only for production deployments.**\n- Day-to-day flow: branch from `develop` → PR → checks → merge commit.\n- Release flow: PR `develop` → `main`, merge commit.\n- CI checks: what `check-deps` and `release-source` do; severity policy (critical/high block, moderate/low warn, audit failure blocks); how to run `npm run check:deps` locally.\n- Protection rules (table in §3), where the ruleset JSON lives, and how to re-apply/update them with `gh`.\n- What's *not* enforced (approvals = 0, no hotfix flow yet).\n\n## Execution steps\n\nCommits are human-written (CLAUDE.md §2): the user commits; Claude prepares files and runs only approved commands. `gh` is invoked as `\"/c/Program Files/GitHub CLI/gh.exe\"`.\n\n**Claude (after approval + explicit go for the push):**\n\n1.
