Default branch `main`. Only `main` exists remotely (`cbf80ec`, same as local `HEAD`).\n- `gh` 2.100.0 installed at `C:\\Program Files\\GitHub CLI\\gh.exe` (not on this session's `PATH`; called by full path). Logged in as `carlossas`, permission `ADMIN`, token scopes `repo`, `workflow`.\n- No rulesets and no classic branch protection yet.\n- Actions: `enabled: true`, `allowed_actions: all` at the repo level.\n- Merge methods allowed: merge, squash, rebase.\n- The submission is scored partly on commit history (\"multiple commits, not one giant squash\" — EVALUATION.md), so merges must preserve individual commits.\n\n## Answers to the open questions (user)\n\n- **Q1 — Required approvals: 0.** It's a single-maintainer challenge; GitHub doesn't allow approving your own PR.\n- **Q2 — Rules apply to administrators: yes.** No bypass actors, so the owner can't push directly either.\n- **Q3 — Default branch: `develop`.** `main` is only for production deployments.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Branch model\n\n```\nfeature/*, fix/*, chore/*  ──PR──▶  develop (default)  ──release PR──▶  main (production)\n```\n\n| Branch | Purpose | Created from | Merges into | Direct pushes |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `main` | Production — only what's deployed | — | — | ❌ |\n| `develop` | Default + integration branch | `main` | `main` (release PR) | ❌ |\n| `feature/<slug>`, `fix/<slug>`, `chore/<slug>` | One topic each (ideally one plan) | `develop` | `develop` | ✅ (owner's branch) |\n\n- **Merge method: merge commit only** (enforced by the rulesets) for both feature → `develop` and `develop` → `main`. Keeps every human-written commit visible.\n- A release = a PR from `develop` into `main`.\n\n### 2. Enforce \"only `develop` can merge into `main`\"\n\nGitHub has no native \"allowed source branch\" rule, so a second job is added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and required on `main`:\n\n```yaml\n  release-source:\n    name: release-source\n    if: github.base_ref == 'main'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - name: Only develop from this repo can be merged into main\n        env:\n          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}\n          HEAD_REPO: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}\n          BASE_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}\n        run: |\n          if [ \"$HEAD_REF\" != \"develop\" ] || [ \"$HEAD_REPO\" != \"$BASE_REPO\" ]; then\n            echo \"::error::PRs into main must come from 'develop' in $BASE_REPO (got '$HEAD_REPO:$HEAD_REF')\"\n            exit 1\n          fi\n```\n\n- Values go through `env`, never interpolated into the shell script (no script injection via branch names).\n- Checks the head **repo** too, so a fork's branch named `develop` can't pass.\n- On PRs into `develop` the job is skipped, which GitHub treats as passing — it's only *required* on `main`.\n\n### 3. Branch protection via repository rulesets (`gh api`)\n\nRulesets instead of classic branch protection: they are the current GitHub mechanism, can restrict merge methods, and accept required checks by name **before they have ever run** (so protection can be applied before the first PR).\n\nThe ruleset definitions are versioned in the repo so they're reviewable and reproducible:\n\n- `.github/rulesets/develop.json`\n- `.github/rulesets/main.json`\n\n(GitHub does not read this folder automatically; it's only storage. They're applied with `gh`.)\n\n| Rule | `develop` | `main` |\n|---|---|---|\n| Restrict deletions | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Block force pushes (`non_fast_forward`) | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Require a pull request | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Required approvals | 0 (Q1) | 0 (Q1) |\n| Allowed merge methods | `merge` only | `merge` only |\n| Required status checks | `check-deps` | `check-deps`, `release-source` |\n| Require branch up to date (`strict`) | ✅ | ❌ — see note |\n| Checks must come from GitHub Actions (`integration_id: 15368`) | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Bypass actors | none (Q2 — applies to admins) | none (Q2) |\n\n**Why `strict` is off on `main`:** each release merge creates a merge commit on `main` that `develop` doesn't have. With `strict` on, the next release PR would require updating `develop` from `main`, which means pushing a merge commit directly to `develop` — blocked by `develop`'s own ruleset. Leaving it off avoids that deadlock; `check-deps` still runs on the release PR.\n\n**`integration_id: 15368`** (the GitHub Actions app) means the required checks only count when reported by Actions, so a manually posted commit status with the same name can't satisfy them.\n\nExample (`develop.json`):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"name\": \"develop\",\n  \"target\": \"branch\",\n  \"enforcement\": \"active\",\n  \"bypass_actors\": [],\n  \"conditions\": { \"ref_name\": { \"include\": [\"refs/heads/develop\"], \"exclude\": [] } },\n  \"rules\": [\n    { \"type\": \"deletion\" },\n    { \"type\": \"non_fast_forward\" },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"pull_request\",\n      \"parameters\": {\n        \"required_approving_review_count\": 0,\n        \"dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push\": false,\n        \"require_code_owner_review\": false,\n        \"require_last_push_approval\": false,\n        \"required_review_thread_resolution\": false,\n        \"allowed_merge_methods\": [\"merge\"]\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"required_status_checks\",\n      \"parameters\": {\n        \"strict_required_status_checks_policy\": true,\n        \"do_not_enforce_on_create\": false,\n        \"required_status_checks\": [{ \"context\": \"check-deps\", \"integration_id\": 15368 }]\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n`main.json` is the same with `refs/heads/main`, `strict_required_status_checks_policy: false`, and both `check-deps` and `release-source`.\n\n### 4. Repository settings (`gh`)\n\n```sh\ngh repo edit carlossas/recruiting-challenge --default-branch develop\ngh repo edit carlossas/recruiting-challenge --enable-merge-commit --enable-squash-merge=false --enable-rebase-merge=false\n```\n\nThe second command mirrors the rulesets at repo level so the PR UI only offers \"Create a merge commit\".\n\n### 5. CLAUDE.md\n\nAdd to §2 (Git): the branch model; `develop` is the default branch and `main` is production-only; Claude never pushes to `main` or `develop`; work happens on `feature/*`/`fix/*`/`chore/*` branches merged via PR.\n\n### 6. At the first release: PR `develop` → `main` passes both checks.","+"," ## Rollback"," ","-- Remove branch protection rules and restore the default branch in GitHub settings.","-- `git push origin --delete develop` (only with explicit go) and `git branch -d develop`.","-- Remove the `release-source` job and the CLAUDE.md §2 additions.","+```sh","+gh api repos/carlossas/recruiting-challenge/rulesets            # find ids","+gh api -X DELETE repos/carlossas/recruiting-challenge/rulesets/<id>","+gh repo edit carlossas/recruiting-challenge --default-branch main --enable-squash-merge --enable-rebase-merge","+git push origin --delete develop    # only with explicit go","+git branch -d develop","+```","+","+Then remove the `release-source` job, the ruleset JSON files, and the CLAUDE.md §2 additions."]}],"originalFile":"# 004 — Branching model (`develop` → `main`), branch protection, and workflow docs\n\n**Status:** draft\n\n## Context\n\nThe user wants:\n- A `develop` branch. **All PRs target `develop`** (protected).\n- Releases go from `develop` to `main` (also protected).\n- The process documented in `docs/` as \"GitHub workflow — Releases and branches\".\n\nCurrent state:\n- Remote `origin` = `github.com/carlossas/recruiting-challenge` — public fork of `PlataformaT1/recruiting-challenge`, default branch `main`. Only `main` exists remotely (`cbf80ec`, same as local `HEAD`).\n- **`gh` CLI is not installed**, so Claude cannot configure GitHub settings (branch protection, default branch, Actions enablement). Those require the user's GitHub authentication → manual steps for the user (or: user installs `gh` + runs `gh auth login`, then Claude can apply them via the API with per-action approval).\n- **GitHub Actions is disabled by default on forks** until enabled in the repo's *Actions* tab.\n- The submission is scored partly on commit history (\"multiple commits, not one giant squash\" — EVALUATION.md), so merges must preserve individual commits.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Branch model\n\n```\nfeature/*, fix/*, chore/*  ──PR──▶  develop  ──release PR──▶  main\n```\n\n| Branch | Purpose | Created from | Merges into | Direct pushes |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `main` | Released state | — | — | ❌ |\n| `develop` | Integration | `main` | `main` (release PR) | ❌ |\n| `feature/<slug>`, `fix/<slug>`, `chore/<slug>` | One topic each (ideally one plan) | `develop` | `develop` | ✅ (owner's branch) |\n\n- **Merge method: \"Create a merge commit\"** for both feature → `develop` and `develop` → `main`. No squash — keeps every human-written commit visible.\n- A release = a PR from `develop` into `main`.\n\n### 2. Enforce \"only `develop` can merge into `main`\"\n\nGitHub has no native \"allowed source branch\" setting, so a second job is added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (from plan 003) and required on `main`:\n\n```yaml\n  release-source:\n    name: release-source\n    if: github.base_ref == 'main'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - name: Only develop from this repo can be merged into main\n        env:\n          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}\n          HEAD_REPO: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}\n          BASE_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}\n        run: |\n          if [ \"$HEAD_REF\" != \"develop\" ] || [ \"$HEAD_REPO\" != \"$BASE_REPO\" ]; then\n            echo \"::error::PRs into main must come from 'develop' in $BASE_REPO (got '$HEAD_REPO:$HEAD_REF')\"\n            exit 1\n          fi\n```\n\n- Values go through `env`, never interpolated into the shell script, to avoid script injection via branch names.\n- Checks the head **repo** too, so a fork's branch named `develop` can't pass.\n- On PRs into `develop` the job is skipped, which GitHub treats as passing — it's only *required* on `main`.\n\n### 3. Branch protection (manual, GitHub UI → Settings → Branches / Rules)\n\n| Setting | `develop` | `main` |\n|---|---|---|\n| Require a pull request before merging | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Required approvals | 0 — see Q1 | 0 — see Q1 |\n| Require status checks to pass | `check-deps` | `check-deps`, `release-source` |\n| Require branches to be up to date before merging | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Block force pushes | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Block deletions | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Apply rules to administrators (no bypass) | ✅ — see Q2 | ✅ — see Q2 |\n\nStatus checks can only be picked in the UI after they have run at least once, so protection is configured **after** the first PR has run the workflow (see bootstrap order).\n\n### 4. Default branch\n\nSwitch the default branch to `develop` so new PRs target it automatically — see Q3.\n\n### 5. CLAUDE.md\n\nAdd to §2 (Git): the branch model; Claude never pushes to `main` or `develop`; work happens on `feature/*`/`fix/*`/`chore/*` branches merged via PR.\n\n### 6. Docs: `docs/github-workflow.md` — \"GitHub workflow — Releases and branches\"\n\nWritten **after** the change is validated (CLAUDE.md §6; the user has already authorized this doc). Contents:\n- Branch model diagram (mermaid) and naming conventions.\n- Day-to-day flow: branch from `develop` → PR → checks → merge commit.\n- Release flow: PR `develop` → `main`, merge commit.\n- CI checks: what `check-deps` and `release-source` do; severity policy (critical/high block, moderate/low warn, audit failure blocks); how to run `npm run check:deps` locally.\n- Branch protection settings (table above).\n- What's *not* enforced (e.g. approvals with a single maintainer).\n\n## Bootstrap order\n\nCommits are human-written (CLAUDE.md §2), so the user commits; Claude prepares files and runs only approved git commands.\n\n1. **Claude** (after approval, explicit go for the push): `git branch develop main` and `git push -u origin develop`. `develop` starts at `cbf80ec`, identical to `main`. Uncommitted work stays in the working tree.\n2. **User**: enable GitHub Actions on the fork (*Actions* tab → \"I understand my workflows, go ahead and enable them\").\n3. **User**: create a branch from `develop` (e.g. `chore/ci-deps-and-plans`), commit the pending work (plans 001–004, `CLAUDE.md`, `tech_debt.md`, dependency changes, `check:deps`, workflow, docs) with their own messages, push, open a PR into `develop`.\n4. **User**: confirm the `check-deps` check runs and passes on that PR.\n5. **User**: configure branch protection for `develop` and `main` (table in §3) and the default branch (Q3).\n6. **User**: merge the PR into `develop` with a merge commit.\n7. **Validation of the rules** (see below).\n\n## Open questions (need your call before approval)\n\n- **Q1 — Required approvals.** GitHub doesn't let you approve your own PR. With a single maintainer, requiring ≥1 approval would block every merge.\n  - (a) **0 approvals** — *recommended* while you're the only contributor. The PR + green checks is the gate.\n  - (b) 1 approval — only if someone else will review.\n- **Q2 — Apply rules to administrators?** You own the repo, so you're an admin.\n  - (a) **Yes, no bypass** — *recommended*. Otherwise you can still push directly and the protection is decorative.\n  - (b) Allow admin bypass — emergency escape hatch, at the cost of the guarantee.\n- **Q3 — Default branch.**\n  - (a) **`develop`** — *recommended*. PRs target it by default; fewer mistakes.\n  - (b) Keep `main` — visitors (e.g. reviewers opening the fork link) land on the released state, but every PR must be retargeted by hand.\n\n## Scope\n\n- Local + remote branch `develop` (created by Claude, push only with explicit go).\n- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — add `release-source` job.\n- `CLAUDE.md` — branch rules in §2.\n- `docs/github-workflow.md` (new) — after validation.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Hotfix flow (`hotfix/*` from `main` + back-merge into `develop`) — can be added later if needed.\n- Tags / GitHub Releases / versioning / changelog.\n- Any change to the upstream `PlataformaT1/recruiting-challenge` repo.\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `git ls-remote --heads origin` → `develop` and `main` at the same commit (Claude).\n2. First PR into `develop` shows `check-deps` passing and `release-source` skipped (user).\n3. Direct `git push` to `develop` or `main` is rejected (user, after protection).\n4. A PR from any branch other than `develop` into `main` fails `release-source` and can't be merged (user — can be tested with a throwaway branch and then closed).\n5. Release PR `develop` → `main` passes both checks (user, at the first release).\n\n## Rollback\n\n- Remove branch protection rules and restore the default branch in GitHub settings.\n- `git push origin --delete develop` (only with explicit go) and `git branch -d develop`.\n- Remove the `release-source` job and the CLAUDE.md §2 additions.\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"ad7fe967-0caa-4944-926a-d1bd413ce020","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"main"}

What's evaluated is the candidate's judgment, and some deliverables **must be written by a human, without AI**. See [SUBMISSION.md](SUBMISSION.md) and [EVALUATION.md](EVALUATION.md).\n\n## 1. Language\n- **Everything written to the repo is in English**: code, identifiers, code comments, docs, plans, and any other file.\n- Conversation with the user may stay in Spanish.\n- **Docstrings are mandatory**: every exported function, class, router handler, and module gets a TSDoc/JSDoc `/** ... */` block. Inline `//` comments only for non-obvious logic.\n\n## 2. Git: never without an explicit order\n- **No commits, amends, rebases, squashes, or pushes.** Commit messages are human deliverables.\n- **Never propose or draft commit messages**, not even as a suggestion.\n- No branches, PRs, or forks unless the user explicitly asks.\n\n## 3. Human deliverables: never write or edit them\nNever create, draft, rewrite, polish, or restyle:\n- `decision_log.md`\n- `validation_design.md`\n- `signoff.md`\n- `written_answers.md`\n- The **authorship declarations** of any of them.\n\nNo drafts, prose outlines, or copy-ready sentences either. If asked for help, provide only **technical facts** (code facts, paths, line numbers) and let the user write.\n\n## 4. `prompt_history.md` is a raw transcript\n- Never generate, summarize, curate, or edit it. The user assembles it.\n- Never write the \"What Claude got wrong\" section.\n\n## 5. Plans first: `plans/`\n- **Every decision agreed with the user is documented in `plans/` before writing any code.**\n- One file per change: `plans/NNN-short-slug.md` (e.g. `plans/001-orders-tenant-scope.md`).\n- `NNN` is a zero-padded, strictly ascending sequence (`001`, `002`, `003`, …) reflecting the order plans are executed. Always take the next number after the highest existing one; never reuse or renumber.\n- Each plan covers: context/problem, agreed decision, rejected alternatives, scope and out-of-scope, validation (tests, manual checks), and status (`draft` → `approved` → `done`).\n- No code changes until the user approves the plan. If the approach changes mid-way, update the plan first.\n\n## 6. Documentation: `docs/`\n- `docs/` holds the repository documentation.\n- Update it **only after the change is finished and validated**, and **only after asking the user for authorization**.\n- Never modify `README.md`, `EVALUATION.md`, `SUBMISSION.md`, or the `*.template.md` files without an explicit instruction.\n- `tech_debt.md` is managed by the user: update it only when told to (check off, discard, or add items).\n\n## 7. Code: the user decides\n- Never fix issues on your own initiative. Propose → plan → approval → implement only what was agreed.\n- Keep changes small and scoped to one topic so the user can review and commit them separately.\n- When a change is done, state honestly what was verified (tests, browser) and what wasn't.\n\n## 8. It only receives release PRs from `develop`.\n- One topic per branch — ideally one plan from `plans/`.\n- Use lowercase, hyphen-separated slugs: `fix/orders-tenant-scope`, `chore/upgrade-tsx`.\n\n## Day-to-day flow\n\n1. Start from an up-to-date `develop`:\n   ```sh\n   git switch develop\n   git pull\n   git switch -c fix/orders-tenant-scope\n   ```\n2. Commit in small steps, with descriptive messages.\n3. Push and open a PR into `develop`:\n   ```sh\n   git push -u origin fix/orders-tenant-scope\n   ```\n4. Wait for the required checks (see [CI checks](#ci-checks)). If `develop` moved ahead, update the branch before merging (required on `develop`).\n5. Merge with **\"Create a merge commit\"** — the only method enabled. Squash and rebase are disabled so every commit stays visible in the history.\n\n## Release flow\n\nA release is a PR from `develop` into `main`.\n\n1. Open a PR with base `main` and head `develop`.\n2. Required checks: `check-deps` and `release-source`.\n3. Merge with **\"Create a merge commit\"**.\n4. `main` now reflects production.\n\nThe release merge commit exists only on `main`; `develop` doesn't need it back. That's why `main` does **not** require the branch to be up to date — otherwise every release would require pushing that merge commit to `develop`, which its own rules forbid.\n\n## CI checks\n\nDefined in [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](../.github/workflows/ci.yml). They run on every PR into `develop` or `main`, and can be started manually (`workflow_dispatch`).\n\n### `check-deps`\n\nRuns `npm run check:deps` ([`src/scripts/check-deps.ts`](../src/scripts/check-deps.ts)), which wraps `npm audit --json` (prod + dev dependencies) and applies this policy:\n\n| Result | Effect |\n|---|---|\n| `critical` or `high` vulnerability | ❌ Error — the check fails and the PR can't be merged |\n| `moderate` or `low` vulnerability | ⚠️ Warning annotation on the PR — the check passes |\n| `info` | Ignored |\n| `npm audit` could not run (registry/network error, unexpected output) | ❌ Error `npm audit could not run: <reason>` — the check fails, since nothing was verified |\n\nEach finding shows the package, severity, advisory title and URL, whether it's a direct or transitive dependency, whether it's prod or dev, and whether a fix is available.\n\nRun it locally before opening a PR:\n\n```sh\nnpm run check:deps\n```\n\nThe job installs with `npm ci --ignore-scripts` (no third-party install scripts in a security check) on Node 24.\n\n### `release-source`\n\nRuns only on PRs into `main`. It fails unless the PR's head branch is `develop` **from this same repository**, so a feature branch — or a fork's branch named `develop` — can't be merged into production directly. On PRs into `develop` it is skipped, which counts as passing.\n\n## Branch protection\n\nBoth branches are protected with repository **rulesets**. There are **no bypass actors** — the rules also apply to repository admins.\n\n| Rule | `develop` | `main` |\n|---|---|---|\n| Deletion blocked | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Force pushes blocked | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Pull request required | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Required approvals | 0 | 0 |\n| Allowed merge method | Merge commit | Merge commit |\n| Required checks | `check-deps` | `check-deps`, `release-source` |\n| Branch must be up to date | ✅ | ❌ (see [Release flow](#release-flow)) |\n| Checks must be reported by GitHub Actions | ✅ | ✅ |\n\n\"Checks must be reported by GitHub Actions\" (`integration_id: 15368`) means a commit status posted manually with the same name doesn't satisfy the rule.\n\n### Where the rules live\n\nThe ruleset definitions are versioned in [`.github/rulesets/`](../.github/rulesets/). GitHub doesn't read that folder automatically — the files are applied with the GitHub CLI.\n\n| Ruleset | File | GitHub id |\n|---|---|---|\n| `develop` | [`.github/rulesets/develop.json`](../.github/rulesets/develop.json) | `22970322` |\n| `main` | [`.github/rulesets/main.json`](../.github/rulesets/main.json) | `22970325` |\n\nTo change a rule, edit the JSON file in a PR, and after it's merged apply it:\n\n```sh\ngh api -X PUT repos/carlossas/recruiting-challenge/rulesets/<id> --input .github/rulesets/<branch>.json\n```\n\nTo inspect what is actually enforced on a branch:\n\n```sh\ngh api repos/carlossas/recruiting-challenge/rules/branches/develop\n```\n\n### Repository settings\n\n- Default branch: `develop`.\n- Merge methods: merge commit only (squash and rebase disabled).\n\n## Not covered yet\n\n- **Code review:** approvals are set to 0 because the repository has a single maintainer (GitHub doesn't allow approving your own PR). Raise `required_approving_review_count` when more people contribute.\n- **Hotfixes:** there is no `hotfix/*` flow from `main`. Urgent fixes follow the normal path (`fix/*` → `develop` → release).\n- **Deployment:** merging into `main` defines what production should run, but no deployment pipeline is wired to it yet.\n- **Tags / versioning / changelog:** releases are not tagged.\n- **Other CI checks:** tests and type-checking don't run in CI yet; only `check-deps` and `release-source` do.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":53,"cache_read_input_tokens":228131,"output_tokens":3377,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":420},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":53,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":3377,"cache_read_input_tokens":228131,"cache_creation_input_tokens":53,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":53},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01X9c8p388gobNyALpKSHarL":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\docs\\github-workflow.md","content":"# {"parentUuid":"99fd7a5a-6a03-43cd-b0d4-8c38860ce52f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CexQNtWyKijfnwj85wcAA","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_019duo7Sxc4fvssVgFqUkPzk","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\tech_debt.md","content":"# Tech debt\n\nFindings from reviewing the current architecture, **ordered by priority, highest first**. Nothing here is resolved yet: each item is documented, prioritized, or discarded one at a time.\n\n## How this is ranked\n\nPriority balances **product impact** against **security and financial risk**, not raw severity:\n\n- An item that lets an attacker read another merchant's data, or that can cost money, outranks an item that only shows a wrong number on a dashboard.\n- Items that **amplify each other** are ranked together — e.g. spoofing a merchant id (TD-01) plus an unbounded `limit` (TD-10) turns a small bug into a bulk data dump.\n- Wrong revenue math (TD-05) is ranked high anyway: merchants make decisions with that number, and it overstates income.\n\nTiers:\n\n| Tier | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| **MUST — urgent** | Ship before anything else. Money, data leakage, or attack surface. |\n| **SHOULD — next** | Wrong or fragile behavior users will hit. Fix right after the MUSTs. |\n| **CAN WAIT** | Real, but low blast radius. Cleanup / hygiene. |\n\nIDs are stable (`TD-01` … `TD-17`) and don't change when the order does. Original severity from the first review is kept for reference.\n\n---\n\n# Tier 1 — MUST (urgent)\n\n- [ ] **TD-01 · The `X-Merchant-Id` header is not verified** — Severity: High\n  - **Why first:** this is the whole authorization model. Any client can impersonate any merchant by editing one header, which turns every other endpoint into a cross-tenant data source. It also multiplies TD-02 and TD-10.\n  - Where: [src/auth.ts:16](src/auth.ts:16), [public/app.js:9](public/app.js:9)\n  - What happens: `authMiddleware` only checks that the header is present and copies it to `req.merchantId`. There is no signature, no session, no verification that the caller owns that merchant.\n  - Note: documented as an intentional simplification for the challenge (\"Real auth would be a signed JWT\"), so the decision to make is *what shape* replaces it.\n\n- [ ] **TD-02 · `GET /api/orders/:id` does not filter by merchant** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** direct cross-tenant read of order data (customer emails and amounts), independent of TD-01. Even with real auth in place, this endpoint would still leak.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:16](src/routes/orders.ts:16), [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38)\n  - What happens: `ordersDal.getById(id)` looks up by `id` only and ignores `req.merchantId`.\n\n- [ ] **TD-10 · `limit` is not validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why so high:** in SQLite `LIMIT -1` means \"no limit\", so `?limit=-1` returns every order of the merchant in one request. Combined with TD-01 that's a bulk export of the whole database, and on its own it's an easy way to exhaust the server.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:11](src/routes/orders.ts:11), [src/routes/metrics.ts:43](src/routes/metrics.ts:43)\n  - What happens: `Number(req.query.limit)` can yield `NaN`, a decimal, or a negative number. There is no upper bound.\n\n- [ ] **TD-12 · Stored XSS in the orders table** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** any merchant's dashboard executes attacker-controlled markup, and the payload is planted through the public `POST /api/orders` (TD-11). With TD-01 an attacker can plant it in *someone else's* dashboard.\n  - Where: [public/app.js:35](public/app.js:35)\n  - What happens: each row is built with `innerHTML`, interpolating `o.customer_email` and `o.type` unsanitized.\n\n- [ ] **TD-11 · The `POST /api/orders` body is barely validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** it's the entry point that feeds TD-12, and it lets corrupt money into the database — negative or fractional amounts in a column that holds integer cents.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:25](src/routes/orders.ts:25)\n  - What happens: `type` accepts any string (not only `sale`/`refund`), `total_amount` accepts negatives and decimals, and `customer_email` isn't validated as an email.\n\n- [ ] **TD-05 · Revenue counts refunds as income** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** the headline number of the product is wrong, and wrong in the optimistic direction. A merchant reading \"Revenue (last 30 days)\" is told they earned money they refunded.\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54)\n  - What happens: `sumAmountByMerchant` runs `SUM(total_amount)` without looking at `type`. Refunds are stored with a positive amount (see [src/scripts/seed.ts:43](src/scripts/seed.ts:43)), so they add instead of subtracting. Per [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), a refund represents a reversed sale.\n\n---\n\n# Tier 2 — SHOULD (next)\n\n- [ ] **TD-04 · `metrics.ts` bypasses the DAL** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** it's the seam that decides how expensive the Tier 1 fixes are. A tenancy filter, auditing, or caching added to `ordersDal` silently won't apply to metrics, so this should be closed *while* fixing the security items, not after.\n  - Where: [src/routes/metrics.ts:5](src/routes/metrics.ts:5)\n  - What happens: it opens its own `new Database(DB_PATH, { readonly: true })` and runs raw SQL. Two connections to the same database, and `DB_PATH` resolved twice.\n\n- [ ] **TD-16 · Test coverage is minimal** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** the gate that keeps Tier 1 fixed. Right now nothing would catch a regression in auth, tenancy scoping, or revenue math.\n  - Where: [test/orders.test.ts](test/orders.test.ts)\n  - What happens: only the DAL's `create`, `listByMerchant`, and `getById` are covered. No route, auth, revenue, or metrics tests.\n\n- [ ] **TD-06 · Summary metrics treat refunds as sales** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** same class of error as TD-05 and visible on the same screen, but these numbers are informational rather than the money figure.\n  - Where: [src/routes/metrics.ts:17](src/routes/metrics.ts:17), [src/routes/metrics.ts:45](src/routes/metrics.ts:45)\n  - What happens: `total_orders`, `unique_customers`, `avg_order_value_cents`, and `top-customers.total_spent` count every row the same way.\n\n- [ ] **TD-07 · The revenue range excludes the `to` day, so the dashboard leaves out today** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** a visibly wrong number every day, with an obvious fix, but it under-reports rather than overstating.\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:59](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:59), [public/app.js:28](public/app.js:28)\n  - What happens: the filter is `created_at < to` with `to` as a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, so the whole `to` day is excluded — and the frontend sends `to = today`.\n\n- [ ] **TD-08 · `created_at` is stored in mixed formats** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** data-integrity debt that gets more expensive the more rows accumulate, and it quietly corrupts ordering and range filters.\n  - Where: [src/db.ts:30](src/db.ts:30), [src/scripts/seed.ts:21](src/scripts/seed.ts:21)\n  - What happens: the seed stores ISO 8601 (`2026-09-10T12:00:00.000Z`) while `POST`-created orders use SQLite's `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` (`2026-09-10 12:00:00`). Comparisons and `ORDER BY` are string-based, so ordering within a day can be wrong; the browser also reads the format without `T`/`Z` as local time.\n\n- [ ] **TD-03 · `POST /api/orders` with a non-existent merchant returns 500** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** wrong status code and a leaked internal error, not a data or money problem. With TD-01 an attacker can plant it in *someone else's* dashboard.\n  - Where: [public/app.js:35](public/app.js:35)\n  - What happens: each row is built with `innerHTML`, interpolating `o.customer_email` and `o.type` unsanitized.\n\n- [ ] **TD-11 · The `POST /api/orders` body is barely validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** it's the entry point that feeds TD-12, and it lets corrupt money into the database — negative or fractional amounts in a column that holds integer cents.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:25](src/routes/orders.ts:25)\n  - What happens: `type` accepts any string (not only `sale`/`refund`), `total_amount` accepts negatives and decimals, and `customer_email` isn't validated as an email.\n\n- [ ] **TD-05 · Revenue counts refunds as income** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** the headline number of the product is wrong, and wrong in the optimistic direction. A merchant reading \"Revenue (last 30 days)\" is told they earned money they refunded.\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54)\n  - What happens: `sumAmountByMerchant` runs `SUM(total_amount)` without looking at `type`. Refunds are stored with a positive amount (see [src/scripts/seed.ts:43](src/scripts/seed.ts:43)), so they add instead of subtracting. Per [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), a refund represents a reversed sale.\n\n---\n\n# Tier 2 — SHOULD (next)\n\n- [ ] **TD-04 · `metrics.ts` bypasses the DAL** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** it's the seam that decides how expensive the Tier 1 fixes are. A tenancy filter, auditing, or caching added to `ordersDal` silently won't apply to metrics, so this should be closed *while* fixing the security items, not after.\n  - Where: [src/routes/metrics.ts:5](src/routes/metrics.ts:5)\n  - What happens: it opens its own `new Database(DB_PATH, { readonly: true })` and runs raw SQL. Two connections to the same database, and `DB_PATH` resolved twice.\n\n- [ ] **TD-16 · Test coverage is minimal** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** the gate that keeps Tier 1 fixed. Right now nothing would catch a regression in auth, tenancy scoping, or revenue math.\n  - Where: [test/orders.test.ts](test/orders.test.ts)\n  - What happens: only the DAL's `create`, `listByMerchant`, and `getById` are covered. No route, auth, revenue, or metrics tests.\n\n- [ ] **TD-06 · Summary metrics treat refunds as sales** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** same class of error as TD-05 and visible on the same screen, but these numbers are informational rather than the money figure.\n  - Where: [src/routes/metrics.ts:17](src/routes/metrics.ts:17), [src/routes/metrics.ts:45](src/routes/metrics.ts:45)\n  - What happens: `total_orders`, `unique_customers`, `avg_order_value_cents`, and `top-customers.total_spent` count every row the same way.\n\n- [ ] **TD-07 · The revenue range excludes the `to` day, so the dashboard leaves out today** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** a visibly wrong number every day, with an obvious fix, but it under-reports rather than overstating.\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:59](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:59), [public/app.js:28](public/app.js:28)\n  - What happens: the filter is `created_at < to` with `to` as a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, so the whole `to` day is excluded — and the frontend sends `to = today`.\n\n- [ ] **TD-08 · `created_at` is stored in mixed formats** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** data-integrity debt that gets more expensive the more rows accumulate, and it quietly corrupts ordering and range filters.\n  - Where: [src/db.ts:30](src/db.ts:30), [src/scripts/seed.ts:21](src/scripts/seed.ts:21)\n  - What happens: the seed stores ISO 8601 (`2026-09-10T12:00:00.000Z`) while `POST`-created orders use SQLite's `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` (`2026-09-10 12:00:00`). Comparisons and `ORDER BY` are string-based, so ordering within a day can be wrong; the browser also reads the format without `T`/`Z` as local time.\n\n- [ ] **TD-03 · `POST /api/orders` with a non-existent merchant returns 500** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** wrong status code and a leaked internal error, not a data or money problem. Largely disappears once TD-01 is fixed.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:35](src/routes/orders.ts:35)\n  - What happens: an unknown `merchantId` violates the `orders.merchant_id → merchants.id` FK (`foreign_keys = ON`); the exception reaches the generic handler and returns `500 internal_error`.\n\n---\n\n# Tier 3 — CAN WAIT\n\n- [ ] **TD-09 · `from`/`to` are not validated** — Severity: Low\n  - **Why here:** garbage dates produce empty or odd results for the caller who sent them; no cross-tenant or money impact.\n  - Where: [src/routes/revenue.ts:12](src/routes/revenue.ts:12), [src/routes/orders.ts:9](src/routes/orders.ts:9)\n  - What happens: any string is accepted and compared lexicographically. None of these are resolved yet:\neach item will be documented, prioritized, or discarded one at a time.\n\nRough severity: **High** (security / wrong data), **Medium** (robustness / design), **Low** (hygiene).\n\n---\n\n## Authentication and merchant isolation\n\n- [ ] **TD-01 · The `X-Merchant-Id` header is not verified** — High\n  - Where: [src/auth.ts:16](src/auth.ts:16), [public/app.js:9](public/app.js:9)\n  - What happens: `authMiddleware` only checks that the header is present and copies it to `req.merchantId`. Any client can impersonate any merchant by changing the value.\n  - Note: documented as an intentional simplification for the challenge (\"Real auth would be a signed JWT\").\n\n- [ ] **TD-02 · `GET /api/orders/:id` does not filter by merchant** — High\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:16](src/routes/orders.ts:16), [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38)\n  - What happens: `ordersDal.getById(id)` looks up by `id` only and ignores `req.merchantId`. A merchant can read another merchant's orders if they know the id.\n\n- [ ] **TD-03 · `POST /api/orders` with a non-existent merchant returns 500** — Medium\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:35](src/routes/orders.ts:35)\n  - What happens: since auth accepts any value, a `merchantId` that doesn't exist violates the `orders.merchant_id → merchants.id` FK (`foreign_keys = ON`). The exception reaches the generic error handler and returns `500 internal_error` instead of a 4xx.\n\n## Data access layer\n\n- [ ] **TD-04 · `metrics.ts` bypasses the DAL** — Medium\n  - Where: [src/routes/metrics.ts:5](src/routes/metrics.ts:5)\n  - What happens: it opens its own `new Database(DB_PATH, { readonly: true })` connection and runs raw SQL. According to [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), all order queries should go through `ordersDal`. Any tenancy filter, auditing, or caching added to the DAL won't apply to metrics.\n  - Side effect: there are two connections to the same database (one in `db.ts`, one here), and `DB_PATH` is resolved twice.\n\n## Calculation correctness (refunds)\n\n- [ ] **TD-05 · Revenue counts refunds as income** — High\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54)\n  - What happens: `sumAmountByMerchant` runs `SUM(total_amount)` without looking at `type`. Refunds are stored with a positive amount (see [src/scripts/seed.ts:43](src/scripts/seed.ts:43)), so they add to revenue instead of subtracting. According to [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), a refund represents a reversed sale.\n\n- [ ] **TD-06 · Summary metrics treat refunds as sales** — Medium\n  - Where: [src/routes/metrics.ts:17](src/routes/metrics.ts:17), [src/routes/metrics.ts:45](src/routes/metrics.ts:45)\n  - What happens: `total_orders`, `unique_customers`, `avg_order_value_cents`, and `top-customers.total_spent` count every row the same way, without distinguishing `sale` from `refund`.\n\n## Dates\n\n- [ ] **TD-07 · The revenue range excludes the `to` day, so the dashboard leaves out today** — Medium\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:59](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:59), [public/app.js:28](public/app.js:28)\n  - What happens: the filter is `created_at < to` and `to` is a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, so the whole `to` day is excluded. The frontend sends `to = today`, so \"Revenue (last 30 days)\" doesn't include today's orders.\n\n- [ ] **TD-08 · `created_at` is stored in mixed formats** — Medium\n  - Where: [src/db.ts:30](src/db.ts:30), [src/scripts/seed.ts:21](src/scripts/seed.ts:21)\n  - What happens: the seed stores ISO 8601 (`2026-09-10T12:00:00.000Z`), while orders created via `POST` use SQLite's `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` (`2026-09-10 12:00:00`). Comparisons and `ORDER BY` are string-based, so ordering within the same day can be wrong. The browser also parses the format without `T`/`Z` as local time.\n\n- [ ] **TD-09 · `from`/`to` are not validated** — Low\n  - Where: [src/routes/revenue.ts:12](src/routes/revenue.ts:12), [src/routes/orders.ts:9](src/routes/orders.ts:9)\n  - What happens: any string is accepted as a date and compared lexicographically. In `GET /api/orders`, if only one of the two parameters is sent, the filter is silently ignored.\n\n## Input validation\n\n- [ ] **TD-10 · `limit` is not validated** — Medium\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:11](src/routes/orders.ts:11), [src/routes/metrics.ts:43](src/routes/metrics.ts:43)\n  - What happens: `Number(req.query.limit)` can yield `NaN`, a decimal, or a negative number. In SQLite, `LIMIT -1` means \"no limit\", so `?limit=-1` returns all of the merchant's orders. There is no upper bound.\n\n- [ ] **TD-11 · The `POST /api/orders` body is barely validated** — Medium\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:25](src/routes/orders.ts:25)\n  - What happens: `type` accepts any string (not just `sale`/`refund`), `total_amount` accepts negatives and decimals even though the column holds integer cents, and `customer_email` is not validated as an email.\n\n## Frontend\n\n- [ ] **TD-12 · Stored XSS in the orders table** — High\n  - Where: [public/app.js:35](public/app.js:35)\n  - What happens: each row is built with `innerHTML` interpolating `o.customer_email` and `o.type`, which come unsanitized from `POST /api/orders` (see TD-11). An order with HTML/JS in those fields executes in the dashboard of whoever views it.\n\n- [ ] **TD-13 · The frontend doesn't handle API errors** — Low\n  - Where: [public/app.js:8](public/app.js:8)\n  - What happens: `api()` doesn't check `r.ok`. A 401/500 is parsed as if it were a valid response, and the fields end up showing `—` or `$0.00` with no warning.\n\n- [ ] **TD-14 · The merchant list is hardcoded in the HTML** — Low\n  - Where: [public/index.html:28](public/index.html:28)\n  - What happens: the selector's merchants duplicate [src/scripts/seed.ts:4](src/scripts/seed.ts:4) and don't come from the API.\n\n## Tooling, tests, and documentation\n\n- [ ] **TD-15 · `npm run seed` probably does nothing on Windows** — Low\n  - Where: [src/scripts/seed.ts:60](src/scripts/seed.ts:60)\n  - What happens: the `isMain` check compares `import.meta.url` (`file:///C:/...`, with `/`) against `process.argv[1]` (`C:\\...`, with `\\`), so neither condition matches. In practice this is masked because the server calls `seedIfEmpty()` on startup.\n\n- [ ] **TD-16 · Test coverage is minimal** — Medium\n  - Where: [test/orders.test.ts](test/orders.test.ts)\n  - What happens: only the DAL's `create`, `listByMerchant`, and `getById` are tested. There are no tests for routes, auth, revenue, or metrics, which is where most of the items above live.\n\n- [ ] **TD-17 · `docs/architecture.md` is outdated** — Low\n  - Where: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)\n  - What happens: it mentions a `lib/` folder that doesn't exist and labels itself as an unmaintained draft.\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"f87baac4-da09-44f6-b903-cc212df92df9","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

Nothing here is resolved yet: each item is documented, prioritized, or discarded one at a time.\n\n## How this is ranked\n\nPriority balances **product impact** against **security and financial risk**, not raw severity:\n\n- An item that lets an attacker read another merchant's data, or that can cost money, outranks an item that only shows a wrong number on a dashboard.\n- Items that **amplify each other** are ranked together — e.g. spoofing a merchant id (TD-01) plus an unbounded `limit` (TD-10) turns a small bug into a bulk data dump.\n- Wrong revenue math (TD-05) is ranked high anyway: merchants make decisions with that number, and it overstates income.\n\nTiers:\n\n| Tier | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| **MUST — urgent** | Ship before anything else. Money, data leakage, or attack surface. |\n| **SHOULD — next** | Wrong or fragile behavior users will hit. Fix right after the MUSTs. |\n| **CAN WAIT** | Real, but low blast radius. Cleanup / hygiene. |\n\nIDs are stable (`TD-01` … `TD-17`) and don't change when the order does. Original severity from the first review is kept for reference.\n\n---\n\n# Tier 1 — MUST (urgent)\n\n- [ ] **TD-01 · The `X-Merchant-Id` header is not verified** — Severity: High\n  - **Why first:** this is the whole authorization model. Any client can impersonate any merchant by editing one header, which turns every other endpoint into a cross-tenant data source. It also multiplies TD-02 and TD-10.\n  - Where: [src/auth.ts:16](src/auth.ts:16), [public/app.js:9](public/app.js:9)\n  - What happens: `authMiddleware` only checks that the header is present and copies it to `req.merchantId`. There is no signature, no session, no verification that the caller owns that merchant.\n  - Note: documented as an intentional simplification for the challenge (\"Real auth would be a signed JWT\"), so the decision to make is *what shape* replaces it.\n\n- [ ] **TD-02 · `GET /api/orders/:id` does not filter by merchant** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** direct cross-tenant read of order data (customer emails and amounts), independent of TD-01. Even with real auth in place, this endpoint would still leak.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:16](src/routes/orders.ts:16), [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38)\n  - What happens: `ordersDal.getById(id)` looks up by `id` only and ignores `req.merchantId`.\n\n- [ ] **TD-10 · `limit` is not validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why so high:** in SQLite `LIMIT -1` means \"no limit\", so `?limit=-1` returns every order of the merchant in one request. Combined with TD-01 that's a bulk export of the whole database, and on its own it's an easy way to exhaust the server.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:11](src/routes/orders.ts:11), [src/routes/metrics.ts:43](src/routes/metrics.ts:43)\n  - What happens: `Number(req.query.limit)` can yield `NaN`, a decimal, or a negative number. There is no upper bound.\n\n- [ ] **TD-12 · Stored XSS in the orders table** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** any merchant's dashboard executes attacker-controlled markup, and the payload is planted through the public `POST /api/orders` (TD-11). With TD-01 an attacker can plant it in *someone else's* dashboard.\n  - Where: [public/app.js:35](public/app.js:35)\n  - What happens: each row is built with `innerHTML`, interpolating `o.customer_email` and `o.type` unsanitized.\n\n- [ ] **TD-11 · The `POST /api/orders` body is barely validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** it's the entry point that feeds TD-12, and it lets corrupt money into the database — negative or fractional amounts in a column that holds integer cents.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:25](src/routes/orders.ts:25)\n  - What happens: `type` accepts any string (not only `sale`/`refund`), `total_amount` accepts negatives and decimals, and `customer_email` isn't validated as an email.\n\n- [ ] **TD-05 · Revenue counts refunds as income** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** the headline number of the product is wrong, and wrong in the optimistic direction. A merchant reading \"Revenue (last 30 days)\" is told they earned money they refunded.\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54)\n  - What happens: `sumAmountByMerchant` runs `SUM(total_amount)` without looking at `type`. Refunds are stored with a positive amount (see [src/scripts/seed.ts:43](src/scripts/seed.ts:43)), so they add instead of subtracting. Per [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), a refund represents a reversed sale.\n\n---\n\n# Tier 2 — SHOULD (next)\n\n- [ ] **TD-04 · `metrics.ts` bypasses the DAL** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** it's the seam that decides how expensive the Tier 1 fixes are. A tenancy filter, auditing, or caching added to `ordersDal` silently won't apply to metrics, so this should be closed *while* fixing the security items, not after.\n  - Where: [src/routes/metrics.ts:5](src/routes/metrics.ts:5)\n  - What happens: it opens its own `new Database(DB_PATH, { readonly: true })` and runs raw SQL. Two connections to the same database, and `DB_PATH` resolved twice.\n\n- [ ] **TD-16 · Test coverage is minimal** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** the gate that keeps Tier 1 fixed. Right now nothing would catch a regression in auth, tenancy scoping, or revenue math.\n  - Where: [test/orders.test.ts](test/orders.test.ts)\n  - What happens: only the DAL's `create`, `listByMerchant`, and `getById` are covered. No route, auth, revenue, or metrics tests.\n\n- [ ] **TD-06 · Summary metrics treat refunds as sales** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** same class of error as TD-05 and visible on the same screen, but these numbers are informational rather than the money figure.\n  - Where: [src/routes/metrics.ts:17](src/routes/metrics.ts:17), [src/routes/metrics.ts:45](src/routes/metrics.ts:45)\n  - What happens: `total_orders`, `unique_customers`, `avg_order_value_cents`, and `top-customers.total_spent` count every row the same way.\n\n- [ ] **TD-07 · The revenue range excludes the `to` day, so the dashboard leaves out today** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** a visibly wrong number every day, with an obvious fix, but it under-reports rather than overstating.\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:59](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:59), [public/app.js:28](public/app.js:28)\n  - What happens: the filter is `created_at < to` with `to` as a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, so the whole `to` day is excluded — and the frontend sends `to = today`.\n\n- [ ] **TD-08 · `created_at` is stored in mixed formats** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** data-integrity debt that gets more expensive the more rows accumulate, and it quietly corrupts ordering and range filters.\n  - Where: [src/db.ts:30](src/db.ts:30), [src/scripts/seed.ts:21](src/scripts/seed.ts:21)\n  - What happens: the seed stores ISO 8601 (`2026-09-10T12:00:00.000Z`) while `POST`-created orders use SQLite's `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` (`2026-09-10 12:00:00`). Comparisons and `ORDER BY` are string-based, so ordering within a day can be wrong; the browser also reads the format without `T`/`Z` as local time.\n\n- [ ] **TD-03 · `POST /api/orders` with a non-existent merchant returns 500** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** wrong status code and a leaked internal error, not a data or money problem. Largely disappears once TD-01 is fixed.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:35](src/routes/orders.ts:35)\n  - What happens: an unknown `merchantId` violates the `orders.merchant_id → merchants.id` FK (`foreign_keys = ON`); the exception reaches the generic handler and returns `500 internal_error`.\n\n---\n\n# Tier 3 — CAN WAIT\n\n- [ ] **TD-09 · `from`/`to` are not validated** — Severity: Low\n  - **Why here:** garbage dates produce empty or odd results for the caller who sent them; no cross-tenant or money impact.\n  - Where: [src/routes/revenue.ts:12](src/routes/revenue.ts:12), [src/routes/orders.ts:9](src/routes/orders.ts:9)\n  - What happens: any string is accepted and compared lexicographically. In `GET /api/orders`, sending only one of the two parameters silently drops the filter.\n\n- [ ] **TD-13 · The frontend doesn't handle API errors** — Severity: Low\n  - **Why here:** poor UX, not incorrect data — although \"silently shows `$0.00` on a 500\" can be mistaken for real data.\n  - Where: [public/app.js:8](public/app.js:8)\n  - What happens: `api()` never checks `r.ok`, so error responses are rendered as empty values.\n\n- [ ] **TD-14 · The merchant list is hardcoded in the HTML** — Severity: Low\n  - **Why here:** demo-scaffolding duplication; it will be revisited anyway when real auth lands (TD-01).\n  - Where: [public/index.html:28](public/index.html:28)\n  - What happens: the selector duplicates [src/scripts/seed.ts:4](src/scripts/seed.ts:4) instead of coming from the API.\n\n- [ ] **TD-17 · `docs/architecture.md` is outdated** — Severity: Low\n  - **Why here:** cheap to fix and worth doing alongside whichever change touches the module it misdescribes.\n  - Where: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)\n  - What happens: it mentions a `lib/` folder that doesn't exist and labels itself an unmaintained draft.\n\n- [ ] **TD-15 · `npm run seed` probably does nothing on Windows** — Severity: Low\n  - **Why last:** masked in practice — the server calls `seedIfEmpty()` on startup — so the visible impact is zero today.\n  - Where: [src/scripts/seed.ts:60](src/scripts/seed.ts:60)\n  - What happens: the `isMain` check compares `import.meta.url` (`file:///C:/...`) against `process.argv[1]` (`C:\\...`), so neither condition matches.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":35,"oldLines":6,"newStart":35,"newLines":11,"lines":["   - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:16](src/routes/orders.ts:16), [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38)","   - What happens: `ordersDal.getById(id)` looks up by `id` only and ignores `req.merchantId`."," ","+- [ ] **TD-04 · `metrics.ts` bypasses the DAL** — Severity: Medium","+  - **Why here:** the DAL is where tenancy filtering, auditing, and caching are supposed to live, and `metrics.ts` is outside it. {"parentUuid":"11ac4148-b8e9-474e-89af-fff239559905","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CexRMe4uhgGYZKoTS3vdu","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01LsUk7QpB5SJZ82jrS8mFgg","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\tech_debt.md","content":"# Tech debt — Tier 1 (MUST, urgent)\n\nThe items we're working on now. Everything else lives in [tech_debt_backlog.md](tech_debt_backlog.md) (Tier 2 and Tier 3) and is deliberately out of sight until this file is empty.\n\n## How this is ranked\n\nPriority balances **product impact** against **security and financial risk**, not raw severity:\n\n- An item that lets an attacker read another merchant's data, or that can cost money, outranks an item that only shows a wrong number on a dashboard.\n- Items that **amplify each other** are ranked together — spoofing a merchant id (TD-01) plus an unbounded `limit` (TD-10) turns a small bug into a bulk data dump.\n- Wrong revenue math (TD-05) is ranked here anyway: merchants make decisions with that number, and it overstates income.\n\nIDs are stable (`TD-01` … `TD-17`) and don't change when the order does. Severity is the one from the first review.\n\n## Groups at a glance\n\nItems are grouped by the domain and files they touch, so each group can land as one commit.\n\n| Group | Items | Files | Ships as |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **A — Tenancy scoping through the DAL** | TD-02, TD-04 | `dal/orders-dal.ts`, `routes/orders.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | One commit |\n| **B — Authentication layer** | TD-01 | `auth.ts`, `server.ts`, `public/app.js` | One commit |\n| **C — Input validation at the API edge** | TD-10, TD-11 | `routes/orders.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | One commit |\n| **D — Output escaping in the dashboard** | TD-12 | `public/app.js` | One commit |\n| **E — Refund semantics in money math** | TD-05 | `dal/orders-dal.ts`, `routes/revenue.ts` | One commit |\n\n**Files touched by more than one group** — sequence these to avoid conflicts:\n\n| File | Groups |\n|---|---|\n| `src/dal/orders-dal.ts` | A, E |\n| `src/routes/orders.ts` | A, C |\n| `src/routes/metrics.ts` | A, C |\n| `public/app.js` | B, D |\n\nSuggested order: **A → C → E → B → D**. A defines the shape every query goes through, so doing it first keeps C and E from being rewritten; B changes how `merchantId` arrives, which is easier once A guarantees every query is scoped by it.\n\n---\n\n## Group A — Tenancy scoping through the DAL\n\n*Files: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts](src/dal/orders-dal.ts), [src/routes/orders.ts](src/routes/orders.ts), [src/routes/metrics.ts](src/routes/metrics.ts)*\n\nThese two are one piece of work: make every order query go through the DAL **and** carry the merchant scope. Fixing either alone leaves a hole.\n\n- [ ] **TD-02 · `GET /api/orders/:id` does not filter by merchant** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** direct cross-tenant read of order data (customer emails and amounts), independent of TD-01. Even with real auth in place, this endpoint would still leak.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:16](src/routes/orders.ts:16), [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38)\n  - What happens: `ordersDal.getById(id)` looks up by `id` only and ignores `req.merchantId`.\n\n- [ ] **TD-04 · `metrics.ts` bypasses the DAL** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** the DAL is where tenancy filtering, auditing, and caching are supposed to live, and `metrics.ts` is outside it. Every Tier 1 fix applied to `ordersDal` would silently *not* cover the metrics endpoints, which read the same order rows — so the bypass must be closed as part of the security work, not after it.\n  - Where: [src/routes/metrics.ts:5](src/routes/metrics.ts:5)\n  - What happens: it opens its own `new Database(DB_PATH, { readonly: true })` and runs raw SQL. Two connections to the same database, and `DB_PATH` resolved twice.\n\n## Group B — Authentication layer\n\n*Files: [src/auth.ts](src/auth.ts), [src/server.ts](src/server.ts), [public/app.js](public/app.js)*\n\n- [ ] **TD-01 · The `X-Merchant-Id` header is not verified** — Severity: High\n  - **Why first in priority:** this is the whole authorization model. Any client can impersonate any merchant by editing one header, which turns every other endpoint into a cross-tenant data source. It also multiplies TD-02 and TD-10.\n  - **Why it ships after group A:** the scope enforcement in the DAL is what makes the auth change meaningful; changing how `merchantId` is produced is a smaller, isolated diff once every query already consumes it.\n  - Where: [src/auth.ts:16](src/auth.ts:16), [public/app.js:9](public/app.js:9)\n  - What happens: `authMiddleware` only checks that the header is present and copies it to `req.merchantId`. There is no signature, no session, no verification that the caller owns that merchant.\n  - Note: documented as an intentional simplification for the challenge (\"Real auth would be a signed JWT\"), so the decision to make is *what shape* replaces it — and whether the dashboard's merchant picker survives it.\n\n## Group C — Input validation at the API edge\n\n*Files: [src/routes/orders.ts](src/routes/orders.ts), [src/routes/metrics.ts](src/routes/metrics.ts)*\n\nBoth are \"the API trusts whatever the client sends\". Same layer, same kind of fix (one validation shape applied to query params and body).\n\n- [ ] **TD-10 · `limit` is not validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** in SQLite `LIMIT -1` means \"no limit\", so `?limit=-1` returns every order of the merchant in one request. Combined with TD-01 that's a bulk export of the whole database, and on its own it's an easy way to exhaust the server.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:11](src/routes/orders.ts:11), [src/routes/metrics.ts:43](src/routes/metrics.ts:43)\n  - What happens: `Number(req.query.limit)` can yield `NaN`, a decimal, or a negative number. There is no upper bound.\n\n- [ ] **TD-11 · The `POST /api/orders` body is barely validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** it's the entry point that feeds TD-12, and it lets corrupt money into the database — negative or fractional amounts in a column that holds integer cents.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:25](src/routes/orders.ts:25)\n  - What happens: `type` accepts any string (not only `sale`/`refund`), `total_amount` accepts negatives and decimals, and `customer_email` isn't validated as an email.\n\n## Group D — Output escaping in the dashboard\n\n*File: [public/app.js](public/app.js)*\n\n- [ ] **TD-12 · Stored XSS in the orders table** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** any merchant's dashboard executes attacker-controlled markup, and the payload is planted through `POST /api/orders` (TD-11). With TD-01 an attacker can plant it in *someone else's* dashboard.\n  - **Why it ships after C:** C stops new payloads from being stored; D makes rendering safe regardless of what's already in the database. Both are needed — C alone doesn't clean existing rows.\n  - Where: [public/app.js:35](public/app.js:35)\n  - What happens: each row is built with `innerHTML`, interpolating `o.customer_email` and `o.type` unsanitized.\n\n## Group E — Refund semantics in money math\n\n*Files: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts](src/dal/orders-dal.ts), [src/routes/revenue.ts](src/routes/revenue.ts)*\n\n- [ ] **TD-05 · Revenue counts refunds as income** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** the headline number of the product is wrong, and wrong in the optimistic direction. A merchant reading \"Revenue (last 30 days)\" is told they earned money they refunded.\n  - **Related, deferred:** TD-06 (summary metrics treat refunds as sales) is the same class of bug on informational numbers and sits in the backlog. If group A has already moved the metrics queries into the DAL, fixing TD-06 in this same commit may be nearly free — decide when you get there.\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54)\n  - What happens: `sumAmountByMerchant` runs `SUM(total_amount)` without looking at `type`. Refunds are stored with a positive amount (see [src/scripts/seed.ts:43](src/scripts/seed.ts:43)), so they add instead of subtracting. Per [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), a refund represents a reversed sale.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":201,"cache_read_input_tokens":240519,"output_tokens":6442,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":786},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":201,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":6442,"cache_read_input_tokens":240519,"cache_creation_input_tokens":201,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":201},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01LsUk7QpB5SJZ82jrS8mFgg":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\tech_debt.md","content":"# Tech debt — Tier 1 (MUST, urgent)\n\nThe items we're working on now. Everything else lives in [tech_debt_backlog.md](tech_debt_backlog.md) (Tier 2 and Tier 3) and is deliberately out of sight until this file is empty.\n\n## How this is ranked\n\nPriority balances **product impact** against **security and financial risk**, not raw severity:\n\n- An item that lets an attacker read another merchant's data, or that can cost money, outranks an item that only shows a wrong number on a dashboard.\n- Items that **amplify each other** are ranked together — spoofing a merchant id (TD-01) plus an unbounded `limit` (TD-10) turns a small bug into a bulk data dump.\n- Wrong revenue math (TD-05) is ranked here anyway: merchants make decisions with that number, and it overstates income.\n\nIDs are stable (`TD-01` … `TD-17`) and don't change when the order does. Severity is the one from the first review.\n\n## Groups at a glance\n\nItems are grouped by the domain and files they touch, so each group can land as one commit.\n\n| Group | Items | Files | Ships as |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **A — Tenancy scoping through the DAL** | TD-02, TD-04 | `dal/orders-dal.ts`, `routes/orders.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | One commit |\n| **B — Authentication layer** | TD-01 | `auth.ts`, `server.ts`, `public/app.js` | One commit |\n| **C — Input validation at the API edge** | TD-10, TD-11 | `routes/orders.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | One commit |\n| **D — Output escaping in the dashboard** | TD-12 | `public/app.js` | One commit |\n| **E — Refund semantics in money math** | TD-05 | `dal/orders-dal.ts`, `routes/revenue.ts` | One commit |\n\n**Files touched by more than one group** — sequence these to avoid conflicts:\n\n| File | Groups |\n|---|---|\n| `src/dal/orders-dal.ts` | A, E |\n| `src/routes/orders.ts` | A, C |\n| `src/routes/metrics.ts` | A, C |\n| `public/app.js` | B, D |\n\nSuggested order: **A → C → E → B → D**. A defines the shape every query goes through, so doing it first keeps C and E from being rewritten; B changes how `merchantId` arrives, which is easier once A guarantees every query is scoped by it.\n\n---\n\n## Group A — Tenancy scoping through the DAL\n\n*Files: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts](src/dal/orders-dal.ts), [src/routes/orders.ts](src/routes/orders.ts), [src/routes/metrics.ts](src/routes/metrics.ts)*\n\nThese two are one piece of work: make every order query go through the DAL **and** carry the merchant scope. Fixing either alone leaves a hole.\n\n- [ ] **TD-02 · `GET /api/orders/:id` does not filter by merchant** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** direct cross-tenant read of order data (customer emails and amounts), independent of TD-01. Even with real auth in place, this endpoint would still leak.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:16](src/routes/orders.ts:16), [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38)\n  - What happens: `ordersDal.getById(id)` looks up by `id` only and ignores `req.merchantId`.\n\n- [ ] **TD-04 · `metrics.ts` bypasses the DAL** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** the DAL is where tenancy filtering, auditing, and caching are supposed to live, and `metrics.ts` is outside it. Every Tier 1 fix applied to `ordersDal` would silently *not* cover the metrics endpoints, which read the same order rows — so the bypass must be closed as part of the security work, not after it.\n  - Where: [src/routes/metrics.ts:5](src/routes/metrics.ts:5)\n  - What happens: it opens its own `new Database(DB_PATH, { readonly: true })` and runs raw SQL. Two connections to the same database, and `DB_PATH` resolved twice.\n\n## Group B — Authentication layer\n\n*Files: [src/auth.ts](src/auth.ts), [src/server.ts](src/server.ts), [public/app.js](public/app.js)*\n\n- [ ] **TD-01 · The `X-Merchant-Id` header is not verified** — Severity: High\n  - **Why first in priority:** this is the whole authorization model. Any client can impersonate any merchant by editing one header, which turns every other endpoint into a cross-tenant data source. It also multiplies TD-02 and TD-10.\n  - **Why it ships after group A:** the scope enforcement in the DAL is what makes the auth change meaningful; changing how `merchantId` is produced is a smaller, isolated diff once every query already consumes it.\n  - Where: [src/auth.ts:16](src/auth.ts:16), [public/app.js:9](public/app.js:9)\n  - What happens: `authMiddleware` only checks that the header is present and copies it to `req.merchantId`. There is no signature, no session, no verification that the caller owns that merchant.\n  - Note: documented as an intentional simplification for the challenge (\"Real auth would be a signed JWT\"), so the decision to make is *what shape* replaces it — and whether the dashboard's merchant picker survives it.\n\n## Group C — Input validation at the API edge\n\n*Files: [src/routes/orders.ts](src/routes/orders.ts), [src/routes/metrics.ts](src/routes/metrics.ts)*\n\nBoth are \"the API trusts whatever the client sends\". Same layer, same kind of fix (one validation shape applied to query params and body).\n\n- [ ] **TD-10 · `limit` is not validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** in SQLite `LIMIT -1` means \"no limit\", so `?limit=-1` returns every order of the merchant in one request. Combined with TD-01 that's a bulk export of the whole database, and on its own it's an easy way to exhaust the server.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:11](src/routes/orders.ts:11), [src/routes/metrics.ts:43](src/routes/metrics.ts:43)\n  - What happens: `Number(req.query.limit)` can yield `NaN`, a decimal, or a negative number. There is no upper bound.\n\n- [ ] **TD-11 · The `POST /api/orders` body is barely validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** it's the entry point that feeds TD-12, and it lets corrupt money into the database — negative or fractional amounts in a column that holds integer cents.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:25](src/routes/orders.ts:25)\n  - What happens: `type` accepts any string (not only `sale`/`refund`), `total_amount` accepts negatives and decimals, and `customer_email` isn't validated as an email.\n\n## Group D — Output escaping in the dashboard\n\n*File: [public/app.js](public/app.js)*\n\n- [ ] **TD-12 · Stored XSS in the orders table** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** any merchant's dashboard executes attacker-controlled markup, and the payload is planted through `POST /api/orders` (TD-11). With TD-01 an attacker can plant it in *someone else's* dashboard.\n  - **Why it ships after C:** C stops new payloads from being stored; D makes rendering safe regardless of what's already in the database. Both are needed — C alone doesn't clean existing rows.\n  - Where: [public/app.js:35](public/app.js:35)\n  - What happens: each row is built with `innerHTML`, interpolating `o.customer_email` and `o.type` unsanitized.\n\n## Group E — Refund semantics in money math\n\n*Files: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts](src/dal/orders-dal.ts), [src/routes/revenue.ts](src/routes/revenue.ts)*\n\n- [ ] **TD-05 · Revenue counts refunds as income** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** the headline number of the product is wrong, and wrong in the optimistic direction. A merchant reading \"Revenue (last 30 days)\" is told they earned money they refunded.\n  - **Related, deferred:** TD-06 (summary metrics treat refunds as sales) is the same class of bug on informational numbers and sits in the backlog. If group A has already moved the metrics queries into the DAL, fixing TD-06 in this same commit may be nearly free — decide when you get there.\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54)\n  - What happens: `sumAmountByMerchant` runs `SUM(total_amount)` without looking at `type`. Refunds are stored with a positive amount (see [src/scripts/seed.ts:43](src/scripts/seed.ts:43)), so they add instead of subtracting. Per [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), a refund represents a reversed sale.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":35,"newStart":1,"newLines":48,"lines":["-# Tech debt","+# Tech debt — Tier 1 (MUST, urgent)"," ","-Findings from reviewing the current architecture, **ordered by priority, highest first**. There is no signature, no session, no verification that the caller owns that merchant.\n  - Note: documented as an intentional simplification for the challenge (\"Real auth would be a signed JWT\"), so the decision to make is *what shape* replaces it.\n\n- [ ] **TD-02 · `GET /api/orders/:id` does not filter by merchant** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** direct cross-tenant read of order data (customer emails and amounts), independent of TD-01. Even with real auth in place, this endpoint would still leak.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:16](src/routes/orders.ts:16), [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38)\n  - What happens: `ordersDal.getById(id)` looks up by `id` only and ignores `req.merchantId`.\n\n- [ ] **TD-04 · `metrics.ts` bypasses the DAL** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** the DAL is where tenancy filtering, auditing, and caching are supposed to live, and `metrics.ts` is outside it. Every Tier 1 fix applied to `ordersDal` would silently *not* cover the metrics endpoints, which read the same order rows — so the bypass must be closed as part of the security work, not after it.\n  - Where: [src/routes/metrics.ts:5](src/routes/metrics.ts:5)\n  - What happens: it opens its own `new Database(DB_PATH, { readonly: true })` and runs raw SQL. Two connections to the same database, and `DB_PATH` resolved twice.\n\n- [ ] **TD-10 · `limit` is not validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why so high:** in SQLite `LIMIT -1` means \"no limit\", so `?limit=-1` returns every order of the merchant in one request. Combined with TD-01 that's a bulk export of the whole database, and on its own it's an easy way to exhaust the server.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:11](src/routes/orders.ts:11), [src/routes/metrics.ts:43](src/routes/metrics.ts:43)\n  - What happens: `Number(req.query.limit)` can yield `NaN`, a decimal, or a negative number. There is no upper bound.\n\n- [ ] **TD-12 · Stored XSS in the orders table** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** any merchant's dashboard executes attacker-controlled markup, and the payload is planted through the public `POST /api/orders` (TD-11). With TD-01 an attacker can plant it in *someone else's* dashboard.\n  - Where: [public/app.js:35](public/app.js:35)\n  - What happens: each row is built with `innerHTML`, interpolating `o.customer_email` and `o.type` unsanitized.\n\n- [ ] **TD-11 · The `POST /api/orders` body is barely validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** it's the entry point that feeds TD-12, and it lets corrupt money into the database — negative or fractional amounts in a column that holds integer cents.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:25](src/routes/orders.ts:25)\n  - What happens: `type` accepts any string (not only `sale`/`refund`), `total_amount` accepts negatives and decimals, and `customer_email` isn't validated as an email.\n\n- [ ] **TD-05 · Revenue counts refunds as income** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** the headline number of the product is wrong, and wrong in the optimistic direction. A merchant reading \"Revenue (last 30 days)\" is told they earned money they refunded.\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54)\n  - What happens: `sumAmountByMerchant` runs `SUM(total_amount)` without looking at `type`. Refunds are stored with a positive amount (see [src/scripts/seed.ts:43](src/scripts/seed.ts:43)), so they add instead of subtracting. Per [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), a refund represents a reversed sale.\n\n---\n\n# Tier 2 — SHOULD (next)\n\n- [ ] **TD-16 · Test coverage is minimal** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** the gate that keeps Tier 1 fixed. Right now nothing would catch a regression in auth, tenancy scoping, or revenue math.\n  - Where: [test/orders.test.ts](test/orders.test.ts)\n  - What happens: only the DAL's `create`, `listByMerchant`, and `getById` are covered. No route, auth, revenue, or metrics tests.\n\n- [ ] **TD-06 · Summary metrics treat refunds as sales** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** same class of error as TD-05 and visible on the same screen, but these numbers are informational rather than the money figure.\n  - Where: [src/routes/metrics.ts:17](src/routes/metrics.ts:17), [src/routes/metrics.ts:45](src/routes/metrics.ts:45)\n  - What happens: `total_orders`, `unique_customers`, `avg_order_value_cents`, and `top-customers.total_spent` count every row the same way.\n\n- [ ] **TD-07 · The revenue range excludes the `to` day, so the dashboard leaves out today** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** a visibly wrong number every day, with an obvious fix, but it under-reports rather than overstating.\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:59](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:59), [public/app.js:28](public/app.js:28)\n  - What happens: the filter is `created_at < to` with `to` as a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, so the whole `to` day is excluded — and the frontend sends `to = today`.\n\n- [ ] **TD-08 · `created_at` is stored in mixed formats** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** data-integrity debt that gets more expensive the more rows accumulate, and it quietly corrupts ordering and range filters.\n  - Where: [src/db.ts:30](src/db.ts:30), [src/scripts/seed.ts:21](src/scripts/seed.ts:21)\n  - What happens: the seed stores ISO 8601 (`2026-09-10T12:00:00.000Z`) while `POST`-created orders use SQLite's `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` (`2026-09-10 12:00:00`). Cheap to fold into the TD-05 commit if the metrics queries already moved into the DAL (TD-04).\n  - Where: [src/routes/metrics.ts:17](src/routes/metrics.ts:17), [src/routes/metrics.ts:45](src/routes/metrics.ts:45)\n  - What happens: `total_orders`, `unique_customers`, `avg_order_value_cents`, and `top-customers.total_spent` count every row the same way.\n\n- [ ] **TD-07 · The revenue range excludes the `to` day, so the dashboard leaves out today** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** a visibly wrong number every day, with an obvious fix, but it under-reports rather than overstating.\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:59](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:59), [public/app.js:28](public/app.js:28)\n  - What happens: the filter is `created_at < to` with `to` as a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, so the whole `to` day is excluded — and the frontend sends `to = today`.\n\n- [ ] **TD-08 · `created_at` is stored in mixed formats** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** data-integrity debt that gets more expensive the more rows accumulate, and it quietly corrupts ordering and range filters.\n  - Where: [src/db.ts:30](src/db.ts:30), [src/scripts/seed.ts:21](src/scripts/seed.ts:21)\n  - What happens: the seed stores ISO 8601 (`2026-09-10T12:00:00.000Z`) while `POST`-created orders use SQLite's `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` (`2026-09-10 12:00:00`). Comparisons and `ORDER BY` are string-based, so ordering within a day can be wrong; the browser also reads the format without `T`/`Z` as local time.\n\n- [ ] **TD-03 · `POST /api/orders` with a non-existent merchant returns 500** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** wrong status code and a leaked internal error, not a data or money problem. {"type":"queue-operation","operation":"enqueue","timestamp":"2026-09-12T04:49:26.147Z","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","content":"Creemos algo sencillo para resolver el groupo a y b. \n\n1.- crearemos un script para generar tokens, ese script podra recibir 2 opciones, el merchantId= \"merchantId\" o admin=\"true\"\n\nsi es merchantId se genera con el id del merchant y si es admin se crea sin merchantId\n\nel token debe ser un jwt firmado por el backend que contenga como claim el merchantId y el role, si es merchan debe ser merchan y si es admin el role debe ser ese. \n\nel token debe almacenarse como una cookie y no como localstorage por temas de seguridad. \n\ndebemos actualizar el repositorio de las entidades de la bd para que automaticamente se le asigne el merchantId del claim del token, podemos implementar una super clase o clase padre que haga automaticamente esto y fuerce a todos los repositorios a usarla, de esa manera evitamos que un repositorio no implemente el merchantId, también debemos verificar si el role es un admin, si es un admin podemos devolver el merchantId que venga del frontend. \n\nEl merchanId del token debe sobreescribir siempre el valor enviado por el cliente, si el valor es diferente debemos arrojar un error de autorización, pero si es admin dejamos el merchantId del cliente. \n\nLa capa de authenticación/role debe poder inyectarse en cualquier clase o metodo, crea un guard que protega las rutas existentes y nuevas de la app. \n\ncrea el plan en base a esto."}
