{"parentUuid":"07b6beb8-9974-4f2d-b9d8-a15ba9abd582","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CexwfvQAygfv4Br9otuqg","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01SUW2VpJ3NaYhovip6weZSQ","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md","content":"# 005 — JWT auth (cookie) + merchant-scoped repository base class\n\n**Status:** draft\n\nCloses Tier 1 groups **A** (TD-02, TD-04) and **B** (TD-01) from [tech_debt.md](../tech_debt.md).\n\n## Context\n\nToday `authMiddleware` trusts an `X-Merchant-Id` header, `ordersDal.getById` ignores the merchant entirely, and `metrics.ts` queries SQLite through its own connection, bypassing the DAL. The result: any client can read any merchant's data, and a tenancy filter added to the DAL wouldn't even cover the metrics endpoints.\n\nThe user's requirements:\n\n1. A script that issues tokens, taking either `merchantId=\"<id>\"` or `admin=\"true\"`.\n2. The token is a **JWT signed by the backend**, with `merchantId` and `role` claims (`merchant` or `admin`; an admin token carries no merchantId).\n3. The token is stored in a **cookie**, not localStorage.\n4. Entity repositories must apply the merchant scope **automatically**, via a **base class every repository must use**, so no repository can forget it.\n5. If the caller is an **admin**, the merchantId supplied by the client is used.\n6. The token's merchantId **always wins**; if the client sends a different one → **authorization error**. For admins, the client's value is kept.\n7. The auth/role layer must be **injectable anywhere** (any class or method), with a **guard** protecting existing and future routes.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Dependencies\n\n| Choice | Why |\n|---|---|\n| **`jose@^6.2.12`** for JWT (new prod dependency) | MIT, **zero transitive dependencies**, native ESM, typed, modern API. `jsonwebtoken@9` pulls 10 packages (lodash.*, semver, jws); hand-rolling HS256 with `node:crypto` was rejected — no hand-rolled crypto for an auth boundary. |\n| **No cookie library** | `cookie@2` requires Node ≥22 while the project declares `>=20`, and `cookie-parser` is another dependency for ~15 lines. The JWT is self-signed, so cookie integrity isn't needed — a small `parseCookies()` helper is enough. |\n\n### 2. Token\n\n- Algorithm **HS256**, secret from `process.env.JWT_SECRET`.\n  - Missing secret → **hard failure at startup** when `NODE_ENV=production`; in development, a fixed dev secret is used and a loud warning is printed (so `npm run dev` still works out of the box).\n- Claims: `role` (`merchant` | `admin`), `merchantId` (only for `merchant`), `sub` (merchantId or `admin`), `iss: recruiting-challenge`, `iat`, `exp`.\n- Default TTL **8h** (dev convenience), overridable with `--expiresIn`.\n\n### 3. Script — `src/scripts/issue-token.ts`\n\n```sh\nnpm run token -- merchantId=m_acme     # role: merchant\nnpm run token -- admin=true            # role: admin, no merchantId\nnpm run token -- merchantId=m_acme expiresIn=30m\n```\n\n- Exactly one of `merchantId=` / `admin=true` is required; both or neither → usage error, exit 1.\n- Prints the JWT, its expiry, and a ready-to-use `curl` example.\n- `package.json`: `\"token\": \"tsx src/scripts/issue-token.ts\"`.\n\n### 4. Cookie + session endpoints — `src/routes/session.ts`\n\nA cookie can't be set as `HttpOnly` from JavaScript, so the token is exchanged for a cookie:\n\n| Endpoint | Behavior |\n|---|---|\n| `POST /api/auth/session` | Body `{ token }`. Verifies the JWT; on success replies `204` with `Set-Cookie`. Invalid/expired → `401`. |\n| `DELETE /api/auth/session` | Clears the cookie. |\n\nCookie `session` attributes: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, `Max-Age` = token TTL, and `Secure` when `NODE_ENV=production` (so it still works over `http://localhost` in dev).\n\n### 5. Auth layer\n\n```\ncookie ──▶ verifyToken ──▶ AuthContext (AsyncLocalStorage) ──▶ guard ──▶ route ──▶ repository\n```\n\n- **`src/auth/jwt.ts`** — `signToken(claims, expiresIn)` / `verifyToken(token)` (jose, HS256, issuer check).\n- **`src/auth/context.ts`** — an `AsyncLocalStorage<AuthContext>`; `runWithAuthContext(ctx, fn)` and `getAuthContext()`. This is what makes the layer **injectable anywhere**: any class or function can read the caller's identity without threading parameters. `getAuthContext()` **throws** when there is no context (fail closed).\n- **`src/auth/guard.ts`** — `requireAuth({ roles })`, usable per-router or per-route:\n  ```ts\n  app.use('/api/orders', requireAuth(), ordersRouter);          // merchant or admin\n  app.use('/api/admin',  requireAuth({ roles: ['admin'] }), …);  // admin only\n  ```\n  It reads the cookie, verifies the JWT, resolves the **effective merchantId** (next section), and runs the rest of the request inside the context.\n- `src/auth.ts` is deleted; `server.ts` wires the guard instead.\n\n**Effective merchantId resolution** (the core rule):\n\n| Role | Client sends no merchantId | Client sends the same one | Client sends a different one |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `merchant` | token's merchantId | token's merchantId | **`403 merchant_mismatch`** |\n| `admin` | context without merchantId | client's | client's |\n\n- The client channel for the merchantId stays the `X-Merchant-Id` header (same shape as today, so the dashboard and `curl` examples barely change).\n- No token / invalid / expired → `401`.\n- An **admin with no merchantId** hitting a merchant-scoped endpoint → `400 merchant_id_required`. Cross-merchant aggregation is out of scope (see Q3).\n\n### 6. Repository base class — `src/dal/base-repository.ts`\n\n```ts\nabstract class BaseRepository<TRow> {\n  protected abstract readonly table: string;\n  protected abstract readonly merchantColumn: string;  // 'merchant_id'\n  protected scope(): string        // merchantId from the context, throws if absent\n  protected select(sql, params)    // injects `AND <merchantColumn> = ?`\n  protected insert(row)            // forces merchantColumn = scope()\n}\n```\n\n- The merchant filter is **not** something a subclass passes in: it comes from `getAuthContext()` inside the base class, so a repository physically cannot query without it.\n- `OrdersRepository` (replaces `ordersDal`) and `MetricsRepository` (replaces the raw SQL in `metrics.ts`, dropping its second read-only connection) both extend it. **TD-04 closed.**\n- `getById` becomes merchant-scoped. **TD-02 closed.**\n\n**Enforcement gate:** an architecture test (`test/architecture.test.ts`) asserts that **only `src/dal/base-repository.ts` imports `db` from `src/db.ts`** (`src/scripts/*` excluded). A new repository that reaches for `db` directly fails the test — that's what stops requirement 4 from decaying.\n\n### 7. Dashboard (`public/index.html`, `public/app.js`)\n\n- The browser sends the cookie automatically (same origin); the `X-Merchant-Id` header is only sent when the session is an **admin**.\n- The merchant picker becomes **admin-only**: with a merchant token it's hidden and the dashboard shows the merchant from the token.\n- A small \"paste your token\" box calls `POST /api/auth/session` so the dev flow is: run `npm run token`, paste, use. Token never touches `localStorage`.\n- `GET /api/auth/session` (whoami) returns `{ role, merchantId }` so the UI knows what to render.\n\n### 8. Commits (in this order)\n\n| # | Content | Tech debt |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `jose` dep + `src/auth/jwt.ts` + `src/scripts/issue-token.ts` + `npm run token` + tests | — |\n| 2 | `src/auth/context.ts` + `src/auth/guard.ts` + session routes + cookie helper + `server.ts` wiring; `src/auth.ts` removed | TD-01 |\n| 3 | `src/dal/base-repository.ts` + `OrdersRepository` + architecture test | TD-02 |\n| 4 | `MetricsRepository`; `metrics.ts` stops touching `db`/SQLite directly | TD-04 |\n| 5 | Dashboard: cookie session, admin-only picker, token box | TD-01 (UI side) |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — `jose` as a new prod dependency?** Recommended (zero transitive deps). Alternative: hand-rolled HS256 with `node:crypto` and no dependency at all, which I'd rather avoid on an auth boundary.\n- **Q2 — Dev fallback secret.** Recommended: fixed dev secret + warning when `JWT_SECRET` is missing and `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`, hard failure in production. Stricter alternative: always fail without `JWT_SECRET` (every dev must export one before `npm run dev`).\n- **Q3 — Admin with no merchantId on a scoped endpoint.** Recommended: `400 merchant_id_required`. Alternative: aggregate across all merchants (bigger change, new query shapes).\n- **Q4 — Merchant picker for admins.** Recommended: keep it, admin-only, sending `X-Merchant-Id`. Alternative: drop the picker and use a `?merchantId=` query param.\n- **Q5 — Token TTL 8h.** Fine for a dev/challenge flow; say if you want something shorter.\n\n## Scope\n\n- New: `src/auth/jwt.ts`, `src/auth/context.ts`, `src/auth/guard.ts`, `src/auth/cookies.ts`, `src/routes/session.ts`, `src/dal/base-repository.ts`, `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/dal/metrics-repository.ts`, `src/scripts/issue-token.ts`.\n- Changed: `src/server.ts`, `src/routes/orders.ts`, `src/routes/revenue.ts`, `src/routes/metrics.ts`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`, `package.json`, `test/orders.test.ts`.\n- Removed: `src/auth.ts`, `src/dal/orders-dal.ts`.\n- Tests: `test/auth-guard.test.ts`, `test/base-repository.test.ts`, `test/architecture.test.ts`, updated `test/orders.test.ts`.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Refund math (TD-05), input validation (TD-10, TD-11), XSS escaping (TD-12) — groups C, D, E.\n- Token refresh/rotation, revocation lists, real login with credentials, user table.\n- Rate limiting, CSRF tokens (mitigated here by `SameSite=Strict`).\n- `docs/` updates — requested for authorization after validation (CLAUDE.md §6): `docs/api.md` (auth + session endpoints) and `docs/architecture.md` (auth layer + repository base class, which also closes TD-17).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — new tests plus the existing ones pass.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `npm run check:deps` → no new advisories from `jose`.\n4. Script: `npm run token -- merchantId=m_acme` and `-- admin=true` produce tokens whose decoded claims match; invalid combinations exit 1.\n5. Guard, by `curl`:\n   - no cookie → `401`;\n   - merchant cookie → `200` with its own data;\n   - merchant cookie + `X-Merchant-Id` of **another** merchant → `403`;\n   - merchant cookie + its **own** `X-Merchant-Id` → `200`;\n   - admin cookie + `X-Merchant-Id: m_bistro` → `200` with `m_bistro` data;\n   - admin cookie with no header on a scoped endpoint → `400`;\n   - expired token (`expiresIn=1s`) → `401`.\n6. TD-02: `GET /api/orders/:id` with an id belonging to another merchant → `404` (not `200`).\n7. TD-04: `grep` finds no `better-sqlite3` import in `src/routes/`; the architecture test passes.\n8. Browser: paste token → dashboard loads; picker hidden for merchant, visible for admin; `document.cookie` does **not** expose the session (HttpOnly).\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits; `src/auth.ts` and `src/dal/orders-dal.ts` come back with them. No database migration is involved.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4106,"cache_read_input_tokens":248834,"output_tokens":4803,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":107},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4106,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":4803,"cache_read_input_tokens":248834,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4106,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4106},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01SUW2VpJ3NaYhovip6weZSQ":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md","content":"# 005 — JWT auth (cookie) + merchant-scoped repository base class\n\n**Status:** draft\n\nCloses Tier 1 groups **A** (TD-02, TD-04) and **B** (TD-01) from [tech_debt.md](../tech_debt.md).\n\n## Context\n\nToday `authMiddleware` trusts an `X-Merchant-Id` header, `ordersDal.getById` ignores the merchant entirely, and `metrics.ts` queries SQLite through its own connection, bypassing the DAL. Script — `src/scripts/issue-token.ts`\n\n```sh\nnpm run token -- merchantId=m_acme     # role: merchant\nnpm run token -- admin=true            # role: admin, no merchantId\nnpm run token -- merchantId=m_acme expiresIn=30m\n```\n\n- Exactly one of `merchantId=` / `admin=true` is required; both or neither → usage error, exit 1.\n- Prints the JWT, its expiry, and a ready-to-use `curl` example.\n- `package.json`: `\"token\": \"tsx src/scripts/issue-token.ts\"`.\n\n### 4. Verifies the JWT; on success replies `204` with `Set-Cookie`. Invalid/expired → `401`. |\n| `DELETE /api/auth/session` | Clears the cookie. |\n\nCookie `session` attributes: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, `Max-Age` = token TTL, and `Secure` when `NODE_ENV=production` (so it still works over `http://localhost` in dev).\n\n### 5. Auth layer\n\n```\ncookie ──▶ verifyToken ──▶ AuthContext (AsyncLocalStorage) ──▶ guard ──▶ route ──▶ repository\n```\n\n- **`src/auth/jwt.ts`** — `signToken(claims, expiresIn)` / `verifyToken(token)` (jose, HS256, issuer check).\n- **`src/auth/context.ts`** — an `AsyncLocalStorage<AuthContext>`; `runWithAuthContext(ctx, fn)` and `getAuthContext()`. Cross-merchant aggregation is out of scope (see Q3).\n\n### 6. Repository base class — `src/dal/base-repository.ts`\n\n```ts\nabstract class BaseRepository<TRow> {\n  protected abstract readonly table: string;\n  protected abstract readonly merchantColumn: string;  // 'merchant_id'\n  protected scope(): string        // merchantId from the context, throws if absent\n  protected select(sql, params)    // injects `AND <merchantColumn> = ?`\n  protected insert(row)            // forces merchantColumn = scope()\n}\n```\n\n- The merchant filter is **not** something a subclass passes in: it comes from `getAuthContext()` inside the base class, so a repository physically cannot query without it.\n- `OrdersRepository` (replaces `ordersDal`) and `MetricsRepository` (replaces the raw SQL in `metrics.ts`, dropping its second read-only connection) both extend it. **TD-04 closed.**\n- `getById` becomes merchant-scoped. **TD-02 closed.**\n\n**Enforcement gate:** an architecture test (`test/architecture.test.ts`) asserts that **only `src/dal/base-repository.ts` imports `db` from `src/db.ts`** (`src/scripts/*` excluded). A new repository that reaches for `db` directly fails the test — that's what stops requirement 4 from decaying.\n\n### 7. Dashboard (`public/index.html`, `public/app.js`)\n\n- The browser sends the cookie automatically (same origin); the `X-Merchant-Id` header is only sent when the session is an **admin**.\n- The merchant picker becomes **admin-only**: with a merchant token it's hidden and the dashboard shows the merchant from the token.\n- A small \"paste your token\" box calls `POST /api/auth/session` so the dev flow is: run `npm run token`, paste, use. Token never touches `localStorage`.\n- `GET /api/auth/session` (whoami) returns `{ role, merchantId }` so the UI knows what to render.\n\n### 8. Commits (in this order)\n\n| # | Content | Tech debt |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `jose` dep + `src/auth/jwt.ts` + `src/scripts/issue-token.ts` + `npm run token` + tests | — |\n| 2 | `src/auth/context.ts` + `src/auth/guard.ts` + session routes + cookie helper + `server.ts` wiring; `src/auth.ts` removed | TD-01 |\n| 3 | `src/dal/base-repository.ts` + `OrdersRepository` + architecture test | TD-02 |\n| 4 | `MetricsRepository`; `metrics.ts` stops touching `db`/SQLite directly | TD-04 |\n| 5 | Dashboard: cookie session, admin-only picker, token box | TD-01 (UI side) |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — `jose` as a new prod dependency?** Recommended (zero transitive deps). Alternative: hand-rolled HS256 with `node:crypto` and no dependency at all, which I'd rather avoid on an auth boundary.\n- **Q2 — Dev fallback secret.** Recommended: fixed dev secret + warning when `JWT_SECRET` is missing and `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`, hard failure in production. El token nunca pasa por `localStorage`.\n- **Repositorios:** una clase `BaseRepository` que saca el merchantId del contexto de autenticación por dentro, no de un parámetro. Un repositorio no puede consultar sin el filtro porque no tiene acceso al filtro. `OrdersRepository` y `MetricsRepository` la extienden, y `metrics.ts` deja de abrir su propia conexión.\n- **Inyectable en cualquier clase o método:** uso `AsyncLocalStorage`, así que cualquier función puede llamar a `getAuthContext()` sin recibir parámetros. Si no hay contexto, lanza error.\n- **Guard:** `requireAuth({ roles })`, que se puede poner en un router o en una ruta suelta.\n- **La regla del merchantId:** si el rol es `merchant` y el cliente manda otro id, sale `403`. Si manda el suyo o ninguno, gana el del token. Si es `admin`, se usa el del cliente.\n\n**Lo que aporto yo sobre lo que pediste:**\n\n- **Un test de arquitectura** que comprueba que solo `base-repository.ts` importa `db`. Sin eso, tu requisito de \"que ningún repositorio se salte el merchantId\" se cumple hoy y se rompe en tres meses, cuando alguien escriba un repositorio nuevo.\n- **`jose` en vez de `jsonwebtoken`:** `jose` es MIT y no arrastra dependencias; `jsonwebtoken` mete 10 paquetes.\n- **Cinco commits** en orden, uno por pieza, para que se puedan revisar por separado.\n\n**Decisiones que necesito que confirmes (Q1 a Q5 del plan):**\n- **Q1:** añadir `jose` como dependencia de producción. La alternativa es implementar HS256 a mano, que prefiero evitar en una capa de autenticación.\n- **Q2:** si falta `JWT_SECRET`, en desarrollo usar un secreto fijo con aviso y en producción fallar al arrancar. La alternativa es fallar siempre.\n- **Q3:** un admin sin merchantId en un endpoint con scope recibe `400`. {"parentUuid":"0dd54fdf-ac17-4522-8215-453cf27b9412","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CexxbATEwZAZq8mysseEH","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Tviym8gfcVBurPJJZqwJzT","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md","content":"# 005 — JWT auth (HttpOnly cookies, admin-minted merchant tokens) + scoped repository base class\n\n**Status:** draft (rev 2 — token model reworked per the user's correction)\n\nCloses Tier 1 groups **A** (TD-02, TD-04) and **B** (TD-01) from [tech_debt.md](../tech_debt.md).\n\n## Context\n\nToday `authMiddleware` trusts an `X-Merchant-Id` header, `ordersDal.getById` ignores the merchant entirely, and `metrics.ts` queries SQLite through its own connection, bypassing the DAL. Any client can read any merchant's data, and a tenancy filter added to the DAL wouldn't cover the metrics endpoints.\n\nThe challenge also requires being able to **look at both seeded merchants** from the dashboard, so the design needs a legitimate way to switch merchants without trusting a client-sent id.\n\n### Token model (user's correction to rev 1)\n\nInstead of a CLI flag choosing between merchant and admin tokens:\n\n- An **admin token** is a *minting* credential. It is injected into an HttpOnly cookie when the server starts (dev), and it can mint merchant-scoped tokens.\n- Every time the **merchant selector changes**, the frontend asks the auth endpoint for a **new merchant token** for that merchant.\n- Merchant tokens are **short-lived**; the admin token acts like a refresh token and mints new ones.\n\nThis isolates all data access behind a token whose `merchantId` claim is fixed by the backend.\n\n### Security boundary (explicit, because it's the risky part)\n\nAuto-injecting an admin cookie means *whoever can reach the server gets a credential that can mint any merchant's token*. That is acceptable as a local dev convenience and unacceptable in production. Therefore:\n\n- The auto-injection middleware runs **only when `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`**, and logs a warning on every server start.\n- In production the same endpoint exists, but the admin token must come from a real login (out of scope here) or from `npm run token`.\n- If this is ever deployed as-is, TD-01 is back in a nicer costume. That is written into the docs, not just this plan.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Dependencies\n\n| Choice | Why |\n|---|---|\n| **`jose@^6.2.12`** for JWT (new prod dependency) | MIT, **zero transitive dependencies**, native ESM, typed. `jsonwebtoken@9` pulls 10 packages; hand-rolled HS256 rejected on an auth boundary. |\n| **No cookie library** | `cookie@2` needs Node ≥22 (project declares `>=20`) and `cookie-parser` is a dependency for ~15 lines. The JWT is signed, so cookie integrity isn't needed — a small `parseCookies()` helper suffices. |\n\n### 2. Two token types\n\n| | Admin token | Merchant token |\n|---|---|---|\n| Claims | `role: 'admin'`, `scope: 'mint'`, `sub: 'admin'` | `role: 'merchant'`, `scope: 'data'`, `merchantId`, `sub: <merchantId>` |\n| TTL | 8h | **10 min** |\n| Cookie | `admin_session` (HttpOnly) | `merchant_session` (HttpOnly) |\n| Can read data? | ❌ no — `403 token_not_scoped_for_data` | ✅ yes, only its own merchant |\n| Can mint tokens? | ✅ yes | ❌ no |\n\nBoth: HS256, `iss: recruiting-challenge`, `iat`, `exp`. Secret from `JWT_SECRET` (see Q2).\n\nCookies: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, `Max-Age` = TTL, `Secure` when `NODE_ENV=production`.\n\n**Why the admin token can't read data (Q3):** it keeps a single rule for every data query — *the merchantId always comes from the token, never from the client*. Without this, the admin path would reintroduce \"trust the client's `X-Merchant-Id`\", which is exactly TD-01.\n\n### 3. Endpoints — `src/routes/auth.ts`\n\n| Endpoint | Auth | Behavior |\n|---|---|---|\n| `POST /api/auth/token` | `admin_session` cookie (or `Authorization: Bearer <admin token>`) | Body `{ merchantId }`. Verifies the merchant exists, mints a 10-min merchant token, replies `204` + `Set-Cookie: merchant_session`. Called by the dashboard on every selector change. |\n| `GET /api/auth/session` | any cookie | \"Who am I\": `{ role, merchantId, expiresAt }`, so the UI knows what to render. |\n| `DELETE /api/auth/session` | — | Clears both cookies. |\n| `POST /api/auth/admin-session` | — | Exchanges an admin token (body `{ token }`, e.g. from `npm run token`) for the `admin_session` cookie. The non-dev way in. |\n\n### 4. Dev bootstrap\n\nMiddleware `devAdminSession` (only when `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`): if the request has no `admin_session` cookie, mint one and attach it to the response. So `npm run dev` / `npm run start` → open the dashboard → the admin cookie is already there, and the selector works.\n\nStartup log: `⚠ dev mode: auto-issuing admin session cookies (never enable in production)`.\n\n### 5. Script — `src/scripts/issue-token.ts`\n\nNow mints **admin** tokens only (merchant tokens come from the endpoint):\n\n```sh\nnpm run token                 # admin token, 8h\nnpm run token -- expiresIn=30m\n```\n\nPrints the token plus a `curl` example for `POST /api/auth/admin-session`. `package.json`: `\"token\": \"tsx src/scripts/issue-token.ts\"`.\n\n### 6. Auth layer\n\n```\nmerchant_session cookie ──▶ verifyToken ──▶ AuthContext (AsyncLocalStorage) ──▶ guard ──▶ route ──▶ repository\n```\n\n- **`src/auth/jwt.ts`** — `signToken(claims, expiresIn)` / `verifyToken(token)` (jose, HS256, issuer + scope checks).\n- **`src/auth/context.ts`** — `AsyncLocalStorage<AuthContext>` with `runWithAuthContext(ctx, fn)` and `getAuthContext()`. This is what makes the layer **injectable in any class or method** without threading parameters. `getAuthContext()` **throws** when there's no context (fail closed).\n- **`src/auth/guard.ts`** — `requireAuth({ scope })`, usable per-router or per-route:\n  ```ts\n  app.use('/api/orders', requireAuth(), ordersRouter);              // needs a data-scoped token\n  app.post('/api/auth/token', requireAuth({ scope: 'mint' }), …);   // needs the admin token\n  ```\n- `src/auth.ts` is deleted; `server.ts` wires the guard.\n\n**Rules enforced by the guard:**\n\n| Situation | Result |\n|---|---|\n| No token | `401 unauthenticated` |\n| Expired / invalid / wrong issuer | `401 session_expired` (distinct code so the UI can re-mint) |\n| Admin token on a data route | `403 token_not_scoped_for_data` |\n| Merchant token on a mint route | `403 token_not_scoped_for_mint` |\n| Client sends `X-Merchant-Id` ≠ token's | `403 merchant_mismatch` |\n| Client sends `X-Merchant-Id` = token's | allowed (ignored; the token wins) |\n\nThe client-sent merchantId is never *used*, only compared — so the \"token always wins\" rule holds by construction.\n\n### 7. Repository base class — `src/dal/base-repository.ts`\n\n```ts\nabstract class BaseRepository<TRow> {\n  protected abstract readonly table: string;\n  protected abstract readonly merchantColumn: string;  // 'merchant_id'\n  protected scope(): string        // merchantId from the auth context; throws if absent\n  protected select(sql, params)    // injects `AND <merchantColumn> = ?`\n  protected insert(row)            // forces merchantColumn = scope()\n}\n```\n\n- The merchant filter is **not** a parameter a subclass can forget: the base class reads it from `getAuthContext()`.\n- `OrdersRepository` (replaces `ordersDal`) and `MetricsRepository` (replaces the raw SQL in `metrics.ts`, dropping its second read-only connection) extend it. **TD-04 closed.**\n- `getById` becomes merchant-scoped. **TD-02 closed.**\n\n**Enforcement gate:** `test/architecture.test.ts` asserts that **only `src/dal/base-repository.ts` imports `db` from `src/db.ts`** (`src/scripts/*` excluded). A new repository reaching for `db` directly fails the test.\n\n### 8. Dashboard (`public/index.html`, `public/app.js`)\n\n- Cookies travel automatically (same origin); no `X-Merchant-Id` header, no `localStorage`.\n- On load: `GET /api/auth/session`. On selector change: `POST /api/auth/token { merchantId }`, then refresh the data.\n- On `401 session_expired` (merchant token aged out after 10 min): re-mint once with the current selection and retry the request; if that also fails, show \"session expired\".\n- The merchant list comes from a new `GET /api/merchants` (mint-scoped) instead of being hardcoded — small, and it kills TD-14 on the way.\n\n### 9. Commits (in order)\n\n| # | Content | Tech debt |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `jose` + `src/auth/jwt.ts` + `src/scripts/issue-token.ts` + `npm run token` + tests | — |\n| 2 | `src/auth/context.ts` + `guard.ts` + cookies helper + `src/routes/auth.ts` + dev bootstrap + `server.ts` wiring; `src/auth.ts` removed | TD-01 |\n| 3 | `src/dal/base-repository.ts` + `OrdersRepository` + architecture test | TD-02 |\n| 4 | `MetricsRepository`; `metrics.ts` no longer touches `db`/SQLite | TD-04 |\n| 5 | Dashboard: session bootstrap, selector minting, 401 re-mint, `/api/merchants` | TD-01 (UI), TD-14 |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — `jose` as a new prod dependency?** Recommended (zero transitive deps). Alternative: hand-rolled HS256 with `node:crypto`.\n- **Q2 — Dev fallback secret.** Recommended: fixed dev secret + warning when `JWT_SECRET` is missing and `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`; hard failure in production. Alternative: always require `JWT_SECRET`.\n- **Q3 — Admin token is mint-only** (can't read data). Recommended, see §2. Alternative: let it also read data with an explicit `X-Merchant-Id`, which softens the \"token always wins\" rule.\n- **Q4 — TTLs:** admin 8h, merchant 10 min. Say if you want the merchant token shorter (e.g. 2 min) — the dashboard re-mints transparently either way.\n- **Q5 — Expiry handling.** Recommended: `401 session_expired` and the frontend re-mints once, because the server doesn't know which merchant the user is looking at. Any client can read any merchant's data, and a tenancy filter added to the DAL wouldn't cover the metrics endpoints.\n\nThe challenge also requires being able to **look at both seeded merchants** from the dashboard, so the design needs a legitimate way to switch merchants without trusting a client-sent id.\n\n### Token model (user's correction to rev 1)\n\nInstead of a CLI flag choosing between merchant and admin tokens:\n\n- An **admin token** is a *minting* credential. It is injected into an HttpOnly cookie when the server starts (dev), and it can mint merchant-scoped tokens.\n- Every time the **merchant selector changes**, the frontend asks the auth endpoint for a **new merchant token** for that merchant.\n- Merchant tokens are **short-lived**; the admin token acts like a refresh token and mints new ones.\n\nThis isolates all data access behind a token whose `merchantId` claim is fixed by the backend.\n\n### Security boundary (explicit, because it's the risky part)\n\nAuto-injecting an admin cookie means *whoever can reach the server gets a credential that can mint any merchant's token*. That is acceptable as a local dev convenience and unacceptable in production. Therefore:\n\n- The auto-injection middleware runs **only when `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`**, and logs a warning on every server start.\n- In production the same endpoint exists, but the admin token must come from a real login (out of scope here) or from `npm run token`.\n- If this is ever deployed as-is, TD-01 is back in a nicer costume. That is written into the docs, not just this plan.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Dependencies\n\n| Choice | Why |\n|---|---|\n| **`jose@^6.2.12`** for JWT (new prod dependency) | MIT, **zero transitive dependencies**, native ESM, typed. `jsonwebtoken@9` pulls 10 packages; hand-rolled HS256 rejected on an auth boundary. |\n| **No cookie library** | `cookie@2` needs Node ≥22 (project declares `>=20`) and `cookie-parser` is a dependency for ~15 lines. The JWT is signed, so cookie integrity isn't needed — a small `parseCookies()` helper suffices. |\n\n### 2. Two token types\n\n| | Admin token | Merchant token |\n|---|---|---|\n| Claims | `role: 'admin'`, `scope: 'mint'`, `sub: 'admin'` | `role: 'merchant'`, `scope: 'data'`, `merchantId`, `sub: <merchantId>` |\n| TTL | 8h | **10 min** |\n| Cookie | `admin_session` (HttpOnly) | `merchant_session` (HttpOnly) |\n| Can read data? | ❌ no — `403 token_not_scoped_for_data` | ✅ yes, only its own merchant |\n| Can mint tokens? | ✅ yes | ❌ no |\n\nBoth: HS256, `iss: recruiting-challenge`, `iat`, `exp`. Secret from `JWT_SECRET` (see Q2).\n\nCookies: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, `Max-Age` = TTL, `Secure` when `NODE_ENV=production`.\n\n**Why the admin token can't read data (Q3):** it keeps a single rule for every data query — *the merchantId always comes from the token, never from the client*. Without this, the admin path would reintroduce \"trust the client's `X-Merchant-Id`\", which is exactly TD-01.\n\n### 3. Endpoints — `src/routes/auth.ts`\n\n| Endpoint | Auth | Behavior |\n|---|---|---|\n| `POST /api/auth/token` | `admin_session` cookie (or `Authorization: Bearer <admin token>`) | Body `{ merchantId }`. Verifies the merchant exists, mints a 10-min merchant token, replies `204` + `Set-Cookie: merchant_session`. Called by the dashboard on every selector change. |\n| `GET /api/auth/session` | any cookie | \"Who am I\": `{ role, merchantId, expiresAt }`, so the UI knows what to render. |\n| `DELETE /api/auth/session` | — | Clears both cookies. |\n| `POST /api/auth/admin-session` | — | Exchanges an admin token (body `{ token }`, e.g. from `npm run token`) for the `admin_session` cookie. The non-dev way in. |\n\n### 4. Dev bootstrap\n\nMiddleware `devAdminSession` (only when `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`): if the request has no `admin_session` cookie, mint one and attach it to the response. So `npm run dev` / `npm run start` → open the dashboard → the admin cookie is already there, and the selector works.\n\nStartup log: `⚠ dev mode: auto-issuing admin session cookies (never enable in production)`.\n\n### 5. Script — `src/scripts/issue-token.ts`\n\nNow mints **admin** tokens only (merchant tokens come from the endpoint):\n\n```sh\nnpm run token                 # admin token, 8h\nnpm run token -- expiresIn=30m\n```\n\nPrints the token plus a `curl` example for `POST /api/auth/admin-session`. `package.json`: `\"token\": \"tsx src/scripts/issue-token.ts\"`.\n\n### 6. Auth layer\n\n```\nmerchant_session cookie ──▶ verifyToken ──▶ AuthContext (AsyncLocalStorage) ──▶ guard ──▶ route ──▶ repository\n```\n\n- **`src/auth/jwt.ts`** — `signToken(claims, expiresIn)` / `verifyToken(token)` (jose, HS256, issuer + scope checks).\n- **`src/auth/context.ts`** — `AsyncLocalStorage<AuthContext>` with `runWithAuthContext(ctx, fn)` and `getAuthContext()`. This is what makes the layer **injectable in any class or method** without threading parameters. `getAuthContext()` **throws** when there's no context (fail closed).\n- **`src/auth/guard.ts`** — `requireAuth({ scope })`, usable per-router or per-route:\n  ```ts\n  app.use('/api/orders', requireAuth(), ordersRouter);              // needs a data-scoped token\n  app.post('/api/auth/token', requireAuth({ scope: 'mint' }), …);   // needs the admin token\n  ```\n- `src/auth.ts` is deleted; `server.ts` wires the guard.\n\n**Rules enforced by the guard:**\n\n| Situation | Result |\n|---|---|\n| No token | `401 unauthenticated` |\n| Expired / invalid / wrong issuer | `401 session_expired` (distinct code so the UI can re-mint) |\n| Admin token on a data route | `403 token_not_scoped_for_data` |\n| Merchant token on a mint route | `403 token_not_scoped_for_mint` |\n| Client sends `X-Merchant-Id` ≠ token's | `403 merchant_mismatch` |\n| Client sends `X-Merchant-Id` = token's | allowed (ignored; the token wins) |\n\nThe client-sent merchantId is never *used*, only compared — so the \"token always wins\" rule holds by construction.\n\n### 7. Repository base class — `src/dal/base-repository.ts`\n\n```ts\nabstract class BaseRepository<TRow> {\n  protected abstract readonly table: string;\n  protected abstract readonly merchantColumn: string;  // 'merchant_id'\n  protected scope(): string        // merchantId from the auth context; throws if absent\n  protected select(sql, params)    // injects `AND <merchantColumn> = ?`\n  protected insert(row)            // forces merchantColumn = scope()\n}\n```\n\n- The merchant filter is **not** a parameter a subclass can forget: the base class reads it from `getAuthContext()`.\n- `OrdersRepository` (replaces `ordersDal`) and `MetricsRepository` (replaces the raw SQL in `metrics.ts`, dropping its second read-only connection) extend it. **TD-04 closed.**\n- `getById` becomes merchant-scoped. **TD-02 closed.**\n\n**Enforcement gate:** `test/architecture.test.ts` asserts that **only `src/dal/base-repository.ts` imports `db` from `src/db.ts`** (`src/scripts/*` excluded). A new repository reaching for `db` directly fails the test.\n\n### 8. Dashboard (`public/index.html`, `public/app.js`)\n\n- Cookies travel automatically (same origin); no `X-Merchant-Id` header, no `localStorage`.\n- On load: `GET /api/auth/session`. On selector change: `POST /api/auth/token { merchantId }`, then refresh the data.\n- On `401 session_expired` (merchant token aged out after 10 min): re-mint once with the current selection and retry the request; if that also fails, show \"session expired\".\n- The merchant list comes from a new `GET /api/merchants` (mint-scoped) instead of being hardcoded — small, and it kills TD-14 on the way.\n\n### 9. Commits (in order)\n\n| # | Content | Tech debt |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `jose` + `src/auth/jwt.ts` + `src/scripts/issue-token.ts` + `npm run token` + tests | — |\n| 2 | `src/auth/context.ts` + `guard.ts` + cookies helper + `src/routes/auth.ts` + dev bootstrap + `server.ts` wiring; `src/auth.ts` removed | TD-01 |\n| 3 | `src/dal/base-repository.ts` + `OrdersRepository` + architecture test | TD-02 |\n| 4 | `MetricsRepository`; `metrics.ts` no longer touches `db`/SQLite | TD-04 |\n| 5 | Dashboard: session bootstrap, selector minting, 401 re-mint, `/api/merchants` | TD-01 (UI), TD-14 |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — `jose` as a new prod dependency?** Recommended (zero transitive deps). Alternative: hand-rolled HS256 with `node:crypto`.\n- **Q2 — Dev fallback secret.** Recommended: fixed dev secret + warning when `JWT_SECRET` is missing and `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`; hard failure in production. Alternative: always require `JWT_SECRET`.\n- **Q3 — Admin token is mint-only** (can't read data). Recommended, see §2. Alternative: let it also read data with an explicit `X-Merchant-Id`, which softens the \"token always wins\" rule.\n- **Q4 — TTLs:** admin 8h, merchant 10 min. Say if you want the merchant token shorter (e.g. 2 min) — the dashboard re-mints transparently either way.\n- **Q5 — Expiry handling.** Recommended: `401 session_expired` and the frontend re-mints once, because the server doesn't know which merchant the user is looking at. Alternative: store the last merchantId in the admin cookie so the server can refresh transparently (more state in the cookie).\n\n## Scope\n\n- New: `src/auth/jwt.ts`, `src/auth/context.ts`, `src/auth/guard.ts`, `src/auth/cookies.ts`, `src/auth/dev-session.ts`, `src/routes/auth.ts`, `src/routes/merchants.ts`, `src/dal/base-repository.ts`, `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/dal/metrics-repository.ts`, `src/scripts/issue-token.ts`.\n- Changed: `src/server.ts`, `src/routes/orders.ts`, `src/routes/revenue.ts`, `src/routes/metrics.ts`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`, `package.json`, `test/orders.test.ts`.\n- Removed: `src/auth.ts`, `src/dal/orders-dal.ts`.\n- Tests: `test/auth-jwt.test.ts`, `test/auth-guard.test.ts`, `test/base-repository.test.ts`, `test/architecture.test.ts`, updated `test/orders.test.ts`.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Refund math (TD-05), input validation (TD-10, TD-11), XSS escaping (TD-12) — groups C, D, E.\n- Real login (credentials, user table), token revocation, rotation of the admin token.\n- Rate limiting; CSRF tokens (mitigated by `SameSite=Strict` on state-changing endpoints).\n- `docs/` — authorization to be requested after validation (CLAUDE.md §6): `docs/api.md` (auth endpoints, token types, the production caveat) and `docs/architecture.md` (auth layer + repository base class, closing TD-17).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` → new + existing tests pass.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `npm run check:deps` → no new advisories from `jose`.\n4. `npm run token` → admin token whose claims decode to `role: admin`, `scope: mint`, no `merchantId`.\n5. Script — `src/scripts/issue-token.ts`\n\nNow mints **admin** tokens only (merchant tokens come from the endpoint):\n\n```sh\nnpm run token                 # admin token, 8h\nnpm run token -- expiresIn=30m\n```\n\nPrints the token plus a `curl` example for `POST /api/auth/admin-session`. `package.json`: `\"token\": \"tsx src/scripts/issue-token.ts\"`.\n\n### 6. Auth layer\n\n```\nmerchant_session cookie ──▶ verifyToken ──▶ AuthContext (AsyncLocalStorage) ──▶ guard ──▶ route ──▶ repository\n```\n\n- **`src/auth/jwt.ts`** — `signToken(claims, expiresIn)` / `verifyToken(token)` (jose, HS256, issuer + scope checks).\n- **`src/auth/context.ts`** — `AsyncLocalStorage<AuthContext>` with `runWithAuthContext(ctx, fn)` and `getAuthContext()`. This is what makes the layer **injectable in any class or method** without threading parameters. `getAuthContext()` **throws** when there's no context (fail closed).\n- **`src/auth/guard.ts`** — `requireAuth({ scope })`, usable per-router or per-route:\n  ```ts\n  app.use('/api/orders', requireAuth(), ordersRouter);              // needs a data-scoped token\n  app.post('/api/auth/token', requireAuth({ scope: 'mint' }), …);   // needs the admin token\n  ```\n- `src/auth.ts` is deleted; `server.ts` wires the guard.\n\n**Rules enforced by the guard:**\n\n| Situation | Result |\n|---|---|\n| No token | `401 unauthenticated` |\n| Expired / invalid / wrong issuer | `401 session_expired` (distinct code so the UI can re-mint) |\n| Admin token on a data route | `403 token_not_scoped_for_data` |\n| Merchant token on a mint route | `403 token_not_scoped_for_mint` |\n| Client sends `X-Merchant-Id` ≠ token's | `403 merchant_mismatch` |\n| Client sends `X-Merchant-Id` = token's | allowed (ignored; the token wins) |\n\nThe client-sent merchantId is never *used*, only compared — so the \"token always wins\" rule holds by construction.\n\n### 7. Repository base class — `src/dal/base-repository.ts`\n\n```ts\nabstract class BaseRepository<TRow> {\n  protected abstract readonly table: string;\n  protected abstract readonly merchantColumn: string;  // 'merchant_id'\n  protected scope(): string        // merchantId from the auth context; throws if absent\n  protected select(sql, params)    // injects `AND <merchantColumn> = ?`\n  protected insert(row)            // forces merchantColumn = scope()\n}\n```\n\n- The merchant filter is **not** a parameter a subclass can forget: the base class reads it from `getAuthContext()`.\n- `OrdersRepository` (replaces `ordersDal`) and `MetricsRepository` (replaces the raw SQL in `metrics.ts`, dropping its second read-only connection) extend it. **TD-04 closed.**\n- `getById` becomes merchant-scoped. **TD-02 closed.**\n\n**Enforcement gate:** `test/architecture.test.ts` asserts that **only `src/dal/base-repository.ts` imports `db` from `src/db.ts`** (`src/scripts/*` excluded). A new repository reaching for `db` directly fails the test.\n\n### 8. Dashboard (`public/index.html`, `public/app.js`)\n\n- Cookies travel automatically (same origin); no `X-Merchant-Id` header, no `localStorage`.\n- On load: `GET /api/auth/session`. On selector change: `POST /api/auth/token { merchantId }`, then refresh the data.\n- On `401 session_expired` (merchant token aged out after 10 min): re-mint once with the current selection and retry the request; if that also fails, show \"session expired\".\n- The merchant list comes from a new `GET /api/merchants` (mint-scoped) instead of being hardcoded — small, and it kills TD-14 on the way.\n\n### 9. Commits (in order)\n\n| # | Content | Tech debt |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `jose` + `src/auth/jwt.ts` + `src/scripts/issue-token.ts` + `npm run token` + tests | — |\n| 2 | `src/auth/context.ts` + `guard.ts` + cookies helper + `src/routes/auth.ts` + dev bootstrap + `server.ts` wiring; `src/auth.ts` removed | TD-01 |\n| 3 | `src/dal/base-repository.ts` + `OrdersRepository` + architecture test | TD-02 |\n| 4 | `MetricsRepository`; `metrics.ts` no longer touches `db`/SQLite | TD-04 |\n| 5 | Dashboard: session bootstrap, selector minting, 401 re-mint, `/api/merchants` | TD-01 (UI), TD-14 |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — `jose` as a new prod dependency?** Recommended (zero transitive deps). Alternative: hand-rolled HS256 with `node:crypto`.\n- **Q2 — Dev fallback secret.** Recommended: fixed dev secret + warning when `JWT_SECRET` is missing and `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`; hard failure in production. Alternative: always require `JWT_SECRET`.\n- **Q3 — Admin token is mint-only** (can't read data). Recommended, see §2. Alternative: let it also read data with an explicit `X-Merchant-Id`, which softens the \"token always wins\" rule.\n- **Q4 — TTLs:** admin 8h, merchant 10 min. Say if you want the merchant token shorter (e.g. 2 min) — the dashboard re-mints transparently either way.\n- **Q5 — Expiry handling.** Recommended: `401 session_expired` and the frontend re-mints once, because the server doesn't know which merchant the user is looking at. Alternative: store the last merchantId in the admin cookie so the server can refresh transparently (more state in the cookie).\n\n## Scope\n\n- New: `src/auth/jwt.ts`, `src/auth/context.ts`, `src/auth/guard.ts`, `src/auth/cookies.ts`, `src/auth/dev-session.ts`, `src/routes/auth.ts`, `src/routes/merchants.ts`, `src/dal/base-repository.ts`, `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/dal/metrics-repository.ts`, `src/scripts/issue-token.ts`.\n- Changed: `src/server.ts`, `src/routes/orders.ts`, `src/routes/revenue.ts`, `src/routes/metrics.ts`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`, `package.json`, `test/orders.test.ts`.\n- Removed: `src/auth.ts`, `src/dal/orders-dal.ts`.\n- Tests: `test/auth-jwt.test.ts`, `test/auth-guard.test.ts`, `test/base-repository.test.ts`, `test/architecture.test.ts`, updated `test/orders.test.ts`.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Refund math (TD-05), input validation (TD-10, TD-11), XSS escaping (TD-12) — groups C, D, E.\n- Real login (credentials, user table), token revocation, rotation of the admin token.\n- Rate limiting; CSRF tokens (mitigated by `SameSite=Strict` on state-changing endpoints).\n- `docs/` — authorization to be requested after validation (CLAUDE.md §6): `docs/api.md` (auth endpoints, token types, the production caveat) and `docs/architecture.md` (auth layer + repository base class, closing TD-17).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` → new + existing tests pass.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `npm run check:deps` → no new advisories from `jose`.\n4. `npm run token` → admin token whose claims decode to `role: admin`, `scope: mint`, no `merchantId`.\n5. Guard, by `curl`:\n   - no cookie → `401`;\n   - admin cookie on `/api/orders` → `403 token_not_scoped_for_data`;\n   - merchant cookie → `200` with its own data;\n   - merchant cookie + another merchant's `X-Merchant-Id` → `403 merchant_mismatch`;\n   - merchant token minted with `expiresIn=1s` → `401 session_expired`;\n   - `POST /api/auth/token` without an admin cookie → `401`;\n   - `POST /api/auth/token { merchantId: 'nope' }` → `404 merchant_not_found`.\n6. TD-02: `GET /api/orders/:id` with another merchant's order id → `404`.\n7. TD-04: no `better-sqlite3` import under `src/routes/`; architecture test passes.\n8. Dev bootstrap: with `NODE_ENV=production` and no cookie → `401` (no auto-admin); without it → the dashboard works on first load.\n9. Browser: selector switches between `m_acme` and `m_bistro` (each change mints a new token); after 10 min idle the next action re-mints instead of failing; `document.cookie` exposes neither cookie.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits; `src/auth.ts` and `src/dal/orders-dal.ts` return with them. {"parentUuid":"7cba87e8-5ea3-4a39-8af7-086a1f761196","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CexxhaHs4mXuE3ZsesR2o","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Actualicé el [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md) con tu modelo. Sigue en `draft`.\n\n**Cómo queda:**\n\n| | Token de admin | Token de merchant |\n|---|---|---|\n| Para qué sirve | Emitir tokens | Leer datos de su merchant |\n| Duración | 8 h | 10 min |\n| Cookie | `admin_session`, HttpOnly | `merchant_session`, HttpOnly |\n\n- **Al levantar el servidor** (`npm run dev` o `npm run start`), un middleware inyecta la cookie de admin si no está.\n- **Al cambiar el selector**, el frontend llama a `POST /api/auth/token { merchantId }` y recibe una cookie de merchant nueva.\n- **Cuando el token de merchant caduca**, la API responde `401 session_expired`, el frontend vuelve a emitir uno con la selección actual y reintenta.\n- **El script** ahora solo emite tokens de admin, porque los de merchant salen del endpoint.\n\n**Tres cosas que decidí y conviene que revises:**\n\n- **El token de admin no puede leer datos** (`403 token_not_scoped_for_data`); solo emite. Así se mantiene una única regla: el merchantId siempre viene del token y nunca del cliente. Si el admin pudiera leer datos pasando `X-Merchant-Id`, volveríamos a confiar en el cliente, que es justo TD-01.\n- **La inyección automática de la cookie de admin solo corre fuera de producción,** y el servidor lo avisa en cada arranque. Si eso se desplegara tal cual, cualquier visitante recibiría un token capaz de emitir tokens de cualquier merchant. Queda escrito también en las docs, no solo en el plan.\n- **La lista de merchants pasa a un endpoint** `GET /api/merchants` en vez de estar escrita a mano en el HTML. {"parentUuid":"189defc5-02e0-407f-b2f9-4961ab11059a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CexxsuEgBS2EmZk9TP8af","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_011dSEHVwVBR5ZCw8JFfthVU","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md","content":"# 005 — JWT auth (HttpOnly cookies, admin-minted merchant tokens) + scoped repository base class\n\n**Status:** draft (rev 3 — localhost-based dev gating + `.env` configuration)\n\nCloses Tier 1 groups **A** (TD-02, TD-04) and **B** (TD-01) from [tech_debt.md](../tech_debt.md).\n\n## Context\n\nToday `authMiddleware` trusts an `X-Merchant-Id` header, `ordersDal.getById` ignores the merchant entirely, and `metrics.ts` queries SQLite through its own connection, bypassing the DAL. Any client can read any merchant's data, and a tenancy filter added to the DAL wouldn't cover the metrics endpoints.\n\nThe challenge also requires being able to **look at both seeded merchants** from the dashboard, so the design needs a legitimate way to switch merchants without trusting a client-sent id.\n\n### Token model\n\n- An **admin token** is a *minting* credential. It is injected into an HttpOnly cookie on a local request (dev), and it mints merchant-scoped tokens.\n- Every time the **merchant selector changes**, the frontend asks the auth endpoint for a **new merchant token** for that merchant.\n- Merchant tokens are **short-lived**; the admin token acts like a refresh token.\n\nAll data access therefore goes through a token whose `merchantId` claim is fixed by the backend.\n\n### Security boundary (explicit, because it's the risky part)\n\nAuto-injecting an admin cookie means *whoever gets it can mint any merchant's token*. Acceptable as a local dev convenience, unacceptable when exposed. Therefore the auto-injection is gated on the request being **local**, and the gate does **not** trust the `Host` header:\n\n```ts\nisLocalRequest(req) =\n  isLoopback(req.socket.remoteAddress)        // 127.0.0.1, ::1, ::ffff:127.0.0.1 — from the TCP connection\n  && hostnameOf(req.headers.host) in {localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]}\n```\n\n- The **connection address** is the real gate: a remote attacker sending `Host: localhost` still fails, because their packets don't come from loopback. The host check is a secondary guard for local-but-unexpected origins.\n- `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Forwarded-Host` are deliberately **ignored** (a proxy could forge them).\n- Every server start logs: `⚠ local dev: auto-issuing admin session cookies for loopback requests`.\n- Documented in `docs/`: deploying this behind a proxy that terminates on loopback would reopen TD-01.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 0. Configuration and `.env`\n\nNew module **`src/config/env.ts`** — the single place that reads configuration:\n\n```ts\nloadEnv();                      // process.loadEnvFile('.env') when the file exists (no-op otherwise)\nexport const config = {\n  port, dbPath, jwtSecret,\n  adminTokenTtl, merchantTokenTtl,\n};\n```\n\n- **Loader:** Node's built-in `process.loadEnvFile()` (available in this Node; verified on v24). No `dotenv` dependency — see Q6.\n- **`.env.example`** is committed with every variable documented; **`.env`** is already covered by `.gitignore` and never committed.\n\n| Variable | Default | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `JWT_SECRET` | — | Required. See the rule below. |\n| `PORT` | `3000` | Existing behavior. |\n| `DB_PATH` | `data/dashboard.db` | Existing behavior. |\n| `ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL` | `8h` | |\n| `MERCHANT_TOKEN_TTL` | `10m` | |\n\n**`JWT_SECRET` rule:**\n\n1. If set (env or `.env`) → use it.\n2. If missing and the process is being started for local development → **generate a random secret, write it to `.env`, and warn**. This persists it, so `npm run token` (a separate process) signs with the same secret.\n3. If missing and `.env` can't be written → **fail fast at startup** with a message pointing to `npm run setup:env`.\n\nNew script `\"setup:env\": \"tsx src/scripts/setup-env.ts\"` creates `.env` from `.env.example` with a freshly generated `JWT_SECRET`, and is idempotent (never overwrites an existing value).\n\n### 1. Dependencies\n\n| Choice | Why |\n|---|---|\n| **`jose@^6.2.12`** for JWT (new prod dependency) | MIT, **zero transitive dependencies**, native ESM, typed. `jsonwebtoken@9` pulls 10 packages; hand-rolled HS256 rejected on an auth boundary. |\n| **No `dotenv`** | `process.loadEnvFile()` is built in. |\n| **No cookie library** | `cookie@2` needs Node ≥22 (project declares `>=20`), `cookie-parser` is a dependency for ~15 lines, and the JWT is signed so cookie integrity isn't needed. A small `parseCookies()` helper suffices. |\n\n### 2. Two token types\n\n| | Admin token | Merchant token |\n|---|---|---|\n| Claims | `role: 'admin'`, `scope: 'mint'`, `sub: 'admin'` | `role: 'merchant'`, `scope: 'data'`, `merchantId`, `sub: <merchantId>` |\n| TTL | `ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL` (8h) | `MERCHANT_TOKEN_TTL` (10m) |\n| Cookie | `admin_session` (HttpOnly) | `merchant_session` (HttpOnly) |\n| Can read data? | ❌ `403 token_not_scoped_for_data` | ✅ its own merchant only |\n| Can mint tokens? | ✅ | ❌ |\n\nBoth: HS256, `iss: recruiting-challenge`, `iat`, `exp`.\n\nCookie attributes: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, `Max-Age` = TTL, and `Secure` **unless the request is local** (so `http://localhost` works in dev and anything else gets `Secure`).\n\n**Why the admin token can't read data (Q3):** it keeps one rule for every data query — *the merchantId comes from the token, never from the client*. Otherwise the admin path reintroduces \"trust the client's `X-Merchant-Id`\", which is TD-01.\n\n### 3. Endpoints — `src/routes/auth.ts`\n\n| Endpoint | Auth | Behavior |\n|---|---|---|\n| `POST /api/auth/token` | `admin_session` cookie (or `Authorization: Bearer <admin token>`) | Body `{ merchantId }`. Verifies the merchant exists, mints a short-lived merchant token, replies `204` + `Set-Cookie: merchant_session`. Called on every selector change. |\n| `GET /api/auth/session` | any cookie | `{ role, merchantId, expiresAt }` so the UI knows what to render. |\n| `DELETE /api/auth/session` | — | Clears both cookies. |\n| `POST /api/auth/admin-session` | — | Exchanges an admin token (body `{ token }`, from `npm run token`) for the `admin_session` cookie. The non-local way in. |\n\n### 4. Dev bootstrap\n\nMiddleware `devAdminSession`: when `isLocalRequest(req)` and there's no `admin_session` cookie, mint one and set it on the response. Non-local requests are untouched and hit the normal `401`.\n\n### 5. Script — `src/scripts/issue-token.ts`\n\nMints **admin** tokens (merchant tokens come from the endpoint):\n\n```sh\nnpm run token                 # admin token, ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL\nnpm run token -- expiresIn=30m\n```\n\nPrints the token plus a `curl` example for `POST /api/auth/admin-session`. `package.json`: `\"token\": \"tsx src/scripts/issue-token.ts\"`.\n\n### 6. Auth layer\n\n```\nmerchant_session cookie ──▶ verifyToken ──▶ AuthContext (AsyncLocalStorage) ──▶ guard ──▶ route ──▶ repository\n```\n\n- **`src/auth/jwt.ts`** — `signToken(claims, expiresIn)` / `verifyToken(token)` (jose, HS256, issuer + scope checks).\n- **`src/auth/context.ts`** — `AsyncLocalStorage<AuthContext>` with `runWithAuthContext(ctx, fn)` and `getAuthContext()`. This is what makes the layer **injectable in any class or method** without threading parameters; it **throws** when there's no context (fail closed).\n- **`src/auth/local.ts`** — `isLocalRequest(req)` as defined above; used by the dev bootstrap and by the cookie's `Secure` flag.\n- **`src/auth/guard.ts`** — `requireAuth({ scope })`, usable per-router or per-route:\n  ```ts\n  app.use('/api/orders', requireAuth(), ordersRouter);              // data-scoped token\n  app.post('/api/auth/token', requireAuth({ scope: 'mint' }), …);   // admin token\n  ```\n- `src/auth.ts` is deleted; `server.ts` wires the guard.\n\n**Rules enforced by the guard:**\n\n| Situation | Result |\n|---|---|\n| No token | `401 unauthenticated` |\n| Expired / invalid / wrong issuer | `401 session_expired` |\n| Admin token on a data route | `403 token_not_scoped_for_data` |\n| Merchant token on a mint route | `403 token_not_scoped_for_mint` |\n| Client sends `X-Merchant-Id` ≠ token's | `403 merchant_mismatch` |\n| Client sends `X-Merchant-Id` = token's | allowed (ignored; the token wins) |\n\nThe client-sent merchantId is never *used*, only compared.\n\n### 7. Repository base class — `src/dal/base-repository.ts`\n\n```ts\nabstract class BaseRepository<TRow> {\n  protected abstract readonly table: string;\n  protected abstract readonly merchantColumn: string;  // 'merchant_id'\n  protected scope(): string        // merchantId from the auth context; throws if absent\n  protected select(sql, params)    // injects `AND <merchantColumn> = ?`\n  protected insert(row)            // forces merchantColumn = scope()\n}\n```\n\n- The merchant filter is **not** a parameter a subclass can forget: the base class reads it from `getAuthContext()`.\n- `OrdersRepository` (replaces `ordersDal`) and `MetricsRepository` (replaces the raw SQL in `metrics.ts`, dropping its second read-only connection) extend it. **TD-04 closed.**\n- `getById` becomes merchant-scoped. **TD-02 closed.**\n\n**Enforcement gate:** `test/architecture.test.ts` asserts that **only `src/dal/base-repository.ts` imports `db` from `src/db.ts`** (`src/scripts/*` excluded), so a new repository that reaches for `db` fails the suite.\n\n### 8. Dashboard (`public/index.html`, `public/app.js`)\n\n- Cookies travel automatically (same origin); no `X-Merchant-Id` header, no `localStorage`.\n- On load: `GET /api/auth/session`. On selector change: `POST /api/auth/token { merchantId }`, then reload the data.\n- On `401 session_expired`: re-mint once with the current selection and retry; if it fails again, show \"session expired\".\n- The merchant list comes from a new `GET /api/merchants` (mint-scoped) instead of being hardcoded — closes TD-14 on the way.\n\n### 9. Commits (in order)\n\n| # | Content | Tech debt |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `src/config/env.ts`, `.env.example`, `setup:env`, `.gitignore` check | — |\n| 2 | `jose` + `src/auth/jwt.ts` + `src/scripts/issue-token.ts` + `npm run token` + tests | — |\n| 3 | `context.ts` + `local.ts` + `guard.ts` + cookies helper + `src/routes/auth.ts` + dev bootstrap + `server.ts` wiring; `src/auth.ts` removed | TD-01 |\n| 4 | `base-repository.ts` + `OrdersRepository` + architecture test | TD-02 |\n| 5 | `MetricsRepository`; `metrics.ts` no longer touches `db`/SQLite | TD-04 |\n| 6 | Dashboard: session bootstrap, selector minting, 401 re-mint, `/api/merchants` | TD-01 (UI), TD-14 |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — `jose` as a new prod dependency?** Recommended (zero transitive deps). Alternative: hand-rolled HS256 with `node:crypto`.\n- **Q3 — Admin token is mint-only** (can't read data). Recommended, see §2.\n- **Q4 — TTLs:** admin 8h, merchant 10m, both configurable in `.env`.\n- **Q5 — Expiry handling.** Recommended: `401 session_expired` + frontend re-mints once. Alternative: keep the last merchantId in the admin cookie for a transparent server-side refresh.\n- **Q6 — `.env` loader.** Recommended: Node's built-in `process.loadEnvFile()` (zero dependencies; confirmed available on Node 24 here). Alternative: the `dotenv@17` package, if you prefer the conventional setup — it's one more prod dependency for the same result.\n- **Q7 — Auto-generating `JWT_SECRET` into `.env` on first local start.** Recommended (dev never has to think about it, and the CLI shares the secret). Alternative: always fail with \"run `npm run setup:env`\".\n\n*(Q2 from rev 2 is folded into §0.)*\n\n## Scope\n\n- New: `src/config/env.ts`, `src/auth/jwt.ts`, `src/auth/context.ts`, `src/auth/guard.ts`, `src/auth/cookies.ts`, `src/auth/local.ts`, `src/auth/dev-session.ts`, `src/routes/auth.ts`, `src/routes/merchants.ts`, `src/dal/base-repository.ts`, `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/dal/metrics-repository.ts`, `src/scripts/issue-token.ts`, `src/scripts/setup-env.ts`, `.env.example`.\n- Changed: `src/server.ts`, `src/db.ts` (reads `config`), `src/routes/orders.ts`, `src/routes/revenue.ts`, `src/routes/metrics.ts`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`, `package.json`, `test/orders.test.ts`.\n- Removed: `src/auth.ts`, `src/dal/orders-dal.ts`.\n- Tests: `test/env.test.ts`, `test/auth-jwt.test.ts`, `test/auth-guard.test.ts`, `test/auth-local.test.ts`, `test/base-repository.test.ts`, `test/architecture.test.ts`, updated `test/orders.test.ts`.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Refund math (TD-05), input validation (TD-10, TD-11), XSS escaping (TD-12) — groups C, D, E.\n- Real login (credentials, user table), token revocation, admin-token rotation.\n- Rate limiting; CSRF tokens (mitigated by `SameSite=Strict`).\n- `docs/` — authorization to be requested after validation (CLAUDE.md §6): `docs/api.md` (auth endpoints, token types, the local-only caveat), `docs/architecture.md` (auth layer + repository base class, closing TD-17), and a `.env` section in the README setup (needs your explicit go, README is not normally touched).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` → new + existing tests pass.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `npm run check:deps` → no new advisories from `jose`.\n4. `.env`: with no `.env`, a local start creates it with a random `JWT_SECRET` and warns; re-running doesn't overwrite it; `npm run token` signs with the same secret (the token verifies against the running server).\n5. `npm run token` → claims decode to `role: admin`, `scope: mint`, no `merchantId`.\n6. Guard, by `curl`:\n   - no cookie → `401`;\n   - admin cookie on `/api/orders` → `403 token_not_scoped_for_data`;\n   - merchant cookie → `200` with its own data;\n   - merchant cookie + another merchant's `X-Merchant-Id` → `403 merchant_mismatch`;\n   - merchant token with `expiresIn=1s` → `401 session_expired`;\n   - `POST /api/auth/token` without an admin cookie → `401`;\n   - `POST /api/auth/token { merchantId: 'nope' }` → `404 merchant_not_found`.\n7. TD-02: `GET /api/orders/:id` with another merchant's order id → `404`.\n8. TD-04: no `better-sqlite3` import under `src/routes/`; architecture test passes.\n9. Local gating: request to `http://localhost:3000/` gets the admin cookie; the same request from a non-loopback address (or with `Host: localhost` spoofed from another machine, simulated in a unit test of `isLocalRequest`) does **not**.\n10. Browser: the selector switches between `m_acme` and `m_bistro` (each change mints a token); after the merchant token expires the next action re-mints instead of failing; `document.cookie` exposes neither cookie.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits; `src/auth.ts` and `src/dal/orders-dal.ts` return with them. Delete `.env` if it was generated. No database migration involved.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1992,"cache_read_input_tokens":267607,"output_tokens":6724,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":304},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1992,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":6724,"cache_read_input_tokens":267607,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1992,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1992},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_011dSEHVwVBR5ZCw8JFfthVU":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md","content":"# 005 — JWT auth (HttpOnly cookies, admin-minted merchant tokens) + scoped repository base class\n\n**Status:** draft (rev 3 — localhost-based dev gating + `.env` configuration)\n\nCloses Tier 1 groups **A** (TD-02, TD-04) and **B** (TD-01) from [tech_debt.md](../tech_debt.md).\n\n## Context\n\nToday `authMiddleware` trusts an `X-Merchant-Id` header, `ordersDal.getById` ignores the merchant entirely, and `metrics.ts` queries SQLite through its own connection, bypassing the DAL. Any client can read any merchant's data, and a tenancy filter added to the DAL wouldn't cover the metrics endpoints.\n\nThe challenge also requires being able to **look at both seeded merchants** from the dashboard, so the design needs a legitimate way to switch merchants without trusting a client-sent id.\n\n### Token model\n\n- An **admin token** is a *minting* credential. It is injected into an HttpOnly cookie on a local request (dev), and it mints merchant-scoped tokens.\n- Every time the **merchant selector changes**, the frontend asks the auth endpoint for a **new merchant token** for that merchant.\n- Merchant tokens are **short-lived**; the admin token acts like a refresh token.\n\nAll data access therefore goes through a token whose `merchantId` claim is fixed by the backend.\n\n### Security boundary (explicit, because it's the risky part)\n\nAuto-injecting an admin cookie means *whoever gets it can mint any merchant's token*. Acceptable as a local dev convenience, unacceptable when exposed. Therefore the auto-injection is gated on the request being **local**, and the gate does **not** trust the `Host` header:\n\n```ts\nisLocalRequest(req) =\n  isLoopback(req.socket.remoteAddress)        // 127.0.0.1, ::1, ::ffff:127.0.0.1 — from the TCP connection\n  && hostnameOf(req.headers.host) in {localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]}\n```\n\n- The **connection address** is the real gate: a remote attacker sending `Host: localhost` still fails, because their packets don't come from loopback. The host check is a secondary guard for local-but-unexpected origins.\n- `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Forwarded-Host` are deliberately **ignored** (a proxy could forge them).\n- Every server start logs: `⚠ local dev: auto-issuing admin session cookies for loopback requests`.\n- Documented in `docs/`: deploying this behind a proxy that terminates on loopback would reopen TD-01.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 0. Configuration and `.env`\n\nNew module **`src/config/env.ts`** — the single place that reads configuration:\n\n```ts\nloadEnv();                      // process.loadEnvFile('.env') when the file exists (no-op otherwise)\nexport const config = {\n  port, dbPath, jwtSecret,\n  adminTokenTtl, merchantTokenTtl,\n};\n```\n\n- **Loader:** Node's built-in `process.loadEnvFile()` (available in this Node; verified on v24). No `dotenv` dependency — see Q6.\n- **`.env.example`** is committed with every variable documented; **`.env`** is already covered by `.gitignore` and never committed.\n\n| Variable | Default | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `JWT_SECRET` | — | Required. See the rule below. |\n| `PORT` | `3000` | Existing behavior. |\n| `DB_PATH` | `data/dashboard.db` | Existing behavior. |\n| `ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL` | `8h` | |\n| `MERCHANT_TOKEN_TTL` | `10m` | |\n\n**`JWT_SECRET` rule:**\n\n1. If set (env or `.env`) → use it.\n2. If missing and the process is being started for local development → **generate a random secret, write it to `.env`, and warn**. This persists it, so `npm run token` (a separate process) signs with the same secret.\n3. If missing and `.env` can't be written → **fail fast at startup** with a message pointing to `npm run setup:env`.\n\nNew script `\"setup:env\": \"tsx src/scripts/setup-env.ts\"` creates `.env` from `.env.example` with a freshly generated `JWT_SECRET`, and is idempotent (never overwrites an existing value).\n\n### 1. Dependencies\n\n| Choice | Why |\n|---|---|\n| **`jose@^6.2.12`** for JWT (new prod dependency) | MIT, **zero transitive dependencies**, native ESM, typed. `jsonwebtoken@9` pulls 10 packages; hand-rolled HS256 rejected on an auth boundary. |\n| **No `dotenv`** | `process.loadEnvFile()` is built in. |\n| **No cookie library** | `cookie@2` needs Node ≥22 (project declares `>=20`), `cookie-parser` is a dependency for ~15 lines, and the JWT is signed so cookie integrity isn't needed. A small `parseCookies()` helper suffices. |\n\n### 2. Two token types\n\n| | Admin token | Merchant token |\n|---|---|---|\n| Claims | `role: 'admin'`, `scope: 'mint'`, `sub: 'admin'` | `role: 'merchant'`, `scope: 'data'`, `merchantId`, `sub: <merchantId>` |\n| TTL | `ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL` (8h) | `MERCHANT_TOKEN_TTL` (10m) |\n| Cookie | `admin_session` (HttpOnly) | `merchant_session` (HttpOnly) |\n| Can read data? | ❌ `403 token_not_scoped_for_data` | ✅ its own merchant only |\n| Can mint tokens? | ✅ | ❌ |\n\nBoth: HS256, `iss: recruiting-challenge`, `iat`, `exp`.\n\nCookie attributes: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, `Max-Age` = TTL, and `Secure` **unless the request is local** (so `http://localhost` works in dev and anything else gets `Secure`).\n\n**Why the admin token can't read data (Q3):** it keeps one rule for every data query — *the merchantId comes from the token, never from the client*. Otherwise the admin path reintroduces \"trust the client's `X-Merchant-Id`\", which is TD-01.\n\n### 3. Endpoints — `src/routes/auth.ts`\n\n| Endpoint | Auth | Behavior |\n|---|---|---|\n| `POST /api/auth/token` | `admin_session` cookie (or `Authorization: Bearer <admin token>`) | Body `{ merchantId }`. Verifies the merchant exists, mints a short-lived merchant token, replies `204` + `Set-Cookie: merchant_session`. Called on every selector change. |\n| `GET /api/auth/session` | any cookie | `{ role, merchantId, expiresAt }` so the UI knows what to render. |\n| `DELETE /api/auth/session` | — | Clears both cookies. |\n| `POST /api/auth/admin-session` | — | Exchanges an admin token (body `{ token }`, from `npm run token`) for the `admin_session` cookie. The non-local way in. |\n\n### 4. Dev bootstrap\n\nMiddleware `devAdminSession`: when `isLocalRequest(req)` and there's no `admin_session` cookie, mint one and set it on the response. Non-local requests are untouched and hit the normal `401`.\n\n### 5. Script — `src/scripts/issue-token.ts`\n\nMints **admin** tokens (merchant tokens come from the endpoint):\n\n```sh\nnpm run token                 # admin token, ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL\nnpm run token -- expiresIn=30m\n```\n\nPrints the token plus a `curl` example for `POST /api/auth/admin-session`. `package.json`: `\"token\": \"tsx src/scripts/issue-token.ts\"`.\n\n### 6. Auth layer\n\n```\nmerchant_session cookie ──▶ verifyToken ──▶ AuthContext (AsyncLocalStorage) ──▶ guard ──▶ route ──▶ repository\n```\n\n- **`src/auth/jwt.ts`** — `signToken(claims, expiresIn)` / `verifyToken(token)` (jose, HS256, issuer + scope checks).\n- **`src/auth/context.ts`** — `AsyncLocalStorage<AuthContext>` with `runWithAuthContext(ctx, fn)` and `getAuthContext()`. This is what makes the layer **injectable in any class or method** without threading parameters; it **throws** when there's no context (fail closed).\n- **`src/auth/local.ts`** — `isLocalRequest(req)` as defined above; used by the dev bootstrap and by the cookie's `Secure` flag.\n- **`src/auth/guard.ts`** — `requireAuth({ scope })`, usable per-router or per-route:\n  ```ts\n  app.use('/api/orders', requireAuth(), ordersRouter);              // data-scoped token\n  app.post('/api/auth/token', requireAuth({ scope: 'mint' }), …);   // admin token\n  ```\n- `src/auth.ts` is deleted; `server.ts` wires the guard.\n\n**Rules enforced by the guard:**\n\n| Situation | Result |\n|---|---|\n| No token | `401 unauthenticated` |\n| Expired / invalid / wrong issuer | `401 session_expired` |\n| Admin token on a data route | `403 token_not_scoped_for_data` |\n| Merchant token on a mint route | `403 token_not_scoped_for_mint` |\n| Client sends `X-Merchant-Id` ≠ token's | `403 merchant_mismatch` |\n| Client sends `X-Merchant-Id` = token's | allowed (ignored; the token wins) |\n\nThe client-sent merchantId is never *used*, only compared.\n\n### 7. Repository base class — `src/dal/base-repository.ts`\n\n```ts\nabstract class BaseRepository<TRow> {\n  protected abstract readonly table: string;\n  protected abstract readonly merchantColumn: string;  // 'merchant_id'\n  protected scope(): string        // merchantId from the auth context; throws if absent\n  protected select(sql, params)    // injects `AND <merchantColumn> = ?`\n  protected insert(row)            // forces merchantColumn = scope()\n}\n```\n\n- The merchant filter is **not** a parameter a subclass can forget: the base class reads it from `getAuthContext()`.\n- `OrdersRepository` (replaces `ordersDal`) and `MetricsRepository` (replaces the raw SQL in `metrics.ts`, dropping its second read-only connection) extend it. **TD-04 closed.**\n- `getById` becomes merchant-scoped. **TD-02 closed.**\n\n**Enforcement gate:** `test/architecture.test.ts` asserts that **only `src/dal/base-repository.ts` imports `db` from `src/db.ts`** (`src/scripts/*` excluded), so a new repository that reaches for `db` fails the suite.\n\n### 8. Dashboard (`public/index.html`, `public/app.js`)\n\n- Cookies travel automatically (same origin); no `X-Merchant-Id` header, no `localStorage`.\n- On load: `GET /api/auth/session`. On selector change: `POST /api/auth/token { merchantId }`, then reload the data.\n- On `401 session_expired`: re-mint once with the current selection and retry; if it fails again, show \"session expired\".\n- The merchant list comes from a new `GET /api/merchants` (mint-scoped) instead of being hardcoded — closes TD-14 on the way.\n\n### 9. Commits (in order)\n\n| # | Content | Tech debt |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `src/config/env.ts`, `.env.example`, `setup:env`, `.gitignore` check | — |\n| 2 | `jose` + `src/auth/jwt.ts` + `src/scripts/issue-token.ts` + `npm run token` + tests | — |\n| 3 | `context.ts` + `local.ts` + `guard.ts` + cookies helper + `src/routes/auth.ts` + dev bootstrap + `server.ts` wiring; `src/auth.ts` removed | TD-01 |\n| 4 | `base-repository.ts` + `OrdersRepository` + architecture test | TD-02 |\n| 5 | `MetricsRepository`; `metrics.ts` no longer touches `db`/SQLite | TD-04 |\n| 6 | Dashboard: session bootstrap, selector minting, 401 re-mint, `/api/merchants` | TD-01 (UI), TD-14 |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — `jose` as a new prod dependency?** Recommended (zero transitive deps). Alternative: hand-rolled HS256 with `node:crypto`.\n- **Q3 — Admin token is mint-only** (can't read data). Recommended, see §2.\n- **Q4 — TTLs:** admin 8h, merchant 10m, both configurable in `.env`.\n- **Q5 — Expiry handling.** Recommended: `401 session_expired` + frontend re-mints once. Alternative: keep the last merchantId in the admin cookie for a transparent server-side refresh.\n- **Q6 — `.env` loader.** Recommended: Node's built-in `process.loadEnvFile()` (zero dependencies; confirmed available on Node 24 here). Alternative: the `dotenv@17` package, if you prefer the conventional setup — it's one more prod dependency for the same result.\n- **Q7 — Auto-generating `JWT_SECRET` into `.env` on first local start.** Recommended (dev never has to think about it, and the CLI shares the secret). Alternative: always fail with \"run `npm run setup:env`\".\n\n*(Q2 from rev 2 is folded into §0.)*\n\n## Scope\n\n- New: `src/config/env.ts`, `src/auth/jwt.ts`, `src/auth/context.ts`, `src/auth/guard.ts`, `src/auth/cookies.ts`, `src/auth/local.ts`, `src/auth/dev-session.ts`, `src/routes/auth.ts`, `src/routes/merchants.ts`, `src/dal/base-repository.ts`, `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/dal/metrics-repository.ts`, `src/scripts/issue-token.ts`, `src/scripts/setup-env.ts`, `.env.example`.\n- Changed: `src/server.ts`, `src/db.ts` (reads `config`), `src/routes/orders.ts`, `src/routes/revenue.ts`, `src/routes/metrics.ts`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`, `package.json`, `test/orders.test.ts`.\n- Removed: `src/auth.ts`, `src/dal/orders-dal.ts`.\n- Tests: `test/env.test.ts`, `test/auth-jwt.test.ts`, `test/auth-guard.test.ts`, `test/auth-local.test.ts`, `test/base-repository.test.ts`, `test/architecture.test.ts`, updated `test/orders.test.ts`.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Refund math (TD-05), input validation (TD-10, TD-11), XSS escaping (TD-12) — groups C, D, E.\n- Real login (credentials, user table), token revocation, admin-token rotation.\n- Rate limiting; CSRF tokens (mitigated by `SameSite=Strict`).\n- `docs/` — authorization to be requested after validation (CLAUDE.md §6): `docs/api.md` (auth endpoints, token types, the local-only caveat), `docs/architecture.md` (auth layer + repository base class, closing TD-17), and a `.env` section in the README setup (needs your explicit go, README is not normally touched).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` → new + existing tests pass.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `npm run check:deps` → no new advisories from `jose`.\n4. `.env`: with no `.env`, a local start creates it with a random `JWT_SECRET` and warns; re-running doesn't overwrite it; `npm run token` signs with the same secret (the token verifies against the running server).\n5. `npm run token` → claims decode to `role: admin`, `scope: mint`, no `merchantId`.\n6. Guard, by `curl`:\n   - no cookie → `401`;\n   - admin cookie on `/api/orders` → `403 token_not_scoped_for_data`;\n   - merchant cookie → `200` with its own data;\n   - merchant cookie + another merchant's `X-Merchant-Id` → `403 merchant_mismatch`;\n   - merchant token with `expiresIn=1s` → `401 session_expired`;\n   - `POST /api/auth/token` without an admin cookie → `401`;\n   - `POST /api/auth/token { merchantId: 'nope' }` → `404 merchant_not_found`.\n7. TD-02: `GET /api/orders/:id` with another merchant's order id → `404`.\n8. TD-04: no `better-sqlite3` import under `src/routes/`; architecture test passes.\n9. Local gating: request to `http://localhost:3000/` gets the admin cookie; the same request from a non-loopback address (or with `Host: localhost` spoofed from another machine, simulated in a unit test of `isLocalRequest`) does **not**.\n10. Browser: the selector switches between `m_acme` and `m_bistro` (each change mints a token); after the merchant token expires the next action re-mints instead of failing; `document.cookie` exposes neither cookie.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits; `src/auth.ts` and `src/dal/orders-dal.ts` return with them. Delete `.env` if it was generated.
