Repository base class — `src/dal/base-repository.ts`\n\n```ts\nabstract class BaseRepository<TRow> {\n  protected abstract readonly table: string;\n  protected abstract readonly merchantColumn: string;  // 'merchant_id'\n  protected scope(): string        // merchantId from the auth context; throws if absent\n  protected select(sql, params)    // injects `AND <merchantColumn> = ?`\n  protected insert(row)            // forces merchantColumn = scope()\n}\n```\n\n- The merchant filter is **not** a parameter a subclass can forget: the base class reads it from `getAuthContext()`.\n- `OrdersRepository` (replaces `ordersDal`) and `MetricsRepository` (replaces the raw SQL in `metrics.ts`, dropping its second read-only connection) extend it. **TD-04 closed.**\n- `getById` becomes merchant-scoped. **TD-02 closed.**\n\n**Enforcement gate:** `test/architecture.test.ts` asserts that **only `src/dal/base-repository.ts` imports `db` from `src/db.ts`** (`src/scripts/*` excluded), so a new repository that reaches for `db` fails the suite.\n\n### 8. Dashboard (`public/index.html`, `public/app.js`)\n\n- Cookies travel automatically (same origin); no `X-Merchant-Id` header, no `localStorage`.\n- On load: `GET /api/auth/session`. On selector change: `POST /api/auth/token { merchantId }`, then reload the data.\n- On `401 session_expired`: re-mint once with the current selection and retry; if it fails again, show \"session expired\".\n- The merchant list comes from a new `GET /api/merchants` (mint-scoped) instead of being hardcoded — closes TD-14 on the way.\n\n### 9. Commits (in order)\n\n| # | Content | Tech debt |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `src/config/env.ts`, `.env.example`, `setup:env`, `.gitignore` check | — |\n| 2 | `jose` + `src/auth/jwt.ts` + `src/scripts/issue-token.ts` + `npm run token` + tests | — |\n| 3 | `context.ts` + `local.ts` + `guard.ts` + cookies helper + `src/routes/auth.ts` + dev bootstrap + `server.ts` wiring; `src/auth.ts` removed | TD-01 |\n| 4 | `base-repository.ts` + `OrdersRepository` + architecture test | TD-02 |\n| 5 | `MetricsRepository`; `metrics.ts` no longer touches `db`/SQLite | TD-04 |\n| 6 | Dashboard: session bootstrap, selector minting, 401 re-mint, `/api/merchants` | TD-01 (UI), TD-14 |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — `jose` as a new prod dependency?** Recommended (zero transitive deps). Alternative: hand-rolled HS256 with `node:crypto`.\n- **Q3 — Admin token is mint-only** (can't read data). Recommended, see §2.\n- **Q4 — TTLs:** admin 8h, merchant 10m, both configurable in `.env`.\n- **Q5 — Expiry handling.** Recommended: `401 session_expired` + frontend re-mints once. Alternative: keep the last merchantId in the admin cookie for a transparent server-side refresh.\n- **Q6 — `.env` loader.** Recommended: Node's built-in `process.loadEnvFile()` (zero dependencies; confirmed available on Node 24 here). Alternative: the `dotenv@17` package, if you prefer the conventional setup — it's one more prod dependency for the same result.\n- **Q7 — Auto-generating `JWT_SECRET` into `.env` on first local start.** Recommended (dev never has to think about it, and the CLI shares the secret). Alternative: always fail with \"run `npm run setup:env`\".\n\n*(Q2 from rev 2 is folded into §0.)*\n\n## Scope\n\n- New: `src/config/env.ts`, `src/auth/jwt.ts`, `src/auth/context.ts`, `src/auth/guard.ts`, `src/auth/cookies.ts`, `src/auth/local.ts`, `src/auth/dev-session.ts`, `src/routes/auth.ts`, `src/routes/merchants.ts`, `src/dal/base-repository.ts`, `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/dal/metrics-repository.ts`, `src/scripts/issue-token.ts`, `src/scripts/setup-env.ts`, `.env.example`.\n- Changed: `src/server.ts`, `src/db.ts` (reads `config`), `src/routes/orders.ts`, `src/routes/revenue.ts`, `src/routes/metrics.ts`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`, `package.json`, `test/orders.test.ts`.\n- Removed: `src/auth.ts`, `src/dal/orders-dal.ts`.\n- Tests: `test/env.test.ts`, `test/auth-jwt.test.ts`, `test/auth-guard.test.ts`, `test/auth-local.test.ts`, `test/base-repository.test.ts`, `test/architecture.test.ts`, updated `test/orders.test.ts`.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Refund math (TD-05), input validation (TD-10, TD-11), XSS escaping (TD-12) — groups C, D, E.\n- Real login (credentials, user table), token revocation, admin-token rotation.\n- Rate limiting; CSRF tokens (mitigated by `SameSite=Strict`).\n- `docs/` — authorization to be requested after validation (CLAUDE.md §6): `docs/api.md` (auth endpoints, token types, the local-only caveat), `docs/architecture.md` (auth layer + repository base class, closing TD-17), and a `.env` section in the README setup (needs your explicit go, README is not normally touched).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` → new + existing tests pass.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `npm run check:deps` → no new advisories from `jose`.\n4. `.env`: with no `.env`, a local start creates it with a random `JWT_SECRET` and warns; re-running doesn't overwrite it; `npm run token` signs with the same secret (the token verifies against the running server).\n5. `npm run token` → claims decode to `role: admin`, `scope: mint`, no `merchantId`.\n6. Guard, by `curl`:\n   - no cookie → `401`;\n   - admin cookie on `/api/orders` → `403 token_not_scoped_for_data`;\n   - merchant cookie → `200` with its own data;\n   - merchant cookie + another merchant's `X-Merchant-Id` → `403 merchant_mismatch`;\n   - merchant token with `expiresIn=1s` → `401 session_expired`;\n   - `POST /api/auth/token` without an admin cookie → `401`;\n   - `POST /api/auth/token { merchantId: 'nope' }` → `404 merchant_not_found`.\n7. TD-02: `GET /api/orders/:id` with another merchant's order id → `404`.\n8. TD-04: no `better-sqlite3` import under `src/routes/`; architecture test passes.\n9. Local gating: request to `http://localhost:3000/` gets the admin cookie; the same request from a non-loopback address (or with `Host: localhost` spoofed from another machine, simulated in a unit test of `isLocalRequest`) does **not**.\n10. Browser: the selector switches between `m_acme` and `m_bistro` (each change mints a token); after the merchant token expires the next action re-mints instead of failing; `document.cookie` exposes neither cookie.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits; `src/auth.ts` and `src/dal/orders-dal.ts` return with them. Delete `.env` if it was generated. {"parentUuid":"b0ed0c99-2b30-4f96-b67f-d5d6a5832062","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cexy3g99Vvxm5YxL262Wq","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01YRf3bCLPVBdfr8jMD4QVXv","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\src\\auth\\jwt.ts","content":"/**\n * Signing and verification of session tokens (HS256 JWT, via `jose`).\n *\n * Two kinds of token exist:\n * - **admin** (`scope: 'mint'`): may mint merchant tokens, may not read data.\n * - **merchant** (`scope: 'data'`): may read only its own merchant's data.\n *\n * @see plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md\n */\nimport { SignJWT, jwtVerify } from 'jose';\nimport { getConfig, getJwtSecret } from '../config/env.js';\n\n/** Issuer claim of every token this app produces. */\nexport const TOKEN_ISSUER = 'recruiting-challenge';\n\n/** Role of the caller. */\nexport type Role = 'merchant' | 'admin';\n\n/** What a token is allowed to do. */\nexport type TokenScope = 'data' | 'mint';\n\n/** Claims carried by a session token. */\nexport interface TokenClaims {\n  role: Role;\n  scope: TokenScope;\n  /** Present only on merchant tokens. */\n  merchantId?: string;\n}\n\n/** A verified token: its claims plus its expiry. */\nexport interface VerifiedToken extends TokenClaims {\n  expiresAt: Date;\n}\n\n/** A freshly signed token. */\nexport interface IssuedToken extends VerifiedToken {\n  token: string;\n}\n\n/** Raised when a token is missing, malformed, expired or signed with another key. */\nexport class InvalidTokenError extends Error {\n  constructor(message = 'invalid token') {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = 'InvalidTokenError';\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Signs a token.\n *\n * @param claims - Claims to embed.\n * @param expiresIn - Lifetime in `jose` notation, e.g. `10m`, `8h`.\n */\nexport async function signToken(claims: TokenClaims, expiresIn: string): Promise<string> {\n  const payload: Record<string, unknown> = { role: claims.role, scope: claims.scope };\n  if (claims.merchantId) payload.merchantId = claims.merchantId;\n\n  return new SignJWT(payload)\n    .setProtectedHeader({ alg: 'HS256' })\n    .setIssuer(TOKEN_ISSUER)\n    .setSubject(claims.merchantId ?? 'admin')\n    .setIssuedAt()\n    .setExpirationTime(expiresIn)\n    .sign(secretKey());\n}\n\n/**\n * Verifies a token's signature, issuer, algorithm, expiry and claim shape.\n *\n * @param token - Encoded JWT.\n * @throws InvalidTokenError when the token can't be trusted.\n */\nexport async function verifyToken(token: string): Promise<VerifiedToken> {\n  let payload;\n  try {\n    ({ payload } = await jwtVerify(token, secretKey(), {\n      issuer: TOKEN_ISSUER,\n      algorithms: ['HS256'],\n    }));\n  } catch (error) {\n    throw new InvalidTokenError(error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'invalid token');\n  }\n\n  const role = payload.role;\n  const scope = payload.scope;\n  const merchantId = payload.merchantId;\n\n  if (role !== 'merchant' && role !== 'admin') throw new InvalidTokenError('unknown role claim');\n  if (scope !== 'data' && scope !== 'mint') throw new InvalidTokenError('unknown scope claim');\n  if (role === 'merchant' && typeof merchantId !== 'string') {\n    throw new InvalidTokenError('merchant token without merchantId');\n  }\n  if (typeof payload.exp !== 'number') throw new InvalidTokenError('token without expiry');\n\n  return {\n    role,\n    scope,\n    ...(typeof merchantId === 'string' ? { merchantId } : {}),\n    expiresAt: new Date(payload.exp * 1000),\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Issues an admin (mint-scoped) token.\n *\n * @param expiresIn - ');\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":16807,"cache_read_input_tokens":277251,"output_tokens":8841,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1416},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":16807,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":8841,"cache_read_input_tokens":277251,"cache_creation_input_tokens":16807,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":16807},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01JxZ99YiA8UkgQiE7AFReo9":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\src\\auth\\dev-session.ts","content":"/**\n * Local development bootstrap: hands an admin session cookie to local requests.\n *\n * This exists so `npm run dev` works without a manual login step. {"parentUuid":"48f902cd-4138-47a6-a0dc-3cfe5ded5236","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CexyGFzwgFKMwWT3N1w7u","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_018MVu2SwG9BcxwgctokiaJm","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\src\\dal\\base-repository.ts","content":"/**\n * Repository base classes — the only place in the application that touches the database.\n *\n * `BaseRepository` applies the merchant scope itself, reading it from the request's\n * {@link getAuthContext}. Subclasses cannot opt out: they never see the raw connection and\n * never pass the merchant id in, so \"the repository forgot the tenancy filter\" stops being a\n * possible bug. `AdminRepository` covers the few tables that are not merchant-scoped and\n * requires an admin (mint-scoped) caller instead.\n *\n * `test/architecture.test.ts` enforces that no other module imports the database handle.\n *\n * @see plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md\n */\nimport { getAuthContext } from '../auth/context.js';\nimport { db } from '../db.js';\n\n/** Raised when the current caller isn't allowed to run a repository query. */\nexport class ScopeError extends Error {\n  constructor(message: string) {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = 'ScopeError';\n  }\n}\n\n/** Optional fragments appended to a generated query. */\nexport interface QueryOptions {\n  /** Extra condition, ANDed with the scope filter. */\n  where?: string;\n  /** Trailing clauses, e.g. `GROUP BY … ORDER BY … LIMIT ?`. */\n  tail?: string;\n  /** Parameters for `where` first, then `tail`. */\n  params?: unknown[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Base class for every merchant-scoped entity.\n */\nexport abstract class BaseRepository<TRow> {\n  /** Table backing this repository. */\n  protected abstract readonly table: string;\n\n  /** Column holding the merchant id. */\n  protected readonly merchantColumn: string = 'merchant_id';\n\n  /**\n   * Merchant id of the current caller.\n   *\n   * @throws ScopeError when the caller has no merchant scope (e.g. an admin token).\n   */\n  protected scope(): string {\n    const context = getAuthContext();\n    if (!context.merchantId) {\n      throw new ScopeError(`${context.role} caller has no merchant scope for ${this.table}`);\n    }\n    return context.merchantId;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Runs a scoped `SELECT`. The merchant filter is always applied.\n   *\n   * @param columns - Column list or aggregate expressions.\n   * @param options - Extra condition, trailing clauses and their parameters.\n   */\n  protected select<T>(columns: string, options: QueryOptions = {}): T[] {\n    const where = options.where ? ` AND ${options.where}` : '';\n    const tail = options.tail ? ` ${options.tail}` : '';\n    const sql = `SELECT ${columns} FROM ${this.table} WHERE ${this.merchantColumn} = ?${where}${tail}`;\n    return db.prepare(sql).all(this.scope(), ...(options.params ?? [])) as T[];\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Runs a scoped `SELECT` and returns the first row, if any.\n   *\n   * @param columns - Column list or aggregate expressions.\n   * @param options - Extra condition, trailing clauses and their parameters.\n   */\n  protected selectFirst<T>(columns: string, options: QueryOptions = {}): T | undefined {\n    return this.select<T>(columns, options)[0];\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Inserts a row, forcing the merchant column to the caller's scope.\n   *\n   * @param values - Column values, excluding the merchant column.\n   */\n  protected insert(values: Record<string, unknown>): void {\n    const row: Record<string, unknown> = { ...values, [this.merchantColumn]: this.scope() };\n    const columns = Object.keys(row);\n    const placeholders = columns.map(() => '?').join(', ');\n    db.prepare(`INSERT INTO ${this.table} (${columns.join(', ')}) VALUES (${placeholders})`).run(\n      ...columns.map((column) => row[column]),\n    );\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Base class for tables that are not merchant-scoped (the tenant list itself).\n * Only admin (mint-scoped) callers may read them.\n */\nexport abstract class AdminRepository {\n  /** Table backing this repository. */\n  protected abstract readonly table: string;\n\n  /**\n   * Ensures the caller is an admin.\n   *\n   * @throws ScopeError for any non-admin caller.\n   */\n  protected requireAdmin(): void {\n    const context = getAuthContext();\n    if (context.role !== 'admin' || context.scope !== 'mint') {\n      throw new ScopeError(`${context.role} caller may not read ${this.table}`);\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Runs an unscoped `SELECT` on behalf of an admin caller.\n   *\n   * @param columns - Column list.\n   * @param options - Condition, trailing clauses and their parameters.\n   */\n  protected select<T>(columns: string, options: QueryOptions = {}): T[] {\n    this.requireAdmin();\n    const where = options.where ? ` WHERE ${options.where}` : '';\n    const tail = options.tail ? ` ${options.tail}` : '';\n    return db.prepare(`SELECT ${columns} FROM ${this.table}${where}${tail}`).all(...(options.params ?? [])) as T[];\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Runs an unscoped `SELECT` and returns the first row, if any.\n   *\n   * @param columns - Column list.\n   * @param options - Condition, trailing clauses and their parameters.\n   */\n  protected selectFirst<T>(columns: string, options: QueryOptions = {}): T | undefined {\n    return this.select<T>(columns, options)[0];\n  }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":16807,"cache_read_input_tokens":277251,"output_tokens":8841,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1416},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":16807,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":8841,"cache_read_input_tokens":277251,"cache_creation_input_tokens":16807,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":16807},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_018MVu2SwG9BcxwgctokiaJm":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\src\\dal\\base-repository.ts","content":"/**\n * Repository base classes — the only place in the application that touches the database.\n *\n * `BaseRepository` applies the merchant scope itself, reading it from the request's\n * {@link getAuthContext}. [])) as T[];\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Runs a scoped `SELECT` and returns the first row, if any.\n   *\n   * @param columns - Column list or aggregate expressions.\n   * @param options - Extra condition, trailing clauses and their parameters.\n   */\n  protected selectFirst<T>(columns: string, options: QueryOptions = {}): T | undefined {\n    return this.select<T>(columns, options)[0];\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Inserts a row, forcing the merchant column to the caller's scope.\n   *\n   * @param values - Column values, excluding the merchant column.\n   */\n  protected insert(values: Record<string, unknown>): void {\n    const row: Record<string, unknown> = { ...values, [this.merchantColumn]: this.scope() };\n    const columns = Object.keys(row);\n    const placeholders = columns.map(() => '?').join(', ');\n    db.prepare(`INSERT INTO ${this.table} (${columns.join(', ')}) VALUES (${placeholders})`).run(\n      ...columns.map((column) => row[column]),\n    );\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Base class for tables that are not merchant-scoped (the tenant list itself).\n * Only admin (mint-scoped) callers may read them.\n */\nexport abstract class AdminRepository {\n  /** Table backing this repository. */\n  protected abstract readonly table: string;\n\n  /**\n   * Ensures the caller is an admin.\n   *\n   * @throws ScopeError for any non-admin caller.\n   */\n  protected requireAdmin(): void {\n    const context = getAuthContext();\n    if (context.role !== 'admin' || context.scope !== 'mint') {\n      throw new ScopeError(`${context.role} caller may not read ${this.table}`);\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Runs an unscoped `SELECT` on behalf of an admin caller.\n   *\n   * @param columns - Column list.\n   * @param options - Condition, trailing clauses and their parameters.\n   */\n  protected select<T>(columns: string, options: QueryOptions = {}): T[] {\n    this.requireAdmin();\n    const where = options.where ? ` WHERE ${options.where}` : '';\n    const tail = options.tail ? ` ${options.tail}` : '';\n    return db.prepare(`SELECT ${columns} FROM ${this.table}${where}${tail}`).all(...(options.params ?? [])) as T[];\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Runs an unscoped `SELECT` and returns the first row, if any.\n   *\n   * @param columns - Column list.\n   * @param options - Condition, trailing clauses and their parameters.\n   */\n  protected selectFirst<T>(columns: string, options: QueryOptions = {}): T | undefined {\n    return this.select<T>(columns, options)[0];\n  }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"8210087d-14d7-44f0-bf8e-0f81782e881e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

unique_customers: number; avg_order_value: number }>(\n      'COUNT(*) AS total_orders, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_email) AS unique_customers, COALESCE(AVG(total_amount), 0) AS avg_order_value',\n    );\n    return {\n      total_orders: row?.total_orders ?? 0,\n      unique_customers: row?.unique_customers ?? 0,\n      avg_order_value_cents: Math.round(row?.avg_order_value ?? 0),\n    };\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Customers ranked by amount spent.\n   *\n   * @param limit - Maximum rows to return.\n   */\n  topCustomers(limit: number): TopCustomer[] {\n    return this.select<TopCustomer>(\n      'customer_email, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(total_amount) AS total_spent',\n      {\n        tail: 'GROUP BY customer_email ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT ?',\n        params: [limit],\n      },\n    );\n  }\n}\n\n/** Shared instance; the merchant scope comes from the per-request auth context. */\nexport const metricsRepository = new MetricsRepository();\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"de0db5d1-5ac9-48cd-abbc-79406af6aaaf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

{"parentUuid":"6d58c39d-ab66-471c-bd61-7887927293e5","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CexyNDWYrEHKJT8oVfUAY","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01HEdgkjK8bkuHeuY9TErmxk","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\src\\routes\\auth.ts","content":"/**\n * Session endpoints.\n *\n * The admin token is a minting credential: it exchanges itself for short-lived,\n * merchant-scoped tokens, one per merchant the dashboard switches to. Data endpoints only\n * ever accept merchant tokens, so the merchant id always comes from a token the backend\n * signed, never from the client.\n *\n * @see plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md\n */\nimport { Router } from 'express';\nimport {\n  ADMIN_COOKIE,\n  MERCHANT_COOKIE,\n  parseCookies,\n  secondsUntil,\n  serializeClearedCookie,\n  serializeSessionCookie,\n} from '../auth/cookies.js';\nimport { requireAuth } from '../auth/guard.js';\nimport { InvalidTokenError, issueMerchantToken, verifyToken } from '../auth/jwt.js';\nimport { isLocalRequest } from '../auth/local.js';\nimport { merchantsRepository } from '../dal/merchants-repository.js';\nimport { asyncHandler } from './async-handler.js';\n\nexport const authRouter = Router();\n\n/**\n * `POST /api/auth/token` — mints a merchant-scoped session for the requested merchant.\n * Requires an admin (mint-scoped) token.\n */\nauthRouter.post(\n  '/token',\n  requireAuth({ scope: 'mint' }),\n  asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {\n    const body = req.body as { merchantId?: unknown } | undefined;\n    const merchantId = typeof body?.merchantId === 'string' ? body.merchantId : undefined;\n    if (!merchantId) {\n      res.status(400).json({ error: 'merchant_id_required' });\n      return;\n    }\n    if (!merchantsRepository.exists(merchantId)) {\n      res.status(404).json({ error: 'merchant_not_found' });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const { token, expiresAt } = await issueMerchantToken(merchantId);\n    res.append(\n      'Set-Cookie',\n      serializeSessionCookie(MERCHANT_COOKIE, token, {\n        maxAgeSeconds: secondsUntil(expiresAt),\n        secure: !isLocalRequest(req),\n      }),\n    );\n    res.status(204).end();\n  }),\n);\n\n/**\n * `POST /api/auth/admin-session` — exchanges an admin token (from `npm run token`) for the\n * admin session cookie. The way in when the request isn't local.\n */\nauthRouter.post(\n  '/admin-session',\n  asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {\n    const body = req.body as { token?: unknown } | undefined;\n    const token = typeof body?.token === 'string' ? body.token : undefined;\n    if (!token) {\n      res.status(400).json({ error: 'token_required' });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    let verified;\n    try {\n      verified = await verifyToken(token);\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (error instanceof InvalidTokenError) {\n        res.status(401).json({ error: 'session_expired' });\n        return;\n      }\n      throw error;\n    }\n    if (verified.scope !== 'mint') {\n      res.status(403).json({ error: 'token_not_scoped_for_mint' });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    res.append(\n      'Set-Cookie',\n      serializeSessionCookie(ADMIN_COOKIE, token, {\n        maxAgeSeconds: secondsUntil(verified.expiresAt),\n        secure: !isLocalRequest(req),\n      }),\n    );\n    res.status(204).end();\n  }),\n);\n\n/**\n * `GET /api/auth/session` — describes the current session so the dashboard knows what to render.\n */\nauthRouter.get(\n  '/session',\n  asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {\n    const cookies = parseCookies(req.headers.cookie);\n    for (const name of [MERCHANT_COOKIE, ADMIN_COOKIE]) {\n      const token = cookies[name];\n      if (!token) continue;\n      try {\n        const verified = await verifyToken(token);\n        res.json({\n          role: verified.role,\n          scope: verified.scope,\n          merchantId: verified.merchantId ?? null,\n          expiresAt: verified.expiresAt.toISOString(),\n        });\n        return;\n      } catch (error) {\n        if (!(error instanceof InvalidTokenError)) throw error;\n      }\n    }\n    res.status(401).json({ error: 'unauthenticated' });\n  }),\n);\n\n/**\n * `DELETE /api/auth/session` — clears both session cookies.\n */\nauthRouter.delete('/session', (_req, res) => {\n  res.append('Set-Cookie', serializeClearedCookie(MERCHANT_COOKIE));\n  res.append('Set-Cookie', serializeClearedCookie(ADMIN_COOKIE));\n  res.status(204).end();\n});\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":9906,"cache_read_input_tokens":294058,"output_tokens":9716,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":2216},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":9906,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":9716,"cache_read_input_tokens":294058,"cache_creation_input_tokens":9906,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":9906},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01HEdgkjK8bkuHeuY9TErmxk":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\src\\routes\\auth.ts","content":"/**\n * Session endpoints.\n *\n * The admin token is a minting credential: it exchanges itself for short-lived,\n * merchant-scoped tokens, one per merchant the dashboard switches to. 'data/dashboard.db';\nconst metricsDb = new Database(DB_PATH, { readonly: true });\n\nexport const metricsRouter = Router();\n\n/**\n * GET /api/metrics/summary\n *\n * Returns dashboard summary stats for the current merchant.\n */\nmetricsRouter.get('/summary', (req, res) => {\n  const merchantId = req.merchantId!;\n\n  const totalOrdersRow = metricsDb\n    .prepare(`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE merchant_id = ?`)\n    .get(merchantId) as { n: number };\n\n  const totalCustomersRow = metricsDb\n    .prepare(\n      `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_email) AS n FROM orders WHERE merchant_id = ?`,\n    )\n    .get(merchantId) as { n: number };\n\n  const avgOrderRow = metricsDb\n    .prepare(\n      `SELECT COALESCE(AVG(total_amount), 0) AS avg FROM orders WHERE merchant_id = ?`,\n    )\n    .get(merchantId) as { avg: number };\n\n  res.json({\n    merchant_id: merchantId,\n    total_orders: totalOrdersRow.n,\n    unique_customers: totalCustomersRow.n,\n    avg_order_value_cents: Math.round(avgOrderRow.avg),\n  });\n});\n\nmetricsRouter.get('/top-customers', (req, res) => {\n  const merchantId = req.merchantId!;\n  const limit = Number(req.query.limit ?? 5);\n\n  const rows = metricsDb\n    .prepare(\n      `SELECT customer_email, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(total_amount) AS total_spent\n       FROM orders\n       WHERE merchant_id = ?\n       GROUP BY customer_email\n       ORDER BY total_spent DESC\n       LIMIT ?`,\n    )\n    .all(merchantId, limit) as Array<{ customer_email: string; order_count: number; total_spent: number }>;\n\n  res.json({ customers: rows });\n});\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"bfd3395d-2788-45b7-9f1a-52742b4e7ebc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

Set DB_PATH before importing the db module — the connection is created on import.\nif (!process.env.DB_PATH) process.env.DB_PATH = ':memory:';\n\nimport { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { MissingAuthContextError, runWithAuthContext } from '../src/auth/context.js';\nimport { ScopeError } from '../src/dal/base-repository.js';\nimport { merchantsRepository } from '../src/dal/merchants-repository.js';\nimport { metricsRepository } from '../src/dal/metrics-repository.js';\nimport { ordersRepository } from '../src/dal/orders-repository.js';\nimport { initSchema, db } from '../src/db.js';\n\n/** Seeds two merchants with one order each. */\nfunction seed(): void {\n  initSchema();\n  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO merchants (id, name) VALUES ('m_acme', 'Acme'), ('m_bistro', 'Bistro')`).run();\n  db.prepare(\n    `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO orders (id, merchant_id, customer_email, total_amount, type, status)\n     VALUES ('acme-1', 'm_acme', 'ana@example.com', 1000, 'sale', 'completed'),\n            ('bistro-1', 'm_bistro', 'bruno@example.com', 2000, 'sale', 'completed')`,\n  ).run();\n}\n\n/** Runs a function as a merchant caller. */\nfunction asMerchant<T>(merchantId: string, fn: () => T): T {\n  return runWithAuthContext({ role: 'merchant', scope: 'data', merchantId }, fn);\n}\n\n/** Runs a function as an admin caller. */\nfunction asAdmin<T>(fn: () => T): T {\n  return runWithAuthContext({ role: 'admin', scope: 'mint' }, fn);\n}\n\ntest('base repository: refuses to query without an auth context', () => {\n Set DB_PATH before importing the db module — the connection is created on import.\nif (!process.env.DB_PATH) process.env.DB_PATH = ':memory:';\nprocess.env.JWT_SECRET ??= 'test-secret-for-guard';\n\nimport { test, after, before } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport type { AddressInfo } from 'node:net';\nimport type { Server } from 'node:http';\nimport { createApp } from '../src/app.js';\nimport { ADMIN_COOKIE, MERCHANT_COOKIE } from '../src/auth/cookies.js';\nimport { issueAdminToken, issueMerchantToken, signToken } from '../src/auth/jwt.js';\nimport { initSchema, db } from '../src/db.js';\n\nlet server: Server;\nlet baseUrl: string;\nlet adminCookie: string;\nlet acmeCookie: string;\nlet bistroCookie: string;\n\nbefore(async () => {\n  initSchema();\n  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO merchants (id, name) VALUES ('m_acme', 'Acme'), ('m_bistro', 'Bistro')`).run();\n  db.prepare(\n    `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO orders (id, merchant_id, customer_email, total_amount, type, status)\n     VALUES ('acme-1', 'm_acme', 'ana@example.com', 1000, 'sale', 'completed'),\n            ('bistro-1', 'm_bistro', 'bruno@example.com', 2000, 'sale', 'completed')`,\n  ).run();\n\n  // Dev bootstrap off: these tests exercise the real authentication flow.\n  server = createApp({ enableDevAdminSession: false }).listen(0);\n  await new Promise((resolve) => server.once('listening', resolve));\n  baseUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${(server.address() as AddressInfo).port}`;\n\n  adminCookie = `${ADMIN_COOKIE}=${(await issueAdminToken('5m')).token}`;\n  acmeCookie = `${MERCHANT_COOKIE}=${(await issueMerchantToken('m_acme', '5m')).token}`;\n  bistroCookie = `${MERCHANT_COOKIE}=${(await issueMerchantToken('m_bistro', '5m')).token}`;\n});\n\nafter(() => {\n  server.close();\n});\n\n/** Issues a request with optional cookie and headers. */\nfunction call(path: string, init: { cookie?: string; headers?: Record<string, string>; method?: string; body?: unknown } = {}) {\n  const headers: Record<string, string> = { ...init.headers };\n  if (init.cookie) headers.Cookie = init.cookie;\n  if (init.body !== undefined) headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json';\n  return fetch(`${baseUrl}${path}`, {\n    method: init.method ?? 'GET',\n    headers,\n    ...(init.body === undefined ? {} : { body: JSON.stringify(init.body) }),\n  });\n}\n\ntest('guard: no token is rejected', async () => {\n  const response = await initSchema();\n  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO merchants (id, name) VALUES ('m_acme', 'Acme'), ('m_bistro', 'Bistro')`).run();\n  db.prepare(\n    `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO orders (id, merchant_id, ordersRepository.list());\n  assert.deepEqual(bistro.map((o) => o.id), ['bistro-1']);\n});\n\ntest(\"base repository: getById hides another merchant's order (TD-02)\", () => {\n  seed();\n    id: 'scoped-1',\n      customer_email: 'x@y.com',\n      total_amount: 700,\n      type: 'sale',\n      status: 'completed',\n    }),\n  );\n  assert.equal(created.merchant_id, 'm_bistro');\n Can be applied to a whole router or a single\n * route, so new routes are protected by adding one middleware.\n *\n * Rules:\n * - no token → `401 unauthenticated`\n * - invalid/expired token → `401 session_expired`\n * - admin token on a data route → `403 token_not_scoped_for_data`\n * - merchant token on a mint route → `403 token_not_scoped_for_mint`\n * - `X-Merchant-Id` different from the token's merchant → `403 merchant_mismatch`\n *\n * The client-supplied merchant id is never used, only compared: the token always wins.\n *\n * @see plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md\n */\nimport type { NextFunction, Request, RequestHandler, Response } from 'express';\nimport { ADMIN_COOKIE, MERCHANT_COOKIE, parseCookies } from './cookies.js';\nimport { runWithAuthContext } from './context.js';\nimport { InvalidTokenError, verifyToken, type TokenScope } from './jwt.js';\n\n/** Options accepted by {@link requireAuth}. */\nexport interface GuardOptions {\n  /** Scope the caller's token must carry. 'token_not_scoped_for_data' : 'token_not_scoped_for_mint',\n    });\n    return;\n  }\n\n  if (scope === 'data') {\n    const requested = req.header('X-Merchant-Id');\n    if (requested && requested !== verified.merchantId) {\n      res.status(403).json({ error: 'merchant_mismatch' });\n      return;\n    }\n  }\n\n  runWithAuthContext(\n    {\n      role: verified.role,\n      scope: verified.scope,\n      ...(verified.merchantId ? { merchantId: verified.merchantId } : {}),\n    },\n    next,\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * Picks the credential for the requested scope: the admin cookie (or a bearer token) for\n * minting, the merchant cookie for data.\n */\nfunction extractToken(req: Request, scope: TokenScope): string | undefined {\n  const cookies = parseCookies(req.headers.cookie);\n  if (scope === 'mint') return bearerToken(req) ?? cookies[ADMIN_COOKIE];\n  return cookies[MERCHANT_COOKIE];\n}\n\n/**\n * Extracts an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` value, if present.\n */\nfunction bearerToken(req: Request): string | undefined {\n  const header = req.header('Authorization');\n  if (!header?.toLowerCase().startsWith('bearer ')) return undefined;\n  const token = header.slice('bearer '.length).trim();\n  return token.length > 0 ? token : undefined;\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":91,"oldLines":8,"newStart":91,"newLines":11,"lines":["  */"," function extractToken(req: Request, scope: TokenScope): string | undefined {","   const cookies = parseCookies(req.headers.cookie);","-  if (scope === 'mint') return bearerToken(req) ?? cookies[ADMIN_COOKIE];","-  return cookies[MERCHANT_COOKIE];","+  const preferred = scope === 'mint' ? Everything else must go through a\n * repository, which is what guarantees the merchant scope can't be forgotten (TD-02, TD-04).\n */\nconst ALLOWED_DB_IMPORTERS = new Set(['src/dal/base-repository.ts']);\n\n/** Standalone scripts are out of the request path and may use the handle directly. */\nconst EXCLUDED_PREFIXES = ['src/scripts/'];\n\n/** Lists every TypeScript file under a directory. */\nfunction listFiles(directory: string): string[] {\n  return readdirSync(directory).flatMap((entry) => {\n    const path = join(directory, entry);\n    if (statSync(path).isDirectory()) return listFiles(path);\n    return path.endsWith('.ts') ? [path] : [];\n  });\n}\n\ntest('architecture: only the repository base class imports the database handle', () => {\n  const offenders = listFiles('src')\n    .map((path) => relative('src', path).split(sep).join('/'))\n    .map((path) => `src/${path}`)\n    .filter((path) => path !== 'src/db.ts')\n    .filter((path) => !EXCLUDED_PREFIXES.some((prefix) => path.startsWith(prefix)))\n    .filter((path) => /from\\s+'(?:\\.\\.\\/)*\\.?\\.?\\/?db\\.js'/.test(readFileSync(path, 'utf8')))\n    .filter((path) => !ALLOWED_DB_IMPORTERS.has(path));\n\n  assert.deepEqual(\n    offenders,\n    [],\n    `these modules bypass the repository layer: ${offenders.join(', ')}. ` +\n      'Extend BaseRepository (or AdminRepository) instead of importing db directly.',\n  );\n});\n\ntest('architecture: routes do not open their own database connection', () => {\n  const offenders = listFiles(join('src', 'routes')).filter((path) =>\n    readFileSync(path, 'utf8').includes('better-sqlite3'),\n  );\n  assert.deepEqual(offenders, [], `routes must not talk to SQLite directly: ${offenders.join(', ')}`);\n});\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":27,"oldLines":7,"newStart":27,"newLines":7,"lines":["     .map((path) => `src/${path}`)","     .filter((path) => path !== 'src/db.ts')","     .filter((path) => !EXCLUDED_PREFIXES.some((prefix) => path.startsWith(prefix)))","-    .filter((path) => /from\\s+'(?:\\.\\.\\/)*\\.?\\.?\\/?db\\.js'/.test(readFileSync(path, 'utf8')))","+    .filter((path) => importsDbHandle(readFileSync(path, 'utf8')))","     .filter((path) => !ALLOWED_DB_IMPORTERS.has(path));"," ","   assert.deepEqual("]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"2a28879f-8785-4705-b564-86b3ef11b968","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

[path] : [];\n  });\n}\n\ntest('architecture: only the repository base class imports the database handle', () => {\n  const offenders = listFiles('src')\n    .map((path) => relative('src', path).split(sep).join('/'))\n    .map((path) => `src/${path}`)\n    .filter((path) => path !== 'src/db.ts')\n    .filter((path) => !EXCLUDED_PREFIXES.some((prefix) => path.startsWith(prefix)))\n    .filter((path) => importsDbHandle(readFileSync(path, 'utf8')))\n    .filter((path) => !ALLOWED_DB_IMPORTERS.has(path));\n\n  assert.deepEqual(\n    offenders,\n    [],\n    `these modules bypass the repository layer: ${offenders.join(', ')}. ` +\n      'Extend BaseRepository (or AdminRepository) instead of importing db directly.',\n  );\n});\n\ntest('architecture: routes do not open their own database connection', () => {\n  const offenders = listFiles(join('src', 'routes')).filter((path) =>\n    readFileSync(path, 'utf8').includes('better-sqlite3'),\n  );\n  assert.deepEqual(offenders, [], `routes must not talk to SQLite directly: ${offenders.join(', ')}`);\n});\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":12,"oldLines":6,"newStart":12,"newLines":19,"lines":[" /** Standalone scripts are out of the request path and may use the handle directly. */"," const EXCLUDED_PREFIXES = ['src/scripts/'];"," ","+/**","+ * Whether a module imports the `db` handle itself. Delete `.env` if it was generated. No database migration involved.\n\n## Results\n\nAll open questions were approved as recommended (jose; mint-only admin token; 8h/10m TTLs; frontend-driven re-mint; native `loadEnvFile`; auto-generated secret).\n\n| Step | Result |\n|---|---|\n| 1. `npm test` | ✅ 52/52 (37 new) |\n| 2. `tsc --noEmit` | ✅ exit 0 |\n| 3. `npm run check:deps` | ✅ `No known vulnerabilities` with `jose@6.2.12` |\n| 4. `.env` | ✅ absent → `npm run token` created it with a random `JWT_SECRET`; a second run kept the same secret (server and CLI share it) |\n| 5. `npm run token` | ✅ claims `{role: admin, scope: mint}`, no `merchantId`, 8h |\n| 6. Guard (curl) | ✅ admin cookie on `/api/orders` → `403 token_not_scoped_for_data`; merchant cookie → own data; spoofed `X-Merchant-Id` → `403 merchant_mismatch`; own header → `200`; mint unknown merchant → `404`; expired token → `401 session_expired` (unit test) |\n| 7. TD-02 | ✅ `GET /api/orders/bistro-1` with an `m_acme` session → `404` |\n| 8. TD-04 | ✅ architecture test passes; no `better-sqlite3` under `src/routes/` |\n| 9. Local gating | ✅ `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION=off` → no auto cookie and `/api/orders` → `401`; `isLocalRequest` unit tests cover a spoofed `Host` from a remote peer |\n| 10. Browser | ✅ picker populated from `/api/merchants`; switching `m_acme` → `m_bistro` mints a new token and the numbers change; `document.cookie` is empty (HttpOnly); TTLs decoded from the jar: merchant 10.0 min, admin 480 min |\n\n### Deviations from the plan\n\n- **`src/app.ts` extracted from `src/server.ts`** (`createApp(options)`), so HTTP tests can bind an ephemeral port. Not in the original file list.\n- **`src/routes/async-handler.ts`** added: Express 4 doesn't forward rejected promises, and the auth routes are async.\n- **Guard reads the \"wrong\" cookie on purpose.** Presenting an admin token to a data route (or vice versa) now returns `403 token_not_scoped_for_*` instead of `401`; looking only at the expected cookie made a wrong-token request indistinguishable from no session.\n- **Architecture test checks the imported binding, not the module.** `server.ts` legitimately imports `initSchema` from `db.ts`; only importing the `db` handle is an offense.\n- **Validation step \"no cookie → 401\" reads `403` on a local request** with the dev bootstrap on, because the middleware attaches an admin cookie to that very request. The true `401` is verified with `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION=off`.\n\n### Known gaps (by design, still open)\n\n- **TD-12 (stored XSS)** is untouched: `public/app.js` still renders rows with `innerHTML`. {"parentUuid":"6edbdbdb-b075-4877-bb70-9aaece0e02ab","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cexyusa8sNG3BbTUNjRop","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Ejecuté el [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md) y quedó validado en local. Cierra TD-01, TD-02 y TD-04.\n\n**Lo que hay ahora:**\n\n- **Tokens:** `jose` con HS256. El de admin (`scope: mint`, 8 h) solo emite tokens; el de merchant (`scope: data`, 10 min) solo lee datos de su merchant.\n- **Cookies HttpOnly:** verificado en el navegador, `document.cookie` sale vacío.\n- **Arranque:** un middleware entrega la cookie de admin, pero solo si la conexión viene de loopback. Se apaga con `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION=off`, y el servidor avisa en cada arranque.\n- **Selector:** llama a `POST /api/auth/token` en cada cambio y recibe un token nuevo. Los merchants salen de `GET /api/merchants`, ya no del HTML.\n- **Repositorios:** `BaseRepository` saca el merchantId del contexto y lo inyecta en cada query e insert; una subclase no puede omitirlo porque nunca ve la conexión. `AdminRepository` cubre la tabla de merchants, que no tiene scope, y exige rol admin.\n- **`.env`:** `src/config/env.ts` con carga nativa, `.env.example` commiteado, y el secreto se genera y se guarda en el primer arranque para que el servidor y el CLI firmen igual.\n\n**Validación:** 52 tests (37 nuevos), `tsc` limpio, `check:deps` sin vulnerabilidades, el flujo completo por `curl` y el dashboard en el navegador cambiando entre los dos merchants.\n\n**Cuatro desviaciones respecto al plan,** todas anotadas en sus resultados:\n- Extraje `src/app.ts` para poder probar la capa HTTP en un puerto efímero.\n- Añadí `async-handler.ts`, porque Express 4 no propaga promesas rechazadas.\n- **El guard lee también la cookie \"equivocada\" a propósito:** presentar un token de admin en una ruta de datos ahora da `403 token_not_scoped_for_data` en vez de `401`. Si solo mirase la cookie esperada, un token inválido sería indistinguible de no tener sesión.\n- **El test de arquitectura mira qué se importa, no de dónde:** `server.ts` importa `initSchema` legítimamente; lo que no puede salir de la clase base es el handle `db`.\n\n**Lo que sigue abierto a propósito:** TD-12 (el XSS del dashboard) sigue ahí, porque toca `app.js` y pertenece al grupo D. Reescribí ese archivo por el flujo de sesión, así que era tentador arreglarlo de paso, pero lo dejé para que el fix tenga su propio commit revisable. {"parentUuid":"d4e04430-b45b-4709-80bf-6a150d20e91f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cexzo7VhZE2Qy3WrC9NWS","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_012PjoaUBjZ3pmUnK9ecPzjC","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\docs\\api.md","content":"# API reference\n\nBase URL: `http://localhost:3000` (or `PORT`). All responses are JSON.\n\nAuthentication and the branch/release process are described in [github-workflow.md](github-workflow.md) and [architecture.md](architecture.md).\n\n## Authentication\n\nTwo token types, both HS256 JWTs signed by the backend and delivered as **HttpOnly** cookies (`SameSite=Strict`, `Secure` on non-local requests). Nothing is stored in `localStorage`.\n\n| Token | Cookie | Claims | TTL | Can do |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Admin | `admin_session` | `role: admin`, `scope: mint` | `ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL` (8h) | Mint merchant tokens, list merchants |\n| Merchant | `merchant_session` | `role: merchant`, `scope: data`, `merchantId` | `MERCHANT_TOKEN_TTL` (10m) | Read that merchant's data |\n\nRules enforced by the guard:\n\n- **The token decides the merchant.** `X-Merchant-Id` is never used to select data; if it is sent and differs from the token's merchant, the request is rejected with `403 merchant_mismatch`.\n- **The admin token cannot read data** (`403 token_not_scoped_for_data`), and a merchant token cannot mint (`403 token_not_scoped_for_mint`). One rule, no exceptions: data always comes from a merchant-scoped token.\n- Merchant tokens are short-lived. When one expires the API answers `401 session_expired`; the client mints a new one and retries.\n\n### Getting a session\n\n**Locally**, the server hands an `admin_session` cookie to any request coming from loopback, so opening the dashboard is enough. This is a development convenience: it is gated on the TCP peer address (a spoofed `Host: localhost` from another machine does not pass) and can be disabled with `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION=off`. **It must never be enabled on a deployed instance** — it would hand a minting credential to every visitor.\n\n**Otherwise**, mint an admin token from the CLI and exchange it for the cookie:\n\n```sh\nnpm run token                    # prints an admin token (add expiresIn=30m to shorten it)\ncurl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/admin-session \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"token\":\"<token>\"}'\n```\n\n## Errors\n\n| Status | `error` | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| 400 | `merchant_id_required`, `token_required`, `invalid_body`, `missing_date_range` | Malformed request |\n| 401 | `unauthenticated` | No session cookie |\n| 401 | `session_expired` | Token invalid, expired, or signed with another key |\n| 403 | `merchant_mismatch` | `X-Merchant-Id` differs from the token's merchant |\n| 403 | `token_not_scoped_for_data` / `token_not_scoped_for_mint` | Right session, wrong token type |\n| 404 | `not_found`, `merchant_not_found` | Unknown id — including another merchant's order |\n| 500 | `internal_error` | Unhandled server error |\n\n---\n\n## Auth endpoints\n\n### `POST /api/auth/token`\nMints a merchant session. **Requires the admin token** (cookie or `Authorization: Bearer`).\n\nBody: `{ \"merchantId\": \"m_acme\" }` → `204` with `Set-Cookie: merchant_session`.\nErrors: `400 merchant_id_required`, `404 merchant_not_found`.\n\n### `POST /api/auth/admin-session`\nExchanges an admin token for the `admin_session` cookie. Body: `{ \"token\": \"<jwt>\" }` → `204`.\n\n### `GET /api/auth/session`\nDescribes the current session: `{ role, scope, merchantId, expiresAt }`. `401` when there is none.\n\n### `DELETE /api/auth/session`\nClears both cookies. `204`.\n\n## Data endpoints\n\nAll of these require a **merchant** session.\n\n### `GET /api/health`\nNo auth. `{ ok: true }`.\n\n### `GET /api/merchants`\nEvery merchant: `{ merchants: [{ id, name }] }`. **Requires the admin token** — a merchant session is bound to one merchant and gets `403`.\n\n### `GET /api/orders`\nOrders of the session's merchant, newest first.\n\nQuery: `from`, `to` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, applied only when both are present; `to` is exclusive), `limit` (default 100).\n\n```json\n{ \"orders\": [{ \"id\": \"…\", \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"customer_email\": \"ana@example.com\",\n               \"total_amount\": 11136, \"type\": \"sale\", \"status\": \"completed\",\n               \"created_at\": \"2026-09-11T11:45:35.866Z\" }] }\n```\n\n> `limit` is not validated yet — see TD-10 in `tech_debt.md`.\n\n### `GET /api/orders/:id`\nOne order: `{ order }`. An order belonging to another merchant returns `404 not_found`, not the row.\n\n### `POST /api/orders`\nCreates an order for the session's merchant. The merchant is taken from the token, never from the body.\n\nBody: `{ customer_email, total_amount, type? }` — `total_amount` in integer cents, `type` is `sale` (default) or `refund`. Returns `201` with `{ order }`.\n\n> Body validation is still thin — see TD-11 in `tech_debt.md`.\n\n### `GET /api/revenue?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD`\nBoth parameters are required.\n\n```json\n{ \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"from\": \"2026-08-01\", \"to\": \"2026-09-12\",\n  \"revenue_cents\": 238200, \"revenue\": 2382 }\n```\n\n> Refunds are currently summed as income, and `to` is exclusive so \"today\" is excluded — see TD-05 and TD-07 in `tech_debt.md`.\n\n### `GET /api/metrics/summary`\n\n```json\n{ \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"total_orders\": 40,\n  \"unique_customers\": 3, \"avg_order_value_cents\": 10609 }\n```\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `total_orders` | Rows in `orders` for the merchant (refunds included — TD-06) |\n| `unique_customers` | Distinct `customer_email` values |\n| `avg_order_value_cents` | Rounded average of `total_amount` |\n\n### `GET /api/metrics/top-customers`\nQuery: `limit` (default 5).\n\n```json\n{ \"customers\": [{ \"customer_email\": \"ana@example.com\", \"order_count\": 14, \"total_spent\": 181968 }] API reference\n\nBase URL: `http://localhost:3000` (or `PORT`). All responses are JSON.\n\nAuthentication and the branch/release process are described in [github-workflow.md](github-workflow.md) and [architecture.md](architecture.md).\n\n## Authentication\n\nTwo token types, both HS256 JWTs signed by the backend and delivered as **HttpOnly** cookies (`SameSite=Strict`, `Secure` on non-local requests). Nothing is stored in `localStorage`.\n\n| Token | Cookie | Claims | TTL | Can do |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Admin | `admin_session` | `role: admin`, `scope: mint` | `ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL` (8h) | Mint merchant tokens, list merchants |\n| Merchant | `merchant_session` | `role: merchant`, `scope: data`, `merchantId` | `MERCHANT_TOKEN_TTL` (10m) | Read that merchant's data |\n\nRules enforced by the guard:\n\n- **The token decides the merchant.** `X-Merchant-Id` is never used to select data; if it is sent and differs from the token's merchant, the request is rejected with `403 merchant_mismatch`.\n- **The admin token cannot read data** (`403 token_not_scoped_for_data`), and a merchant token cannot mint (`403 token_not_scoped_for_mint`). One rule, no exceptions: data always comes from a merchant-scoped token.\n- Merchant tokens are short-lived. When one expires the API answers `401 session_expired`; the client mints a new one and retries.\n\n### Getting a session\n\n**Locally**, the server hands an `admin_session` cookie to any request coming from loopback, so opening the dashboard is enough. This is a development convenience: it is gated on the TCP peer address (a spoofed `Host: localhost` from another machine does not pass) and can be disabled with `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION=off`. **It must never be enabled on a deployed instance** — it would hand a minting credential to every visitor.\n\n**Otherwise**, mint an admin token from the CLI and exchange it for the cookie:\n\n```sh\nnpm run token                    # prints an admin token (add expiresIn=30m to shorten it)\ncurl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/admin-session \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"token\":\"<token>\"}'\n```\n\n## Errors\n\n| Status | `error` | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| 400 | `merchant_id_required`, `token_required`, `invalid_body`, `missing_date_range` | Malformed request |\n| 401 | `unauthenticated` | No session cookie |\n| 401 | `session_expired` | Token invalid, expired, or signed with another key |\n| 403 | `merchant_mismatch` | `X-Merchant-Id` differs from the token's merchant |\n| 403 | `token_not_scoped_for_data` / `token_not_scoped_for_mint` | Right session, wrong token type |\n| 404 | `not_found`, `merchant_not_found` | Unknown id — including another merchant's order |\n| 500 | `internal_error` | Unhandled server error |\n\n---\n\n## Auth endpoints\n\n### `POST /api/auth/token`\nMints a merchant session. **Requires the admin token** (cookie or `Authorization: Bearer`).\n\nBody: `{ \"merchantId\": \"m_acme\" }` → `204` with `Set-Cookie: merchant_session`.\nErrors: `400 merchant_id_required`, `404 merchant_not_found`.\n\n### `POST /api/auth/admin-session`\nExchanges an admin token for the `admin_session` cookie. Body: `{ \"token\": \"<jwt>\" }` → `204`.\n\n### `GET /api/auth/session`\nDescribes the current session: `{ role, scope, merchantId, expiresAt }`. `401` when there is none.\n\n### `DELETE /api/auth/session`\nClears both cookies. `204`.\n\n## Data endpoints\n\nAll of these require a **merchant** session.\n\n### `GET /api/health`\nNo auth. `{ ok: true }`.\n\n### `GET /api/merchants`\nEvery merchant: `{ merchants: [{ id, name }] }`. **Requires the admin token** — a merchant session is bound to one merchant and gets `403`.\n\n### `GET /api/orders`\nOrders of the session's merchant, newest first.\n\nQuery: `from`, `to` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, applied only when both are present; `to` is exclusive), `limit` (default 100).\n\n```json\n{ \"orders\": [{ \"id\": \"…\", \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"customer_email\": \"ana@example.com\",\n               \"total_amount\": 11136, \"type\": \"sale\", \"status\": \"completed\",\n               \"created_at\": \"2026-09-11T11:45:35.866Z\" }] }\n```\n\n> `limit` is not validated yet — see TD-10 in `tech_debt.md`.\n\n### `GET /api/orders/:id`\nOne order: `{ order }`. An order belonging to another merchant returns `404 not_found`, not the row.\n\n### `POST /api/orders`\nCreates an order for the session's merchant. The merchant is taken from the token, never from the body.\n\nBody: `{ customer_email, total_amount, type? }` — `total_amount` in integer cents, `type` is `sale` (default) or `refund`. Returns `201` with `{ order }`.\n\n> Body validation is still thin — see TD-11 in `tech_debt.md`.\n\n### `GET /api/revenue?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD`\nBoth parameters are required.\n\n```json\n{ \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"from\": \"2026-08-01\", \"to\": \"2026-09-12\",\n  \"revenue_cents\": 238200, \"revenue\": 2382 }\n```\n\n> Refunds are currently summed as income, and `to` is exclusive so \"today\" is excluded — see TD-05 and TD-07 in `tech_debt.md`.\n\n### `GET /api/metrics/summary`\n\n```json\n{ \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"total_orders\": 40,\n  \"unique_customers\": 3, \"avg_order_value_cents\": 10609 }\n```\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `total_orders` | Rows in `orders` for the merchant (refunds included — TD-06) |\n| `unique_customers` | Distinct `customer_email` values |\n| `avg_order_value_cents` | Rounded average of `total_amount` |\n\n### `GET /api/metrics/top-customers`\nQuery: `limit` (default 5).\n\n```json\n{ \"customers\": [{ \"customer_email\": \"ana@example.com\", \"order_count\": 14, \"total_spent\": 181968 }] }\n```\n"}},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cexzo6Uw3ysPvS2puuYds","type":"assistant","uuid":"3f4e65f5-c643-4b14-9065-5752f33e4af1","timestamp":"2026-09-12T05:32:07.093Z","effort":"medium","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

{"parentUuid":"ee09d5e8-352e-49d6-a828-f71a6dece30b","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cexzo7VhZE2Qy3WrC9NWS","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_014NDYjV263naheMQxMqRBf8","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\docs\\architecture.md","content":"# Architecture\n\nA small merchant sales dashboard: static frontend, Express API, SQLite database.\n\nEndpoint details are in [api.md](api.md); branch and release rules in [github-workflow.md](github-workflow.md).\n\n## Request flow\n\n```\nbrowser (public/)\n  │  fetch with HttpOnly cookies\n  ▼\nexpress (src/app.ts)\n  ├─ devAdminSession      local requests only: hands out an admin cookie\n  ├─ express.static       serves public/\n  ├─ /api/auth            session endpoints (mint, exchange, whoami, logout)\n  ├─ /api/merchants       admin-scoped\n  └─ /api/orders|revenue|metrics\n        │  requireAuth() verifies the token and opens the auth context\n        ▼\n     routes → repositories (src/dal) → SQLite (src/db.ts)\n```\n\n## Modules\n\n| Path | Role |\n|---|---|\n| `src/server.ts` | Entry point: schema init, seed, listen. |\n| `src/app.ts` | Express wiring. `createApp()` is exported so tests can bind an ephemeral port. |\n| `src/config/env.ts` | The only reader of configuration. Loads `.env` with Node's built-in `process.loadEnvFile()`. |\n| `src/auth/jwt.ts` | Signs and verifies session tokens (`jose`, HS256). |\n| `src/auth/guard.ts` | `requireAuth({ scope })` — the middleware that protects routes. |\n| `src/auth/context.ts` | Per-request identity in an `AsyncLocalStorage`. |\n| `src/auth/local.ts` | Loopback detection for the development bootstrap. |\n| `src/auth/dev-session.ts` | Issues the admin cookie to local requests (dev only). |\n| `src/auth/cookies.ts` | Cookie parsing/serialization (no dependency). |\n| `src/dal/base-repository.ts` | `BaseRepository` / `AdminRepository`. **The only module that touches the database handle.** |\n| `src/dal/*-repository.ts` | One repository per entity. |\n| `src/routes/*.ts` | Express routers, one file per resource. |\n| `src/scripts/` | CLI entry points: `seed`, `issue-token`, `setup-env`, `check-deps`. |\n| `public/` | Static dashboard (plain HTML + `fetch`, no framework). |\n\n## Authentication\n\nTwo HS256 JWTs in HttpOnly cookies:\n\n- **Admin token** (`scope: mint`, 8h) — mints merchant tokens and lists merchants. It cannot read data.\n- **Merchant token** (`scope: data`, 10m) — reads only the merchant named in its `merchantId` claim.\n\nThe design rule is one line: **the merchant id always comes from a token the backend signed.** A client-sent `X-Merchant-Id` is only compared against the token, never used; a mismatch is `403`. Switching merchants in the dashboard means asking the backend for a new token, not sending a different header.\n\n`requireAuth()` verifies the cookie, then runs the rest of the request inside an `AsyncLocalStorage` context. Any class or function reached during the request can call `getAuthContext()` — no parameter threading — and the call **throws** if no context exists, so code can't accidentally run unauthenticated.\n\n### Development bootstrap, and its limit\n\n`devAdminSession` hands an admin cookie to requests whose **TCP peer address is loopback** (a spoofed `Host: localhost` from elsewhere does not qualify), so `npm run dev` works without a login step. `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION=off` disables it.\n\nThis is a convenience, not a login. On a deployed instance it would give every visitor a credential that can mint any merchant's token. A real deployment needs an actual login issuing the admin token, and this middleware removed.\n\n## Data access\n\nEvery order query goes through a repository. `BaseRepository` reads the merchant id from the auth context and injects it into each `SELECT` and `INSERT`; subclasses never see the connection and never pass a merchant id, so a repository *cannot* forget the tenancy filter. `AdminRepository` covers `merchants` — the tenant list itself, which isn't merchant-scoped — and requires an admin caller instead.\n\n`test/architecture.test.ts` enforces the rule: if any module other than `base-repository.ts` imports the `db` handle, the suite fails. Standalone scripts are exempt.\n\n## Data model\n\nTwo tables, `merchants` and `orders`; canonical DDL in `src/db.ts`.\n\n`orders.type` is `'sale' | 'refund'`. A refund row records that a sale was reversed; it does not by itself reverse the sale row, and the revenue query currently sums both (TD-05).\n\n## Configuration\n\n| Variable | Default | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `JWT_SECRET` | generated | Missing on a local start → generated and appended to `.env` so server and CLI share it. |\n| `PORT` | `3000` | |\n| `DB_PATH` | `data/dashboard.db` | `:memory:` in tests. |\n| `ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL` | `8h` | |\n| `MERCHANT_TOKEN_TTL` | `10m` | |\n| `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION` | `on` | `off` disables the local admin cookie. |\n\n`npm run setup:env` creates `.env` from `.env.example`; it never overwrites an existing value.\n\n## Known gaps\n\nTracked in `tech_debt.md` (active) and `tech_debt_backlog.md` (deferred). Loads `.env` with Node's built-in `process.loadEnvFile()`. |\n| `src/auth/jwt.ts` | Signs and verifies session tokens (`jose`, HS256). |\n| `src/auth/guard.ts` | `requireAuth({ scope })` — the middleware that protects routes. |\n| `src/auth/context.ts` | Per-request identity in an `AsyncLocalStorage`. |\n| `src/auth/local.ts` | Loopback detection for the development bootstrap. |\n| `src/auth/dev-session.ts` | Issues the admin cookie to local requests (dev only). |\n| `src/auth/cookies.ts` | Cookie parsing/serialization (no dependency). |\n| `src/dal/base-repository.ts` | `BaseRepository` / `AdminRepository`. **The only module that touches the database handle.** |\n| `src/dal/*-repository.ts` | One repository per entity. |\n| `src/routes/*.ts` | Express routers, one file per resource. |\n| `src/scripts/` | CLI entry points: `seed`, `issue-token`, `setup-env`, `check-deps`. |\n| `public/` | Static dashboard (plain HTML + `fetch`, no framework). |\n\n## Authentication\n\nTwo HS256 JWTs in HttpOnly cookies:\n\n- **Admin token** (`scope: mint`, 8h) — mints merchant tokens and lists merchants. It cannot read data.\n- **Merchant token** (`scope: data`, 10m) — reads only the merchant named in its `merchantId` claim.\n\nThe design rule is one line: **the merchant id always comes from a token the backend signed.** A client-sent `X-Merchant-Id` is only compared against the token, never used; a mismatch is `403`. Switching merchants in the dashboard means asking the backend for a new token, not sending a different header.\n\n`requireAuth()` verifies the cookie, then runs the rest of the request inside an `AsyncLocalStorage` context. On a deployed instance it would give every visitor a credential that can mint any merchant's token. A real deployment needs an actual login issuing the admin token, and this middleware removed.\n\n## Data access\n\nEvery order query goes through a repository. `BaseRepository` reads the merchant id from the auth context and injects it into each `SELECT` and `INSERT`; subclasses never see the connection and never pass a merchant id, so a repository *cannot* forget the tenancy filter. `AdminRepository` covers `merchants` — the tenant list itself, which isn't merchant-scoped — and requires an admin caller instead.\n\n`test/architecture.test.ts` enforces the rule: if any module other than `base-repository.ts` imports the `db` handle, the suite fails. Standalone scripts are exempt.\n\n## Data model\n\nTwo tables, `merchants` and `orders`; canonical DDL in `src/db.ts`.\n\n`orders.type` is `'sale' | 'refund'`. A refund row records that a sale was reversed; it does not by itself reverse the sale row, and the revenue query currently sums both (TD-05).\n\n## Configuration\n\n| Variable | Default | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `JWT_SECRET` | generated | Missing on a local start → generated and appended to `.env` so server and CLI share it. |\n| `PORT` | `3000` | |\n| `DB_PATH` | `data/dashboard.db` | `:memory:` in tests. |\n| `ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL` | `8h` | |\n| `MERCHANT_TOKEN_TTL` | `10m` | |\n| `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION` | `on` | `off` disables the local admin cookie. |\n\n`npm run setup:env` creates `.env` from `.env.example`; it never overwrites an existing value.\n\n## Known gaps\n\nTracked in `tech_debt.md` (active) and `tech_debt_backlog.md` (deferred). {"parentUuid":"b72be2b6-ae0d-4c04-b23c-d269a57068b9","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cexzo7VhZE2Qy3WrC9NWS","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01WyNyw7YcEvAoHS67TyZysk","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\tech_debt.md","content":"# Tech debt — Tier 1 (MUST, urgent)\n\nThe items we're working on now. Everything else lives in [tech_debt_backlog.md](tech_debt_backlog.md) (Tier 2 and Tier 3) and is deliberately out of sight until this file is empty.\n\n## How this is ranked\n\nPriority balances **product impact** against **security and financial risk**, not raw severity:\n\n- An item that lets an attacker read another merchant's data, or that can cost money, outranks an item that only shows a wrong number on a dashboard.\n- Items that **amplify each other** are ranked together — an unbounded `limit` (TD-10) is worth more to an attacker the weaker the tenancy boundary is.\n- Wrong revenue math (TD-05) is ranked here anyway: merchants make decisions with that number, and it overstates income.\n\nIDs are stable (`TD-01` … `TD-17`) and don't change when the order does. Severity is the one from the first review.\n\n## Groups at a glance\n\nItems are grouped by the domain and files they touch, so each group can land as one commit.\n\n| Group | Items | Files | Status |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **A — Tenancy scoping through the DAL** | TD-02, TD-04 | `dal/`, `routes/orders.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | ✅ Done — [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md) |\n| **B — Authentication layer** | TD-01 | `auth/`, `server.ts`, `public/app.js` | ✅ Done — [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md) |\n| **C — Input validation at the API edge** | TD-10, TD-11 | `routes/orders.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | ⬜ Open |\n| **D — Output escaping in the dashboard** | TD-12 | `public/app.js` | ⬜ Open |\n| **E — Refund semantics in money math** | TD-05 | `dal/orders-repository.ts`, `routes/revenue.ts` | ⬜ Open |\n\nSuggested order for what's left: **C → E → D**. C stops new payloads from being stored, E fixes the money number, D makes rendering safe regardless of what's already in the database.\n\n---\n\n## Group C — Input validation at the API edge\n\n*Files: [src/routes/orders.ts](src/routes/orders.ts), [src/routes/metrics.ts](src/routes/metrics.ts)*\n\nBoth are \"the API trusts whatever the client sends\". Same layer, same kind of fix (one validation shape applied to query params and body).\n\n- [ ] **TD-10 · `limit` is not validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** in SQLite `LIMIT -1` means \"no limit\", so `?limit=-1` returns every order of the merchant in one request — an easy way to exhaust the server, and a bulk export of everything a compromised session can reach.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:11](src/routes/orders.ts:11), [src/routes/metrics.ts:43](src/routes/metrics.ts:43)\n  - What happens: `Number(req.query.limit)` can yield `NaN`, a decimal, or a negative number. There is no upper bound.\n\n- [ ] **TD-11 · The `POST /api/orders` body is barely validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** it's the entry point that feeds TD-12, and it lets corrupt money into the database — negative or fractional amounts in a column that holds integer cents.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:25](src/routes/orders.ts:25)\n  - What happens: `type` accepts any string (not only `sale`/`refund`), `total_amount` accepts negatives and decimals, and `customer_email` isn't validated as an email.\n\n## Group D — Output escaping in the dashboard\n\n*File: [public/app.js](public/app.js)*\n\n- [ ] **TD-12 · Stored XSS in the orders table** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** the dashboard executes attacker-controlled markup, and the payload is planted through `POST /api/orders` (TD-11).\n  - **Why it ships after C:** C stops new payloads from being stored; D makes rendering safe regardless of what's already in the database. Everything else lives in [tech_debt_backlog.md](tech_debt_backlog.md) (Tier 2 and Tier 3) and is deliberately out of sight until this file is empty.\n\n## How this is ranked\n\nPriority balances **product impact** against **security and financial risk**, not raw severity:\n\n- An item that lets an attacker read another merchant's data, or that can cost money, outranks an item that only shows a wrong number on a dashboard.\n- Items that **amplify each other** are ranked together — spoofing a merchant id (TD-01) plus an unbounded `limit` (TD-10) turns a small bug into a bulk data dump.\n- Wrong revenue math (TD-05) is ranked here anyway: merchants make decisions with that number, and it overstates income.\n\nIDs are stable (`TD-01` … `TD-17`) and don't change when the order does. Severity is the one from the first review.\n\n## Groups at a glance\n\nItems are grouped by the domain and files they touch, so each group can land as one commit.\n\n| Group | Items | Files | Ships as |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **A — Tenancy scoping through the DAL** | TD-02, TD-04 | `dal/orders-dal.ts`, `routes/orders.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | One commit |\n| **B — Authentication layer** | TD-01 | `auth.ts`, `server.ts`, `public/app.js` | One commit |\n| **C — Input validation at the API edge** | TD-10, TD-11 | `routes/orders.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | One commit |\n| **D — Output escaping in the dashboard** | TD-12 | `public/app.js` | One commit |\n| **E — Refund semantics in money math** | TD-05 | `dal/orders-dal.ts`, `routes/revenue.ts` | One commit |\n\n**Files touched by more than one group** — sequence these to avoid conflicts:\n\n| File | Groups |\n|---|---|\n| `src/dal/orders-dal.ts` | A, E |\n| `src/routes/orders.ts` | A, C |\n| `src/routes/metrics.ts` | A, C |\n| `public/app.js` | B, D |\n\nSuggested order: **A → C → E → B → D**. A defines the shape every query goes through, so doing it first keeps C and E from being rewritten; B changes how `merchantId` arrives, which is easier once A guarantees every query is scoped by it.\n\n---\n\n## Group A — Tenancy scoping through the DAL\n\n*Files: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts](src/dal/orders-dal.ts), [src/routes/orders.ts](src/routes/orders.ts), [src/routes/metrics.ts](src/routes/metrics.ts)*\n\nThese two are one piece of work: make every order query go through the DAL **and** carry the merchant scope. Fixing either alone leaves a hole.\n\n- [ ] **TD-02 · `GET /api/orders/:id` does not filter by merchant** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** direct cross-tenant read of order data (customer emails and amounts), independent of TD-01. Even with real auth in place, this endpoint would still leak.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:16](src/routes/orders.ts:16), [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:38)\n  - What happens: `ordersDal.getById(id)` looks up by `id` only and ignores `req.merchantId`.\n\n- [ ] **TD-04 · `metrics.ts` bypasses the DAL** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** the DAL is where tenancy filtering, auditing, and caching are supposed to live, and `metrics.ts` is outside it. Every Tier 1 fix applied to `ordersDal` would silently *not* cover the metrics endpoints, which read the same order rows — so the bypass must be closed as part of the security work, not after it.\n  - Where: [src/routes/metrics.ts:5](src/routes/metrics.ts:5)\n  - What happens: it opens its own `new Database(DB_PATH, { readonly: true })` and runs raw SQL. Two connections to the same database, and `DB_PATH` resolved twice.\n\n## Group B — Authentication layer\n\n*Files: [src/auth.ts](src/auth.ts), [src/server.ts](src/server.ts), [public/app.js](public/app.js)*\n\n- [ ] **TD-01 · The `X-Merchant-Id` header is not verified** — Severity: High\n  - **Why first in priority:** this is the whole authorization model. Any client can impersonate any merchant by editing one header, which turns every other endpoint into a cross-tenant data source. It also multiplies TD-02 and TD-10.\n  - **Why it ships after group A:** the scope enforcement in the DAL is what makes the auth change meaningful; changing how `merchantId` is produced is a smaller, isolated diff once every query already consumes it.\n  - Where: [src/auth.ts:16](src/auth.ts:16), [public/app.js:9](public/app.js:9)\n  - What happens: `authMiddleware` only checks that the header is present and copies it to `req.merchantId`. There is no signature, no session, no verification that the caller owns that merchant.\n  - Note: documented as an intentional simplification for the challenge (\"Real auth would be a signed JWT\"), so the decision to make is *what shape* replaces it — and whether the dashboard's merchant picker survives it.\n\n## Group C — Input validation at the API edge\n\n*Files: [src/routes/orders.ts](src/routes/orders.ts), [src/routes/metrics.ts](src/routes/metrics.ts)*\n\nBoth are \"the API trusts whatever the client sends\". Same layer, same kind of fix (one validation shape applied to query params and body).\n\n- [ ] **TD-10 · `limit` is not validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** in SQLite `LIMIT -1` means \"no limit\", so `?limit=-1` returns every order of the merchant in one request. Combined with TD-01 that's a bulk export of the whole database, and on its own it's an easy way to exhaust the server.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:11](src/routes/orders.ts:11), [src/routes/metrics.ts:43](src/routes/metrics.ts:43)\n  - What happens: `Number(req.query.limit)` can yield `NaN`, a decimal, or a negative number. There is no upper bound.\n\n- [ ] **TD-11 · The `POST /api/orders` body is barely validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** it's the entry point that feeds TD-12, and it lets corrupt money into the database — negative or fractional amounts in a column that holds integer cents.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:25](src/routes/orders.ts:25)\n  - What happens: `type` accepts any string (not only `sale`/`refund`), `total_amount` accepts negatives and decimals, and `customer_email` isn't validated as an email.\n\n## Group D — Output escaping in the dashboard\n\n*File: [public/app.js](public/app.js)*\n\n- [ ] **TD-12 · Stored XSS in the orders table** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** any merchant's dashboard executes attacker-controlled markup, and the payload is planted through `POST /api/orders` (TD-11). With TD-01 an attacker can plant it in *someone else's* dashboard.\n  - **Why it ships after C:** C stops new payloads from being stored; D makes rendering safe regardless of what's already in the database. Both are needed — C alone doesn't clean existing rows.\n  - Where: [public/app.js:35](public/app.js:35)\n  - What happens: each row is built with `innerHTML`, interpolating `o.customer_email` and `o.type` unsanitized.\n\n## Group E — Refund semantics in money math\n\n*Files: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts](src/dal/orders-dal.ts), [src/routes/revenue.ts](src/routes/revenue.ts)*\n\n- [ ] **TD-05 · Revenue counts refunds as income** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** the headline number of the product is wrong, and wrong in the optimistic direction. A merchant reading \"Revenue (last 30 days)\" is told they earned money they refunded.\n  - **Related, deferred:** TD-06 (summary metrics treat refunds as sales) is the same class of bug on informational numbers and sits in the backlog. If group A has already moved the metrics queries into the DAL, fixing TD-06 in this same commit may be nearly free — decide when you get there.\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:54)\n  - What happens: `sumAmountByMerchant` runs `SUM(total_amount)` without looking at `type`. Refunds are stored with a positive amount (see [src/scripts/seed.ts:43](src/scripts/seed.ts:43)), so they add instead of subtracting. Per [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), a refund represents a reversed sale.\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"c83ad8f6-0cd2-49e6-9487-f5926d62ff8b","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}
