Everything else lives in [tech_debt_backlog.md](tech_debt_backlog.md) (Tier 2 and Tier 3) and is deliberately out of sight until this file is empty.\n\n## How this is ranked\n\nPriority balances **product impact** against **security and financial risk**, not raw severity:\n\n- An item that lets an attacker read another merchant's data, or that can cost money, outranks an item that only shows a wrong number on a dashboard.\n- Items that **amplify each other** are ranked together — an unbounded `limit` (TD-10) is worth more to an attacker the weaker the tenancy boundary is.\n- Wrong revenue math (TD-05) is ranked here anyway: merchants make decisions with that number, and it overstates income.\n\nIDs are stable (`TD-01` … `TD-17`) and don't change when the order does. Severity is the one from the first review.\n\n## Groups at a glance\n\nItems are grouped by the domain and files they touch, so each group can land as one commit.\n\n| Group | Items | Files | Status |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **A — Tenancy scoping through the DAL** | TD-02, TD-04 | `dal/`, `routes/orders.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | ✅ Done — [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md) |\n| **B — Authentication layer** | TD-01 | `auth/`, `server.ts`, `public/app.js` | ✅ Done — [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md) |\n| **C — Input validation at the API edge** | TD-10, TD-11 | `routes/orders.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | ⬜ Open |\n| **D — Output escaping in the dashboard** | TD-12 | `public/app.js` | ⬜ Open |\n| **E — Refund semantics in money math** | TD-05 | `dal/orders-repository.ts`, `routes/revenue.ts` | ⬜ Open |\n\nSuggested order for what's left: **C → E → D**. C stops new payloads from being stored, E fixes the money number, D makes rendering safe regardless of what's already in the database.\n\n---\n\n## Group C — Input validation at the API edge\n\n*Files: [src/routes/orders.ts](src/routes/orders.ts), [src/routes/metrics.ts](src/routes/metrics.ts)*\n\nBoth are \"the API trusts whatever the client sends\". Same layer, same kind of fix (one validation shape applied to query params and body).\n\n- [ ] **TD-10 · `limit` is not validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** in SQLite `LIMIT -1` means \"no limit\", so `?limit=-1` returns every order of the merchant in one request — an easy way to exhaust the server, and a bulk export of everything a compromised session can reach.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:11](src/routes/orders.ts:11), [src/routes/metrics.ts:43](src/routes/metrics.ts:43)\n  - What happens: `Number(req.query.limit)` can yield `NaN`, a decimal, or a negative number. There is no upper bound.\n\n- [ ] **TD-11 · The `POST /api/orders` body is barely validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** it's the entry point that feeds TD-12, and it lets corrupt money into the database — negative or fractional amounts in a column that holds integer cents.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:25](src/routes/orders.ts:25)\n  - What happens: `type` accepts any string (not only `sale`/`refund`), `total_amount` accepts negatives and decimals, and `customer_email` isn't validated as an email.\n\n## Group D — Output escaping in the dashboard\n\n*File: [public/app.js](public/app.js)*\n\n- [ ] **TD-12 · Stored XSS in the orders table** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** the dashboard executes attacker-controlled markup, and the payload is planted through `POST /api/orders` (TD-11).\n  - **Why it ships after C:** C stops new payloads from being stored; D makes rendering safe regardless of what's already in the database. Both are needed — C alone doesn't clean existing rows.\n  - Where: [public/app.js:78](public/app.js:78)\n  - What happens: each row is built with `innerHTML`, interpolating `o.customer_email` and `o.type` unsanitized. (The file was rewritten for the session flow in plan 005; this line was left as-is on purpose so the fix is its own reviewable change.)\n\n## Group E — Refund semantics in money math\n\n*Files: [src/dal/orders-repository.ts](src/dal/orders-repository.ts), [src/routes/revenue.ts](src/routes/revenue.ts)*\n\n- [ ] **TD-05 · Revenue counts refunds as income** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** the headline number of the product is wrong, and wrong in the optimistic direction. A merchant reading \"Revenue (last 30 days)\" is told they earned money they refunded.\n  - **Related, deferred:** TD-06 (summary metrics treat refunds as sales) is the same class of bug on informational numbers and sits in the backlog. Now that metrics go through `MetricsRepository`, fixing TD-06 in the same commit is nearly free.\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-repository.ts:99](src/dal/orders-repository.ts:99)\n  - What happens: `sumAmount` runs `SUM(total_amount)` without looking at `type`. Refunds are stored with a positive amount (see [src/scripts/seed.ts:43](src/scripts/seed.ts:43)), so they add instead of subtracting. Per [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), a refund represents a reversed sale.\n\n---\n\n# Resolved\n\n- [x] **TD-01 · The `X-Merchant-Id` header is not verified** — Severity: High\n  - Resolved by [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md): sessions are HS256 JWTs in HttpOnly cookies. Data access requires a merchant-scoped token whose `merchantId` claim the backend signs; a client-sent `X-Merchant-Id` is only compared, never used, and a mismatch is `403 merchant_mismatch`. Merchant switching goes through `POST /api/auth/token`, guarded by an admin token that cannot read data.\n  - Caveat carried forward: `devAdminSession` hands an admin cookie to loopback requests for local development. Gated on the TCP peer address and disabled with `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION=off`; it must never run on a deployed instance.\n\n- [x] **TD-02 · `GET /api/orders/:id` does not filter by merchant** — Severity: High\n  - Resolved by [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md): `OrdersRepository.getById` goes through `BaseRepository`, which injects the merchant filter, so another merchant's order returns `404`. Covered by `test/base-repository.test.ts` and `test/auth-guard.test.ts`.\n\n- [x] **TD-04 · `metrics.ts` bypasses the DAL** — Severity: Medium\n  - Resolved by [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md): metrics queries moved into `MetricsRepository`, and the second read-only SQLite connection is gone. `test/architecture.test.ts` fails if any module other than `base-repository.ts` imports the database handle, so the bypass can't come back quietly.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":51,"oldLines":7,"newStart":51,"newLines":7,"lines":[" - [ ] **TD-12 · Stored XSS in the orders table** — Severity: High","   - **Why here:** the dashboard executes attacker-controlled markup, and the payload is planted through `POST /api/orders` (TD-11).","   - **Why it ships after C:** C stops new payloads from being stored; D makes rendering safe regardless of what's already in the database. Los atributos de la cookie** — [src/auth/cookies.ts:50](src/auth/cookies.ts:50)\n\n```ts\nconst attributes = [\n  `${name}=${encodeURIComponent(value)}`,\n  'Path=/', 'HttpOnly', 'SameSite=Strict',\n  `Max-Age=${Math.max(0, Math.floor(options.maxAgeSeconds))}`,\n];\n```\n\n**3. El frontend no toca el token** — [public/app.js:20](public/app.js:20). Solo pide que se emita; el navegador guarda la cookie y la manda sola en las siguientes peticiones gracias a `credentials: 'same-origin'`:\n\n```js\nconst response = await request('/api/auth/token', {\n  method: 'POST',\n  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n  body: JSON.stringify({ merchantId }),\n});\nreturn response.ok;             // ← nunca lee el token\n```\n\n**4. ADMIN_COOKIE : MERCHANT_COOKIE;\n```\n\n**Por qué no lo ves en la pestaña de red:** `HttpOnly` significa exactamente eso. El token no está en el body, no lo puede leer `document.cookie` y por tanto tampoco lo puede robar un XSS. En DevTools sí se puede ver, pero en otro sitio: en **Network → la petición → Response Headers → `set-cookie`**, o en **Application → Cookies → `http://localhost:3000`**, donde aparece `merchant_session` con la casilla HttpOnly marcada.\n\nTu `curl` no lo mostró porque el comando copiado de Chrome no incluye `-i` ni `-v`, así que solo imprime el body, que está vacío a propósito. Hoy el revenue está inflado un **29.7%** para `m_acme` y un **19.2%** para `m_bistro`."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2454,"cache_read_input_tokens":367109,"output_tokens":3220,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":62},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2454,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":3220,"cache_read_input_tokens":367109,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2454,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2454},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cey3oeqTTMW7pcyjjZcrs","type":"assistant","uuid":"11de4956-4f93-43ee-a025-083b91be0074","timestamp":"2026-09-12T06:11:07.876Z","effort":"medium","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}
{"parentUuid":"11de4956-4f93-43ee-a025-083b91be0074","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cey3oftxw5Na8ZJ7rTD7M","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01An3YHRF2UhduRupyZKuKdA","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\006-refund-semantics-in-money-math.md","content":"# 006 — Refund semantics in money math\n\n**Status:** draft\n\nCloses Tier 1 group **E** (TD-05) from [tech_debt.md](../tech_debt.md), and TD-06 from [tech_debt_backlog.md](../tech_debt_backlog.md) since both are the same bug in two places.\n\n## Context\n\n`orders.type` is `'sale' | 'refund'`, and per [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) a refund records a reversed sale. But refunds are stored with a **positive** `total_amount`, and every money query sums `total_amount` without looking at `type`. So a refund *increases* revenue.\n\nMeasured on the current seeded database:\n\n| Merchant | Sales | Refunds | Reported today | Correct (net) | Overstated by |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `m_acme` | 375 736 | 48 628 | 424 364 | 327 108 | **+29.7 %** |\n| `m_bistro` | 383 990 | 33 669 | 417 659 | 350 321 | **+19.2 %** |\n\nA refund doesn't just fail to subtract — it adds the same amount again, so the error is roughly twice the refunded volume. This is the number the product exists to show, wrong in the optimistic direction, which is why it ranks with the security work rather than below it.\n\nSchema facts that shape the fix (verified against the database):\n\n- `total_amount` is always positive, for both types.\n- There is **no column linking a refund to the sale it reverses** — netting can only be amount-based, not order-based.\n- Every row is `status = 'completed'`; no other status exists yet.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. One definition of money, in one place\n\nAll money math moves behind named SQL expressions in `OrdersRepository`, so no route or repository can invent its own:\n\n```ts\n/** Signed amount: sales add, refunds subtract. */\nconst NET_AMOUNT = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN -total_amount ELSE total_amount END\";\nconst SALES_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'sale' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\nconst REFUNDS_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\n```\n\nRejected alternative: **store refunds as negative amounts**. It makes every query trivially correct, but it rewrites existing rows (migration + backfill), breaks the documented meaning of `total_amount`, and makes \"how much did we refund\" harder to ask. Netting at read time keeps the raw facts intact.\n\n### 2. `GET /api/revenue` returns net revenue, with the breakdown\n\n```json\n{\n  \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"from\": \"2026-08-01\", \"to\": \"2026-09-12\",\n  \"revenue_cents\": 327108,\n  \"revenue\": 3271.08,\n  \"gross_sales_cents\": 375736,\n  \"refunds_cents\": 48628\n}\n```\n\n`revenue_cents` keeps its name and becomes **net** (sales − refunds). The two new fields make the number auditable: a merchant seeing revenue drop should be able to tell whether sales fell or refunds rose, without a second endpoint.\n\nNet revenue **can be negative** (a period with only refunds). That's correct and is asserted by a test rather than clamped to zero.\n\n### 3. `GET /api/metrics/summary` counts sales as orders (TD-06)\n\n| Field | Today | After |\n|---|---|---|\n| `total_orders` | all rows | **sales only** — a refund is not an order placed |\n| `refunded_orders` | — | **new**: number of refund rows |\n| `unique_customers` | distinct emails on any row | distinct emails **with at least one sale** |\n| `avg_order_value_cents` | average over all rows | average over **sales only** |\n\n### 4. `GET /api/metrics/top-customers` ranks by net spend\n\n`total_spent` becomes net per customer (sales − refunds) and `order_count` counts sales. A customer who refunded everything then ranks last instead of top — which is the point of the report.\n\n### 5. Gate against regression\n\n- **Unit tests on the repository** with a fixed dataset (golden numbers), plus property-style cases: revenue of a fully refunded period is `0`; a refunds-only period is negative; adding a sale and its refund leaves revenue unchanged.\n- **Architecture test extension:** assert that `total_amount` is only summed inside `src/dal/` — a route or script that computes money on its own fails the suite. This is what stops the next endpoint from re-introducing the bug.\n\n### 6. Dashboard\n\nThe \"Revenue (last 30 days)\" card is labelled **\"Revenue (last 30 days, net of refunds)\"**, and a small line under it shows gross and refunds. Otherwise the number silently changes by ~20–30 % with no explanation.\n\n### 7. Commits\n\n| # | Content | Tech debt |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `OrdersRepository`: net expressions, `revenue()` returning the breakdown; revenue route; tests | TD-05 |\n| 2 | `MetricsRepository`: sales-based counts, net `total_spent`; metrics routes; tests | TD-06 |\n| 3 | Architecture test extension (money math only inside `src/dal/`) | — |\n| 4 | Dashboard labels + gross/refunds line | — |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — `avg_order_value_cents`: average of sale amounts** (recommended) or net revenue ÷ number of sales? The first answers \"what does a typical order look like\"; the second bakes refunds into a per-order figure and is harder to explain.\n- **Q2 — `total_orders` counting sales only** (recommended), with `refunded_orders` alongside. The alternative keeps today's total and adds a breakdown, which avoids a visible drop in the dashboard number but keeps calling refunds \"orders\".\n- **Q3 — Adding `gross_sales_cents` / `refunds_cents` to the revenue response** (recommended). It's a response-shape change; say if you'd rather keep the payload as-is.\n- **Q4 — Ignoring `status` for now** (recommended): every row is `completed`, so filtering would be untested speculation. If cancelled/pending rows ever exist, money math must exclude them — I'd log it as tech debt instead of guessing now.\n- **Q5 — New backlog item for the missing refund→sale link.** Refunds can't be matched to their original sale, so a refund can exceed the sale it reverses, or land in a different period and make that period negative. I'd add it as **TD-18 (Tier 2)** — needs your go, since `tech_debt*.md` is yours.\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/dal/metrics-repository.ts`\n- `src/routes/revenue.ts`, `src/routes/metrics.ts`\n- `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`\n- `test/base-repository.test.ts` (money cases), new `test/money.test.ts`, `test/architecture.test.ts`, `test/auth-guard.test.ts` (updated expectations)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Input validation (TD-10, TD-11) and XSS (TD-12) — groups C and D.\n- Date-range semantics (TD-07) and mixed timestamp formats (TD-08) — backlog; this plan doesn't touch the `created_at` filters.\n- Storing refunds as negative amounts, or adding a refund→sale foreign key (Q5).\n- `docs/` updates — authorization to be requested after validation (CLAUDE.md §6): `api.md` (response shapes) and `architecture.md` (the refund rule).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — new money tests plus the existing suite.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. Golden check against the seeded database: `m_acme` revenue reports `327108`, not `424364`; `m_bistro` `350321`, not `417659`.\n4. `curl /api/revenue` returns net plus gross and refunds, and they reconcile (`gross - refunds === net`).\n5. `curl /api/metrics/summary` → `total_orders` + `refunded_orders` equals the old total; `avg_order_value_cents` computed over sales only.\n6. `top-customers`: a customer with more refunds than sales shows a negative `total_spent` and ranks last.\n7. Browser: the card reads \"net of refunds\" and shows the gross/refunds line; the number matches the API.\n8. Architecture test fails if a route sums `total_amount` (verified by temporarily adding such a line).\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits. No schema or data migration is involved — the fix is read-side only, so rolling back cannot corrupt stored rows.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2454,"cache_read_input_tokens":367109,"output_tokens":3220,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":62},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2454,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":3220,"cache_read_input_tokens":367109,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2454,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2454},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01An3YHRF2UhduRupyZKuKdA":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\006-refund-semantics-in-money-math.md","content":"# 006 — Refund semantics in money math\n\n**Status:** draft\n\nCloses Tier 1 group **E** (TD-05) from [tech_debt.md](../tech_debt.md), and TD-06 from [tech_debt_backlog.md](../tech_debt_backlog.md) since both are the same bug in two places.\n\n## Context\n\n`orders.type` is `'sale' | 'refund'`, and per [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) a refund records a reversed sale. {"parentUuid":"0b2b0f89-7640-441c-bbd1-82c521226c40","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"aae052da-f58c-4816-9cab-ff1be61b699b","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01An3YHRF2UhduRupyZKuKdA","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\006-refund-semantics-in-money-math.md (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"b44ea96b-eb6c-4cee-bbab-210501afa6b2","timestamp":"2026-09-12T06:11:44.984Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"create","filePath":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\006-refund-semantics-in-money-math.md","content":"# 006 — Refund semantics in money math\n\n**Status:** draft\n\nCloses Tier 1 group **E** (TD-05) from [tech_debt.md](../tech_debt.md), and TD-06 from [tech_debt_backlog.md](../tech_debt_backlog.md) since both are the same bug in two places.\n\n## Context\n\n`orders.type` is `'sale' | 'refund'`, and per [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) a refund records a reversed sale. But refunds are stored with a **positive** `total_amount`, and every money query sums `total_amount` without looking at `type`. So a refund *increases* revenue.\n\nMeasured on the current seeded database:\n\n| Merchant | Sales | Refunds | Reported today | Correct (net) | Overstated by |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `m_acme` | 375 736 | 48 628 | 424 364 | 327 108 | **+29.7 %** |\n| `m_bistro` | 383 990 | 33 669 | 417 659 | 350 321 | **+19.2 %** |\n\nA refund doesn't just fail to subtract — it adds the same amount again, so the error is roughly twice the refunded volume. This is the number the product exists to show, wrong in the optimistic direction, which is why it ranks with the security work rather than below it.\n\nSchema facts that shape the fix (verified against the database):\n\n- `total_amount` is always positive, for both types.\n- There is **no column linking a refund to the sale it reverses** — netting can only be amount-based, not order-based.\n- Every row is `status = 'completed'`; no other status exists yet.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. One definition of money, in one place\n\nAll money math moves behind named SQL expressions in `OrdersRepository`, so no route or repository can invent its own:\n\n```ts\n/** Signed amount: sales add, refunds subtract. */\nconst NET_AMOUNT = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN -total_amount ELSE total_amount END\";\nconst SALES_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'sale' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\nconst REFUNDS_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\n```\n\nRejected alternative: **store refunds as negative amounts**. It makes every query trivially correct, but it rewrites existing rows (migration + backfill), breaks the documented meaning of `total_amount`, and makes \"how much did we refund\" harder to ask. Netting at read time keeps the raw facts intact.\n\n### 2. `GET /api/revenue` returns net revenue, with the breakdown\n\n```json\n{\n  \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"from\": \"2026-08-01\", \"to\": \"2026-09-12\",\n  \"revenue_cents\": 327108,\n  \"revenue\": 3271.08,\n  \"gross_sales_cents\": 375736,\n  \"refunds_cents\": 48628\n}\n```\n\n`revenue_cents` keeps its name and becomes **net** (sales − refunds). The two new fields make the number auditable: a merchant seeing revenue drop should be able to tell whether sales fell or refunds rose, without a second endpoint.\n\nNet revenue **can be negative** (a period with only refunds). That's correct and is asserted by a test rather than clamped to zero.\n\n### 3. `GET /api/metrics/summary` counts sales as orders (TD-06)\n\n| Field | Today | After |\n|---|---|---|\n| `total_orders` | all rows | **sales only** — a refund is not an order placed |\n| `refunded_orders` | — | **new**: number of refund rows |\n| `unique_customers` | distinct emails on any row | distinct emails **with at least one sale** |\n| `avg_order_value_cents` | average over all rows | average over **sales only** |\n\n### 4. `GET /api/metrics/top-customers` ranks by net spend\n\n`total_spent` becomes net per customer (sales − refunds) and `order_count` counts sales. A customer who refunded everything then ranks last instead of top — which is the point of the report.\n\n### 5. Gate against regression\n\n- **Unit tests on the repository** with a fixed dataset (golden numbers), plus property-style cases: revenue of a fully refunded period is `0`; a refunds-only period is negative; adding a sale and its refund leaves revenue unchanged.\n- **Architecture test extension:** assert that `total_amount` is only summed inside `src/dal/` — a route or script that computes money on its own fails the suite. This is what stops the next endpoint from re-introducing the bug.\n\n### 6. Dashboard\n\nThe \"Revenue (last 30 days)\" card is labelled **\"Revenue (last 30 days, net of refunds)\"**, and a small line under it shows gross and refunds. Otherwise the number silently changes by ~20–30 % with no explanation.\n\n### 7. Commits\n\n| # | Content | Tech debt |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `OrdersRepository`: net expressions, `revenue()` returning the breakdown; revenue route; tests | TD-05 |\n| 2 | `MetricsRepository`: sales-based counts, net `total_spent`; metrics routes; tests | TD-06 |\n| 3 | Architecture test extension (money math only inside `src/dal/`) | — |\n| 4 | Dashboard labels + gross/refunds line | — |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — `avg_order_value_cents`: average of sale amounts** (recommended) or net revenue ÷ number of sales? The first answers \"what does a typical order look like\"; the second bakes refunds into a per-order figure and is harder to explain.\n- **Q2 — `total_orders` counting sales only** (recommended), with `refunded_orders` alongside. The alternative keeps today's total and adds a breakdown, which avoids a visible drop in the dashboard number but keeps calling refunds \"orders\".\n- **Q3 — Adding `gross_sales_cents` / `refunds_cents` to the revenue response** (recommended). It's a response-shape change; say if you'd rather keep the payload as-is.\n- **Q4 — Ignoring `status` for now** (recommended): every row is `completed`, so filtering would be untested speculation. If cancelled/pending rows ever exist, money math must exclude them — I'd log it as tech debt instead of guessing now.\n- **Q5 — New backlog item for the missing refund→sale link.** Refunds can't be matched to their original sale, so a refund can exceed the sale it reverses, or land in a different period and make that period negative. I'd add it as **TD-18 (Tier 2)** — needs your go, since `tech_debt*.md` is yours.\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/dal/metrics-repository.ts`\n- `src/routes/revenue.ts`, `src/routes/metrics.ts`\n- `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`\n- `test/base-repository.test.ts` (money cases), new `test/money.test.ts`, `test/architecture.test.ts`, `test/auth-guard.test.ts` (updated expectations)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Input validation (TD-10, TD-11) and XSS (TD-12) — groups C and D.\n- Date-range semantics (TD-07) and mixed timestamp formats (TD-08) — backlog; this plan doesn't touch the `created_at` filters.\n- Storing refunds as negative amounts, or adding a refund→sale foreign key (Q5).\n- `docs/` updates — authorization to be requested after validation (CLAUDE.md §6): `api.md` (response shapes) and `architecture.md` (the refund rule).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — new money tests plus the existing suite.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. Golden check against the seeded database: `m_acme` revenue reports `327108`, not `424364`; `m_bistro` `350321`, not `417659`.\n4. `curl /api/revenue` returns net plus gross and refunds, and they reconcile (`gross - refunds === net`).\n5. `curl /api/metrics/summary` → `total_orders` + `refunded_orders` equals the old total; `avg_order_value_cents` computed over sales only.\n6. `top-customers`: a customer with more refunds than sales shows a negative `total_spent` and ranks last.\n7. Browser: the card reads \"net of refunds\" and shows the gross/refunds line; the number matches the API.\n8. Architecture test fails if a route sums `total_amount` (verified by temporarily adding such a line).\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits. No schema or data migration is involved — the fix is read-side only, so rolling back cannot corrupt stored rows.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0b2b0f89-7640-441c-bbd1-82c521226c40","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

Hoy el revenue está inflado un 29.7% en `m_acme` y un 19.2% en `m_bistro`.\n\n**La propuesta:**\n\n- **Una sola definición de dinero:** expresiones SQL con nombre dentro de `OrdersRepository` (`NET_AMOUNT`, `SALES_ONLY`, `REFUNDS_ONLY`), para que ninguna ruta invente su propio cálculo.\n- **Netear al leer, no al guardar.** Descarté guardar los refunds en negativo: haría trivial cada query, pero exige migrar filas, rompe el significado documentado de `total_amount` y complica preguntar \"cuánto devolvimos\".\n- **`/api/revenue` devuelve neto más el desglose** (`gross_sales_cents` y `refunds_cents`), para que se pueda auditar si el revenue bajó porque cayeron las ventas o porque subieron las devoluciones.\n- **Puede salir negativo** en un periodo de solo devoluciones. Es correcto, y hay un test que lo fija en vez de recortarlo a cero.\n- **Métricas (TD-06):** `total_orders` cuenta ventas, aparece `refunded_orders`, y `top-customers` ordena por gasto neto, así que quien devolvió todo deja de salir primero.\n- **La reja anti-regresión:** extender el test de arquitectura para que sumar `total_amount` fuera de `src/dal/` haga fallar la suite.\n- **En el dashboard**, la tarjeta dirá \"net of refunds\" y mostrará bruto y devoluciones. Si no, el número baja un 20-30% sin explicación.\n\n**Cinco decisiones que necesito que confirmes (Q1 a Q5):**\n- **Q1:** el valor medio de pedido se calcula sobre ventas, no sobre neto entre pedidos.\n- **Q2:** `total_orders` cuenta solo ventas. Esto hará bajar visiblemente ese número en el dashboard.\n- **Q3:** añadir los dos campos de desglose a la respuesta de revenue.\n- **Q4:** ignorar `status` por ahora, porque todas las filas son `completed` y filtrar sería especular.\n- **Q5:** un hallazgo nuevo que salió al mirar los datos: **no hay ninguna columna que enlace un refund con su venta original**. Por eso el neteo solo puede ser por importes, y un refund puede superar a la venta que revierte o caer en otro periodo. {"parentUuid":"daf294c6-81b1-4cc4-9ba4-b46c4ada613b","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cey4sMyg4ov5k6AGt7bfG","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01GxwR9UYAPCtyFnqYNDZwUf","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\006-refund-semantics-in-money-math.md","content":"# 006 — Refund semantics in money math\n\n**Status:** draft (rev 2 — open questions answered by the user)\n\nCloses Tier 1 group **E** (TD-05) from [tech_debt.md](../tech_debt.md), and TD-06 from [tech_debt_backlog.md](../tech_debt_backlog.md) since both are the same bug in two places.\n\n## Context\n\n`orders.type` is `'sale' | 'refund'`, and per [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) a refund records a reversed sale. But refunds are stored with a **positive** `total_amount`, and every money query sums `total_amount` without looking at `type`. So a refund *increases* revenue.\n\nMeasured on the current seeded database:\n\n| Merchant | Sales | Refunds | Reported today | Correct (net) | Overstated by |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `m_acme` | 375 736 | 48 628 | 424 364 | 327 108 | **+29.7 %** |\n| `m_bistro` | 383 990 | 33 669 | 417 659 | 350 321 | **+19.2 %** |\n\nA refund doesn't just fail to subtract — it adds the same amount again, so the error is roughly twice the refunded volume. This is the number the product exists to show, wrong in the optimistic direction.\n\nSchema facts that shape the fix (verified against the database):\n\n- `total_amount` is always positive, for both types.\n- There is **no column linking a refund to the sale it reverses** — netting can only be amount-based (logged as TD-18).\n- Every row is `status = 'completed'`; no other status exists yet.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. One definition of money, in one place\n\nAll money math moves behind named SQL expressions in `OrdersRepository`, so no route or repository can invent its own:\n\n```ts\n/** Signed amount: sales add, refunds subtract. */\nconst NET_AMOUNT = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN -total_amount ELSE total_amount END\";\nconst SALES_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'sale' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\nconst REFUNDS_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\n```\n\nRejected alternative: **store refunds as negative amounts**. It makes every query trivially correct, but it rewrites existing rows (migration + backfill), breaks the documented meaning of `total_amount`, and makes \"how much did we refund\" harder to ask. Netting at read time keeps the raw facts intact.\n\n### 2. `GET /api/revenue` returns net revenue, with the breakdown (Q3)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"from\": \"2026-08-01\", \"to\": \"2026-09-12\",\n  \"revenue_cents\": 327108,\n  \"revenue\": 3271.08,\n  \"gross_sales_cents\": 375736,\n  \"refunds_cents\": 48628\n}\n```\n\n`revenue_cents` keeps its name and becomes **net** (sales − refunds). The two new fields make the number auditable: a merchant seeing revenue drop can tell whether sales fell or refunds rose.\n\nNet revenue **can be negative** (a period with only refunds). That's correct and is asserted by a test rather than clamped to zero.\n\n### 3. `GET /api/metrics/summary` (Q1, Q2 — both figures, named explicitly)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"sales_orders\": 35,\n  \"refund_orders\": 5,\n  \"unique_customers\": 3,\n  \"avg_order_value_cents\": 10735,\n  \"avg_net_order_value_cents\": 9346\n}\n```\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `sales_orders` | Rows of type `sale` |\n| `refund_orders` | Rows of type `refund` |\n| `unique_customers` | Distinct customers **with at least one sale** |\n| `avg_order_value_cents` | Average amount of a sale — \"what does a typical order look like\" |\n| `avg_net_order_value_cents` | Net revenue ÷ number of sales — what a sale is worth *after* refunds |\n\nThe ambiguous `total_orders` is **removed** rather than redefined: per Q2 the two counts get dedicated names so nobody has to guess whether refunds are included. Any client reading `total_orders` gets `undefined` instead of a silently changed meaning — a loud break rather than a quiet one, and the only client is this repo's dashboard.\n\n### 4. `GET /api/metrics/top-customers` ranks by net spend\n\n`total_spent` becomes net per customer (sales − refunds) and `order_count` counts sales. A customer who refunded everything ranks last instead of top — which is the point of the report.\n\n### 5. `status` is ignored for now (Q4)\n\nEvery row is `completed`; filtering would be untested speculation. If other statuses ever appear, money math must exclude the non-completed ones — noted in the docs so it isn't forgotten.\n\n### 6. Gate against regression\n\n- **Unit tests on the repository** with a fixed dataset (golden numbers), plus property-style cases: a fully refunded period nets to `0`; a refunds-only period is negative; adding a sale and its refund leaves revenue unchanged.\n- **Architecture test extension:** `total_amount` may only be summed inside `src/dal/`. A route or script computing money on its own fails the suite. This is what stops the next endpoint from re-introducing the bug.\n\n### 7. Dashboard\n\nCards become: **Sales orders**, **Refunds**, **Avg order value**, **Revenue (last 30 days, net of refunds)**, with a small line under revenue showing gross and refunded amounts. Without the relabel the headline number just drops ~20–30 % with no explanation.\n\n### 8. Commits\n\n| # | Content | Tech debt |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `OrdersRepository`: net expressions + `revenue()` breakdown; revenue route; tests | TD-05 |\n| 2 | `MetricsRepository`: sales/refund counts, both averages, net `total_spent`; metrics routes; tests | TD-06 |\n| 3 | Architecture test extension (money math only inside `src/dal/`) | — |\n| 4 | Dashboard cards and labels | — |\n\n## Answers to the open questions\n\n- **Q1 — Both averages**: `avg_order_value_cents` (sales only) and `avg_net_order_value_cents` (net ÷ sales).\n- **Q2 — Both counts, dedicated names**: `sales_orders` and `refund_orders`; `total_orders` removed.\n- **Q3 — Yes**, revenue response carries `gross_sales_cents` and `refunds_cents`.\n- **Q4 — Ignore `status`** for now.\n- **Q5 — Logged** as TD-18 in `tech_debt_backlog.md` (no way to match a refund to its original sale).\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/dal/metrics-repository.ts`\n- `src/routes/revenue.ts`, `src/routes/metrics.ts`\n- `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`\n- `test/base-repository.test.ts`, new `test/money.test.ts`, `test/architecture.test.ts`, `test/auth-guard.test.ts` (updated expectations)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Input validation (TD-10, TD-11) and XSS (TD-12) — groups C and D.\n- Date-range semantics (TD-07) and mixed timestamp formats (TD-08) — backlog; the `created_at` filters are untouched.\n- Storing refunds as negative amounts, or adding a refund→sale link (TD-18).\n- `docs/` updates — authorization to be requested after validation (CLAUDE.md §6): `api.md` (response shapes) and `architecture.md` (the refund rule).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — new money tests plus the existing suite.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. Golden check against the seeded database: `m_acme` revenue reports `327108`, not `424364`; `m_bistro` `350321`, not `417659`.\n4. `curl /api/revenue` → net plus gross and refunds, reconciling (`gross - refunds === net`).\n5. `curl /api/metrics/summary` → `sales_orders + refund_orders` equals the old `total_orders`; both averages present and different when refunds exist.\n6. `top-customers`: a customer with more refunds than sales shows a negative `total_spent` and ranks last.\n7. Browser: cards read \"Sales orders\" / \"Refunds\" / \"Revenue (… net of refunds)\" with the gross/refunds line, matching the API.\n8. Architecture test fails if a route sums `total_amount` (verified by temporarily adding such a line).\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits. No schema or data migration is involved — the fix is read-side only, so rolling back cannot corrupt stored rows.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":160,"cache_read_input_tokens":373892,"output_tokens":4744,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1065},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":160,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":4744,"cache_read_input_tokens":373892,"cache_creation_input_tokens":160,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":160},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01GxwR9UYAPCtyFnqYNDZwUf":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\006-refund-semantics-in-money-math.md","content":"# 006 — Refund semantics in money math\n\n**Status:** draft (rev 2 — open questions answered by the user)\n\nCloses Tier 1 group **E** (TD-05) from [tech_debt.md](../tech_debt.md), and TD-06 from [tech_debt_backlog.md](../tech_debt_backlog.md) since both are the same bug in two places.\n\n## Context\n\n`orders.type` is `'sale' | 'refund'`, and per [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) a refund records a reversed sale. Any client reading `total_orders` gets `undefined` instead of a silently changed meaning — a loud break rather than a quiet one, and the only client is this repo's dashboard.\n\n### 4. `GET /api/metrics/top-customers` ranks by net spend\n\n`total_spent` becomes net per customer (sales − refunds) and `order_count` counts sales. But refunds are stored with a **positive** `total_amount`, and every money query sums `total_amount` without looking at `type`. So a refund *increases* revenue.\n\nMeasured on the current seeded database:\n\n| Merchant | Sales | Refunds | Reported today | Correct (net) | Overstated by |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `m_acme` | 375 736 | 48 628 | 424 364 | 327 108 | **+29.7 %** |\n| `m_bistro` | 383 990 | 33 669 | 417 659 | 350 321 | **+19.2 %** |\n\nA refund doesn't just fail to subtract — it adds the same amount again, so the error is roughly twice the refunded volume. This is the number the product exists to show, wrong in the optimistic direction.\n\nSchema facts that shape the fix (verified against the database):\n\n- `total_amount` is always positive, for both types.\n- There is **no column linking a refund to the sale it reverses** — netting can only be amount-based (logged as TD-18).\n- Every row is `status = 'completed'`; no other status exists yet.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. One definition of money, in one place\n\nAll money math moves behind named SQL expressions in `OrdersRepository`, so no route or repository can invent its own:\n\n```ts\n/** Signed amount: sales add, refunds subtract. */\nconst NET_AMOUNT = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN -total_amount ELSE total_amount END\";\nconst SALES_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'sale' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\nconst REFUNDS_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\n```\n\nRejected alternative: **store refunds as negative amounts**. It makes every query trivially correct, but it rewrites existing rows (migration + backfill), breaks the documented meaning of `total_amount`, and makes \"how much did we refund\" harder to ask. Netting at read time keeps the raw facts intact.\n\n### 2. `GET /api/revenue` returns net revenue, with the breakdown (Q3)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"from\": \"2026-08-01\", \"to\": \"2026-09-12\",\n  \"revenue_cents\": 327108,\n  \"revenue\": 3271.08,\n  \"gross_sales_cents\": 375736,\n  \"refunds_cents\": 48628\n}\n```\n\n`revenue_cents` keeps its name and becomes **net** (sales − refunds). The two new fields make the number auditable: a merchant seeing revenue drop can tell whether sales fell or refunds rose.\n\nNet revenue **can be negative** (a period with only refunds). That's correct and is asserted by a test rather than clamped to zero.\n\n### 3. `GET /api/metrics/summary` (Q1, Q2 — both figures, named explicitly)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"sales_orders\": 35,\n  \"refund_orders\": 5,\n  \"unique_customers\": 3,\n  \"avg_order_value_cents\": 10735,\n  \"avg_net_order_value_cents\": 9346\n}\n```\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `sales_orders` | Rows of type `sale` |\n| `refund_orders` | Rows of type `refund` |\n| `unique_customers` | Distinct customers **with at least one sale** |\n| `avg_order_value_cents` | Average amount of a sale — \"what does a typical order look like\" |\n| `avg_net_order_value_cents` | Net revenue ÷ number of sales — what a sale is worth *after* refunds |\n\nThe ambiguous `total_orders` is **removed** rather than redefined: per Q2 the two counts get dedicated names so nobody has to guess whether refunds are included. Any client reading `total_orders` gets `undefined` instead of a silently changed meaning — a loud break rather than a quiet one, and the only client is this repo's dashboard.\n\n### 4. `GET /api/metrics/top-customers` ranks by net spend\n\n`total_spent` becomes net per customer (sales − refunds) and `order_count` counts sales. A customer who refunded everything ranks last instead of top — which is the point of the report.\n\n### 5. `status` is ignored for now (Q4)\n\nEvery row is `completed`; filtering would be untested speculation. If other statuses ever appear, money math must exclude the non-completed ones — noted in the docs so it isn't forgotten.\n\n### 6. Gate against regression\n\n- **Unit tests on the repository** with a fixed dataset (golden numbers), plus property-style cases: a fully refunded period nets to `0`; a refunds-only period is negative; adding a sale and its refund leaves revenue unchanged.\n- **Architecture test extension:** `total_amount` may only be summed inside `src/dal/`. A route or script computing money on its own fails the suite. This is what stops the next endpoint from re-introducing the bug.\n\n### 7. Dashboard\n\nCards become: **Sales orders**, **Refunds**, **Avg order value**, **Revenue (last 30 days, net of refunds)**, with a small line under revenue showing gross and refunded amounts. Without the relabel the headline number just drops ~20–30 % with no explanation.\n\n### 8. Commits\n\n| # | Content | Tech debt |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `OrdersRepository`: net expressions + `revenue()` breakdown; revenue route; tests | TD-05 |\n| 2 | `MetricsRepository`: sales/refund counts, both averages, net `total_spent`; metrics routes; tests | TD-06 |\n| 3 | Architecture test extension (money math only inside `src/dal/`) | — |\n| 4 | Dashboard cards and labels | — |\n\n## Answers to the open questions\n\n- **Q1 — Both averages**: `avg_order_value_cents` (sales only) and `avg_net_order_value_cents` (net ÷ sales).\n- **Q2 — Both counts, dedicated names**: `sales_orders` and `refund_orders`; `total_orders` removed.\n- **Q3 — Yes**, revenue response carries `gross_sales_cents` and `refunds_cents`.\n- **Q4 — Ignore `status`** for now.\n- **Q5 — Logged** as TD-18 in `tech_debt_backlog.md` (no way to match a refund to its original sale).\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/dal/metrics-repository.ts`\n- `src/routes/revenue.ts`, `src/routes/metrics.ts`\n- `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`\n- `test/base-repository.test.ts`, new `test/money.test.ts`, `test/architecture.test.ts`, `test/auth-guard.test.ts` (updated expectations)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Input validation (TD-10, TD-11) and XSS (TD-12) — groups C and D.\n- Date-range semantics (TD-07) and mixed timestamp formats (TD-08) — backlog; the `created_at` filters are untouched.\n- Storing refunds as negative amounts, or adding a refund→sale link (TD-18).\n- `docs/` updates — authorization to be requested after validation (CLAUDE.md §6): `api.md` (response shapes) and `architecture.md` (the refund rule).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — new money tests plus the existing suite.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. So a refund *increases* revenue.\n\nMeasured on the current seeded database:\n\n| Merchant | Sales | Refunds | Reported today | Correct (net) | Overstated by |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `m_acme` | 375 736 | 48 628 | 424 364 | 327 108 | **+29.7 %** |\n| `m_bistro` | 383 990 | 33 669 | 417 659 | 350 321 | **+19.2 %** |\n\nA refund doesn't just fail to subtract — it adds the same amount again, so the error is roughly twice the refunded volume. This is the number the product exists to show, wrong in the optimistic direction, which is why it ranks with the security work rather than below it.\n\nSchema facts that shape the fix (verified against the database):\n\n- `total_amount` is always positive, for both types.\n- There is **no column linking a refund to the sale it reverses** — netting can only be amount-based, not order-based.\n- Every row is `status = 'completed'`; no other status exists yet.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. One definition of money, in one place\n\nAll money math moves behind named SQL expressions in `OrdersRepository`, so no route or repository can invent its own:\n\n```ts\n/** Signed amount: sales add, refunds subtract. */\nconst NET_AMOUNT = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN -total_amount ELSE total_amount END\";\nconst SALES_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'sale' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\nconst REFUNDS_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\n```\n\nRejected alternative: **store refunds as negative amounts**. It makes every query trivially correct, but it rewrites existing rows (migration + backfill), breaks the documented meaning of `total_amount`, and makes \"how much did we refund\" harder to ask. Netting at read time keeps the raw facts intact.\n\n### 2. `GET /api/revenue` returns net revenue, with the breakdown\n\n```json\n{\n  \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"from\": \"2026-08-01\", \"to\": \"2026-09-12\",\n  \"revenue_cents\": 327108,\n  \"revenue\": 3271.08,\n  \"gross_sales_cents\": 375736,\n  \"refunds_cents\": 48628\n}\n```\n\n`revenue_cents` keeps its name and becomes **net** (sales − refunds). The two new fields make the number auditable: a merchant seeing revenue drop should be able to tell whether sales fell or refunds rose, without a second endpoint.\n\nNet revenue **can be negative** (a period with only refunds). That's correct and is asserted by a test rather than clamped to zero.\n\n### 3. `GET /api/metrics/summary` counts sales as orders (TD-06)\n\n| Field | Today | After |\n|---|---|---|\n| `total_orders` | all rows | **sales only** — a refund is not an order placed |\n| `refunded_orders` | — | **new**: number of refund rows |\n| `unique_customers` | distinct emails on any row | distinct emails **with at least one sale** |\n| `avg_order_value_cents` | average over all rows | average over **sales only** |\n\n### 4. `GET /api/metrics/top-customers` ranks by net spend\n\n`total_spent` becomes net per customer (sales − refunds) and `order_count` counts sales. A customer who refunded everything then ranks last instead of top — which is the point of the report.\n\n### 5. Gate against regression\n\n- **Unit tests on the repository** with a fixed dataset (golden numbers), plus property-style cases: revenue of a fully refunded period is `0`; a refunds-only period is negative; adding a sale and its refund leaves revenue unchanged.\n- **Architecture test extension:** assert that `total_amount` is only summed inside `src/dal/` — a route or script that computes money on its own fails the suite. This is what stops the next endpoint from re-introducing the bug.\n\n### 6. Dashboard\n\nThe \"Revenue (last 30 days)\" card is labelled **\"Revenue (last 30 days, net of refunds)\"**, and a small line under it shows gross and refunds. Otherwise the number silently changes by ~20–30 % with no explanation.\n\n### 7. Commits\n\n| # | Content | Tech debt |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `OrdersRepository`: net expressions, `revenue()` returning the breakdown; revenue route; tests | TD-05 |\n| 2 | `MetricsRepository`: sales-based counts, net `total_spent`; metrics routes; tests | TD-06 |\n| 3 | Architecture test extension (money math only inside `src/dal/`) | — |\n| 4 | Dashboard labels + gross/refunds line | — |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — `avg_order_value_cents`: average of sale amounts** (recommended) or net revenue ÷ number of sales? The first answers \"what does a typical order look like\"; the second bakes refunds into a per-order figure and is harder to explain.\n- **Q2 — `total_orders` counting sales only** (recommended), with `refunded_orders` alongside. The alternative keeps today's total and adds a breakdown, which avoids a visible drop in the dashboard number but keeps calling refunds \"orders\".\n- **Q3 — Adding `gross_sales_cents` / `refunds_cents` to the revenue response** (recommended). It's a response-shape change; say if you'd rather keep the payload as-is.\n- **Q4 — Ignoring `status` for now** (recommended): every row is `completed`, so filtering would be untested speculation. If cancelled/pending rows ever exist, money math must exclude them — I'd log it as tech debt instead of guessing now.\n- **Q5 — New backlog item for the missing refund→sale link.** Refunds can't be matched to their original sale, so a refund can exceed the sale it reverses, or land in a different period and make that period negative. I'd add it as **TD-18 (Tier 2)** — needs your go, since `tech_debt*.md` is yours.\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/dal/metrics-repository.ts`\n- `src/routes/revenue.ts`, `src/routes/metrics.ts`\n- `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`\n- `test/base-repository.test.ts` (money cases), new `test/money.test.ts`, `test/architecture.test.ts`, `test/auth-guard.test.ts` (updated expectations)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Input validation (TD-10, TD-11) and XSS (TD-12) — groups C and D.\n- Date-range semantics (TD-07) and mixed timestamp formats (TD-08) — backlog; this plan doesn't touch the `created_at` filters.\n- Storing refunds as negative amounts, or adding a refund→sale foreign key (Q5).\n- `docs/` updates — authorization to be requested after validation (CLAUDE.md §6): `api.md` (response shapes) and `architecture.md` (the refund rule).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — new money tests plus the existing suite.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. Golden check against the seeded database: `m_acme` revenue reports `327108`, not `424364`; `m_bistro` `350321`, not `417659`.\n4. `curl /api/revenue` returns net plus gross and refunds, and they reconcile (`gross - refunds === net`).\n5. `curl /api/metrics/summary` → `total_orders` + `refunded_orders` equals the old total; `avg_order_value_cents` computed over sales only.\n6. `top-customers`: a customer with more refunds than sales shows a negative `total_spent` and ranks last.\n7. Browser: the card reads \"net of refunds\" and shows the gross/refunds line; the number matches the API.\n8. Architecture test fails if a route sums `total_amount` (verified by temporarily adding such a line).\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits. {"parentUuid":"f1427d1b-5f8b-4b87-ae19-c32dd5c1d9ab","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cey4ygCi7yQ64HaZ27cNG","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01FGabyHa2ufaX3aHUCxRAfS","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\src\\dal\\money.ts","content":"/**\n * Money semantics, in one place.\n *\n * A refund row records a reversed sale but stores a **positive** `total_amount`, so any query\n * that sums `total_amount` blindly counts a refund as income — the amount is added instead of\n * subtracted, making the error roughly twice the refunded volume.\n *\n * Every money figure is therefore derived from these expressions, and `test/architecture.test.ts`\n * fails the build if `total_amount` is aggregated anywhere outside `src/dal/`.\n *\n * @see plans/006-refund-semantics-in-money-math.md\n */\n\n/** Signed amount: sales add, refunds subtract. Sums to net revenue. */\nexport const NET_AMOUNT = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN -total_amount ELSE total_amount END\";\n\n/** Sale amounts only; refunds contribute zero. Sums to the number of sales. */\nexport const SALE_COUNT = \"CASE WHEN type = 'sale' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END\";\n\n/** 1 for a refund, 0 otherwise. {"parentUuid":"28ffc64a-bb90-4a0b-ab58-c28aaa5cfac9","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"d7eebfe9-5ab8-4ace-bf8f-571fed31cd77","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FGabyHa2ufaX3aHUCxRAfS","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\src\\dal\\money.ts (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"69323188-70eb-4c9e-9653-6ef579e0dfd1","timestamp":"2026-09-12T06:26:53.211Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"create","filePath":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\src\\dal\\money.ts","content":"/**\n * Money semantics, in one place.\n *\n * A refund row records a reversed sale but stores a **positive** `total_amount`, so any query\n * that sums `total_amount` blindly counts a refund as income — the amount is added instead of\n * subtracted, making the error roughly twice the refunded volume.\n *\n * Every money figure is therefore derived from these expressions, and `test/architecture.test.ts`\n * fails the build if `total_amount` is aggregated anywhere outside `src/dal/`.\n *\n * @see plans/006-refund-semantics-in-money-math.md\n */\n\n/** Signed amount: sales add, refunds subtract. Sums to net revenue. */\nexport const NET_AMOUNT = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN -total_amount ELSE total_amount END\";\n\n/** Sale amounts only; refunds contribute zero. Sums to gross sales. */\nexport const SALES_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'sale' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\n\n/** Refund amounts only, as positive numbers. Sums to the refunded total. */\nexport const REFUNDS_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\n\n/** 1 for a sale, 0 otherwise. Sums to the number of sales. */\nexport const SALE_COUNT = \"CASE WHEN type = 'sale' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END\";\n\n/** 1 for a refund, 0 otherwise. Sums to the number of refunds. */\nexport const REFUND_COUNT = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END\";\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"28ffc64a-bb90-4a0b-ab58-c28aaa5cfac9","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}
{"parentUuid":"69323188-70eb-4c9e-9653-6ef579e0dfd1","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cey4ygCi7yQ64HaZ27cNG","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01HNb8affwXLJP8hGVsQ1452","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\src\\dal\\orders-repository.ts","content":"/**\n * Orders repository. Every query is scoped to the caller's merchant by {@link BaseRepository}.\n *\n * @see plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md\n * @see plans/006-refund-semantics-in-money-math.md\n */\nimport { BaseRepository } from './base-repository.js';\nimport { NET_AMOUNT, REFUNDS_ONLY, SALES_ONLY } from './money.js';\n\n/** A row of the `orders` table. */\nexport interface OrderRow {\n  id: string;\n  merchant_id: string;\n  customer_email: string;\n  total_amount: number;\n  type: 'sale' | 'refund';\n  status: string;\n  created_at: string;\n}\n\n/** Values needed to create an order; the merchant comes from the auth context. */\nexport interface NewOrder {\n  id: string;\n  customer_email: string;\n  total_amount: number;\n  type: 'sale' | 'refund';\n  status: string;\n}\n\n/** Filters accepted when listing orders. */\nexport interface ListOrdersOptions {\n  from?: string;\n  to?: string;\n  limit?: number;\n}\n\n/** Revenue over a period, split so the net figure can be audited. */\nexport interface RevenueBreakdown {\n  /** Gross sales minus refunds. Negative when refunds exceed sales. */\n  netCents: number;\n  /** Sales only. */\n  grossSalesCents: number;\n  /** Refunds only, as a positive number. */\n  refundsCents: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Data access for orders.\n */\nexport class OrdersRepository extends BaseRepository<OrderRow> {\n  protected readonly table = 'orders';\n\n  /**\n   * Lists the caller's orders, newest first.\n   *\n   * @param options - Optional date range and row limit.\n   */\n  list(options: ListOrdersOptions = {}): OrderRow[] {\n    const limit = options.limit ?? 100;\n    if (options.from && options.to) {\n      return this.select<OrderRow>('*', {\n        where: 'created_at >= ? AND created_at < ?',\n        tail: 'ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?',\n        params: [options.from, options.to, limit],\n      });\n    }\n    return this.select<OrderRow>('*', {\n      tail: 'ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?',\n      params: [limit],\n    });\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Reads one of the caller's orders.\n   *\n   * @param id - Order id.\n   * @returns The order, or `undefined` when it doesn't exist **or belongs to another merchant**.\n   */\n  getById(id: string): OrderRow | undefined {\n    return this.selectFirst<OrderRow>('*', { where: 'id = ?', params: [id] });\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Creates an order for the caller's merchant.\n   *\n   * @param order - Order values.\n   * @returns The stored row.\n   */\n  create(order: NewOrder): OrderRow {\n    this.insert({\n      id: order.id,\n      customer_email: order.customer_email,\n      total_amount: order.total_amount,\n      type: order.type,\n      status: order.status,\n    });\n    return this.getById(order.id)!;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Revenue over a date range: net, plus the gross and refunded amounts it is made of.\n   *\n   * Refunds subtract, so a period with more refunds than sales reports a negative net — that\n   * is a real state of the business and is not clamped to zero.\n   *\n   * @param from - Inclusive lower bound (`YYYY-MM-DD`).\n   * @param to - Exclusive upper bound (`YYYY-MM-DD`).\n   */\n  revenue(from: string, to: string): RevenueBreakdown {\n    const row = this.selectFirst<{ net: number; gross: number; refunds: number }>(\n      `COALESCE(SUM(${NET_AMOUNT}), 0) AS net,\n       COALESCE(SUM(${SALES_ONLY}), 0) AS gross,\n       COALESCE(SUM(${REFUNDS_ONLY}), 0) AS refunds`,\n      { where: 'created_at >= ? AND created_at < ?', params: [from, to] },\n    );\n    return {\n      netCents: row?.net ?? 0,\n      grossSalesCents: row?.gross ?? 0,\n      refundsCents: row?.refunds ?? 0,\n    };\n  }\n}\n\n/** Shared instance; the merchant scope comes from the per-request auth context. */\nexport const ordersRepository = new OrdersRepository();\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":38,"cache_read_input_tokens":379729,"output_tokens":6676,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1838},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":38,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":6676,"cache_read_input_tokens":379729,"cache_creation_input_tokens":38,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":38},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01HNb8affwXLJP8hGVsQ1452":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\src\\dal\\orders-repository.ts","content":"/**\n * Orders repository. Negative when refunds exceed sales. */\n  netCents: number;\n  /** Sales only. */\n  grossSalesCents: number;\n  /** Refunds only, as a positive number. */\n  refundsCents: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Data access for orders.\n */\nexport class OrdersRepository extends BaseRepository<OrderRow> {\n  protected readonly table = 'orders';\n\n  /**\n   * Lists the caller's orders, newest first.\n   *\n   * @param options - Optional date range and row limit.\n   */\n  list(options: ListOrdersOptions = {}): OrderRow[] {\n    const limit = options.limit ?? 100;\n    if (options.from && options.to) {\n      return this.select<OrderRow>('*', {\n        where: 'created_at >= ? AND created_at < ?',\n        tail: 'ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?',\n        params: [options.from, options.to, limit],\n      });\n    }\n    return this.select<OrderRow>('*', {\n      tail: 'ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?',\n      params: [limit],\n    });\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Reads one of the caller's orders.\n   *\n   * @param id - Order id.\n   * @returns The order, or `undefined` when it doesn't exist **or belongs to another merchant**.\n   */\n  getById(id: string): OrderRow | undefined {\n    return this.selectFirst<OrderRow>('*', { where: 'id = ?', params: [id] });\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Creates an order for the caller's merchant.\n   *\n   * @param order - Order values.\n   * @returns The stored row.\n   */\n  create(order: NewOrder): OrderRow {\n    this.insert({\n      id: order.id,\n      customer_email: order.customer_email,\n      total_amount: order.total_amount,\n      type: order.type,\n      status: order.status,\n    });\n    return this.getById(order.id)!;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Revenue over a date range: net, plus the gross and refunded amounts it is made of.\n   *\n   * Refunds subtract, so a period with more refunds than sales reports a negative net — that\n   * is a real state of the business and is not clamped to zero.\n   *\n   * @param from - Inclusive lower bound (`YYYY-MM-DD`).\n   * @param to - Exclusive upper bound (`YYYY-MM-DD`).\n   */\n  revenue(from: string, to: string): RevenueBreakdown {\n    const row = this.selectFirst<{ net: number; gross: number; refunds: number }>(\n      `COALESCE(SUM(${NET_AMOUNT}), 0) AS net,\n       COALESCE(SUM(${SALES_ONLY}), 0) AS gross,\n       COALESCE(SUM(${REFUNDS_ONLY}), 0) AS refunds`,\n      { where: 'created_at >= ? AND created_at < ?',\n        tail: 'ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?',\n        params: [options.from, options.to, limit],\n      });\n    }\n    return this.select<OrderRow>('*', {\n      tail: 'ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?',\n      params: [limit],\n    });\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Reads one of the caller's orders.\n   *\n   * @param id - Order id.\n   * @returns The order, or `undefined` when it doesn't exist **or belongs to another merchant**.\n   */\n  getById(id: string): OrderRow | undefined {\n    return this.selectFirst<OrderRow>('*', { where: 'id = ?', params: [id] });\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Creates an order for the caller's merchant.\n   *\n   * @param order - Order values.\n   * @returns The stored row.\n   */\n  create(order: NewOrder): OrderRow {\n    this.insert({\n      id: order.id,\n      customer_email: order.customer_email,\n      total_amount: order.total_amount,\n      type: order.type,\n      status: order.status,\n    });\n    return this.getById(order.id)!;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Sums order amounts over a date range.\n   *\n   * Note: refunds are stored as positive amounts and are summed like sales — see TD-05 in\n   * `tech_debt.md`. Behavior is unchanged here on purpose; the fix is its own change.\n   *\n   * @param from - Inclusive lower bound (`YYYY-MM-DD`).\n   * @param to - Exclusive upper bound (`YYYY-MM-DD`).\n   */\n  sumAmount(from: string, to: string): number {\n    const row = this.selectFirst<{ total: number }>('COALESCE(SUM(total_amount), 0) AS total', {\n      where: 'created_at >= ? unique_customers: number; avg_order_value: number }>(\n      'COUNT(*) AS total_orders, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_email) AS unique_customers, COALESCE(AVG(total_amount), 0) AS avg_order_value',\n    );\n    return {\n      total_orders: row?.total_orders ?? 0,\n      unique_customers: row?.unique_customers ?? 0,\n      avg_order_value_cents: Math.round(row?.avg_order_value ?? 0),\n    };\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Customers ranked by amount spent.\n   *\n   * @param limit - Maximum rows to return.\n   */\n  topCustomers(limit: number): TopCustomer[] {\n    return this.select<TopCustomer>(\n      'customer_email, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(total_amount) AS total_spent',\n      {\n        tail: 'GROUP BY customer_email ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT ?',\n        params: [limit],\n      },\n    );\n  }\n}\n\n/** Shared instance; The\n * gross and refunded amounts are returned alongside so the net figure can be explained.\n */\nrevenueRouter.get('/', (req, res) => {\n  const from = typeof req.query.from === 'string' ? req.query.from : undefined;\n  const to = typeof req.query.to === 'string' ? document.getElementById('revenue-30d');\nconst ordersTbody = document.getElementById('orders-tbody');\n\n// The session lives in HttpOnly cookies, so this page never holds a token.\n// Merchant tokens are short-lived: on a 401 we ask for a new one and retry once.\nlet selectedMerchantId = null;\n\nfunction request(path, options = {}) {\n  return fetch(path, { credentials: 'same-origin', ...options });\n}\n\nasync function mintMerchantToken(merchantId) {\n  const response = await request('/api/auth/token', {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n    body: JSON.stringify({ merchantId }),\n  });\n  return response.ok;\n}\n\nasync function api(path) {\n  let response = await request(path);\n  if (response.status === 401 && selectedMerchantId && (await mintMerchantToken(selectedMerchantId))) {\n    response = await request(path);\n  }\n  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`${path} responded ${response.status}`);\n  return response.json();\n}\n\nfunction money(cents) {\n  return (cents / 100).toLocaleString('en-US', { style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' });\n}\n\nfunction isoDate(d) {\n  return d.toISOString().slice(0, 10);\n}\n\nfunction setStatus(text) {\n  sessionLabel.textContent = text;\n}\n\nasync function refresh() {\n  const summary = await api('/api/metrics/summary');\n  totalOrdersEl.textContent = summary.total_orders ?? '—';\n  uniqueCustomersEl.textContent = summary.unique_customers ?? '—';\n  avgOrderEl.textContent = money(summary.avg_order_value_cents ?? 0);\n\n  const now = new Date();\n  const thirtyAgo = new Date(now.getTime() - 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);\n  const revenue = await api(`/api/revenue?from=${isoDate(thirtyAgo)}&to=${isoDate(now)}`);\n  revenue30dEl.textContent = money(revenue.revenue_cents ?? 0);\n\n  const ordersRes = await api('/api/orders?limit=10');\n  ordersTbody.innerHTML = '';\n  for (const o of ordersRes.orders ?? []) {\n    const tr = document.createElement('tr');\n    tr.innerHTML = `\n      <td>${new Date(o.created_at).toLocaleDateString()}</td>\n      <td>${o.customer_email}</td>\n      <td>${o.type}</td>\n      <td>${money(o.total_amount)}</td>\n    `;\n    ordersTbody.appendChild(tr);\n  }\n}\n\nasync function selectMerchant(merchantId) {\n  selectedMerchantId = merchantId;\n  if (!(await mintMerchantToken(merchantId))) {\n    setStatus(`Could not open a session for ${merchantId}.`);\n    return;\n  }\n  setStatus(`Viewing ${merchantId}`);\n  await refresh();\n}\n\nasync function start() {\n  const sessionResponse = await request('/api/auth/session');\n  if (!sessionResponse.ok) {\n    merchantPicker.hidden = true;\n    setStatus('No session. Run \"npm run token\" and POST it to /api/auth/admin-session.');\n    return;\n  }\n  const session = await sessionResponse.json();\n\n  if (session.role === 'merchant') {\n    // A merchant session is bound to one merchant: no picker to show.\n    merchantPicker.hidden = true;\n    selectedMerchantId = session.merchantId;\n    setStatus(`Viewing ${session.merchantId}`);\n    await refresh();\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const { merchants } = await api('/api/merchants');\n  merchantSelect.innerHTML = '';\n  for (const merchant of merchants) {\n    const option = document.createElement('option');\n    option.value = merchant.id;\n    option.textContent = merchant.name;\n    merchantSelect.appendChild(option);\n  }\n  merchantPicker.hidden = merchants.length === 0;\n  if (merchants.length > 0) await selectMerchant(merchantSelect.value);\n}\n\nmerchantSelect.addEventListener('change', () => {\n  selectMerchant(merchantSelect.value).catch((error) => merchantPicker = document.getElementById('merchant-picker');\nconst merchantSelect = document.getElementById('merchant-select');\nconst sessionLabel = document.getElementById('session-label');\nconst salesOrdersEl = document.getElementById('sales-orders');\nconst refundOrdersEl = document.getElementById('refund-orders');\nconst avgOrderEl = document.getElementById('avg-order');\nconst avgNetOrderEl = document.getElementById('avg-net-order');\nconst revenue30dEl = document.getElementById('revenue-30d');\nconst revenueBreakdownEl = document.getElementById('revenue-breakdown');\nconst ordersTbody = document.getElementById('orders-tbody');\n\n// The session lives in HttpOnly cookies, so this page never holds a token.\n// Merchant tokens are short-lived: on a 401 we ask for a new one and retry once.\nlet selectedMerchantId = null;\n\nfunction request(path, options = {}) {\n  return fetch(path, { credentials: 'same-origin', ...options });\n}\n\nasync function mintMerchantToken(merchantId) {\n  const response = await request('/api/auth/token', {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n    body: JSON.stringify({ merchantId }),\n  });\n  return response.ok;\n}\n\nasync function api(path) {\n  let response = await request(path);\n  if (response.status === 401 && selectedMerchantId && (await mintMerchantToken(selectedMerchantId))) {\n    response = await request(path);\n  }\n  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`${path} responded ${response.status}`);\n  return response.json();\n}\n\nfunction money(cents) {\n  return (cents / 100).toLocaleString('en-US', { style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' });\n}\n\nfunction isoDate(d) {\n  return d.toISOString().slice(0, 10);\n}\n\nfunction setStatus(text) {\n  sessionLabel.textContent = text;\n}\n\nasync function refresh() {\n  const summary = await api('/api/metrics/summary');\n  totalOrdersEl.textContent = summary.total_orders ?? '—';\n  uniqueCustomersEl.textContent = summary.unique_customers ?? '—';\n  avgOrderEl.textContent = money(summary.avg_order_value_cents ?? 0);\n\n  const now = new Date();\n  const thirtyAgo = new Date(now.getTime() - 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);\n  const revenue = await api(`/api/revenue?from=${isoDate(thirtyAgo)}&to=${isoDate(now)}`);\n  revenue30dEl.textContent = money(revenue.revenue_cents ?? 0);\n\n  const ordersRes = await api('/api/orders?limit=10');\n  ordersTbody.innerHTML = '';\n  for (const o of ordersRes.orders ?? []) {\n    const tr = document.createElement('tr');\n    tr.innerHTML = `\n      <td>${new Date(o.created_at).toLocaleDateString()}</td>\n      <td>${o.customer_email}</td>\n      <td>${o.type}</td>\n      <td>${money(o.total_amount)}</td>\n    `;\n    ordersTbody.appendChild(tr);\n  }\n}\n\nasync function selectMerchant(merchantId) {\n  selectedMerchantId = merchantId;\n  if (!(await mintMerchantToken(merchantId))) {\n    setStatus(`Could not open a session for ${merchantId}.`);\n    return;\n  }\n  setStatus(`Viewing ${merchantId}`);\n  await refresh();\n}\n\nasync function start() {\n  const sessionResponse = await request('/api/auth/session');\n  if (!sessionResponse.ok) {\n    merchantPicker.hidden = true;\n    setStatus('No session. Run \"npm run token\" and POST it to /api/auth/admin-session.');\n    return;\n  }\n  const session = await sessionResponse.json();\n\n  if (session.role === 'merchant') {\n    // A merchant session is bound to one merchant: no picker to show.\n    merchantPicker.hidden = true;\n    selectedMerchantId = session.merchantId;\n    setStatus(`Viewing ${session.merchantId}`);\n    await refresh();\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const { merchants } = await api('/api/merchants');\n  merchantSelect.innerHTML = '';\n  for (const merchant of merchants) {\n    const option = document.createElement('option');\n    option.value = merchant.id;\n    option.textContent = merchant.name;\n    merchantSelect.appendChild(option);\n  }\n  merchantPicker.hidden = merchants.length === 0;\n  if (merchants.length > 0) await selectMerchant(merchantSelect.value);\n}\n\nmerchantSelect.addEventListener('change', () => {\n  selectMerchant(merchantSelect.value).catch((error) => setStatus(String(error)));\n});\n\nstart().catch((error) => setStatus(String(error)));\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":49,"oldLines":14,"newStart":49,"newLines":16,"lines":[" "," async function refresh() {","   const summary = await api('/api/metrics/summary');","-  totalOrdersEl.textContent = summary.total_orders ??
