{"parentUuid":"826ac94d-a7b7-475c-9fc0-f55fd3575af6","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cey549aMu56Ew54NZp3kL","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01U3mdQuna3oTwcMNgNiimPC","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\test\\money.test.ts","content":"// Set DB_PATH before importing the db module — the connection is created on import.\nif (!process.env.DB_PATH) process.env.DB_PATH = ':memory:';\n\nimport { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';\nimport { runWithAuthContext } from '../src/auth/context.js';\nimport { metricsRepository } from '../src/dal/metrics-repository.js';\nimport { ordersRepository } from '../src/dal/orders-repository.js';\nimport { initSchema, db } from '../src/db.js';\n\nconst MERCHANT = 'm_money';\nconst FROM = '2026-01-01';\nconst TO = '2027-01-01';\n\n/** Runs a function as the test merchant. */\nfunction asMerchant<T>(fn: () => T): T {\n  return runWithAuthContext({ role: 'merchant', scope: 'data', merchantId: MERCHANT }, fn);\n}\n\n/** Resets the orders table and registers the test merchant. */\nfunction reset(): void {\n  initSchema();\n  db.exec('DELETE FROM orders');\n  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO merchants (id, name) VALUES (?, 'Money')`).run(MERCHANT);\n}\n\n/** Inserts an order with an explicit timestamp, bypassing the repository. */\nfunction addOrder(type: 'sale' | 'refund', amount: number, email = 'ana@example.com', createdAt = '2026-06-01T10:00:00.000Z'): void {\n  db.prepare(\n    `INSERT INTO orders (id, merchant_id, customer_email, total_amount, type, status, created_at)\n     VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'completed', ?)`,\n  ).run(randomUUID(), MERCHANT, email, amount, type, createdAt);\n}\n\ntest('revenue: refunds subtract instead of adding (TD-05)', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('sale', 1000);\n  addOrder('sale', 2000);\n  addOrder('refund', 500);\n\n  const revenue = asMerchant(() => ordersRepository.revenue(FROM, TO));\n  assert.deepEqual(revenue, { netCents: 2500, grossSalesCents: 3000, refundsCents: 500 });\n  // The old behaviour (SUM of every amount) would have reported 3500.\n  assert.notEqual(revenue.netCents, 3500);\n});\n\ntest('revenue: a sale and its refund cancel out', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('sale', 4200);\n  const before = asMerchant(() => ordersRepository.revenue(FROM, TO)).netCents;\n\n  addOrder('sale', 7000);\n  addOrder('refund', 7000);\n  const after = asMerchant(() => ordersRepository.revenue(FROM, TO)).netCents;\n\n  assert.equal(after, before);\n});\n\ntest('revenue: a fully refunded period nets to zero', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('sale', 1500);\n  addOrder('refund', 1500);\n\n  assert.equal(asMerchant(() => ordersRepository.revenue(FROM, TO)).netCents, 0);\n});\n\ntest('revenue: a refunds-only period is negative and is not clamped', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('refund', 900);\n  addOrder('refund', 100);\n\n  const revenue = asMerchant(() => ordersRepository.revenue(FROM, TO));\n  assert.equal(revenue.netCents, -1000);\n  assert.equal(revenue.grossSalesCents, 0);\n  assert.equal(revenue.refundsCents, 1000);\n});\n\ntest('revenue: gross minus refunds always reconciles with net', () => {\n  reset();\n  for (const [type, amount] of [\n    ['sale', 1234],\n    ['sale', 5678],\n    ['refund', 999],\n    ['sale', 4321],\n    ['refund', 4321],\n  ] as Array<['sale' | 'refund', number]>) {\n    addOrder(type, amount);\n  }\n\n  const { netCents, grossSalesCents, refundsCents } = asMerchant(() => ordersRepository.revenue(FROM, TO));\n  assert.equal(grossSalesCents - refundsCents, netCents);\n});\n\ntest('revenue: only orders inside the range are counted', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('sale', 1000, 'ana@example.com', '2026-06-01T10:00:00.000Z');\n  addOrder('sale', 2000, 'ana@example.com', '2025-06-01T10:00:00.000Z');\n\n  assert.equal(asMerchant(() => ordersRepository.revenue(FROM, TO)).netCents, 1000);\n});\n\ntest('summary: sales and refunds are counted separately (TD-06)', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('sale', 1000, 'ana@example.com');\n  addOrder('sale', 3000, 'bruno@example.com');\n  addOrder('refund', 1000, 'ana@example.com');\n\n  const summary = asMerchant(() => metricsRepository.summary());\n  assert.equal(summary.sales_orders, 2);\n  assert.equal(summary.refund_orders, 1);\n  assert.equal(summary.unique_customers, 2);\n  // Average of the sales themselves: (1000 + 3000) / 2.\n  assert.equal(summary.avg_order_value_cents, 2000);\n  // Net per sale: (4000 - 1000) / 2.\n  assert.equal(summary.avg_net_order_value_cents, 1500);\n});\n\ntest('summary: a customer who only refunded is not counted as a customer', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('sale', 1000, 'ana@example.com');\n  addOrder('refund', 500, 'ghost@example.com');\n\n  assert.equal(asMerchant(() => metricsRepository.summary()).unique_customers, 1);\n});\n\ntest('summary: an empty merchant reports zeros, not NaN', () => {\n  reset();\n\n  assert.deepEqual(asMerchant(() => metricsRepository.summary()), {\n    sales_orders: 0,\n    refund_orders: 0,\n    unique_customers: 0,\n    avg_order_value_cents: 0,\n    avg_net_order_value_cents: 0,\n  });\n});\n\ntest('top customers: ranked by net spend, refunds push a customer down', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('sale', 10000, 'returns@example.com');\n  addOrder('refund', 12000, 'returns@example.com');\n  addOrder('sale', 3000, 'loyal@example.com');\n\n  const customers = asMerchant(() => metricsRepository.topCustomers(5));\n  assert.deepEqual(customers.map((c) => c.customer_email), ['loyal@example.com', 'returns@example.com']);\n  assert.equal(customers[0]!.total_spent, 3000);\n  assert.equal(customers[1]!.total_spent, -2000);\n  // Refunds are not orders.\n  assert.equal(customers[1]!.order_count, 1);\n});\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":7131,"cache_read_input_tokens":379767,"output_tokens":5969,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1049},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":7131,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":5969,"cache_read_input_tokens":379767,"cache_creation_input_tokens":7131,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":7131},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01U3mdQuna3oTwcMNgNiimPC":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\test\\money.test.ts","content":"// Set DB_PATH before importing the db module — the connection is created on import.\nif (!process.env.DB_PATH) process.env.DB_PATH = ':memory:';\n\nimport { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';\nimport { runWithAuthContext } from '../src/auth/context.js';\nimport { metricsRepository } from '../src/dal/metrics-repository.js';\nimport { ordersRepository } from '../src/dal/orders-repository.js';\nimport { initSchema, db } from '../src/db.js';\n\nconst MERCHANT = 'm_money';\nconst FROM = '2026-01-01';\nconst TO = '2027-01-01';\n\n/** Runs a function as the test merchant. */\nfunction asMerchant<T>(fn: () => T): T {\n  return runWithAuthContext({ role: 'merchant', scope: 'data', merchantId: MERCHANT }, fn);\n}\n\n/** Resets the orders table and registers the test merchant. */\nfunction reset(): void {\n  initSchema();\n  db.exec('DELETE FROM orders');\n  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO merchants (id, name) VALUES (?, 'Money')`).run(MERCHANT);\n}\n\n/** Inserts an order with an explicit timestamp, bypassing the repository. */\nfunction addOrder(type: 'sale' | 'refund', amount: number, email = 'ana@example.com', createdAt = '2026-06-01T10:00:00.000Z'): void {\n  db.prepare(\n    `INSERT INTO orders (id, merchant_id, customer_email, total_amount, type, status, created_at)\n     VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'completed', ?)`,\n  ).run(randomUUID(), MERCHANT, email, amount, type, createdAt);\n}\n\ntest('revenue: refunds subtract instead of adding (TD-05)', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('sale', 1000);\n  addOrder('sale', 2000);\n  addOrder('refund', 500);\n\n  const revenue = asMerchant(() => ordersRepository.revenue(FROM, TO));\n  assert.deepEqual(revenue, { netCents: 2500, grossSalesCents: 3000, refundsCents: 500 });\n  // The old behaviour (SUM of every amount) would have reported 3500.\n  assert.notEqual(revenue.netCents, 3500);\n});\n\ntest('revenue: a sale and its refund cancel out', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('sale', 4200);\n  const before = asMerchant(() => ordersRepository.revenue(FROM, TO)).netCents;\n\n  addOrder('sale', 7000);\n  addOrder('refund', 7000);\n  const after = asMerchant(() => ordersRepository.revenue(FROM, TO)).netCents;\n\n  assert.equal(after, before);\n});\n\ntest('revenue: a fully refunded period nets to zero', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('sale', 1500);\n  addOrder('refund', 1500);\n\n  assert.equal(asMerchant(() => ordersRepository.revenue(FROM, TO)).netCents, 0);\n});\n\ntest('revenue: a refunds-only period is negative and is not clamped', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('refund', 900);\n  addOrder('refund', 100);\n\n  const revenue = asMerchant(() => ordersRepository.revenue(FROM, TO));\n  assert.equal(revenue.netCents, -1000);\n  assert.equal(revenue.grossSalesCents, 0);\n  assert.equal(revenue.refundsCents, 1000);\n});\n\ntest('revenue: gross minus refunds always reconciles with net', () => {\n  reset();\n  for (const [type, amount] of [\n    ['sale', 1234],\n    ['sale', 5678],\n    ['refund', 999],\n    ['sale', 4321],\n    ['refund', 4321],\n  ] as Array<['sale' | 'refund', number]>) {\n    addOrder(type, amount);\n  }\n\n  const { netCents, grossSalesCents, refundsCents } = asMerchant(() => ordersRepository.revenue(FROM, TO));\n  assert.equal(grossSalesCents - refundsCents, netCents);\n});\n\ntest('revenue: only orders inside the range are counted', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('sale', 1000, 'ana@example.com', '2026-06-01T10:00:00.000Z');\n  addOrder('sale', 2000, 'ana@example.com', '2025-06-01T10:00:00.000Z');\n\n  assert.equal(asMerchant(() => ordersRepository.revenue(FROM, TO)).netCents, 1000);\n});\n\ntest('summary: sales and refunds are counted separately (TD-06)', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('sale', 1000, 'ana@example.com');\n  addOrder('sale', 3000, 'bruno@example.com');\n  addOrder('refund', 1000, 'ana@example.com');\n\n  const summary = asMerchant(() => metricsRepository.summary());\n  assert.equal(summary.sales_orders, 2);\n  assert.equal(summary.refund_orders, 1);\n  assert.equal(summary.unique_customers, 2);\n  // Average of the sales themselves: (1000 + 3000) / 2.\n  assert.equal(summary.avg_order_value_cents, 2000);\n  // Net per sale: (4000 - 1000) / 2.\n  assert.equal(summary.avg_net_order_value_cents, 1500);\n});\n\ntest('summary: a customer who only refunded is not counted as a customer', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('sale', 1000, 'ana@example.com');\n  addOrder('refund', 500, 'ghost@example.com');\n\n  assert.equal(asMerchant(() => metricsRepository.summary()).unique_customers, 1);\n});\n\ntest('summary: an empty merchant reports zeros, not NaN', () => {\n  reset();\n\n  assert.deepEqual(asMerchant(() => metricsRepository.summary()), {\n    sales_orders: 0,\n    refund_orders: 0,\n    unique_customers: 0,\n    avg_order_value_cents: 0,\n    avg_net_order_value_cents: 0,\n  });\n});\n\ntest('top customers: ranked by net spend, refunds push a customer down', () => {\n  reset();\n  addOrder('sale', 10000, 'returns@example.com');\n  addOrder('refund', 12000, 'returns@example.com');\n  addOrder('sale', 3000, 'loyal@example.com');\n\n  const customers = asMerchant(() => metricsRepository.topCustomers(5));\n  assert.deepEqual(customers.map((c) => c.customer_email), ['loyal@example.com', 'returns@example.com']);\n  assert.equal(customers[0]!.total_spent, 3000);\n  assert.equal(customers[1]!.total_spent, -2000);\n  // Refunds are not orders.\n  assert.equal(customers[1]!.order_count, 1);\n});\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"42cc566e-f2d8-46b4-b3c9-e3c16646dc93","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

string;\n\nbefore(async () => {\n  initSchema();\n  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO merchants (id, name) VALUES ('m_acme', 'Acme'), ('m_bistro', 'Bistro')`).run();\n  db.prepare(\n    `INSERT OR 'bruno@example.com', 2000, 'sale', 'completed')`,\n  ).run();\n\n  // Dev bootstrap off: these tests exercise the real authentication flow.\n  server = createApp({ enableDevAdminSession: false }).listen(0);\n  await new Promise((resolve) => server.once('listening', resolve));\n  baseUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${(server.address() as AddressInfo).port}`;\n\n  adminCookie = `${ADMIN_COOKIE}=${(await issueAdminToken('5m')).token}`;\n  acmeCookie = `${MERCHANT_COOKIE}=${(await issueMerchantToken('m_acme', '5m')).token}`;\n  bistroCookie = `${MERCHANT_COOKIE}=${(await issueMerchantToken('m_bistro', '5m')).token}`;\n});\n\nafter(() => {\n  server.close();\n});\n\n/** Issues a request with optional cookie and headers. */\nfunction call(path: string, init: { cookie?: string; headers?: Record<string, string>; method?: string; body?: unknown } = {}) {\n  const headers: Record<string, string> = { ...init.headers };\n  if (init.cookie) headers.Cookie = init.cookie;\n  if (init.body !== undefined) headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json';\n  return fetch(`${baseUrl}${path}`, {\n    method: init.method ?? 'GET',\n    headers,\n    ...(init.body === undefined ? {} : { body: JSON.stringify(init.body) }),\n  });\n}\n\ntest('guard: no token is rejected', async () => {\n  const response = await value.startsWith(`${MERCHANT_COOKIE}=`));\n  assert.ok(setCookie, 'expected a merchant_session cookie');\n  assert.match(setCookie!, /HttpOnly/);\n  assert.match(setCookie!, (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"605e453b-782b-4416-8f02-d2f608d72479","timestamp":"2026-09-12T06:29:33.115Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\006-refund-semantics-in-money-math.md","oldString":"**Status:** draft (rev 2 — open questions answered by the user)","newString":"**Status:** done (2026-09-12, rev 2) — implemented and validated locally; `docs/` pending authorization","originalFile":"# 006 — Refund semantics in money math\n\n**Status:** draft (rev 2 — open questions answered by the user)\n\nCloses Tier 1 group **E** (TD-05) from [tech_debt.md](../tech_debt.md), and TD-06 from [tech_debt_backlog.md](../tech_debt_backlog.md) since both are the same bug in two places.\n\n## Context\n\n`orders.type` is `'sale' | 'refund'`, and per [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) a refund records a reversed sale. But refunds are stored with a **positive** `total_amount`, and every money query sums `total_amount` without looking at `type`. So a refund *increases* revenue.\n\nMeasured on the current seeded database:\n\n| Merchant | Sales | Refunds | Reported today | Correct (net) | Overstated by |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `m_acme` | 375 736 | 48 628 | 424 364 | 327 108 | **+29.7 %** |\n| `m_bistro` | 383 990 | 33 669 | 417 659 | 350 321 | **+19.2 %** |\n\nA refund doesn't just fail to subtract — it adds the same amount again, so the error is roughly twice the refunded volume. This is the number the product exists to show, wrong in the optimistic direction.\n\nSchema facts that shape the fix (verified against the database):\n\n- `total_amount` is always positive, for both types.\n- There is **no column linking a refund to the sale it reverses** — netting can only be amount-based (logged as TD-18).\n- Every row is `status = 'completed'`; no other status exists yet.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. One definition of money, in one place\n\nAll money math moves behind named SQL expressions in `OrdersRepository`, so no route or repository can invent its own:\n\n```ts\n/** Signed amount: sales add, refunds subtract. */\nconst NET_AMOUNT = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN -total_amount ELSE total_amount END\";\nconst SALES_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'sale' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\nconst REFUNDS_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\n```\n\nRejected alternative: **store refunds as negative amounts**. It makes every query trivially correct, but it rewrites existing rows (migration + backfill), breaks the documented meaning of `total_amount`, and makes \"how much did we refund\" harder to ask. Netting at read time keeps the raw facts intact.\n\n### 2. `GET /api/revenue` returns net revenue, with the breakdown (Q3)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"from\": \"2026-08-01\", \"to\": \"2026-09-12\",\n  \"revenue_cents\": 327108,\n  \"revenue\": 3271.08,\n  \"gross_sales_cents\": 375736,\n  \"refunds_cents\": 48628\n}\n```\n\n`revenue_cents` keeps its name and becomes **net** (sales − refunds). The two new fields make the number auditable: a merchant seeing revenue drop can tell whether sales fell or refunds rose.\n\nNet revenue **can be negative** (a period with only refunds). That's correct and is asserted by a test rather than clamped to zero.\n\n### 3. `GET /api/metrics/summary` (Q1, Q2 — both figures, named explicitly)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"sales_orders\": 35,\n  \"refund_orders\": 5,\n  \"unique_customers\": 3,\n  \"avg_order_value_cents\": 10735,\n  \"avg_net_order_value_cents\": 9346\n}\n```\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `sales_orders` | Rows of type `sale` |\n| `refund_orders` | Rows of type `refund` |\n| `unique_customers` | Distinct customers **with at least one sale** |\n| `avg_order_value_cents` | Average amount of a sale — \"what does a typical order look like\" |\n| `avg_net_order_value_cents` | Net revenue ÷ number of sales — what a sale is worth *after* refunds |\n\nThe ambiguous `total_orders` is **removed** rather than redefined: per Q2 the two counts get dedicated names so nobody has to guess whether refunds are included. Any client reading `total_orders` gets `undefined` instead of a silently changed meaning — a loud break rather than a quiet one, and the only client is this repo's dashboard.\n\n### 4. `GET /api/metrics/top-customers` ranks by net spend\n\n`total_spent` becomes net per customer (sales − refunds) and `order_count` counts sales. A customer who refunded everything ranks last instead of top — which is the point of the report.\n\n### 5. `status` is ignored for now (Q4)\n\nEvery row is `completed`; filtering would be untested speculation. If other statuses ever appear, money math must exclude the non-completed ones — noted in the docs so it isn't forgotten.\n\n### 6. Gate against regression\n\n- **Unit tests on the repository** with a fixed dataset (golden numbers), plus property-style cases: a fully refunded period nets to `0`; a refunds-only period is negative; adding a sale and its refund leaves revenue unchanged.\n- **Architecture test extension:** `total_amount` may only be summed inside `src/dal/`. A route or script computing money on its own fails the suite. This is what stops the next endpoint from re-introducing the bug.\n\n### 7. Dashboard\n\nCards become: **Sales orders**, **Refunds**, **Avg order value**, **Revenue (last 30 days, net of refunds)**, with a small line under revenue showing gross and refunded amounts. Without the relabel the headline number just drops ~20–30 % with no explanation.\n\n### 8. Commits\n\n| # | Content | Tech debt |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `OrdersRepository`: net expressions + `revenue()` breakdown; revenue route; tests | TD-05 |\n| 2 | `MetricsRepository`: sales/refund counts, both averages, net `total_spent`; metrics routes; tests | TD-06 |\n| 3 | Architecture test extension (money math only inside `src/dal/`) | — |\n| 4 | Dashboard cards and labels | — |\n\n## Answers to the open questions\n\n- **Q1 — Both averages**: `avg_order_value_cents` (sales only) and `avg_net_order_value_cents` (net ÷ sales).\n- **Q2 — Both counts, dedicated names**: `sales_orders` and `refund_orders`; `total_orders` removed.\n- **Q3 — Yes**, revenue response carries `gross_sales_cents` and `refunds_cents`.\n- **Q4 — Ignore `status`** for now.\n- **Q5 — Logged** as TD-18 in `tech_debt_backlog.md` (no way to match a refund to its original sale).\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/dal/metrics-repository.ts`\n- `src/routes/revenue.ts`, `src/routes/metrics.ts`\n- `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`\n- `test/base-repository.test.ts`, new `test/money.test.ts`, `test/architecture.test.ts`, `test/auth-guard.test.ts` (updated expectations)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Input validation (TD-10, TD-11) and XSS (TD-12) — groups C and D.\n- Date-range semantics (TD-07) and mixed timestamp formats (TD-08) — backlog; the `created_at` filters are untouched.\n- Storing refunds as negative amounts, or adding a refund→sale link (TD-18).\n- `docs/` updates — authorization to be requested after validation (CLAUDE.md §6): `api.md` (response shapes) and `architecture.md` (the refund rule).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — new money tests plus the existing suite.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. Golden check against the seeded database: `m_acme` revenue reports `327108`, not `424364`; `m_bistro` `350321`, not `417659`.\n4. `curl /api/revenue` → net plus gross and refunds, reconciling (`gross - refunds === net`).\n5. `curl /api/metrics/summary` → `sales_orders + refund_orders` equals the old `total_orders`; both averages present and different when refunds exist.\n6. `top-customers`: a customer with more refunds than sales shows a negative `total_spent` and ranks last.\n7. Browser: cards read \"Sales orders\" / \"Refunds\" / \"Revenue (… net of refunds)\" with the gross/refunds line, matching the API.\n8. Architecture test fails if a route sums `total_amount` (verified by temporarily adding such a line).\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits. No schema or data migration is involved — the fix is read-side only, so rolling back cannot corrupt stored rows.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":6,"newStart":1,"newLines":6,"lines":[" # 006 — Refund semantics in money math"," ","-**Status:** draft (rev 2 — open questions answered by the user)","+**Status:** done (2026-09-12, rev 2) — implemented and validated locally; `docs/` pending authorization"," "," Closes Tier 1 group **E** (TD-05) from [tech_debt.md](../tech_debt.md), and TD-06 from [tech_debt_backlog.md](../tech_debt_backlog.md) since both are the same bug in two places."," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"f597262f-190f-4f4a-b82c-8989e3c46609","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"85c54576-1170-4533-b550-082143ddb20b","timestamp":"2026-09-12T06:38:32.112Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\docs\\api.md","oldString":"```json\n{ \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"from\": \"2026-08-01\", \"to\": \"2026-09-12\",\n  \"revenue_cents\": 238200, \"revenue\": 2382 }\n```\n\n> Refunds are currently summed as income, and `to` is exclusive so \"today\" is excluded — see TD-05 and TD-07 in `tech_debt.md`.","newString":"```json\n{ \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"from\": \"2026-08-01\", \"to\": \"2026-09-12\",\n  \"revenue_cents\": 327108, \"revenue\": 3271.08,\n  \"gross_sales_cents\": 375736, \"refunds_cents\": 48628 }\n```\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `revenue_cents` | **Net**: gross sales minus refunds. Can be negative when refunds exceed sales in the period — that is a real state, not an error |\n| `revenue` | The same figure in currency units |\n| `gross_sales_cents` | Sales only |\n| `refunds_cents` | Refunds only, as a positive number |\n\n`gross_sales_cents - refunds_cents === revenue_cents` always holds, so a drop in revenue can be attributed to falling sales or rising refunds without another call.\n\n> `to` is exclusive, so orders placed on the `to` date are not counted — see TD-07 in `tech_debt_backlog.md`.","originalFile":"# API reference\n\nBase URL: `http://localhost:3000` (or `PORT`). All responses are JSON.\n\nAuthentication and the branch/release process are described in [github-workflow.md](github-workflow.md) and [architecture.md](architecture.md).\n\n## Authentication\n\nTwo token types, both HS256 JWTs signed by the backend and delivered as **HttpOnly** cookies (`SameSite=Strict`, `Secure` on non-local requests). Nothing is stored in `localStorage`.\n\n| Token | Cookie | Claims | TTL | Can do |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Admin | `admin_session` | `role: admin`, `scope: mint` | `ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL` (8h) | Mint merchant tokens, list merchants |\n| Merchant | `merchant_session` | `role: merchant`, `scope: data`, `merchantId` | `MERCHANT_TOKEN_TTL` (10m) | Read that merchant's data |\n\nRules enforced by the guard:\n\n- **The token decides the merchant.** `X-Merchant-Id` is never used to select data; if it is sent and differs from the token's merchant, the request is rejected with `403 merchant_mismatch`.\n- **The admin token cannot read data** (`403 token_not_scoped_for_data`), and a merchant token cannot mint (`403 token_not_scoped_for_mint`). One rule, no exceptions: data always comes from a merchant-scoped token.\n- Merchant tokens are short-lived. When one expires the API answers `401 session_expired`; the client mints a new one and retries.\n\n### Getting a session\n\n**Locally**, the server hands an `admin_session` cookie to any request coming from loopback, so opening the dashboard is enough. This is a development convenience: it is gated on the TCP peer address (a spoofed `Host: localhost` from another machine does not pass) and can be disabled with `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION=off`. **It must never be enabled on a deployed instance** — it would hand a minting credential to every visitor.\n\n**Otherwise**, mint an admin token from the CLI and exchange it for the cookie:\n\n```sh\nnpm run token                    # prints an admin token (add expiresIn=30m to shorten it)\ncurl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/admin-session \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"token\":\"<token>\"}'\n```\n\n## Errors\n\n| Status | `error` | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| 400 | `merchant_id_required`, `token_required`, `invalid_body`, `missing_date_range` | Malformed request |\n| 401 | `unauthenticated` | No session cookie |\n| 401 | `session_expired` | Token invalid, expired, or signed with another key |\n| 403 | `merchant_mismatch` | `X-Merchant-Id` differs from the token's merchant |\n| 403 | `token_not_scoped_for_data` / `token_not_scoped_for_mint` | Right session, wrong token type |\n| 404 | `not_found`, `merchant_not_found` | Unknown id — including another merchant's order |\n| 500 | `internal_error` | Unhandled server error |\n\n---\n\n## Auth endpoints\n\n### `POST /api/auth/token`\nMints a merchant session. **Requires the admin token** (cookie or `Authorization: Bearer`).\n\nBody: `{ \"merchantId\": \"m_acme\" }` → `204` with `Set-Cookie: merchant_session`.\nErrors: `400 merchant_id_required`, `404 merchant_not_found`.\n\n### `POST /api/auth/admin-session`\nExchanges an admin token for the `admin_session` cookie. Body: `{ \"token\": \"<jwt>\" }` → `204`.\n\n### `GET /api/auth/session`\nDescribes the current session: `{ role, scope, merchantId, expiresAt }`. `401` when there is none.\n\n### `DELETE /api/auth/session`\nClears both cookies. `204`.\n\n## Data endpoints\n\nAll of these require a **merchant** session.\n\n### `GET /api/health`\nNo auth. `{ ok: true }`.\n\n### `GET /api/merchants`\nEvery merchant: `{ merchants: [{ id, name }] }`. **Requires the admin token** — a merchant session is bound to one merchant and gets `403`.\n\n### `GET /api/orders`\nOrders of the session's merchant, newest first.\n\nQuery: `from`, `to` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, applied only when both are present; `to` is exclusive), `limit` (default 100).\n\n```json\n{ \"orders\": [{ \"id\": \"…\", \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"customer_email\": \"ana@example.com\",\n               \"total_amount\": 11136, \"type\": \"sale\", \"status\": \"completed\",\n               \"created_at\": \"2026-09-11T11:45:35.866Z\" }] }\n```\n\n> `limit` is not validated yet — see TD-10 in `tech_debt.md`.\n\n### `GET /api/orders/:id`\nOne order: `{ order }`. An order belonging to another merchant returns `404 not_found`, not the row.\n\n### `POST /api/orders`\nCreates an order for the session's merchant. The merchant is taken from the token, never from the body.\n\nBody: `{ customer_email, total_amount, type? }` — `total_amount` in integer cents, `type` is `sale` (default) or `refund`. Returns `201` with `{ order }`.\n\n> Body validation is still thin — see TD-11 in `tech_debt.md`.\n\n### `GET /api/revenue?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD`\nBoth parameters are required.\n\n```json\n{ \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"from\": \"2026-08-01\", \"to\": \"2026-09-12\",\n  \"revenue_cents\": 238200, \"revenue\": 2382 }\n```\n\n> Refunds are currently summed as income, and `to` is exclusive so \"today\" is excluded — see TD-05 and TD-07 in `tech_debt.md`.\n\n### `GET /api/metrics/summary`\n\n```json\n{ \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"total_orders\": 40,\n  \"unique_customers\": 3, \"avg_order_value_cents\": 10609 }\n```\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `total_orders` | Rows in `orders` for the merchant (refunds included — TD-06) |\n| `unique_customers` | Distinct `customer_email` values |\n| `avg_order_value_cents` | Rounded average of `total_amount` |\n\n### `GET /api/metrics/top-customers`\nQuery: `limit` (default 5).\n\n```json\n{ \"customers\": [{ \"customer_email\": \"ana@example.com\", \"order_count\": 14, \"total_spent\": 181968 }] }\n```\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":100,"oldLines":11,"newStart":100,"newLines":21,"lines":[" "," ```json"," { \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"from\": \"2026-08-01\", \"to\": \"2026-09-12\",","-  \"revenue_cents\": 238200, \"revenue\": 2382 }","+  \"revenue_cents\": 327108, \"revenue\": 3271.08,","+  \"gross_sales_cents\": 375736, \"refunds_cents\": 48628 }"," ```"," ","-> Refunds are currently summed as income, and `to` is exclusive so \"today\" is excluded — see TD-05 and TD-07 in `tech_debt.md`.","+| Field | Meaning |","+|---|---|","+| `revenue_cents` | **Net**: gross sales minus refunds. Can be negative when refunds exceed sales in the period — that is a real state, not an error |","+| `revenue` | The same figure in currency units |","+| `gross_sales_cents` | Sales only |","+| `refunds_cents` | Refunds only, as a positive number |"," ","+`gross_sales_cents - refunds_cents === revenue_cents` always holds, so a drop in revenue can be attributed to falling sales or rising refunds without another call.","+","+> `to` is exclusive, so orders placed on the `to` date are not counted — see TD-07 in `tech_debt_backlog.md`.","+"," ### `GET /api/metrics/summary`"," "," ```json"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"426b6195-0e2e-4f86-be88-7983794acf62","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

Add `sales_orders` and `refund_orders` if you need the raw row count.","originalFile":"# API reference\n\nBase URL: `http://localhost:3000` (or `PORT`). All responses are JSON.\n\nAuthentication and the branch/release process are described in [github-workflow.md](github-workflow.md) and [architecture.md](architecture.md).\n\n## Authentication\n\nTwo token types, both HS256 JWTs signed by the backend and delivered as **HttpOnly** cookies (`SameSite=Strict`, `Secure` on non-local requests). Nothing is stored in `localStorage`.\n\n| Token | Cookie | Claims | TTL | Can do |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Admin | `admin_session` | `role: admin`, `scope: mint` | `ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL` (8h) | Mint merchant tokens, list merchants |\n| Merchant | `merchant_session` | `role: merchant`, `scope: data`, `merchantId` | `MERCHANT_TOKEN_TTL` (10m) | Read that merchant's data |\n\nRules enforced by the guard:\n\n- **The token decides the merchant.** `X-Merchant-Id` is never used to select data; if it is sent and differs from the token's merchant, the request is rejected with `403 merchant_mismatch`.\n- **The admin token cannot read data** (`403 token_not_scoped_for_data`), and a merchant token cannot mint (`403 token_not_scoped_for_mint`). One rule, no exceptions: data always comes from a merchant-scoped token.\n- Merchant tokens are short-lived. When one expires the API answers `401 session_expired`; the client mints a new one and retries.\n\n### Getting a session\n\n**Locally**, the server hands an `admin_session` cookie to any request coming from loopback, so opening the dashboard is enough. This is a development convenience: it is gated on the TCP peer address (a spoofed `Host: localhost` from another machine does not pass) and can be disabled with `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION=off`. **It must never be enabled on a deployed instance** — it would hand a minting credential to every visitor.\n\n**Otherwise**, mint an admin token from the CLI and exchange it for the cookie:\n\n```sh\nnpm run token                    # prints an admin token (add expiresIn=30m to shorten it)\ncurl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/admin-session \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"token\":\"<token>\"}'\n```\n\n## Errors\n\n| Status | `error` | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| 400 | `merchant_id_required`, `token_required`, `invalid_body`, `missing_date_range` | Malformed request |\n| 401 | `unauthenticated` | No session cookie |\n| 401 | `session_expired` | Token invalid, expired, or signed with another key |\n| 403 | `merchant_mismatch` | `X-Merchant-Id` differs from the token's merchant |\n| 403 | `token_not_scoped_for_data` / `token_not_scoped_for_mint` | Right session, wrong token type |\n| 404 | `not_found`, `merchant_not_found` | Unknown id — including another merchant's order |\n| 500 | `internal_error` | Unhandled server error |\n\n---\n\n## Auth endpoints\n\n### `POST /api/auth/token`\nMints a merchant session. **Requires the admin token** (cookie or `Authorization: Bearer`).\n\nBody: `{ \"merchantId\": \"m_acme\" }` → `204` with `Set-Cookie: merchant_session`.\nErrors: `400 merchant_id_required`, `404 merchant_not_found`.\n\n### `POST /api/auth/admin-session`\nExchanges an admin token for the `admin_session` cookie. Body: `{ \"token\": \"<jwt>\" }` → `204`.\n\n### `GET /api/auth/session`\nDescribes the current session: `{ role, scope, merchantId, expiresAt }`. `401` when there is none.\n\n### `DELETE /api/auth/session`\nClears both cookies. `204`.\n\n## Data endpoints\n\nAll of these require a **merchant** session.\n\n### `GET /api/health`\nNo auth. `{ ok: true }`.\n\n### `GET /api/merchants`\nEvery merchant: `{ merchants: [{ id, name }] }`. **Requires the admin token** — a merchant session is bound to one merchant and gets `403`.\n\n### `GET /api/orders`\nOrders of the session's merchant, newest first.\n\nQuery: `from`, `to` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, applied only when both are present; `to` is exclusive), `limit` (default 100).\n\n```json\n{ \"orders\": [{ \"id\": \"…\", \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"customer_email\": \"ana@example.com\",\n               \"total_amount\": 11136, \"type\": \"sale\", \"status\": \"completed\",\n               \"created_at\": \"2026-09-11T11:45:35.866Z\" }] }\n```\n\n> `limit` is not validated yet — see TD-10 in `tech_debt.md`.\n\n### `GET /api/orders/:id`\nOne order: `{ order }`. An order belonging to another merchant returns `404 not_found`, not the row.\n\n### `POST /api/orders`\nCreates an order for the session's merchant. The merchant is taken from the token, never from the body.\n\nBody: `{ customer_email, total_amount, type? }` — `total_amount` in integer cents, `type` is `sale` (default) or `refund`. Returns `201` with `{ order }`.\n\n> Body validation is still thin — see TD-11 in `tech_debt.md`.\n\n### `GET /api/revenue?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD`\nBoth parameters are required.\n\n```json\n{ \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"from\": \"2026-08-01\", \"to\": \"2026-09-12\",\n  \"revenue_cents\": 327108, \"revenue\": 3271.08,\n  \"gross_sales_cents\": 375736, \"refunds_cents\": 48628 }\n```\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `revenue_cents` | **Net**: gross sales minus refunds. Can be negative when refunds exceed sales in the period — that is a real state, not an error |\n| `revenue` | The same figure in currency units |\n| `gross_sales_cents` | Sales only |\n| `refunds_cents` | Refunds only, as a positive number |\n\n`gross_sales_cents - refunds_cents === revenue_cents` always holds, so a drop in revenue can be attributed to falling sales or rising refunds without another call.\n\n> `to` is exclusive, so orders placed on the `to` date are not counted — see TD-07 in `tech_debt_backlog.md`.\n\n### `GET /api/metrics/summary`\n\n```json\n{ \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"total_orders\": 40,\n  \"unique_customers\": 3, \"avg_order_value_cents\": 10609 }\n```\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `total_orders` | Rows in `orders` for the merchant (refunds included — TD-06) |\n| `unique_customers` | Distinct `customer_email` values |\n| `avg_order_value_cents` | Rounded average of `total_amount` |\n\n### `GET /api/metrics/top-customers`\nQuery: `limit` (default 5).\n\n```json\n{ \"customers\": [{ \"customer_email\": \"ana@example.com\", \"order_count\": 14, \"total_spent\": 181968 }] }\n```\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":118,"oldLines":16,"newStart":118,"newLines":21,"lines":[" ### `GET /api/metrics/summary`"," "," ```json","-{ \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\", \"total_orders\": (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"797fbece-8bdb-4c83-af1f-a32b50cb7ad4","timestamp":"2026-09-12T06:38:41.863Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\docs\\architecture.md","oldString":"| `src/dal/base-repository.ts` | `BaseRepository` / `AdminRepository`. **The only module that touches the database handle.** |","newString":"| `src/dal/base-repository.ts` | `BaseRepository` / `AdminRepository`. **The only module that touches the database handle.** |\n| `src/dal/money.ts` | The SQL expressions that define revenue. **The only place refund semantics live.** |","originalFile":"# Architecture\n\nA small merchant sales dashboard: static frontend, Express API, SQLite database.\n\nEndpoint details are in [api.md](api.md); branch and release rules in [github-workflow.md](github-workflow.md).\n\n## Request flow\n\n```\nbrowser (public/)\n  │  fetch with HttpOnly cookies\n  ▼\nexpress (src/app.ts)\n  ├─ devAdminSession      local requests only: hands out an admin cookie\n  ├─ express.static       serves public/\n  ├─ /api/auth            session endpoints (mint, exchange, whoami, logout)\n  ├─ /api/merchants       admin-scoped\n  └─ /api/orders|revenue|metrics\n        │  requireAuth() verifies the token and opens the auth context\n        ▼\n     routes → repositories (src/dal) → SQLite (src/db.ts)\n```\n\n## Modules\n\n| Path | Role |\n|---|---|\n| `src/server.ts` | Entry point: schema init, seed, listen. |\n| `src/app.ts` | Express wiring. `createApp()` is exported so tests can bind an ephemeral port. |\n| `src/config/env.ts` | The only reader of configuration. Loads `.env` with Node's built-in `process.loadEnvFile()`. |\n| `src/auth/jwt.ts` | Signs and verifies session tokens (`jose`, HS256). |\n| `src/auth/guard.ts` | `requireAuth({ scope })` — the middleware that protects routes. |\n| `src/auth/context.ts` | Per-request identity in an `AsyncLocalStorage`. |\n| `src/auth/local.ts` | Loopback detection for the development bootstrap. |\n| `src/auth/dev-session.ts` | Issues the admin cookie to local requests (dev only). |\n| `src/auth/cookies.ts` | Cookie parsing/serialization (no dependency). |\n| `src/dal/base-repository.ts` | `BaseRepository` / `AdminRepository`. **The only module that touches the database handle.** |\n| `src/dal/*-repository.ts` | One repository per entity. |\n| `src/routes/*.ts` | Express routers, one file per resource. |\n| `src/scripts/` | CLI entry points: `seed`, `issue-token`, `setup-env`, `check-deps`. |\n| `public/` | Static dashboard (plain HTML + `fetch`, no framework). |\n\n## Authentication\n\nTwo HS256 JWTs in HttpOnly cookies:\n\n- **Admin token** (`scope: mint`, 8h) — mints merchant tokens and lists merchants. It cannot read data.\n- **Merchant token** (`scope: data`, 10m) — reads only the merchant named in its `merchantId` claim.\n\nThe design rule is one line: **the merchant id always comes from a token the backend signed.** A client-sent `X-Merchant-Id` is only compared against the token, never used; a mismatch is `403`. Switching merchants in the dashboard means asking the backend for a new token, not sending a different header.\n\n`requireAuth()` verifies the cookie, then runs the rest of the request inside an `AsyncLocalStorage` context. Any class or function reached during the request can call `getAuthContext()` — no parameter threading — and the call **throws** if no context exists, so code can't accidentally run unauthenticated.\n\n### Development bootstrap, and its limit\n\n`devAdminSession` hands an admin cookie to requests whose **TCP peer address is loopback** (a spoofed `Host: localhost` from elsewhere does not qualify), so `npm run dev` works without a login step. `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION=off` disables it.\n\nThis is a convenience, not a login. On a deployed instance it would give every visitor a credential that can mint any merchant's token. A real deployment needs an actual login issuing the admin token, and this middleware removed.\n\n## Data access\n\nEvery order query goes through a repository. `BaseRepository` reads the merchant id from the auth context and injects it into each `SELECT` and `INSERT`; subclasses never see the connection and never pass a merchant id, so a repository *cannot* forget the tenancy filter. `AdminRepository` covers `merchants` — the tenant list itself, which isn't merchant-scoped — and requires an admin caller instead.\n\n`test/architecture.test.ts` enforces the rule: if any module other than `base-repository.ts` imports the `db` handle, the suite fails. Standalone scripts are exempt.\n\n## Data model\n\nTwo tables, `merchants` and `orders`; canonical DDL in `src/db.ts`.\n\n`orders.type` is `'sale' | 'refund'`. A refund row records that a sale was reversed; it does not by itself reverse the sale row, and the revenue query currently sums both (TD-05).\n\n## Configuration\n\n| Variable | Default | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `JWT_SECRET` | generated | Missing on a local start → generated and appended to `.env` so server and CLI share it. |\n| `PORT` | `3000` | |\n| `DB_PATH` | `data/dashboard.db` | `:memory:` in tests. |\n| `ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL` | `8h` | |\n| `MERCHANT_TOKEN_TTL` | `10m` | |\n| `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION` | `on` | `off` disables the local admin cookie. |\n\n`npm run setup:env` creates `.env` from `.env.example`; it never overwrites an existing value.\n\n## Known gaps\n\nTracked in `tech_debt.md` (active) and `tech_debt_backlog.md` (deferred). The ones visible from this document: unvalidated `limit` and request bodies (TD-10, TD-11), stored XSS in the dashboard table (TD-12), and refunds counted as income (TD-05, TD-06).\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":35,"oldLines":6,"newStart":35,"newLines":7,"lines":[" | `src/auth/dev-session.ts` | Issues the admin cookie to local requests (dev only). |"," | `src/auth/cookies.ts` | Cookie parsing/serialization (no dependency). |"," | `src/dal/base-repository.ts` | `BaseRepository` / `AdminRepository`. **The only module that touches the database handle.** |","+| `src/dal/money.ts` | The SQL expressions that define revenue. **The only place refund semantics live.** |"," | `src/dal/*-repository.ts` | One repository per entity. |"," | `src/routes/*.ts` | Express routers, one file per resource. |"," | `src/scripts/` | CLI entry points: `seed`, `issue-token`, `setup-env`, `check-deps`. |"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"63556f35-f734-4be6-8754-2a7c04ec7e4a","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

The ones visible from this document: unvalidated `limit` and request bodies (TD-10, TD-11), stored XSS in the dashboard table (TD-12), no refund→sale link (TD-18), and the exclusive `to` bound in date ranges (TD-07).","originalFile":"# Architecture\n\nA small merchant sales dashboard: static frontend, Express API, SQLite database.\n\nEndpoint details are in [api.md](api.md); branch and release rules in [github-workflow.md](github-workflow.md).\n\n## Request flow\n\n```\nbrowser (public/)\n  │  fetch with HttpOnly cookies\n  ▼\nexpress (src/app.ts)\n  ├─ devAdminSession      local requests only: hands out an admin cookie\n  ├─ express.static       serves public/\n  ├─ /api/auth            session endpoints (mint, exchange, whoami, logout)\n  ├─ /api/merchants       admin-scoped\n  └─ /api/orders|revenue|metrics\n        │  requireAuth() verifies the token and opens the auth context\n        ▼\n     routes → repositories (src/dal) → SQLite (src/db.ts)\n```\n\n## Modules\n\n| Path | Role |\n|---|---|\n| `src/server.ts` | Entry point: schema init, seed, listen. |\n| `src/app.ts` | Express wiring. `createApp()` is exported so tests can bind an ephemeral port. |\n| `src/config/env.ts` | The only reader of configuration. Loads `.env` with Node's built-in `process.loadEnvFile()`. |\n| `src/auth/jwt.ts` | Signs and verifies session tokens (`jose`, HS256). |\n| `src/auth/guard.ts` | `requireAuth({ scope })` — the middleware that protects routes. |\n| `src/auth/context.ts` | Per-request identity in an `AsyncLocalStorage`. |\n| `src/auth/local.ts` | Loopback detection for the development bootstrap. |\n| `src/auth/dev-session.ts` | Issues the admin cookie to local requests (dev only). |\n| `src/auth/cookies.ts` | Cookie parsing/serialization (no dependency). |\n| `src/dal/base-repository.ts` | `BaseRepository` / `AdminRepository`. **The only module that touches the database handle.** |\n| `src/dal/money.ts` | The SQL expressions that define revenue. **The only place refund semantics live.** |\n| `src/dal/*-repository.ts` | One repository per entity. |\n| `src/routes/*.ts` | Express routers, one file per resource. |\n| `src/scripts/` | CLI entry points: `seed`, `issue-token`, `setup-env`, `check-deps`. |\n| `public/` | Static dashboard (plain HTML + `fetch`, no framework). |\n\n## Authentication\n\nTwo HS256 JWTs in HttpOnly cookies:\n\n- **Admin token** (`scope: mint`, 8h) — mints merchant tokens and lists merchants. It cannot read data.\n- **Merchant token** (`scope: data`, 10m) — reads only the merchant named in its `merchantId` claim.\n\nThe design rule is one line: **the merchant id always comes from a token the backend signed.** A client-sent `X-Merchant-Id` is only compared against the token, never used; a mismatch is `403`. Switching merchants in the dashboard means asking the backend for a new token, not sending a different header.\n\n`requireAuth()` verifies the cookie, then runs the rest of the request inside an `AsyncLocalStorage` context. Any class or function reached during the request can call `getAuthContext()` — no parameter threading — and the call **throws** if no context exists, so code can't accidentally run unauthenticated.\n\n### Development bootstrap, and its limit\n\n`devAdminSession` hands an admin cookie to requests whose **TCP peer address is loopback** (a spoofed `Host: localhost` from elsewhere does not qualify), so `npm run dev` works without a login step. `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION=off` disables it.\n\nThis is a convenience, not a login. On a deployed instance it would give every visitor a credential that can mint any merchant's token. A real deployment needs an actual login issuing the admin token, and this middleware removed.\n\n## Data access\n\nEvery order query goes through a repository. `BaseRepository` reads the merchant id from the auth context and injects it into each `SELECT` and `INSERT`; subclasses never see the connection and never pass a merchant id, so a repository *cannot* forget the tenancy filter. `AdminRepository` covers `merchants` — the tenant list itself, which isn't merchant-scoped — and requires an admin caller instead.\n\n`test/architecture.test.ts` enforces the rule: if any module other than `base-repository.ts` imports the `db` handle, the suite fails. Standalone scripts are exempt.\n\n## Data model\n\nTwo tables, `merchants` and `orders`; canonical DDL in `src/db.ts`.\n\n`orders.type` is `'sale' | 'refund'`. A refund row records that a sale was reversed and stores a **positive** `total_amount` like any other row; it does not modify the sale row.\n\n## Money\n\nBecause refunds are stored positive, summing `total_amount` counts a refund as income — the amount is added instead of subtracted, so the error is about twice the refunded volume. All money figures are therefore derived from the named expressions in `src/dal/money.ts`:\n\n| Expression | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `NET_AMOUNT` | Sales add, refunds subtract → net revenue |\n| `SALES_ONLY` / `REFUNDS_ONLY` | The two halves, so a net figure can be explained |\n| `SALE_COUNT` / `REFUND_COUNT` | Orders placed vs refunds issued, never mixed |\n\nNet revenue can be negative for a period dominated by refunds; nothing clamps it. `test/architecture.test.ts` fails the build if `total_amount` is aggregated outside `src/dal/`, so a new endpoint can't quietly reintroduce the bug.\n\nTwo limits worth knowing: refunds cannot be matched to the sale they reverse (no link column — TD-18), so netting is exact in total but can't answer \"was *this* sale refunded\"; and `status` is not filtered, because every row is `completed` today. If other statuses appear, money math must exclude the non-completed ones.\n\n## Configuration\n\n| Variable | Default | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `JWT_SECRET` | generated | Missing on a local start → generated and appended to `.env` so server and CLI share it. |\n| `PORT` | `3000` | |\n| `DB_PATH` | `data/dashboard.db` | `:memory:` in tests. |\n| `ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL` | `8h` | |\n| `MERCHANT_TOKEN_TTL` | `10m` | |\n| `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION` | `on` | `off` disables the local admin cookie. |\n\n`npm run setup:env` creates `.env` from `.env.example`; it never overwrites an existing value.\n\n## Known gaps\n\nTracked in `tech_debt.md` (active) and `tech_debt_backlog.md` (deferred). The ones visible from this document: unvalidated `limit` and request bodies (TD-10, TD-11), stored XSS in the dashboard table (TD-12), and refunds counted as income (TD-05, TD-06).\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":99,"oldLines":4,"newStart":99,"newLines":4,"lines":[" "," ## Known gaps"," ","-Tracked in `tech_debt.md` (active) and `tech_debt_backlog.md` (deferred). The active list is [tech_debt.md](tech_debt.md) (Tier 1); nothing here is picked up until that file is empty, unless an item happens to fall inside a file already being changed.\n\n| Tier | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| **SHOULD — next** | Wrong or fragile behavior users will hit. Fix right after the Tier 1 items. |\n| **CAN WAIT** | Real, but low blast radius. Cleanup / hygiene. |\n\nIDs are stable (`TD-01` … `TD-17`) and match the numbering in [tech_debt.md](tech_debt.md). Severity is the one from the first review.\n\n---\n\n# Tier 2 — SHOULD (next)\n\n- [ ] **TD-18 · A refund can't be matched to the sale it reverses** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** found while designing [plan 006](plans/006-refund-semantics-in-money-math.md). Netting revenue by amount makes the totals right, but nothing ties a refund row to its original sale, so the data can't answer \"was this sale refunded?\", a refund can exceed the sale it reverses, and a refund recorded in a later period makes that period negative while the earlier one stays overstated. Partial refunds are indistinguishable from unrelated ones.\n  - Where: [src/db.ts:23](src/db.ts:23) (the `orders` table has no parent/order reference)\n  - What happens: `orders` holds `id, merchant_id, customer_email, total_amount, type, status, created_at` — and no link column. Shape to decide: a nullable `refunded_order_id` referencing `orders(id)`, plus a rule for how much of a sale may be refunded.\n\n- [ ] **TD-16 · Test coverage is minimal** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** the gate that keeps Tier 1 fixed. Right now nothing would catch a regression in auth, tenancy scoping, or revenue math.\n  - Where: [test/orders.test.ts](test/orders.test.ts)\n  - What happens: only the DAL's `create`, `listByMerchant`, and `getById` are covered. No route, auth, revenue, or metrics tests.\n\n- [ ] **TD-06 · Summary metrics treat refunds as sales** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** same class of error as TD-05 and visible on the same screen, but these numbers are informational rather than the money figure. Cheap to fold into the TD-05 commit if the metrics queries already moved into the DAL (TD-04).\n  - Where: [src/routes/metrics.ts:17](src/routes/metrics.ts:17), [src/routes/metrics.ts:45](src/routes/metrics.ts:45)\n  - What happens: `total_orders`, `unique_customers`, `avg_order_value_cents`, and `top-customers.total_spent` count every row the same way.\n\n- [ ] **TD-07 · The revenue range excludes the `to` day, so the dashboard leaves out today** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** a visibly wrong number every day, with an obvious fix, but it under-reports rather than overstating.\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-dal.ts:59](src/dal/orders-dal.ts:59), [public/app.js:28](public/app.js:28)\n  - What happens: the filter is `created_at < to` with `to` as a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, so the whole `to` day is excluded — and the frontend sends `to = today`.\n\n- [ ] **TD-08 · `created_at` is stored in mixed formats** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** data-integrity debt that gets more expensive the more rows accumulate, and it quietly corrupts ordering and range filters.\n  - Where: [src/db.ts:30](src/db.ts:30), [src/scripts/seed.ts:21](src/scripts/seed.ts:21)\n  - What happens: the seed stores ISO 8601 (`2026-09-10T12:00:00.000Z`) while `POST`-created orders use SQLite's `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` (`2026-09-10 12:00:00`). Comparisons and `ORDER BY` are string-based, so ordering within a day can be wrong; the browser also reads the format without `T`/`Z` as local time.\n\n- [ ] **TD-03 · `POST /api/orders` with a non-existent merchant returns 500** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** wrong status code and a leaked internal error, not a data or money problem. Largely disappears once TD-01 is fixed.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:35](src/routes/orders.ts:35)\n  - What happens: an unknown `merchantId` violates the `orders.merchant_id → merchants.id` FK (`foreign_keys = ON`); the exception reaches the generic handler and returns `500 internal_error`.\n\n---\n\n# Tier 3 — CAN WAIT\n\n- [ ] **TD-09 · `from`/`to` are not validated** — Severity: Low\n  - **Why here:** garbage dates produce empty or odd results for the caller who sent them; no cross-tenant or money impact. Natural companion to TD-10/TD-11 (Tier 1, group C) if that validation shape is reusable.\n  - Where: [src/routes/revenue.ts:12](src/routes/revenue.ts:12), [src/routes/orders.ts:9](src/routes/orders.ts:9)\n  - What happens: any string is accepted and compared lexicographically. In `GET /api/orders`, sending only one of the two parameters silently drops the filter.\n\n- [ ] **TD-13 · The frontend doesn't handle API errors** — Severity: Low\n  - **Why here:** poor UX, not incorrect data — although \"silently shows `$0.00` on a 500\" can be mistaken for real data.\n  - Where: [public/app.js:8](public/app.js:8)\n  - What happens: `api()` never checks `r.ok`, so error responses are rendered as empty values.\n\n- [ ] **TD-14 · The merchant list is hardcoded in the HTML** — Severity: Low\n  - **Why here:** demo-scaffolding duplication; it will be revisited anyway when real auth lands (TD-01).\n  - Where: [public/index.html:28](public/index.html:28)\n  - What happens: the selector duplicates [src/scripts/seed.ts:4](src/scripts/seed.ts:4) instead of coming from the API.\n\n- [x] **TD-17 · `docs/architecture.md` is outdated** — Severity: Low — **resolved**\n  - Resolved alongside [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md): `docs/architecture.md` was rewritten (auth layer, repository base class, configuration, request flow) and `docs/api.md` now documents the session model. The stale `lib/` reference and the \"unmaintained draft\" banner are gone.\n\n- [ ] **TD-15 · `npm run seed` probably does nothing on Windows** — Severity: Low\n  - **Why last:** masked in practice — the server calls `seedIfEmpty()` on startup — so the visible impact is zero today.\n  - Where: [src/scripts/seed.ts:60](src/scripts/seed.ts:60)\n  - What happens: the `isMain` check compares `import.meta.url` (`file:///C:/...`) against `process.argv[1]` (`C:\\...`), so neither condition matches.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":23,"oldLines":10,"newStart":23,"newLines":8,"lines":["   - Where: [test/orders.test.ts](test/orders.test.ts)","   - What happens: only the DAL's `create`, `listByMerchant`, and `getById` are covered. C stops new payloads from being stored; D makes rendering safe regardless of what's already in the database.","originalFile":"# Tech debt — Tier 1 (MUST, urgent)\n\nThe items we're working on now. Everything else lives in [tech_debt_backlog.md](tech_debt_backlog.md) (Tier 2 and Tier 3) and is deliberately out of sight until this file is empty.\n\n## How this is ranked\n\nPriority balances **product impact** against **security and financial risk**, not raw severity:\n\n- An item that lets an attacker read another merchant's data, or that can cost money, outranks an item that only shows a wrong number on a dashboard.\n- Items that **amplify each other** are ranked together — an unbounded `limit` (TD-10) is worth more to an attacker the weaker the tenancy boundary is.\n- Wrong revenue math (TD-05) is ranked here anyway: merchants make decisions with that number, and it overstates income.\n\nIDs are stable (`TD-01` … `TD-17`) and don't change when the order does. Severity is the one from the first review.\n\n## Groups at a glance\n\nItems are grouped by the domain and files they touch, so each group can land as one commit.\n\n| Group | Items | Files | Status |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **A — Tenancy scoping through the DAL** | TD-02, TD-04 | `dal/`, `routes/orders.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | ✅ Done — [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md) |\n| **B — Authentication layer** | TD-01 | `auth/`, `server.ts`, `public/app.js` | ✅ Done — [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md) |\n| **C — Input validation at the API edge** | TD-10, TD-11 | `routes/orders.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | ⬜ Open |\n| **D — Output escaping in the dashboard** | TD-12 | `public/app.js` | ⬜ Open |\n| **E — Refund semantics in money math** | TD-05 | `dal/orders-repository.ts`, `routes/revenue.ts` | ⬜ Open |\n\nSuggested order for what's left: **C → E → D**. C stops new payloads from being stored, E fixes the money number, D makes rendering safe regardless of what's already in the database.\n\n---\n\n## Group C — Input validation at the API edge\n\n*Files: [src/routes/orders.ts](src/routes/orders.ts), [src/routes/metrics.ts](src/routes/metrics.ts)*\n\nBoth are \"the API trusts whatever the client sends\". Same layer, same kind of fix (one validation shape applied to query params and body).\n\n- [ ] **TD-10 · `limit` is not validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** in SQLite `LIMIT -1` means \"no limit\", so `?limit=-1` returns every order of the merchant in one request — an easy way to exhaust the server, and a bulk export of everything a compromised session can reach.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:11](src/routes/orders.ts:11), [src/routes/metrics.ts:43](src/routes/metrics.ts:43)\n  - What happens: `Number(req.query.limit)` can yield `NaN`, a decimal, or a negative number. There is no upper bound.\n\n- [ ] **TD-11 · The `POST /api/orders` body is barely validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** it's the entry point that feeds TD-12, and it lets corrupt money into the database — negative or fractional amounts in a column that holds integer cents.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:25](src/routes/orders.ts:25)\n  - What happens: `type` accepts any string (not only `sale`/`refund`), `total_amount` accepts negatives and decimals, and `customer_email` isn't validated as an email.\n\n## Group D — Output escaping in the dashboard\n\n*File: [public/app.js](public/app.js)*\n\n- [ ] **TD-12 · Stored XSS in the orders table** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** the dashboard executes attacker-controlled markup, and the payload is planted through `POST /api/orders` (TD-11).\n  - **Why it ships after C:** C stops new payloads from being stored; D makes rendering safe regardless of what's already in the database. Both are needed — C alone doesn't clean existing rows.\n  - Where: [public/app.js:63](public/app.js:63)\n  - What happens: each row is built with `innerHTML`, interpolating `o.customer_email` and `o.type` unsanitized. (The file was rewritten for the session flow in plan 005; this line was left as-is on purpose so the fix is its own reviewable change.)\n\n## Group E — Refund semantics in money math\n\n*Files: [src/dal/orders-repository.ts](src/dal/orders-repository.ts), [src/routes/revenue.ts](src/routes/revenue.ts)*\n\n- [ ] **TD-05 · Revenue counts refunds as income** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** the headline number of the product is wrong, and wrong in the optimistic direction. A merchant reading \"Revenue (last 30 days)\" is told they earned money they refunded.\n  - **Related, deferred:** TD-06 (summary metrics treat refunds as sales) is the same class of bug on informational numbers and sits in the backlog. Now that metrics go through `MetricsRepository`, fixing TD-06 in the same commit is nearly free.\n  - Where: [src/dal/orders-repository.ts:98](src/dal/orders-repository.ts:98)\n  - What happens: `sumAmount` runs `SUM(total_amount)` without looking at `type`. Refunds are stored with a positive amount (see [src/scripts/seed.ts:43](src/scripts/seed.ts:43)), so they add instead of subtracting. Per [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), a refund represents a reversed sale.\n\n---\n\n# Resolved\n\n- [x] **TD-01 · The `X-Merchant-Id` header is not verified** — Severity: High\n  - Resolved by [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md): sessions are HS256 JWTs in HttpOnly cookies. Data access requires a merchant-scoped token whose `merchantId` claim the backend signs; a client-sent `X-Merchant-Id` is only compared, never used, and a mismatch is `403 merchant_mismatch`. Merchant switching goes through `POST /api/auth/token`, guarded by an admin token that cannot read data.\n  - Caveat carried forward: `devAdminSession` hands an admin cookie to loopback requests for local development. Gated on the TCP peer address and disabled with `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION=off`; it must never run on a deployed instance.\n\n- [x] **TD-02 · `GET /api/orders/:id` does not filter by merchant** — Severity: High\n  - Resolved by [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md): `OrdersRepository.getById` goes through `BaseRepository`, which injects the merchant filter, so another merchant's order returns `404`. Covered by `test/base-repository.test.ts` and `test/auth-guard.test.ts`.\n\n- [x] **TD-04 · `metrics.ts` bypasses the DAL** — Severity: Medium\n  - Resolved by [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md): metrics queries moved into `MetricsRepository`, and the second read-only SQLite connection is gone. `test/architecture.test.ts` fails if any module other than `base-repository.ts` imports the database handle, so the bypass can't come back quietly.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":22,"oldLines":9,"newStart":22,"newLines":9,"lines":[" | **B — Authentication layer** | TD-01 | `auth/`, `server.ts`, `public/app.js` | ✅ Done — [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md) |"," | **C — Input validation at the API edge** | TD-10, TD-11 | `routes/orders.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | ⬜ Open |"," | **D — Output escaping in the dashboard** | TD-12 | `public/app.js` | ⬜ Open |","-| **E — Refund semantics in money math** | TD-05 | `dal/orders-repository.ts`, `routes/revenue.ts` | ⬜ Open |","+| **E — Refund semantics in money math** | TD-05 | `dal/`, `routes/revenue.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | ✅ Done — [plan 006](plans/006-refund-semantics-in-money-math.md) |"," ","-Suggested order for what's left: **C → E → D**. Severity is the one from the first review.\n\n## Groups at a glance\n\nItems are grouped by the domain and files they touch, so each group can land as one commit.\n\n| Group | Items | Files | Status |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **A — Tenancy scoping through the DAL** | TD-02, TD-04 | `dal/`, `routes/orders.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | ✅ Done — [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md) |\n| **B — Authentication layer** | TD-01 | `auth/`, `server.ts`, `public/app.js` | ✅ Done — [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md) |\n| **C — Input validation at the API edge** | TD-10, TD-11 | `routes/orders.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | ⬜ Open |\n| **D — Output escaping in the dashboard** | TD-12 | `public/app.js` | ⬜ Open |\n| **E — Refund semantics in money math** | TD-05 | `dal/`, `routes/revenue.ts`, `routes/metrics.ts` | ✅ Done — [plan 006](plans/006-refund-semantics-in-money-math.md) |\n\nSuggested order for what's left: **C → D**. C stops new payloads from being stored; D makes rendering safe regardless of what's already in the database.\n\n---\n\n## Group C — Input validation at the API edge\n\n*Files: [src/routes/orders.ts](src/routes/orders.ts), [src/routes/metrics.ts](src/routes/metrics.ts)*\n\nBoth are \"the API trusts whatever the client sends\". Same layer, same kind of fix (one validation shape applied to query params and body).\n\n- [ ] **TD-10 · `limit` is not validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** in SQLite `LIMIT -1` means \"no limit\", so `?limit=-1` returns every order of the merchant in one request — an easy way to exhaust the server, and a bulk export of everything a compromised session can reach.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:11](src/routes/orders.ts:11), [src/routes/metrics.ts:43](src/routes/metrics.ts:43)\n  - What happens: `Number(req.query.limit)` can yield `NaN`, a decimal, or a negative number. There is no upper bound.\n\n- [ ] **TD-11 · The `POST /api/orders` body is barely validated** — Severity: Medium\n  - **Why here:** it's the entry point that feeds TD-12, and it lets corrupt money into the database — negative or fractional amounts in a column that holds integer cents.\n  - Where: [src/routes/orders.ts:25](src/routes/orders.ts:25)\n  - What happens: `type` accepts any string (not only `sale`/`refund`), `total_amount` accepts negatives and decimals, and `customer_email` isn't validated as an email.\n\n## Group D — Output escaping in the dashboard\n\n*File: [public/app.js](public/app.js)*\n\n- [ ] **TD-12 · Stored XSS in the orders table** — Severity: High\n  - **Why here:** the dashboard executes attacker-controlled markup, and the payload is planted through `POST /api/orders` (TD-11).\n  - **Why it ships after C:** C stops new payloads from being stored; D makes rendering safe regardless of what's already in the database. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"c09e126e-6cfd-4f50-90cc-c3fc2a0b46b0","timestamp":"2026-09-12T06:39:14.454Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\006-refund-semantics-in-money-math.md","oldString":"**Status:** done (2026-09-12, rev 2) — implemented and validated locally; `docs/` pending authorization","newString":"**Status:** done (2026-09-12, rev 2) — implemented, validated locally, `docs/` updated","originalFile":"# 006 — Refund semantics in money math\n\n**Status:** done (2026-09-12, rev 2) — implemented and validated locally; `docs/` pending authorization\n\nCloses Tier 1 group **E** (TD-05) from [tech_debt.md](../tech_debt.md), and TD-06 from [tech_debt_backlog.md](../tech_debt_backlog.md) since both are the same bug in two places.\n\n## Context\n\n`orders.type` is `'sale' | 'refund'`, and per [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) a refund records a reversed sale. But refunds are stored with a **positive** `total_amount`, and every money query sums `total_amount` without looking at `type`. So a refund *increases* revenue.\n\nMeasured on the current seeded database:\n\n| Merchant | Sales | Refunds | Reported today | Correct (net) | Overstated by |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `m_acme` | 375 736 | 48 628 | 424 364 | 327 108 | **+29.7 %** |\n| `m_bistro` | 383 990 | 33 669 | 417 659 | 350 321 | **+19.2 %** |\n\nA refund doesn't just fail to subtract — it adds the same amount again, so the error is roughly twice the refunded volume. This is the number the product exists to show, wrong in the optimistic direction.\n\nSchema facts that shape the fix (verified against the database):\n\n- `total_amount` is always positive, for both types.\n- There is **no column linking a refund to the sale it reverses** — netting can only be amount-based (logged as TD-18).\n- Every row is `status = 'completed'`; no other status exists yet.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. One definition of money, in one place\n\nAll money math moves behind named SQL expressions in `OrdersRepository`, so no route or repository can invent its own:\n\n```ts\n/** Signed amount: sales add, refunds subtract. */\nconst NET_AMOUNT = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN -total_amount ELSE total_amount END\";\nconst SALES_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'sale' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\nconst REFUNDS_ONLY = \"CASE WHEN type = 'refund' THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END\";\n```\n\nRejected alternative: **store refunds as negative amounts**. It makes every query trivially correct, but it rewrites existing rows (migration + backfill), breaks the documented meaning of `total_amount`, and makes \"how much did we refund\" harder to ask. Netting at read time keeps the raw facts intact.\n\n### 2. `GET /api/revenue` returns net revenue, with the breakdown (Q3)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"from\": \"2026-08-01\", \"to\": \"2026-09-12\",\n  \"revenue_cents\": 327108,\n  \"revenue\": 3271.08,\n  \"gross_sales_cents\": 375736,\n  \"refunds_cents\": 48628\n}\n```\n\n`revenue_cents` keeps its name and becomes **net** (sales − refunds). The two new fields make the number auditable: a merchant seeing revenue drop can tell whether sales fell or refunds rose.\n\nNet revenue **can be negative** (a period with only refunds). That's correct and is asserted by a test rather than clamped to zero.\n\n### 3. `GET /api/metrics/summary` (Q1, Q2 — both figures, named explicitly)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"merchant_id\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"sales_orders\": 35,\n  \"refund_orders\": 5,\n  \"unique_customers\": 3,\n  \"avg_order_value_cents\": 10735,\n  \"avg_net_order_value_cents\": 9346\n}\n```\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `sales_orders` | Rows of type `sale` |\n| `refund_orders` | Rows of type `refund` |\n| `unique_customers` | Distinct customers **with at least one sale** |\n| `avg_order_value_cents` | Average amount of a sale — \"what does a typical order look like\" |\n| `avg_net_order_value_cents` | Net revenue ÷ number of sales — what a sale is worth *after* refunds |\n\nThe ambiguous `total_orders` is **removed** rather than redefined: per Q2 the two counts get dedicated names so nobody has to guess whether refunds are included. Any client reading `total_orders` gets `undefined` instead of a silently changed meaning — a loud break rather than a quiet one, and the only client is this repo's dashboard.\n\n### 4. `GET /api/metrics/top-customers` ranks by net spend\n\n`total_spent` becomes net per customer (sales − refunds) and `order_count` counts sales. A customer who refunded everything ranks last instead of top — which is the point of the report.\n\n### 5. `status` is ignored for now (Q4)\n\nEvery row is `completed`; filtering would be untested speculation. If other statuses ever appear, money math must exclude the non-completed ones — noted in the docs so it isn't forgotten.\n\n### 6. Gate against regression\n\n- **Unit tests on the repository** with a fixed dataset (golden numbers), plus property-style cases: a fully refunded period nets to `0`; a refunds-only period is negative; adding a sale and its refund leaves revenue unchanged.\n- **Architecture test extension:** `total_amount` may only be summed inside `src/dal/`. A route or script computing money on its own fails the suite. This is what stops the next endpoint from re-introducing the bug.\n\n### 7. Dashboard\n\nCards become: **Sales orders**, **Refunds**, **Avg order value**, **Revenue (last 30 days, net of refunds)**, with a small line under revenue showing gross and refunded amounts. Without the relabel the headline number just drops ~20–30 % with no explanation.\n\n### 8. Commits\n\n| # | Content | Tech debt |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `OrdersRepository`: net expressions + `revenue()` breakdown; revenue route; tests | TD-05 |\n| 2 | `MetricsRepository`: sales/refund counts, both averages, net `total_spent`; metrics routes; tests | TD-06 |\n| 3 | Architecture test extension (money math only inside `src/dal/`) | — |\n| 4 | Dashboard cards and labels | — |\n\n## Answers to the open questions\n\n- **Q1 — Both averages**: `avg_order_value_cents` (sales only) and `avg_net_order_value_cents` (net ÷ sales).\n- **Q2 — Both counts, dedicated names**: `sales_orders` and `refund_orders`; `total_orders` removed.\n- **Q3 — Yes**, revenue response carries `gross_sales_cents` and `refunds_cents`.\n- **Q4 — Ignore `status`** for now.\n- **Q5 — Logged** as TD-18 in `tech_debt_backlog.md` (no way to match a refund to its original sale).\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/dal/metrics-repository.ts`\n- `src/routes/revenue.ts`, `src/routes/metrics.ts`\n- `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`\n- `test/base-repository.test.ts`, new `test/money.test.ts`, `test/architecture.test.ts`, `test/auth-guard.test.ts` (updated expectations)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Input validation (TD-10, TD-11) and XSS (TD-12) — groups C and D.\n- Date-range semantics (TD-07) and mixed timestamp formats (TD-08) — backlog; the `created_at` filters are untouched.\n- Storing refunds as negative amounts, or adding a refund→sale link (TD-18).\n- `docs/` updates — authorization to be requested after validation (CLAUDE.md §6): `api.md` (response shapes) and `architecture.md` (the refund rule).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — new money tests plus the existing suite.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. Golden check against the seeded database: `m_acme` revenue reports `327108`, not `424364`; `m_bistro` `350321`, not `417659`.\n4. `curl /api/revenue` → net plus gross and refunds, reconciling (`gross - refunds === net`).\n5. `curl /api/metrics/summary` → `sales_orders + refund_orders` equals the old `total_orders`; both averages present and different when refunds exist.\n6. `top-customers`: a customer with more refunds than sales shows a negative `total_spent` and ranks last.\n7. Browser: cards read \"Sales orders\" / \"Refunds\" / \"Revenue (… net of refunds)\" with the gross/refunds line, matching the API.\n8. Architecture test fails if a route sums `total_amount` (verified by temporarily adding such a line).\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits. No schema or data migration is involved — the fix is read-side only, so rolling back cannot corrupt stored rows.\n\n## Results\n\n| Step | Result |\n|---|---|\n| 1. `npm test` | ✅ 63/63 (11 new money tests) |\n| 2. `tsc --noEmit` | ✅ exit 0 |\n| 3. Golden check (seeded db) | ✅ `m_acme` revenue `327108` (was `424364`), `m_bistro` `350321` (was `417659`) |\n| 4. `/api/revenue` | ✅ `{revenue_cents: 327108, gross_sales_cents: 375736, refunds_cents: 48628}` — reconciles |\n| 5. `/api/metrics/summary` | ✅ `m_acme` `sales_orders: 34` + `refund_orders: 6` = the old total of 40; `avg_order_value_cents: 11051` vs `avg_net_order_value_cents: 9621` |\n| 6. `top-customers` | ✅ ranked by net spend; `order_count` counts sales only (negative-spend case covered by unit test) |\n| 7. Browser | ✅ cards read Sales orders / Refunds / Avg order value (+ \"net of refunds\") / \"Revenue (last 30 days, net of refunds)\" with `$1,688.33 sales − $192.36 refunded` under `$1,495.97` |\n| 8.
