Así se ve:\n\n- **Primera carga:** solo hay cookie de admin → la sesión responde `role: admin` → aparece el selector.\n- **Tras elegir merchant:** existen las dos cookies, pero `/api/auth/session` lee primero la de merchant y responde `role: merchant` → el frontend cree que es una sesión atada a un merchant y esconde el selector ([public/app.js:96](public/app.js:96)).\n\nLa causa de fondo es de diseño: **el endpoint de sesión solo puede describir una identidad**, cuando en realidad puedes tener dos cookies a la vez. Detalle revelador: el bug se cura solo a los 10 minutos, cuando caduca el token de merchant y la sesión vuelve a reportar admin, así que además es intermitente."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1933,"cache_read_input_tokens":408543,"output_tokens":2593,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":548},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1933,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2593,"cache_read_input_tokens":408543,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1933,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1933},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CeyAsfDhaXtVShu2fLFZN","type":"assistant","uuid":"2ff7c971-7842-4094-b636-399b96b6cbb4","timestamp":"2026-09-12T07:43:57.725Z","effort":"medium","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}
{"parentUuid":"2ff7c971-7842-4094-b636-399b96b6cbb4","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CeyAsg9mPt6vPK85xgP3V","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01TxvXDxwWWbjUtxkvNn7JNU","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\007-session-endpoint-reports-both-cookies.md","content":"# 007 — The session endpoint must describe both cookies\n\n**Status:** draft\n\nFixes a regression introduced by [plan 005](005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md). Reported by the user: after reloading the dashboard, the merchant picker disappears and the page is stuck on \"Viewing m_acme\".\n\n## Context\n\nA browser can hold **two** session cookies at once — `admin_session` (minting) and `merchant_session` (data) — but `GET /api/auth/session` describes only one, checking the merchant cookie first:\n\n```ts\nfor (const name of [MERCHANT_COOKIE, ADMIN_COOKIE]) { … }   // src/routes/auth.ts:106\n```\n\nReproduced against a running server:\n\n| State | `/api/auth/session` | Picker |\n|---|---|---|\n| First load (admin cookie only) | `{\"role\":\"admin\",\"merchantId\":null}` | shown ✅ |\n| After picking a merchant (both cookies) | `{\"role\":\"merchant\",\"merchantId\":\"m_acme\"}` | **hidden ❌** |\n\nThe frontend reads `role === 'merchant'` as \"this session is bound to one merchant, there is nothing to switch between\" ([public/app.js:96](../public/app.js)), which is right for a real merchant login and wrong here: the admin cookie is still present and still able to mint.\n\nIt is not a pre-existing bug — before plan 005 the picker was hardcoded in the HTML and always visible.\n\nWorth noting: the bug **heals itself after ~10 minutes**, when the merchant token expires and the endpoint starts answering `admin` again. An intermittent UI bug is worse than a permanent one, because it doesn't reproduce on the second try.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. The endpoint reports capability, not just identity\n\n`GET /api/auth/session` keeps its current top-level shape (the *effective* session, merchant preferred) and gains one field:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"role\": \"merchant\", \"scope\": \"data\", \"merchantId\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"expiresAt\": \"2026-09-12T07:53:45.000Z\",\n  \"canSwitchMerchants\": true\n}\n```\n\n`canSwitchMerchants` is `true` when a **valid** `admin_session` cookie is present — i.e. when `POST /api/auth/token` would succeed. It is derived from verifying that cookie, not from its mere existence, so an expired admin token doesn't leave a picker on screen that fails on click.\n\nRejected alternatives:\n\n- **Return both sessions** (`{ merchant: …, admin: … }`) — more faithful, but it breaks the current response shape and the frontend only needs one bit.\n- **Have the frontend remember it minted a merchant token** (e.g. `sessionStorage`) — client-side state that lies after the admin cookie expires.\n- **Reorder the loop to check the admin cookie first** — that only moves the bug: a real merchant-only session would then be described as admin… and there'd be no admin cookie to describe.\n\n### 2. The frontend decides by capability\n\n`start()` becomes:\n\n- `canSwitchMerchants === true` → load `/api/merchants`, populate and show the picker, preselect `merchantId` from the session when there is one (that's the reload case), otherwise select the first merchant and mint.\n- `canSwitchMerchants === false` and `role === 'merchant'` → hide the picker (a genuine merchant-scoped session).\n- On reload with a still-valid merchant cookie, no new token is minted: the existing session is reused and the data is just refreshed.\n\n### 3. Regression test\n\n`test/auth-guard.test.ts` gains cases for the three cookie combinations:\n\n| Cookies | `role` | `canSwitchMerchants` |\n|---|---|---|\n| admin only | `admin` | `true` |\n| admin + merchant | `merchant` | `true` |\n| merchant only | `merchant` | `false` |\n\nThe middle row is the bug: it fails today.\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/routes/auth.ts` — `GET /api/auth/session`\n- `public/app.js` — `start()`\n- `test/auth-guard.test.ts` — three session cases\n- `docs/api.md` — the new field (needs authorization, CLAUDE.md §6)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Any change to how tokens are minted, scoped or verified.\n- The remaining Tier 1 groups (C, D).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — the new cases fail before the fix and pass after.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `curl` with both cookies → `canSwitchMerchants: true`.\n4. Browser: pick `m_bistro`, **reload** → the picker is still there, still on `m_bistro`, data matches.\n5. Browser: wait out the merchant token (or mint one with a 1s TTL), reload → picker still shown, a fresh token is minted on demand.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commit; the endpoint returns to describing a single session.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1933,"cache_read_input_tokens":408543,"output_tokens":2593,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":548},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1933,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2593,"cache_read_input_tokens":408543,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1933,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1933},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01TxvXDxwWWbjUtxkvNn7JNU":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\007-session-endpoint-reports-both-cookies.md","content":"# 007 — The session endpoint must describe both cookies\n\n**Status:** draft\n\nFixes a regression introduced by [plan 005](005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md). An intermittent UI bug is worse than a permanent one, because it doesn't reproduce on the second try.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. The endpoint reports capability, not just identity\n\n`GET /api/auth/session` keeps its current top-level shape (the *effective* session, merchant preferred) and gains one field:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"role\": \"merchant\", \"scope\": \"data\", \"merchantId\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"expiresAt\": \"2026-09-12T07:53:45.000Z\",\n  \"canSwitchMerchants\": true\n}\n```\n\n`canSwitchMerchants` is `true` when a **valid** `admin_session` cookie is present — i.e. when `POST /api/auth/token` would succeed. It is derived from verifying that cookie, not from its mere existence, so an expired admin token doesn't leave a picker on screen that fails on click.\n\nRejected alternatives:\n\n- **Return both sessions** (`{ merchant: …, admin: … }`) — more faithful, but it breaks the current response shape and the frontend only needs one bit.\n- **Have the frontend remember it minted a merchant token** (e.g. `sessionStorage`) — client-side state that lies after the admin cookie expires.\n- **Reorder the loop to check the admin cookie first** — that only moves the bug: a real merchant-only session would then be described as admin… and there'd be no admin cookie to describe.\n\n### 2. The frontend decides by capability\n\n`start()` becomes:\n\n- `canSwitchMerchants === true` → load `/api/merchants`, populate and show the picker, preselect `merchantId` from the session when there is one (that's the reload case), otherwise select the first merchant and mint.\n- `canSwitchMerchants === false` and `role === 'merchant'` → hide the picker (a genuine merchant-scoped session).\n- On reload with a still-valid merchant cookie, no new token is minted: the existing session is reused and the data is just refreshed.\n\n### 3. Reported by the user: after reloading the dashboard, the merchant picker disappears and the page is stuck on \"Viewing m_acme\".\n\n## Context\n\nA browser can hold **two** session cookies at once — `admin_session` (minting) and `merchant_session` (data) — but `GET /api/auth/session` describes only one, checking the merchant cookie first:\n\n```ts\nfor (const name of [MERCHANT_COOKIE, ADMIN_COOKIE]) { … }   // src/routes/auth.ts:106\n```\n\nReproduced against a running server:\n\n| State | `/api/auth/session` | Picker |\n|---|---|---|\n| First load (admin cookie only) | `{\"role\":\"admin\",\"merchantId\":null}` | shown ✅ |\n| After picking a merchant (both cookies) | `{\"role\":\"merchant\",\"merchantId\":\"m_acme\"}` | **hidden ❌** |\n\nThe frontend reads `role === 'merchant'` as \"this session is bound to one merchant, there is nothing to switch between\" ([public/app.js:96](../public/app.js)), which is right for a real merchant login and wrong here: the admin cookie is still present and still able to mint.\n\nIt is not a pre-existing bug — before plan 005 the picker was hardcoded in the HTML and always visible.\n\nWorth noting: the bug **heals itself after ~10 minutes**, when the merchant token expires and the endpoint starts answering `admin` again. An intermittent UI bug is worse than a permanent one, because it doesn't reproduce on the second try.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. The endpoint reports capability, not just identity\n\n`GET /api/auth/session` keeps its current top-level shape (the *effective* session, merchant preferred) and gains one field:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"role\": \"merchant\", \"scope\": \"data\", \"merchantId\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"expiresAt\": \"2026-09-12T07:53:45.000Z\",\n  \"canSwitchMerchants\": true\n}\n```\n\n`canSwitchMerchants` is `true` when a **valid** `admin_session` cookie is present — i.e. when `POST /api/auth/token` would succeed. It is derived from verifying that cookie, not from its mere existence, so an expired admin token doesn't leave a picker on screen that fails on click.\n\nRejected alternatives:\n\n- **Return both sessions** (`{ merchant: …, admin: … }`) — more faithful, but it breaks the current response shape and the frontend only needs one bit.\n- **Have the frontend remember it minted a merchant token** (e.g. `sessionStorage`) — client-side state that lies after the admin cookie expires.\n- **Reorder the loop to check the admin cookie first** — that only moves the bug: a real merchant-only session would then be described as admin… and there'd be no admin cookie to describe.\n\n### 2. The frontend decides by capability\n\n`start()` becomes:\n\n- `canSwitchMerchants === true` → load `/api/merchants`, populate and show the picker, preselect `merchantId` from the session when there is one (that's the reload case), otherwise select the first merchant and mint.\n- `canSwitchMerchants === false` and `role === 'merchant'` → hide the picker (a genuine merchant-scoped session).\n- On reload with a still-valid merchant cookie, no new token is minted: the existing session is reused and the data is just refreshed.\n\n### 3. Regression test\n\n`test/auth-guard.test.ts` gains cases for the three cookie combinations:\n\n| Cookies | `role` | `canSwitchMerchants` |\n|---|---|---|\n| admin only | `admin` | `true` |\n| admin + merchant | `merchant` | `true` |\n| merchant only | `merchant` | `false` |\n\nThe middle row is the bug: it fails today.\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/routes/auth.ts` — `GET /api/auth/session`\n- `public/app.js` — `start()`\n- `test/auth-guard.test.ts` — three session cases\n- `docs/api.md` — the new field (needs authorization, CLAUDE.md §6)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Any change to how tokens are minted, scoped or verified.\n- The remaining Tier 1 groups (C, D).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — the new cases fail before the fix and pass after.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `curl` with both cookies → `canSwitchMerchants: true`.\n4. Browser: pick `m_bistro`, **reload** → the picker is still there, still on `m_bistro`, data matches.\n5. Browser: wait out the merchant token (or mint one with a 1s TTL), reload → picker still shown, a fresh token is minted on demand.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commit; the endpoint returns to describing a single session.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"a7c2bb98-aaed-48fe-9d0f-5d22eee74ad8","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"e601d700-4b64-4e3f-a30f-4ae86aaee165","timestamp":"2026-09-12T07:45:21.815Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\007-session-endpoint-reports-both-cookies.md","oldString":"**Status:** draft","newString":"**Status:** approved","originalFile":"# 007 — The session endpoint must describe both cookies\n\n**Status:** draft\n\nFixes a regression introduced by [plan 005](005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md). Reported by the user: after reloading the dashboard, the merchant picker disappears and the page is stuck on \"Viewing m_acme\".\n\n## Context\n\nA browser can hold **two** session cookies at once — `admin_session` (minting) and `merchant_session` (data) — but `GET /api/auth/session` describes only one, checking the merchant cookie first:\n\n```ts\nfor (const name of [MERCHANT_COOKIE, ADMIN_COOKIE]) { … }   // src/routes/auth.ts:106\n```\n\nReproduced against a running server:\n\n| State | `/api/auth/session` | Picker |\n|---|---|---|\n| First load (admin cookie only) | `{\"role\":\"admin\",\"merchantId\":null}` | shown ✅ |\n| After picking a merchant (both cookies) | `{\"role\":\"merchant\",\"merchantId\":\"m_acme\"}` | **hidden ❌** |\n\nThe frontend reads `role === 'merchant'` as \"this session is bound to one merchant, there is nothing to switch between\" ([public/app.js:96](../public/app.js)), which is right for a real merchant login and wrong here: the admin cookie is still present and still able to mint.\n\nIt is not a pre-existing bug — before plan 005 the picker was hardcoded in the HTML and always visible.\n\nWorth noting: the bug **heals itself after ~10 minutes**, when the merchant token expires and the endpoint starts answering `admin` again. An intermittent UI bug is worse than a permanent one, because it doesn't reproduce on the second try.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. The endpoint reports capability, not just identity\n\n`GET /api/auth/session` keeps its current top-level shape (the *effective* session, merchant preferred) and gains one field:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"role\": \"merchant\", \"scope\": \"data\", \"merchantId\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"expiresAt\": \"2026-09-12T07:53:45.000Z\",\n  \"canSwitchMerchants\": true\n}\n```\n\n`canSwitchMerchants` is `true` when a **valid** `admin_session` cookie is present — i.e. when `POST /api/auth/token` would succeed. It is derived from verifying that cookie, not from its mere existence, so an expired admin token doesn't leave a picker on screen that fails on click.\n\nRejected alternatives:\n\n- **Return both sessions** (`{ merchant: …, admin: … }`) — more faithful, but it breaks the current response shape and the frontend only needs one bit.\n- **Have the frontend remember it minted a merchant token** (e.g. `sessionStorage`) — client-side state that lies after the admin cookie expires.\n- **Reorder the loop to check the admin cookie first** — that only moves the bug: a real merchant-only session would then be described as admin… and there'd be no admin cookie to describe.\n\n### 2. The frontend decides by capability\n\n`start()` becomes:\n\n- `canSwitchMerchants === true` → load `/api/merchants`, populate and show the picker, preselect `merchantId` from the session when there is one (that's the reload case), otherwise select the first merchant and mint.\n- `canSwitchMerchants === false` and `role === 'merchant'` → hide the picker (a genuine merchant-scoped session).\n- On reload with a still-valid merchant cookie, no new token is minted: the existing session is reused and the data is just refreshed.\n\n### 3. Regression test\n\n`test/auth-guard.test.ts` gains cases for the three cookie combinations:\n\n| Cookies | `role` | `canSwitchMerchants` |\n|---|---|---|\n| admin only | `admin` | `true` |\n| admin + merchant | `merchant` | `true` |\n| merchant only | `merchant` | `false` |\n\nThe middle row is the bug: it fails today.\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/routes/auth.ts` — `GET /api/auth/session`\n- `public/app.js` — `start()`\n- `test/auth-guard.test.ts` — three session cases\n- `docs/api.md` — the new field (needs authorization, CLAUDE.md §6)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Any change to how tokens are minted, scoped or verified.\n- The remaining Tier 1 groups (C, D).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — the new cases fail before the fix and pass after.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `curl` with both cookies → `canSwitchMerchants: true`.\n4. Browser: pick `m_bistro`, **reload** → the picker is still there, still on `m_bistro`, data matches.\n5. Browser: wait out the merchant token (or mint one with a 1s TTL), reload → picker still shown, a fresh token is minted on demand.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commit; the endpoint returns to describing a single session.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":6,"newStart":1,"newLines":6,"lines":[" # 007 — The session endpoint must describe both cookies"," ","-**Status:** draft","+**Status:** approved"," "," Fixes a regression introduced by [plan 005](005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md). Reported by the user: after reloading the dashboard, the merchant picker disappears and the page is stuck on \"Viewing m_acme\"."," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"d822ad03-10bc-49b3-a43e-132e8777b2f4","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

'node:http';\nimport { createApp } from '../src/app.js';\nimport { ADMIN_COOKIE, MERCHANT_COOKIE } from '../src/auth/cookies.js';\nimport { issueAdminToken, issueMerchantToken, signToken } from '../src/auth/jwt.js';\nimport { initSchema, db } from '../src/db.js';\n\nlet server: Server;\nlet baseUrl: string;\nlet adminCookie: string;\nlet acmeCookie: string;\nlet bistroCookie: string;\n\nbefore(async () => {\n  initSchema();\n  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO merchants (id, name) VALUES ('m_acme', 'Acme'), ('m_bistro', 'Bistro')`).run();\n  db.prepare(\n    `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO orders (id, merchant_id, customer_email, total_amount, type, status)\n     VALUES ('acme-1', 'm_acme', 'ana@example.com', 1000, 'sale', 'completed'),\n            ('bistro-1', 'm_bistro', 'bruno@example.com', 2000, 'sale', 'completed')`,\n  ).run();\n\n  // Dev bootstrap off: these tests exercise the real authentication flow.\n  server = createApp({ enableDevAdminSession: false }).listen(0);\n  await new Promise((resolve) => server.once('listening', resolve));\n  baseUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${(server.address() as AddressInfo).port}`;\n\n  adminCookie = `${ADMIN_COOKIE}=${(await issueAdminToken('5m')).token}`;\n  acmeCookie = `${MERCHANT_COOKIE}=${(await issueMerchantToken('m_acme', '5m')).token}`;\n  bistroCookie = `${MERCHANT_COOKIE}=${(await issueMerchantToken('m_bistro', '5m')).token}`;\n});\n\nafter(() => {\n  server.close();\n});\n\n/** Issues a request with optional cookie and headers. */\nfunction call(path: string, init: { cookie?: string; headers?: Record<string, string>; method?: string; body?: unknown } = {}) {\n  const headers: Record<string, string> = { ...init.headers };\n  if (init.cookie) headers.Cookie = init.cookie;\n  if (init.body !== undefined) headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json';\n  return fetch(`${baseUrl}${path}`, {\n    method: init.method ?? 'GET',\n    headers,\n    ...(init.body === undefined ? {} : { body: JSON.stringify(init.body) }),\n  });\n}\n\ntest('guard: no token is rejected', async () => {\n  const response = await call('/api/orders');\n  assert.equal(response.status, 401);\n  assert.deepEqual(await response.json(), { error: 'unauthenticated' });\n});\n\ntest('guard: a merchant token sees only its own orders', async () => {\n  const response = await call('/api/orders', { cookie: acmeCookie });\n  assert.equal(response.status, 200);\n  const body = (await response.json()) as { orders: Array<{ id: string }> };\n  assert.deepEqual(body.orders.map((o) => o.id), ['acme-1']);\n});\n\ntest('guard: a mismatching X-Merchant-Id is rejected', async () => {\n  const response = await call('/api/orders', { cookie: acmeCookie, headers: { 'X-Merchant-Id': 'm_bistro' } });\n  assert.equal(response.status, 403);\n  assert.deepEqual(await response.json(), { error: 'merchant_mismatch' });\n});\n\ntest(\"guard: the caller's own X-Merchant-Id is accepted and ignored\", async () => {\n  const response = await call('/api/orders', { cookie: acmeCookie, headers: { 'X-Merchant-Id': 'm_acme' } });\n  assert.equal(response.status, 200);\n});\n\ntest('guard: an admin token cannot read data', async () => {\n  const response = await call('/api/orders', { cookie: adminCookie });\n  assert.equal(response.status, 403);\n  assert.deepEqual(await response.json(), { error: 'token_not_scoped_for_data' });\n});\n\ntest('guard: a merchant token cannot mint tokens', async () => {\n  const response = await call('/api/auth/token', { method: 'POST', cookie: acmeCookie, body: { merchantId: 'm_acme' } });\n  assert.equal(response.status, 403);\n  assert.deepEqual(await response.json(), { error: 'token_not_scoped_for_mint' });\n});\n\ntest('guard: an expired token is reported as such', async () => {\n  const expired = await signToken({ role: 'merchant', scope: 'data', merchantId: 'm_acme' }, '-1s');\n  const response = await call('/api/orders', { cookie: `${MERCHANT_COOKIE}=${expired}` });\n  assert.equal(response.status, 401);\n  assert.deepEqual(await response.json(), { error: 'session_expired' });\n});\n\ntest('auth: the admin token mints an HttpOnly merchant cookie', async () => {\n  const response = await call('/api/auth/token', { method: 'POST', cookie: adminCookie, body: { merchantId: 'm_bistro' } });\n  assert.equal(response.status, 204);\n  const setCookie = response.headers.getSetCookie().find((value) => value.startsWith(`${MERCHANT_COOKIE}=`));\n  assert.ok(setCookie, 'expected a merchant_session cookie');\n  assert.match(setCookie!, /HttpOnly/);\n  assert.match(setCookie!, /SameSite=Strict/);\n});\n\ntest('auth: minting for an unknown merchant is a 404', async () => {\n  const response = await call('/api/auth/token', { method: 'POST', cookie: adminCookie, body: { merchantId: 'nope' } });\n  assert.equal(response.status, 404);\n  assert.deepEqual(await response.json(), { error: 'merchant_not_found' });\n});\n\ntest('auth: minting without a merchantId is a 400', async () => {\n  const response = await call('/api/auth/token', { method: 'POST', cookie: adminCookie, body: {} });\n  assert.equal(response.status, 400);\n});\n\ntest(\"orders: another merchant's order is reported as missing (TD-02)\", async () => {\n  const mine = await call('/api/orders/acme-1', { cookie: acmeCookie });\n  assert.equal(mine.status, 200);\n  const theirs = await call('/api/orders/bistro-1', { cookie: acmeCookie });\n  assert.equal(theirs.status, 404);\n});\n\ntest('metrics: aggregates are scoped to the session merchant (TD-04)', async () => {\n  const acme = await call('/api/metrics/summary', { cookie: acmeCookie });\n  assert.deepEqual(await acme.json(), {\n    merchant_id: 'm_acme',\n    sales_orders: 1,\n    refund_orders: 0,\n    unique_customers: 1,\n    avg_order_value_cents: 1000,\n    avg_net_order_value_cents: 1000,\n  });\n\n  const bistro = await call('/api/metrics/summary', { cookie: bistroCookie });\n  const bistroBody = (await call('/api/merchants', { cookie: adminCookie });\n  assert.equal(asAdmin.status, 200);\n  const body = (await asAdmin.json()) as { merchants: Array<{ id: string }> };\n Data endpoints only\n * ever accept merchant tokens, so the merchant id always comes from a token the backend\n * signed, never from the client.\n *\n * @see plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md\n */\nimport { Router } from 'express';\nimport {\n  ADMIN_COOKIE,\n  MERCHANT_COOKIE,\n  parseCookies,\n  secondsUntil,\n  serializeClearedCookie,\n  serializeSessionCookie,\n} from '../auth/cookies.js';\nimport { requireAuth } from '../auth/guard.js';\nimport { InvalidTokenError, issueMerchantToken, verifyToken } from '../auth/jwt.js';\nimport { isLocalRequest } from '../auth/local.js';\nimport { merchantsRepository } from '../dal/merchants-repository.js';\nimport { asyncHandler } from './async-handler.js';\n\nexport const authRouter = Router();\n\n/**\n * `POST /api/auth/token` — mints a merchant-scoped session for the requested merchant.\n * Requires an admin (mint-scoped) token.\n */\nauthRouter.post(\n  '/token',\n  requireAuth({ scope: 'mint' }),\n  asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {\n    const body = req.body as { merchantId?: unknown } | undefined;\n    const merchantId = typeof body?.merchantId === 'string' ? body.merchantId : undefined;\n    if (!merchantId) {\n      res.status(400).json({ error: 'merchant_id_required' });\n      return;\n    }\n    if (!merchantsRepository.exists(merchantId)) {\n      res.status(404).json({ error: 'merchant_not_found' });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const { token, expiresAt } = await issueMerchantToken(merchantId);\n    res.append(\n      'Set-Cookie',\n      serializeSessionCookie(MERCHANT_COOKIE, token, {\n        maxAgeSeconds: secondsUntil(expiresAt),\n        secure: !isLocalRequest(req),\n      }),\n    );\n    res.status(204).end();\n  }),\n);\n\n/**\n * `POST /api/auth/admin-session` — exchanges an admin token (from `npm run token`) for the\n * admin session cookie. The way in when the request isn't local.\n */\nauthRouter.post(\n  '/admin-session',\n  asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {\n    const body = req.body as { token?: unknown } | undefined;\n    const token = typeof body?.token === 'string' ? body.token : undefined;\n    if (!token) {\n      res.status(400).json({ error: 'token_required' });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    let verified;\n    try {\n      verified = await verifyToken(token);\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (error instanceof InvalidTokenError) {\n        res.status(401).json({ error: 'session_expired' });\n        return;\n      }\n      throw error;\n    }\n    if (verified.scope !== 'mint') {\n      res.status(403).json({ error: 'token_not_scoped_for_mint' });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    res.append(\n      'Set-Cookie',\n      serializeSessionCookie(ADMIN_COOKIE, token, {\n        maxAgeSeconds: secondsUntil(verified.expiresAt),\n        secure: !isLocalRequest(req),\n      }),\n    );\n    res.status(204).end();\n  }),\n);\n\n/**\n * `GET /api/auth/session` — describes the current session so the dashboard knows what to render.\n */\nauthRouter.get(\n  '/session',\n  asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {\n    const cookies = parseCookies(req.headers.cookie);\n    for (const name of [MERCHANT_COOKIE, ADMIN_COOKIE]) {\n      const token = cookies[name];\n      if (!token) continue;\n      try {\n        const verified = await verifyToken(token);\n        res.json({\n          role: verified.role,\n          scope: verified.scope,\n          merchantId: verified.merchantId ?? null,\n          expiresAt: verified.expiresAt.toISOString(),\n        });\n        return;\n      } catch (error) {\n        if (!(error instanceof InvalidTokenError)) throw error;\n      }\n    }\n    res.status(401).json({ error: 'unauthenticated' });\n  }),\n);\n\n/**\n * `DELETE /api/auth/session` — clears both session cookies.\n */\nauthRouter.delete('/session', (_req, res) => {\n  res.append('Set-Cookie', serializeClearedCookie(MERCHANT_COOKIE));\n  res.append('Set-Cookie', serializeClearedCookie(ADMIN_COOKIE));\n  res.status(204).end();\n});\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":103,"oldLines":27,"newStart":103,"newLines":48,"lines":["   '/session',","   asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {","     const cookies = parseCookies(req.headers.cookie);","-    for (const name of [MERCHANT_COOKIE, ADMIN_COOKIE]) {","-      const token = cookies[name];","-      if (!token) continue;","-      try {","-        const verified = await verifyToken(token);","-        res.json({","-          role: verified.role,","-          scope: verified.scope,","-          merchantId: verified.merchantId ?? Data endpoints only\n * ever accept merchant tokens, so the merchant id always comes from a token the backend\n * signed, never from the client.\n *\n * @see plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md\n */\nimport { Router } from 'express';\nimport {\n  ADMIN_COOKIE,\n  MERCHANT_COOKIE,\n  parseCookies,\n  secondsUntil,\n  serializeClearedCookie,\n  serializeSessionCookie,\n} from '../auth/cookies.js';\nimport { requireAuth } from '../auth/guard.js';\nimport { InvalidTokenError, issueMerchantToken, verifyToken } from '../auth/jwt.js';\nimport { isLocalRequest } from '../auth/local.js';\nimport { merchantsRepository } from '../dal/merchants-repository.js';\nimport { asyncHandler } from './async-handler.js';\n\nexport const authRouter = Router();\n\n/**\n * `POST /api/auth/token` — mints a merchant-scoped session for the requested merchant.\n * Requires an admin (mint-scoped) token.\n */\nauthRouter.post(\n  '/token',\n  requireAuth({ scope: 'mint' }),\n  asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {\n    const body = req.body as { merchantId?: unknown } | undefined;\n    const merchantId = typeof body?.merchantId === 'string' ? body.merchantId : undefined;\n    if (!merchantId) {\n      res.status(400).json({ error: 'merchant_id_required' });\n      return;\n    }\n    if (!merchantsRepository.exists(merchantId)) {\n      res.status(404).json({ error: 'merchant_not_found' });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const { token, expiresAt } = await issueMerchantToken(merchantId);\n    res.append(\n      'Set-Cookie',\n      serializeSessionCookie(MERCHANT_COOKIE, token, {\n        maxAgeSeconds: secondsUntil(expiresAt),\n        secure: !isLocalRequest(req),\n      }),\n    );\n    res.status(204).end();\n  }),\n);\n\n/**\n * `POST /api/auth/admin-session` — exchanges an admin token (from `npm run token`) for the\n * admin session cookie. The way in when the request isn't local.\n */\nauthRouter.post(\n  '/admin-session',\n  asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {\n    const body = req.body as { token?: unknown } | undefined;\n    const token = typeof body?.token === 'string' ? body.token : undefined;\n    if (!token) {\n      res.status(400).json({ error: 'token_required' });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    let verified;\n    try {\n      verified = await verifyToken(token);\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (error instanceof InvalidTokenError) {\n        res.status(401).json({ error: 'session_expired' });\n        return;\n      }\n      throw error;\n    }\n    if (verified.scope !== 'mint') {\n      res.status(403).json({ error: 'token_not_scoped_for_mint' });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    res.append(\n      'Set-Cookie',\n      serializeSessionCookie(ADMIN_COOKIE, token, {\n        maxAgeSeconds: secondsUntil(verified.expiresAt),\n        secure: !isLocalRequest(req),\n      }),\n    );\n    res.status(204).end();\n  }),\n);\n\n/**\n * `GET /api/auth/session` — describes the current session so the dashboard knows what to render.\n */\nauthRouter.get(\n  '/session',\n  asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {\n    const cookies = parseCookies(req.headers.cookie);\n    // A browser can hold both cookies at once. Reporting only one of them is what made the\n    // dashboard's merchant picker disappear on reload (plan 007).\n    const merchant = await readSession(cookies[MERCHANT_COOKIE], 'data');\n    const admin = await readSession(cookies[ADMIN_COOKIE], 'mint');\n\n    const effective = merchant ?? admin;\n    if (!effective) {\n      res.status(401).json({ error: 'unauthenticated' });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    res.json({\n      role: effective.role,\n      scope: effective.scope,\n      merchantId: effective.merchantId ?? null,\n      expiresAt: effective.expiresAt.toISOString(),\n      // Capability, not identity: true when minting a merchant token would actually work.\n      canSwitchMerchants: admin !== undefined,\n    });\n  }),\n);\n\n/**\n * Verifies a session cookie.\n *\n * @param token - Raw cookie value, if present.\n * @param scope - Scope the token must carry to count.\n * @returns The verified claims, or `undefined` when the cookie is absent, invalid, expired or\n *          carries a different scope.\n */\nasync function readSession(token: string | undefined, scope: TokenScope): Promise<VerifiedToken | undefined> {\n  if (!token) return undefined;\n  try {\n    const verified = await verifyToken(token);\n    return verified.scope === scope ? verified : undefined;\n  } catch (error) {\n    if (error instanceof InvalidTokenError) return undefined;\n    throw error;\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * `DELETE /api/auth/session` — clears both session cookies.\n */\nauthRouter.delete('/session', (_req, res) => {\n  res.append('Set-Cookie', serializeClearedCookie(MERCHANT_COOKIE));\n  res.append('Set-Cookie', serializeClearedCookie(ADMIN_COOKIE));\n  res.status(204).end();\n});\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":18,"oldLines":7,"newStart":18,"newLines":13,"lines":["   serializeSessionCookie,"," } from '../auth/cookies.js';"," import { requireAuth } from '../auth/guard.js';","-import { InvalidTokenError, issueMerchantToken, verifyToken } from '../auth/jwt.js';","+import {","+  InvalidTokenError,","+  issueMerchantToken,","+  verifyToken,","+  type TokenScope,","+  type VerifiedToken,","+} from '../auth/jwt.js';"," import { isLocalRequest } from '../auth/local.js';"," import { merchantsRepository } from '../dal/merchants-repository.js';"," import { asyncHandler } from './async-handler.js';"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"6ec2dff8-3132-4bb4-8091-3dbd6a62ee54","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

response = await request(path);\n  }\n  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`${path} responded ${response.status}`);\n  return response.json();\n}\n\nfunction money(cents) {\n  return (cents / (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"1f33e5a2-7b04-42dd-b2c3-bc48611612f3","timestamp":"2026-09-12T07:46:31.224Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\007-session-endpoint-reports-both-cookies.md","oldString":"**Status:** approved","newString":"**Status:** done (2026-09-12) — fixed and validated; `docs/api.md` pending authorization","originalFile":"# 007 — The session endpoint must describe both cookies\n\n**Status:** approved\n\nFixes a regression introduced by [plan 005](005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md). Reported by the user: after reloading the dashboard, the merchant picker disappears and the page is stuck on \"Viewing m_acme\".\n\n## Context\n\nA browser can hold **two** session cookies at once — `admin_session` (minting) and `merchant_session` (data) — but `GET /api/auth/session` describes only one, checking the merchant cookie first:\n\n```ts\nfor (const name of [MERCHANT_COOKIE, ADMIN_COOKIE]) { … }   // src/routes/auth.ts:106\n```\n\nReproduced against a running server:\n\n| State | `/api/auth/session` | Picker |\n|---|---|---|\n| First load (admin cookie only) | `{\"role\":\"admin\",\"merchantId\":null}` | shown ✅ |\n| After picking a merchant (both cookies) | `{\"role\":\"merchant\",\"merchantId\":\"m_acme\"}` | **hidden ❌** |\n\nThe frontend reads `role === 'merchant'` as \"this session is bound to one merchant, there is nothing to switch between\" ([public/app.js:96](../public/app.js)), which is right for a real merchant login and wrong here: the admin cookie is still present and still able to mint.\n\nIt is not a pre-existing bug — before plan 005 the picker was hardcoded in the HTML and always visible.\n\nWorth noting: the bug **heals itself after ~10 minutes**, when the merchant token expires and the endpoint starts answering `admin` again. An intermittent UI bug is worse than a permanent one, because it doesn't reproduce on the second try.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. The endpoint reports capability, not just identity\n\n`GET /api/auth/session` keeps its current top-level shape (the *effective* session, merchant preferred) and gains one field:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"role\": \"merchant\", \"scope\": \"data\", \"merchantId\": \"m_acme\",\n  \"expiresAt\": \"2026-09-12T07:53:45.000Z\",\n  \"canSwitchMerchants\": true\n}\n```\n\n`canSwitchMerchants` is `true` when a **valid** `admin_session` cookie is present — i.e. when `POST /api/auth/token` would succeed. It is derived from verifying that cookie, not from its mere existence, so an expired admin token doesn't leave a picker on screen that fails on click.\n\nRejected alternatives:\n\n- **Return both sessions** (`{ merchant: …, admin: … }`) — more faithful, but it breaks the current response shape and the frontend only needs one bit.\n- **Have the frontend remember it minted a merchant token** (e.g. `sessionStorage`) — client-side state that lies after the admin cookie expires.\n- **Reorder the loop to check the admin cookie first** — that only moves the bug: a real merchant-only session would then be described as admin… and there'd be no admin cookie to describe.\n\n### 2. The frontend decides by capability\n\n`start()` becomes:\n\n- `canSwitchMerchants === true` → load `/api/merchants`, populate and show the picker, preselect `merchantId` from the session when there is one (that's the reload case), otherwise select the first merchant and mint.\n- `canSwitchMerchants === false` and `role === 'merchant'` → hide the picker (a genuine merchant-scoped session).\n- On reload with a still-valid merchant cookie, no new token is minted: the existing session is reused and the data is just refreshed.\n\n### 3. Regression test\n\n`test/auth-guard.test.ts` gains cases for the three cookie combinations:\n\n| Cookies | `role` | `canSwitchMerchants` |\n|---|---|---|\n| admin only | `admin` | `true` |\n| admin + merchant | `merchant` | `true` |\n| merchant only | `merchant` | `false` |\n\nThe middle row is the bug: it fails today.\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/routes/auth.ts` — `GET /api/auth/session`\n- `public/app.js` — `start()`\n- `test/auth-guard.test.ts` — three session cases\n- `docs/api.md` — the new field (needs authorization, CLAUDE.md §6)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Any change to how tokens are minted, scoped or verified.\n- The remaining Tier 1 groups (C, D).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — the new cases fail before the fix and pass after.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `curl` with both cookies → `canSwitchMerchants: true`.\n4. Browser: pick `m_bistro`, **reload** → the picker is still there, still on `m_bistro`, data matches.\n5. Browser: wait out the merchant token (or mint one with a 1s TTL), reload → picker still shown, a fresh token is minted on demand.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commit; the endpoint returns to describing a single session.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":6,"newStart":1,"newLines":6,"lines":[" # 007 — The session endpoint must describe both cookies"," ","-**Status:** approved","+**Status:** done (2026-09-12) — fixed and validated; `docs/api.md` pending authorization"," "," Fixes a regression introduced by [plan 005](005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md). Reported by the user: after reloading the dashboard, the merchant picker disappears and the page is stuck on \"Viewing m_acme\"."," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"55b06826-388d-4748-a07b-9625d641f3c4","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

Regression test\n\n`test/auth-guard.test.ts` gains cases for the three cookie combinations:\n\n| Cookies | `role` | `canSwitchMerchants` |\n|---|---|---|\n| admin only | `admin` | `true` |\n| admin + merchant | `merchant` | `true` |\n| merchant only | `merchant` | `false` |\n\nThe middle row is the bug: it fails today.\n\n## Scope\n\n- `src/routes/auth.ts` — `GET /api/auth/session`\n- `public/app.js` — `start()`\n- `test/auth-guard.test.ts` — three session cases\n- `docs/api.md` — the new field (needs authorization, CLAUDE.md §6)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Any change to how tokens are minted, scoped or verified.\n- The remaining Tier 1 groups (C, D).\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — the new cases fail before the fix and pass after.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. `curl` with both cookies → `canSwitchMerchants: true`.\n4. Browser: pick `m_bistro`, **reload** → the picker is still there, still on `m_bistro`, data matches.\n5. Browser: wait out the merchant token (or mint one with a 1s TTL), reload → picker still shown, a fresh token is minted on demand.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commit; the endpoint returns to describing a single session.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":90,"oldLines":3,"newStart":90,"newLines":21,"lines":[" ## Rollback"," "," Revert the commit; the endpoint returns to describing a single session.","+","+## Results","+","+Written test-first: the four new session cases were added and run **before** the fix, and failed (63 pass / 4 fail) — so the regression test demonstrably catches the bug.","+","+| Step | Result |","+|---|---|","+| 1. `npm test` | ✅ 67/67 after the fix (4 new cases, all failing beforehand) |","+| 2. `tsc --noEmit` | ✅ exit 0 |","+| 3. {"type":"bridge-session","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","bridgeSessionId":"cse_01RevUBptTUx7nmRkHFj8baE","lastSequenceNum":0,"ownerAccountUuid":"fd7153db-c57a-4ed8-a587-cc63ddfe7824","ownerOrganizationUuid":"a0c86979-17db-43c0-bac4-2f5d900230e2"}
{"parentUuid":"0dba6121-9134-4d1f-b39f-14990698553c","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CeyEY3LsrZpoSEA4ToKZY","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01GtA9EXMHgzLiYbd5H5nwXk","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\008-csv-export-of-orders.md","content":"# 008 — Feature: CSV export of orders\n\n**Status:** draft\n\nThe challenge's Feature A. Chosen because it reuses what we just fixed — merchant scoping (plan 005) and refund semantics (plan 006) — and because an export button is the thing merchants ask for first on a dashboard like this.\n\n## Context\n\nThe dashboard can show orders but not take them anywhere. A merchant's real workflow (reconciliation, accounting, sharing with a bookkeeper) ends in a spreadsheet.\n\nThe feature is under-specified on purpose. What we decide here: **column shape, auth model, format conventions, and behavior on large result sets.**\n\nFacts checked before writing this:\n\n- `better-sqlite3` exposes `Statement.iterate()`, so rows can be streamed instead of materialized (confirmed against the real database).\n- `ordersRouter` registers `GET /:id` at [src/routes/orders.ts:26](../src/routes/orders.ts). A later `GET /export.csv` would be swallowed by it and answer `404 not_found`, so **the export route must be registered before `/:id`** — with a test that would catch the ordering mistake.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Endpoint\n\n```\nGET /api/orders/export.csv?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD\n```\n\n- **Auth: the existing merchant session.** No new auth model: the same `requireAuth()` guard, the same `merchant_session` cookie, the same `BaseRepository` scope. An admin (mint-scoped) token gets `403` like on any data route — the export cannot become a way to read another merchant's rows.\n- `from`/`to` are **optional**; when both are present the same range rule as the orders list applies (`from` inclusive, `to` exclusive). One without the other is a `400`, instead of silently exporting everything (the list endpoint's silent-drop behavior is TD-09; the export won't copy it).\n- Rows are ordered **`created_at` ascending** — chronological, which is what a ledger export is for, unlike the dashboard's newest-first view.\n\n### 2. Columns\n\n| Column | Example | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| `order_id` | `e3684c1d-…` | Join key back to the API |\n| `created_at` | `2026-09-11T11:45:35.866Z` | ISO 8601, UTC, unambiguous |\n| `customer_email` | `ana@example.com` | |\n| `type` | `sale` / `refund` | |\n| `status` | `completed` | |\n| `amount_cents` | `11136` | As stored: positive integer, no locale or rounding issues |\n| `signed_amount_cents` | `-11136` for refunds | **Sums to net revenue** |\n| `amount` | `111.36` | Decimal with a dot, for humans |\n\n`signed_amount_cents` is the column that matters: it carries the refund semantics from `src/dal/money.ts` into the spreadsheet, so `=SUM(...)` gives net revenue. Without it, every merchant would recreate TD-05 in Excel on their own.\n\nNo `currency` column: the schema has no currency and inventing a constant would imply multi-currency support we don't have. Documented as USD in `docs/api.md`.\n\n### 3. Format conventions\n\n- **RFC 4180**: `CRLF` line endings, header row, fields quoted only when they contain `,` `\"` `CR` or `LF`, inner quotes doubled.\n- **UTF-8 with BOM**, so Excel on Windows doesn't mangle accented names.\n- **Formula-injection defense**: a field starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR is prefixed with `'`. This matters here specifically: `customer_email` is attacker-controlled and barely validated (TD-11 is still open), so `=HYPERLINK(...)` in an email field would execute when the merchant opens the file.\n- Response headers: `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"orders-<merchantId>-<from>_<to>.csv\"`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.\n\n### 4. Large result sets\n\nRows are **streamed**, not accumulated:\n\n- `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` returns an iterator built on `Statement.iterate()`, with the merchant scope applied by `BaseRepository` like any other query.\n- The route writes the header, then rows in batches, honoring backpressure (`res.write()` returning `false` → wait for `drain`).\n- No row cap: an export that silently truncates is worse than a slow one. Memory stays flat because nothing holds the full result.\n- Failure mid-stream (headers already sent) can't become a JSON error, so the stream is aborted and the incident logged — a truncated file the merchant can notice, rather than a corrupt one that looks complete.\n\n### 5. Dashboard\n\nA **Download CSV** button next to \"Recent orders\", exporting the same 30-day window the cards show.\n\nIt can't be a plain `<a download>`: if the 10-minute merchant token has expired the browser would download a file containing `{\"error\":\"session_expired\"}`. The handler mints a fresh token first (the existing re-mint path), then triggers the download.\n\n### 6. Commits\n\n| # | Content |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | `src/lib/csv.ts` (escaping, injection defense) + unit tests |\n| 2 | `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` + scope tests |\n| 3 | `GET /api/orders/export.csv` (registered before `/:id`) + HTTP tests |\n| 4 | Dashboard button |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — Three amount columns** (`amount_cents`, `signed_amount_cents`, `amount`)? Recommended: the signed one is the whole point, the cents one is exact, the decimal one is readable. Alternative: drop `amount` and keep the file strictly integer.\n- **Q2 — `from`/`to` optional** (export everything when absent)? Recommended. Alternative: required, like `/api/revenue`.\n- **Q3 — BOM + formula-injection prefix**? Recommended for anything opened in Excel. The trade-off: the `'` prefix is visible to a script that parses the file naively, and the BOM confuses a few Unix tools.\n- **Q4 — Button exports the visible 30-day window** (recommended) or the merchant's full history? Chosen because it reuses what we just fixed — merchant scoping (plan 005) and refund semantics (plan 006) — and because an export button is the thing merchants ask for first on a dashboard like this.\n\n## Context\n\nThe dashboard can show orders but not take them anywhere. A merchant's real workflow (reconciliation, accounting, sharing with a bookkeeper) ends in a spreadsheet.\n\nThe feature is under-specified on purpose. What we decide here: **column shape, auth model, format conventions, and behavior on large result sets.**\n\nFacts checked before writing this:\n\n- `better-sqlite3` exposes `Statement.iterate()`, so rows can be streamed instead of materialized (confirmed against the real database).\n- `ordersRouter` registers `GET /:id` at [src/routes/orders.ts:26](../src/routes/orders.ts). A later `GET /export.csv` would be swallowed by it and answer `404 not_found`, so **the export route must be registered before `/:id`** — with a test that would catch the ordering mistake.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Endpoint\n\n```\nGET /api/orders/export.csv?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD\n```\n\n- **Auth: the existing merchant session.** No new auth model: the same `requireAuth()` guard, the same `merchant_session` cookie, the same `BaseRepository` scope. An admin (mint-scoped) token gets `403` like on any data route — the export cannot become a way to read another merchant's rows.\n- `from`/`to` are **optional**; when both are present the same range rule as the orders list applies (`from` inclusive, `to` exclusive). One without the other is a `400`, instead of silently exporting everything (the list endpoint's silent-drop behavior is TD-09; the export won't copy it).\n- Rows are ordered **`created_at` ascending** — chronological, which is what a ledger export is for, unlike the dashboard's newest-first view.\n\n### 2. Columns\n\n| Column | Example | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| `order_id` | `e3684c1d-…` | Join key back to the API |\n| `created_at` | `2026-09-11T11:45:35.866Z` | ISO 8601, UTC, unambiguous |\n| `customer_email` | `ana@example.com` | |\n| `type` | `sale` / `refund` | |\n| `status` | `completed` | |\n| `amount_cents` | `11136` | As stored: positive integer, no locale or rounding issues |\n| `signed_amount_cents` | `-11136` for refunds | **Sums to net revenue** |\n| `amount` | `111.36` | Decimal with a dot, for humans |\n\n`signed_amount_cents` is the column that matters: it carries the refund semantics from `src/dal/money.ts` into the spreadsheet, so `=SUM(...)` gives net revenue. Without it, every merchant would recreate TD-05 in Excel on their own.\n\nNo `currency` column: the schema has no currency and inventing a constant would imply multi-currency support we don't have. Documented as USD in `docs/api.md`.\n\n### 3. Format conventions\n\n- **RFC 4180**: `CRLF` line endings, header row, fields quoted only when they contain `,` `\"` `CR` or `LF`, inner quotes doubled.\n- **UTF-8 with BOM**, so Excel on Windows doesn't mangle accented names.\n- **Formula-injection defense**: a field starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR is prefixed with `'`. This matters here specifically: `customer_email` is attacker-controlled and barely validated (TD-11 is still open), so `=HYPERLINK(...)` in an email field would execute when the merchant opens the file.\n- Response headers: `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"orders-<merchantId>-<from>_<to>.csv\"`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.\n\n### 4. Large result sets\n\nRows are **streamed**, not accumulated:\n\n- `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` returns an iterator built on `Statement.iterate()`, with the merchant scope applied by `BaseRepository` like any other query.\n- The route writes the header, then rows in batches, honoring backpressure (`res.write()` returning `false` → wait for `drain`).\n- No row cap: an export that silently truncates is worse than a slow one. Memory stays flat because nothing holds the full result.\n- Failure mid-stream (headers already sent) can't become a JSON error, so the stream is aborted and the incident logged — a truncated file the merchant can notice, rather than a corrupt one that looks complete.\n\n### 5. Dashboard\n\nA **Download CSV** button next to \"Recent orders\", exporting the same 30-day window the cards show.\n\nIt can't be a plain `<a download>`: if the 10-minute merchant token has expired the browser would download a file containing `{\"error\":\"session_expired\"}`. The handler mints a fresh token first (the existing re-mint path), then triggers the download.\n\n### 6. Commits\n\n| # | Content |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | `src/lib/csv.ts` (escaping, injection defense) + unit tests |\n| 2 | `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` + scope tests |\n| 3 | `GET /api/orders/export.csv` (registered before `/:id`) + HTTP tests |\n| 4 | Dashboard button |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — Three amount columns** (`amount_cents`, `signed_amount_cents`, `amount`)? Recommended: the signed one is the whole point, the cents one is exact, the decimal one is readable. Alternative: drop `amount` and keep the file strictly integer.\n- **Q2 — `from`/`to` optional** (export everything when absent)? Recommended. Alternative: required, like `/api/revenue`.\n- **Q3 — BOM + formula-injection prefix**? Recommended for anything opened in Excel. The trade-off: the `'` prefix is visible to a script that parses the file naively, and the BOM confuses a few Unix tools.\n- **Q4 — Button exports the visible 30-day window** (recommended) or the merchant's full history? A date picker is out of scope for this plan.\n\n## Scope\n\n- New: `src/lib/csv.ts`, `test/csv.test.ts`, `test/orders-export.test.ts`\n- Changed: `src/dal/base-repository.ts` (iterator helper), `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/routes/orders.ts`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`\n- `docs/api.md`, `docs/architecture.md` — after validation, with authorization (CLAUDE.md §6)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Other export formats, scheduled or emailed exports, background jobs.\n- A date-range picker in the UI.\n- The remaining Tier 1 debt (TD-10, TD-11, TD-12) — the injection defense here mitigates the export path but does not replace input validation.\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — CSV unit tests + endpoint tests.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. **Route ordering**: `GET /api/orders/export.csv` returns CSV, not `404 not_found` (the regression this plan predicts).\n4. **Scope**: an `m_acme` session's export contains no `m_bistro` row; an admin token gets `403`.\n5. **Money**: the sum of `signed_amount_cents` for a full range equals `/api/revenue`'s `revenue_cents` for the same range (327 108 for `m_acme` on the seeded data).\n6. **Escaping**: a customer email containing `,`, `\"` and a newline round-trips through a CSV parser; `=HYPERLINK(\"x\")` comes back prefixed with `'`.\n7. **Headers**: `Content-Disposition` names the file with merchant and range; body starts with the UTF-8 BOM.\n8. **Streaming**: exporting a few thousand seeded rows keeps memory flat (measured with `process.memoryUsage()` before/after) and the response is chunked.\n9. **Browser**: the button downloads a file that opens correctly, and still works after the merchant token has expired.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits. La sección la escribes tú; yo solo te paso el material verificado.\n\n## Lo que dejamos igual a propósito (decisiones, no olvidos)\n\n| Qué | Por qué lo dejamos | Dónde está el razonamiento |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Express 4 con un override de `qs`**, en vez de migrar a Express 5 | El override arregla las dos alertas sin cambios de comportamiento. Express 5 es una versión mayor y tiene un cambio real aquí: `req.body` es `undefined` sin JSON, así que un POST sin `Content-Type` pasaría de 400 a 500 | [plan 002](plans/002-qs-override-under-express.md) |\n| **Los refunds siguen guardándose en positivo**; el neteo se hace al leer | Netear al guardar exige migrar filas y rompe el significado documentado de `total_amount`. Al leer, los hechos crudos quedan intactos y sigue siendo fácil preguntar \"cuánto devolvimos\" | [plan 006](plans/006-refund-semantics-in-money-math.md) |\n| **`status` no se filtra en las cuentas de dinero** | Las 80 filas son `completed`. Filtrar sería especular sobre estados que no existen; queda anotado en las docs para cuando aparezcan | plan 006, Q4 |\n| **`X-Merchant-Id` sobrevive como canal de comparación**, no se eliminó | Quitarlo escondería el error: si un cliente manda otro merchant, preferimos un `403` explícito a ignorarlo en silencio | [plan 005](plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md) |\n| **Sin tokens CSRF** | `SameSite=Strict` cubre el caso; un token CSRF encima sería complejidad sin amenaza nueva | plan 005 |\n| **Sin rate limiting, sin revocación, sin login real** | Fuera del alcance del reto; el token de admin es un atajo de desarrollo, no un sistema de identidad | plan 005 |\n| **`src/scripts/` exento de la regla de arquitectura** | `seed.ts` no está en el camino de una petición y no tiene contexto de auth | `test/architecture.test.ts` |\n| **Frontend sin framework ni build** | El reto no lo pide y añadiría un paso de compilación a un dashboard de cuatro tarjetas | — |\n| **`engines: node >=20` sin tocar** aunque el CI usa Node 24 | Cambiar el mínimo soportado es una decisión de producto, no un efecto colateral de arreglar un audit | [plan 003](plans/003-check-deps-script.md) |\n\n## Deuda conocida, priorizada y no tocada\n\n- **Tier 1 abierto:** TD-10 (`limit` sin validar), TD-11 (body sin validar), TD-12 (XSS almacenado). El XSS lo dejé a propósito al reescribir `app.js`, para que el fix sea un commit revisable por sí solo.\n- **Tier 2 y 3:** TD-07 (el rango excluye hoy), TD-08 (formatos de fecha mezclados), TD-03 (500 en vez de 4xx), TD-09, TD-15, TD-18 (no hay forma de enlazar un refund con su venta).\n\n## Dos correcciones de contabilidad que encontré ahora\n\nAl verificar esto salieron dos ítems mal marcados, y conviene que el decision log no herede el error:\n\n- **TD-14 ya está resuelto:** el HTML ya no tiene merchants escritos a mano, salen de `GET /api/merchants`. Sigue marcado como abierto en el backlog.\n- **TD-13 está resuelto a medias:** `app.js` ya comprueba `response.ok` y muestra el error, así que lo de \"enseña `$0.00` en silencio ante un 500\" ya no ocurre. Lo que falta es manejo por tarjeta.\n- **TD-16 mejoró mucho** (de 2 tests a 67, con rutas, auth, dinero y arquitectura), aunque no lo daría por cerrado del todo.\n\n## Y una inconsistencia real en docs\n\n**[README.md:43](README.md:43) sigue diciendo** que el cliente manda `X-Merchant-Id` en cada petición y remite a `src/auth.ts`, un archivo que ya no existe. Es el único doc que quedó desactualizado, porque CLAUDE.md me prohíbe tocar el README sin que me lo pidas. Si lo dejas así, mejor que sea deliberado y escrito como tal; si prefieres, lo actualizo con tu autorización.\n\n¿Quiero corregir el estado de TD-13 y TD-14, y actualizar esa línea del README?"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1239,"cache_read_input_tokens":432560,"output_tokens":1640,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1239,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1640,"cache_read_input_tokens":432560,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1239,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1239},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CeyFwhhy41FZpbZjzkEiw","type":"assistant","uuid":"7f8f210e-37b2-427e-8a4e-6bdf9ca98d8b","timestamp":"2026-09-12T08:50:40.141Z","effort":"medium","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

{"parentUuid":"6e5500a5-2973-43f8-97ef-53447c23f464","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"05f1dbf7-3809-48c5-8c33-d02d47ecce88","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01BCqKCRJPSNjYdyA9oSG74d","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\008-csv-export-of-orders.md has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"b5c3a682-eaf6-445f-985e-dbb7b7b3577d","timestamp":"2026-09-12T09:00:38.089Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\008-csv-export-of-orders.md","oldString":"**Status:** draft","newString":"**Status:** draft (rev 2 — open questions answered by the user)","originalFile":"# 008 — Feature: CSV export of orders\n\n**Status:** draft\n\nThe challenge's Feature A. Chosen because it reuses what we just fixed — merchant scoping (plan 005) and refund semantics (plan 006) — and because an export button is the thing merchants ask for first on a dashboard like this.\n\n## Context\n\nThe dashboard can show orders but not take them anywhere. A merchant's real workflow (reconciliation, accounting, sharing with a bookkeeper) ends in a spreadsheet.\n\nThe feature is under-specified on purpose. What we decide here: **column shape, auth model, format conventions, and behavior on large result sets.**\n\nFacts checked before writing this:\n\n- `better-sqlite3` exposes `Statement.iterate()`, so rows can be streamed instead of materialized (confirmed against the real database).\n- `ordersRouter` registers `GET /:id` at [src/routes/orders.ts:26](../src/routes/orders.ts). A later `GET /export.csv` would be swallowed by it and answer `404 not_found`, so **the export route must be registered before `/:id`** — with a test that would catch the ordering mistake.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Endpoint\n\n```\nGET /api/orders/export.csv?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD\n```\n\n- **Auth: the existing merchant session.** No new auth model: the same `requireAuth()` guard, the same `merchant_session` cookie, the same `BaseRepository` scope. An admin (mint-scoped) token gets `403` like on any data route — the export cannot become a way to read another merchant's rows.\n- `from`/`to` are **optional**; when both are present the same range rule as the orders list applies (`from` inclusive, `to` exclusive). One without the other is a `400`, instead of silently exporting everything (the list endpoint's silent-drop behavior is TD-09; the export won't copy it).\n- Rows are ordered **`created_at` ascending** — chronological, which is what a ledger export is for, unlike the dashboard's newest-first view.\n\n### 2. Columns\n\n| Column | Example | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| `order_id` | `e3684c1d-…` | Join key back to the API |\n| `created_at` | `2026-09-11T11:45:35.866Z` | ISO 8601, UTC, unambiguous |\n| `customer_email` | `ana@example.com` | |\n| `type` | `sale` / `refund` | |\n| `status` | `completed` | |\n| `amount_cents` | `11136` | As stored: positive integer, no locale or rounding issues |\n| `signed_amount_cents` | `-11136` for refunds | **Sums to net revenue** |\n| `amount` | `111.36` | Decimal with a dot, for humans |\n\n`signed_amount_cents` is the column that matters: it carries the refund semantics from `src/dal/money.ts` into the spreadsheet, so `=SUM(...)` gives net revenue. Without it, every merchant would recreate TD-05 in Excel on their own.\n\nNo `currency` column: the schema has no currency and inventing a constant would imply multi-currency support we don't have. Documented as USD in `docs/api.md`.\n\n### 3. Format conventions\n\n- **RFC 4180**: `CRLF` line endings, header row, fields quoted only when they contain `,` `\"` `CR` or `LF`, inner quotes doubled.\n- **UTF-8 with BOM**, so Excel on Windows doesn't mangle accented names.\n- **Formula-injection defense**: a field starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR is prefixed with `'`. This matters here specifically: `customer_email` is attacker-controlled and barely validated (TD-11 is still open), so `=HYPERLINK(...)` in an email field would execute when the merchant opens the file.\n- Response headers: `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"orders-<merchantId>-<from>_<to>.csv\"`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.\n\n### 4. Large result sets\n\nRows are **streamed**, not accumulated:\n\n- `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` returns an iterator built on `Statement.iterate()`, with the merchant scope applied by `BaseRepository` like any other query.\n- The route writes the header, then rows in batches, honoring backpressure (`res.write()` returning `false` → wait for `drain`).\n- No row cap: an export that silently truncates is worse than a slow one. Memory stays flat because nothing holds the full result.\n- Failure mid-stream (headers already sent) can't become a JSON error, so the stream is aborted and the incident logged — a truncated file the merchant can notice, rather than a corrupt one that looks complete.\n\n### 5. Dashboard\n\nA **Download CSV** button next to \"Recent orders\", exporting the same 30-day window the cards show.\n\nIt can't be a plain `<a download>`: if the 10-minute merchant token has expired the browser would download a file containing `{\"error\":\"session_expired\"}`. The handler mints a fresh token first (the existing re-mint path), then triggers the download.\n\n### 6. Commits\n\n| # | Content |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | `src/lib/csv.ts` (escaping, injection defense) + unit tests |\n| 2 | `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` + scope tests |\n| 3 | `GET /api/orders/export.csv` (registered before `/:id`) + HTTP tests |\n| 4 | Dashboard button |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — Three amount columns** (`amount_cents`, `signed_amount_cents`, `amount`)? Recommended: the signed one is the whole point, the cents one is exact, the decimal one is readable. Alternative: drop `amount` and keep the file strictly integer.\n- **Q2 — `from`/`to` optional** (export everything when absent)? Recommended. Alternative: required, like `/api/revenue`.\n- **Q3 — BOM + formula-injection prefix**? Recommended for anything opened in Excel. The trade-off: the `'` prefix is visible to a script that parses the file naively, and the BOM confuses a few Unix tools.\n- **Q4 — Button exports the visible 30-day window** (recommended) or the merchant's full history? A date picker is out of scope for this plan.\n\n## Scope\n\n- New: `src/lib/csv.ts`, `test/csv.test.ts`, `test/orders-export.test.ts`\n- Changed: `src/dal/base-repository.ts` (iterator helper), `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/routes/orders.ts`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`\n- `docs/api.md`, `docs/architecture.md` — after validation, with authorization (CLAUDE.md §6)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Other export formats, scheduled or emailed exports, background jobs.\n- A date-range picker in the UI.\n- The remaining Tier 1 debt (TD-10, TD-11, TD-12) — the injection defense here mitigates the export path but does not replace input validation.\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — CSV unit tests + endpoint tests.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. **Route ordering**: `GET /api/orders/export.csv` returns CSV, not `404 not_found` (the regression this plan predicts).\n4. **Scope**: an `m_acme` session's export contains no `m_bistro` row; an admin token gets `403`.\n5. **Money**: the sum of `signed_amount_cents` for a full range equals `/api/revenue`'s `revenue_cents` for the same range (327 108 for `m_acme` on the seeded data).\n6. **Escaping**: a customer email containing `,`, `\"` and a newline round-trips through a CSV parser; `=HYPERLINK(\"x\")` comes back prefixed with `'`.\n7. **Headers**: `Content-Disposition` names the file with merchant and range; body starts with the UTF-8 BOM.\n8. **Streaming**: exporting a few thousand seeded rows keeps memory flat (measured with `process.memoryUsage()` before/after) and the response is chunked.\n9. **Browser**: the button downloads a file that opens correctly, and still works after the merchant token has expired.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits. The handler mints a fresh token first (the existing re-mint path), then triggers the download.","originalFile":"# 008 — Feature: CSV export of orders\n\n**Status:** draft (rev 2 — open questions answered by the user)\n\nThe challenge's Feature A. Chosen because it reuses what we just fixed — merchant scoping (plan 005) and refund semantics (plan 006) — and because an export button is the thing merchants ask for first on a dashboard like this.\n\n## Context\n\nThe dashboard can show orders but not take them anywhere. A merchant's real workflow (reconciliation, accounting, sharing with a bookkeeper) ends in a spreadsheet.\n\nThe feature is under-specified on purpose. What we decide here: **column shape, auth model, format conventions, and behavior on large result sets.**\n\nFacts checked before writing this:\n\n- `better-sqlite3` exposes `Statement.iterate()`, so rows can be streamed instead of materialized (confirmed against the real database).\n- `ordersRouter` registers `GET /:id` at [src/routes/orders.ts:26](../src/routes/orders.ts). A later `GET /export.csv` would be swallowed by it and answer `404 not_found`, so **the export route must be registered before `/:id`** — with a test that would catch the ordering mistake.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Endpoint\n\n```\nGET /api/orders/export.csv?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD\n```\n\n- **Auth: the existing merchant session.** No new auth model: the same `requireAuth()` guard, the same `merchant_session` cookie, the same `BaseRepository` scope. An admin (mint-scoped) token gets `403` like on any data route — the export cannot become a way to read another merchant's rows.\n- `from`/`to` are **optional**; when both are present the same range rule as the orders list applies (`from` inclusive, `to` exclusive). One without the other is a `400`, instead of silently exporting everything (the list endpoint's silent-drop behavior is TD-09; the export won't copy it).\n- Rows are ordered **`created_at` ascending** — chronological, which is what a ledger export is for, unlike the dashboard's newest-first view.\n\n### 2. Columns\n\n| Column | Example | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| `order_id` | `e3684c1d-…` | Join key back to the API |\n| `created_at` | `2026-09-11T11:45:35.866Z` | ISO 8601, UTC, unambiguous |\n| `customer_email` | `ana@example.com` | |\n| `type` | `sale` / `refund` | |\n| `status` | `completed` | |\n| `amount_cents` | `11136` | As stored: positive integer, no locale or rounding issues |\n| `signed_amount_cents` | `-11136` for refunds | **Sums to net revenue** |\n| `amount` | `111.36` | Decimal with a dot, for humans |\n\n`signed_amount_cents` is the column that matters: it carries the refund semantics from `src/dal/money.ts` into the spreadsheet, so `=SUM(...)` gives net revenue. Without it, every merchant would recreate TD-05 in Excel on their own.\n\nNo `currency` column: the schema has no currency and inventing a constant would imply multi-currency support we don't have. Documented as USD in `docs/api.md`.\n\n### 3. Format conventions\n\n- **RFC 4180**: `CRLF` line endings, header row, fields quoted only when they contain `,` `\"` `CR` or `LF`, inner quotes doubled.\n- **UTF-8 with BOM**, so Excel on Windows doesn't mangle accented names.\n- **Formula-injection defense**: a field starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR is prefixed with `'`. This matters here specifically: `customer_email` is attacker-controlled and barely validated (TD-11 is still open), so `=HYPERLINK(...)` in an email field would execute when the merchant opens the file.\n- Response headers: `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"orders-<merchantId>-<from>_<to>.csv\"`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.\n\n### 4. Large result sets\n\nRows are **streamed**, not accumulated:\n\n- `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` returns an iterator built on `Statement.iterate()`, with the merchant scope applied by `BaseRepository` like any other query.\n- The route writes the header, then rows in batches, honoring backpressure (`res.write()` returning `false` → wait for `drain`).\n- No row cap: an export that silently truncates is worse than a slow one. Memory stays flat because nothing holds the full result.\n- Failure mid-stream (headers already sent) can't become a JSON error, so the stream is aborted and the incident logged — a truncated file the merchant can notice, rather than a corrupt one that looks complete.\n\n### 5. Dashboard\n\nA **Download CSV** button next to \"Recent orders\", exporting the same 30-day window the cards show.\n\nIt can't be a plain `<a download>`: if the 10-minute merchant token has expired the browser would download a file containing `{\"error\":\"session_expired\"}`. The handler mints a fresh token first (the existing re-mint path), then triggers the download.\n\n### 6. Commits\n\n| # | Content |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | `src/lib/csv.ts` (escaping, injection defense) + unit tests |\n| 2 | `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` + scope tests |\n| 3 | `GET /api/orders/export.csv` (registered before `/:id`) + HTTP tests |\n| 4 | Dashboard button |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — Three amount columns** (`amount_cents`, `signed_amount_cents`, `amount`)? Recommended: the signed one is the whole point, the cents one is exact, the decimal one is readable. Alternative: drop `amount` and keep the file strictly integer.\n- **Q2 — `from`/`to` optional** (export everything when absent)? Recommended. Alternative: required, like `/api/revenue`.\n- **Q3 — BOM + formula-injection prefix**? Recommended for anything opened in Excel. The trade-off: the `'` prefix is visible to a script that parses the file naively, and the BOM confuses a few Unix tools.\n- **Q4 — Button exports the visible 30-day window** (recommended) or the merchant's full history? A date picker is out of scope for this plan.\n\n## Scope\n\n- New: `src/lib/csv.ts`, `test/csv.test.ts`, `test/orders-export.test.ts`\n- Changed: `src/dal/base-repository.ts` (iterator helper), `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/routes/orders.ts`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`\n- `docs/api.md`, `docs/architecture.md` — after validation, with authorization (CLAUDE.md §6)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Other export formats, scheduled or emailed exports, background jobs.\n- A date-range picker in the UI.\n- The remaining Tier 1 debt (TD-10, TD-11, TD-12) — the injection defense here mitigates the export path but does not replace input validation.\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — CSV unit tests + endpoint tests.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. **Route ordering**: `GET /api/orders/export.csv` returns CSV, not `404 not_found` (the regression this plan predicts).\n4. **Scope**: an `m_acme` session's export contains no `m_bistro` row; an admin token gets `403`.\n5. **Money**: the sum of `signed_amount_cents` for a full range equals `/api/revenue`'s `revenue_cents` for the same range (327 108 for `m_acme` on the seeded data).\n6. **Escaping**: a customer email containing `,`, `\"` and a newline round-trips through a CSV parser; `=HYPERLINK(\"x\")` comes back prefixed with `'`.\n7. **Headers**: `Content-Disposition` names the file with merchant and range; body starts with the UTF-8 BOM.\n8. **Streaming**: exporting a few thousand seeded rows keeps memory flat (measured with `process.memoryUsage()` before/after) and the response is chunked.\n9. **Browser**: the button downloads a file that opens correctly, and still works after the merchant token has expired.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits.
