What we decide here: **column shape, auth model, format conventions, and behavior on large result sets.**\n\nFacts checked before writing this:\n\n- `better-sqlite3` exposes `Statement.iterate()`, so rows can be streamed instead of materialized (confirmed against the real database).\n- `ordersRouter` registers `GET /:id` at [src/routes/orders.ts:26](../src/routes/orders.ts). A later `GET /export.csv` would be swallowed by it and answer `404 not_found`, so **the export route must be registered before `/:id`** — with a test that would catch the ordering mistake.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Endpoint\n\n```\nGET /api/orders/export.csv?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD\n```\n\n- **Auth: the existing merchant session.** No new auth model: the same `requireAuth()` guard, the same `merchant_session` cookie, the same `BaseRepository` scope. An admin (mint-scoped) token gets `403` like on any data route — the export cannot become a way to read another merchant's rows.\n- `from`/`to` are **optional**; when both are present the same range rule as the orders list applies (`from` inclusive, `to` exclusive). One without the other is a `400`, instead of silently exporting everything (the list endpoint's silent-drop behavior is TD-09; the export won't copy it).\n- Rows are ordered **`created_at` ascending** — chronological, which is what a ledger export is for, unlike the dashboard's newest-first view.\n\n### 2. Columns\n\n| Column | Example | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| `order_id` | `e3684c1d-…` | Join key back to the API |\n| `created_at` | `2026-09-11T11:45:35.866Z` | ISO 8601, UTC, unambiguous |\n| `customer_email` | `ana@example.com` | |\n| `type` | `sale` / `refund` | |\n| `status` | `completed` | |\n| `amount_cents` | `11136` | As stored: positive integer, no locale or rounding issues |\n| `signed_amount_cents` | `-11136` for refunds | **Sums to net revenue** |\n| `amount` | `111.36` | Decimal with a dot, for humans |\n\n`signed_amount_cents` is the column that matters: it carries the refund semantics from `src/dal/money.ts` into the spreadsheet, so `=SUM(...)` gives net revenue. Without it, every merchant would recreate TD-05 in Excel on their own.\n\nNo `currency` column: the schema has no currency and inventing a constant would imply multi-currency support we don't have. Documented as USD in `docs/api.md`.\n\n### 3. Format conventions\n\n- **RFC 4180**: `CRLF` line endings, header row, fields quoted only when they contain `,` `\"` `CR` or `LF`, inner quotes doubled.\n- **UTF-8 with BOM**, so Excel on Windows doesn't mangle accented names.\n- **Formula-injection defense**: a field starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR is prefixed with `'`. This matters here specifically: `customer_email` is attacker-controlled and barely validated (TD-11 is still open), so `=HYPERLINK(...)` in an email field would execute when the merchant opens the file.\n- Response headers: `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"orders-<merchantId>-<from>_<to>.csv\"`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.\n\n### 4. Large result sets\n\nRows are **streamed**, not accumulated:\n\n- `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` returns an iterator built on `Statement.iterate()`, with the merchant scope applied by `BaseRepository` like any other query.\n- The route writes the header, then rows in batches, honoring backpressure (`res.write()` returning `false` → wait for `drain`).\n- No row cap: an export that silently truncates is worse than a slow one. Memory stays flat because nothing holds the full result.\n- Failure mid-stream (headers already sent) can't become a JSON error, so the stream is aborted and the incident logged — a truncated file the merchant can notice, rather than a corrupt one that looks complete.\n\n### 5. Dashboard\n\nA **Download CSV** button next to \"Recent orders\", exporting the **current calendar month to date** (Q4).\n\n- Range: `from` = first day of the current month, `to` = **tomorrow**. `to` is exclusive, so using today would silently drop today's orders — exactly the trap described in TD-07, and much worse in an export the merchant treats as a record.\n- The button is labelled with the range it will produce (e.g. \"Download CSV · Sep 1–12\"), because the cards above it show a rolling 30-day window: without the label the CSV total and the revenue card would disagree and look like a bug. Aligning the card to the calendar month instead is a one-line change if you prefer them identical — not assumed here.\n- It can't be a plain `<a download>`: if the 10-minute merchant token has expired the browser would download a file containing `{\"error\":\"session_expired\"}`. The handler mints a fresh token first (the existing re-mint path), then triggers the download.\n\n### 6. Commits\n\n| # | Content |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | `src/lib/csv.ts` (escaping, injection defense) + unit tests |\n| 2 | `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` + scope tests |\n| 3 | `GET /api/orders/export.csv` (registered before `/:id`) + HTTP tests |\n| 4 | Dashboard button |\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Q1 — Three amount columns** (`amount_cents`, `signed_amount_cents`, `amount`)? Recommended: the signed one is the whole point, the cents one is exact, the decimal one is readable. Alternative: drop `amount` and keep the file strictly integer.\n- **Q2 — `from`/`to` optional** (export everything when absent)? Recommended. Alternative: required, like `/api/revenue`.\n- **Q3 — BOM + formula-injection prefix**? Recommended for anything opened in Excel. The trade-off: the `'` prefix is visible to a script that parses the file naively, and the BOM confuses a few Unix tools.\n- **Q4 — Button exports the visible 30-day window** (recommended) or the merchant's full history? A date picker is out of scope for this plan.\n\n## Scope\n\n- New: `src/lib/csv.ts`, `test/csv.test.ts`, `test/orders-export.test.ts`\n- Changed: `src/dal/base-repository.ts` (iterator helper), `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/routes/orders.ts`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`\n- `docs/api.md`, `docs/architecture.md` — after validation, with authorization (CLAUDE.md §6)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Other export formats, scheduled or emailed exports, background jobs.\n- A date-range picker in the UI.\n- The remaining Tier 1 debt (TD-10, TD-11, TD-12) — the injection defense here mitigates the export path but does not replace input validation.\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — CSV unit tests + endpoint tests.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. **Route ordering**: `GET /api/orders/export.csv` returns CSV, not `404 not_found` (the regression this plan predicts).\n4. **Scope**: an `m_acme` session's export contains no `m_bistro` row; an admin token gets `403`.\n5. **Money**: the sum of `signed_amount_cents` for a full range equals `/api/revenue`'s `revenue_cents` for the same range (327 108 for `m_acme` on the seeded data).\n6. **Escaping**: a customer email containing `,`, `\"` and a newline round-trips through a CSV parser; `=HYPERLINK(\"x\")` comes back prefixed with `'`.\n7. **Headers**: `Content-Disposition` names the file with merchant and range; body starts with the UTF-8 BOM.\n8. **Streaming**: exporting a few thousand seeded rows keeps memory flat (measured with `process.memoryUsage()` before/after) and the response is chunked.\n9. **Browser**: the button downloads a file that opens correctly, and still works after the merchant token has expired.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"64f61c8d-3226-46cf-9433-ca488face8a4","timestamp":"2026-09-12T09:02:52.478Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\008-csv-export-of-orders.md","oldString":"**Status:** draft (rev 2 — open questions answered by the user)","newString":"**Status:** draft (rev 3 — export window aligned with the dashboard)","originalFile":"# 008 — Feature: CSV export of orders\n\n**Status:** draft (rev 2 — open questions answered by the user)\n\nThe challenge's Feature A. Chosen because it reuses what we just fixed — merchant scoping (plan 005) and refund semantics (plan 006) — and because an export button is the thing merchants ask for first on a dashboard like this.\n\n## Context\n\nThe dashboard can show orders but not take them anywhere. A merchant's real workflow (reconciliation, accounting, sharing with a bookkeeper) ends in a spreadsheet.\n\nThe feature is under-specified on purpose. What we decide here: **column shape, auth model, format conventions, and behavior on large result sets.**\n\nFacts checked before writing this:\n\n- `better-sqlite3` exposes `Statement.iterate()`, so rows can be streamed instead of materialized (confirmed against the real database).\n- `ordersRouter` registers `GET /:id` at [src/routes/orders.ts:26](../src/routes/orders.ts). A later `GET /export.csv` would be swallowed by it and answer `404 not_found`, so **the export route must be registered before `/:id`** — with a test that would catch the ordering mistake.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Endpoint\n\n```\nGET /api/orders/export.csv?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD\n```\n\n- **Auth: the existing merchant session.** No new auth model: the same `requireAuth()` guard, the same `merchant_session` cookie, the same `BaseRepository` scope. An admin (mint-scoped) token gets `403` like on any data route — the export cannot become a way to read another merchant's rows.\n- `from`/`to` are **optional**; when both are present the same range rule as the orders list applies (`from` inclusive, `to` exclusive). One without the other is a `400`, instead of silently exporting everything (the list endpoint's silent-drop behavior is TD-09; the export won't copy it).\n- Rows are ordered **`created_at` ascending** — chronological, which is what a ledger export is for, unlike the dashboard's newest-first view.\n\n### 2. Columns\n\n| Column | Example | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| `order_id` | `e3684c1d-…` | Join key back to the API |\n| `created_at` | `2026-09-11T11:45:35.866Z` | ISO 8601, UTC, unambiguous |\n| `customer_email` | `ana@example.com` | |\n| `type` | `sale` / `refund` | |\n| `status` | `completed` | |\n| `amount_cents` | `11136` | As stored: positive integer, no locale or rounding issues |\n| `signed_amount_cents` | `-11136` for refunds | **Sums to net revenue** |\n| `amount` | `111.36` | Decimal with a dot, for humans |\n\n`signed_amount_cents` is the column that matters: it carries the refund semantics from `src/dal/money.ts` into the spreadsheet, so `=SUM(...)` gives net revenue. Without it, every merchant would recreate TD-05 in Excel on their own.\n\nNo `currency` column: the schema has no currency and inventing a constant would imply multi-currency support we don't have. Documented as USD in `docs/api.md`.\n\n### 3. Format conventions\n\n- **RFC 4180**: `CRLF` line endings, header row, fields quoted only when they contain `,` `\"` `CR` or `LF`, inner quotes doubled.\n- **UTF-8 with BOM**, so Excel on Windows doesn't mangle accented names.\n- **Formula-injection defense**: a field starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR is prefixed with `'`. This matters here specifically: `customer_email` is attacker-controlled and barely validated (TD-11 is still open), so `=HYPERLINK(...)` in an email field would execute when the merchant opens the file.\n- Response headers: `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"orders-<merchantId>-<from>_<to>.csv\"`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.\n\n### 4. Large result sets\n\nRows are **streamed**, not accumulated:\n\n- `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` returns an iterator built on `Statement.iterate()`, with the merchant scope applied by `BaseRepository` like any other query.\n- The route writes the header, then rows in batches, honoring backpressure (`res.write()` returning `false` → wait for `drain`).\n- No row cap: an export that silently truncates is worse than a slow one. Memory stays flat because nothing holds the full result.\n- Failure mid-stream (headers already sent) can't become a JSON error, so the stream is aborted and the incident logged — a truncated file the merchant can notice, rather than a corrupt one that looks complete.\n\n### 5. Dashboard\n\nA **Download CSV** button next to \"Recent orders\", exporting the **current calendar month to date** (Q4).\n\n- Range: `from` = first day of the current month, `to` = **tomorrow**. `to` is exclusive, so using today would silently drop today's orders — exactly the trap described in TD-07, and much worse in an export the merchant treats as a record.\n- The button is labelled with the range it will produce (e.g. \"Download CSV · Sep 1–12\"), because the cards above it show a rolling 30-day window: without the label the CSV total and the revenue card would disagree and look like a bug. Aligning the card to the calendar month instead is a one-line change if you prefer them identical — not assumed here.\n- It can't be a plain `<a download>`: if the 10-minute merchant token has expired the browser would download a file containing `{\"error\":\"session_expired\"}`. The handler mints a fresh token first (the existing re-mint path), then triggers the download.\n\n### 6. Commits\n\n| # | Content |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | `src/lib/csv.ts` (escaping, injection defense) + unit tests |\n| 2 | `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` + scope tests |\n| 3 | `GET /api/orders/export.csv` (registered before `/:id`) + HTTP tests |\n| 4 | Dashboard button |\n\n## Answers to the open questions\n\n- **Q1 — Three amount columns**: `amount_cents`, `signed_amount_cents`, `amount`.\n- **Q2 — `from`/`to` optional**; one without the other is a `400`.\n- **Q3 — BOM + formula-injection prefix**: both included.\n- **Q4 — Current calendar month to date** (not the rolling 30 days), with the range shown on the button. See §5 for the exclusive-`to` handling.\n\n## Scope\n\n- New: `src/lib/csv.ts`, `test/csv.test.ts`, `test/orders-export.test.ts`\n- Changed: `src/dal/base-repository.ts` (iterator helper), `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/routes/orders.ts`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`\n- `docs/api.md`, `docs/architecture.md` — after validation, with authorization (CLAUDE.md §6)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Other export formats, scheduled or emailed exports, background jobs.\n- A date-range picker in the UI.\n- The remaining Tier 1 debt (TD-10, TD-11, TD-12) — the injection defense here mitigates the export path but does not replace input validation.\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — CSV unit tests + endpoint tests.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. **Route ordering**: `GET /api/orders/export.csv` returns CSV, not `404 not_found` (the regression this plan predicts).\n4. **Scope**: an `m_acme` session's export contains no `m_bistro` row; an admin token gets `403`.\n5. **Money**: the sum of `signed_amount_cents` for a full range equals `/api/revenue`'s `revenue_cents` for the same range (327 108 for `m_acme` on the seeded data).\n6. **Escaping**: a customer email containing `,`, `\"` and a newline round-trips through a CSV parser; `=HYPERLINK(\"x\")` comes back prefixed with `'`.\n7. **Headers**: `Content-Disposition` names the file with merchant and range; body starts with the UTF-8 BOM.\n8. **Streaming**: exporting a few thousand seeded rows keeps memory flat (measured with `process.memoryUsage()` before/after) and the response is chunked.\n9. **Browser**: the button downloads a file that opens correctly, and still works after the merchant token has expired.\n10. **Month window**: an order created today appears in the export (the exclusive-`to` trap), and one created on the last day of the previous month does not.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits. Read-only feature: no schema change, no data migration.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":6,"newStart":1,"newLines":6,"lines":[" # 008 — Feature: CSV export of orders"," ","-**Status:** draft (rev 2 — open questions answered by the user)","+**Status:** draft (rev 3 — export window aligned with the dashboard)"," "," The challenge's Feature A. Pending your nod on Option A in §5 (both include today) versus Option B (both keep excluding it).","originalFile":"# 008 — Feature: CSV export of orders\n\n**Status:** draft (rev 3 — export window aligned with the dashboard)\n\nThe challenge's Feature A. Chosen because it reuses what we just fixed — merchant scoping (plan 005) and refund semantics (plan 006) — and because an export button is the thing merchants ask for first on a dashboard like this.\n\n## Context\n\nThe dashboard can show orders but not take them anywhere. A merchant's real workflow (reconciliation, accounting, sharing with a bookkeeper) ends in a spreadsheet.\n\nThe feature is under-specified on purpose. What we decide here: **column shape, auth model, format conventions, and behavior on large result sets.**\n\nFacts checked before writing this:\n\n- `better-sqlite3` exposes `Statement.iterate()`, so rows can be streamed instead of materialized (confirmed against the real database).\n- `ordersRouter` registers `GET /:id` at [src/routes/orders.ts:26](../src/routes/orders.ts). A later `GET /export.csv` would be swallowed by it and answer `404 not_found`, so **the export route must be registered before `/:id`** — with a test that would catch the ordering mistake.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Endpoint\n\n```\nGET /api/orders/export.csv?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD\n```\n\n- **Auth: the existing merchant session.** No new auth model: the same `requireAuth()` guard, the same `merchant_session` cookie, the same `BaseRepository` scope. An admin (mint-scoped) token gets `403` like on any data route — the export cannot become a way to read another merchant's rows.\n- `from`/`to` are **optional**; when both are present the same range rule as the orders list applies (`from` inclusive, `to` exclusive). One without the other is a `400`, instead of silently exporting everything (the list endpoint's silent-drop behavior is TD-09; the export won't copy it).\n- Rows are ordered **`created_at` ascending** — chronological, which is what a ledger export is for, unlike the dashboard's newest-first view.\n\n### 2. Columns\n\n| Column | Example | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| `order_id` | `e3684c1d-…` | Join key back to the API |\n| `created_at` | `2026-09-11T11:45:35.866Z` | ISO 8601, UTC, unambiguous |\n| `customer_email` | `ana@example.com` | |\n| `type` | `sale` / `refund` | |\n| `status` | `completed` | |\n| `amount_cents` | `11136` | As stored: positive integer, no locale or rounding issues |\n| `signed_amount_cents` | `-11136` for refunds | **Sums to net revenue** |\n| `amount` | `111.36` | Decimal with a dot, for humans |\n\n`signed_amount_cents` is the column that matters: it carries the refund semantics from `src/dal/money.ts` into the spreadsheet, so `=SUM(...)` gives net revenue. Without it, every merchant would recreate TD-05 in Excel on their own.\n\nNo `currency` column: the schema has no currency and inventing a constant would imply multi-currency support we don't have. Documented as USD in `docs/api.md`.\n\n### 3. Format conventions\n\n- **RFC 4180**: `CRLF` line endings, header row, fields quoted only when they contain `,` `\"` `CR` or `LF`, inner quotes doubled.\n- **UTF-8 with BOM**, so Excel on Windows doesn't mangle accented names.\n- **Formula-injection defense**: a field starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR is prefixed with `'`. This matters here specifically: `customer_email` is attacker-controlled and barely validated (TD-11 is still open), so `=HYPERLINK(...)` in an email field would execute when the merchant opens the file.\n- Response headers: `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"orders-<merchantId>-<from>_<to>.csv\"`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.\n\n### 4. Large result sets\n\nRows are **streamed**, not accumulated:\n\n- `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` returns an iterator built on `Statement.iterate()`, with the merchant scope applied by `BaseRepository` like any other query.\n- The route writes the header, then rows in batches, honoring backpressure (`res.write()` returning `false` → wait for `drain`).\n- No row cap: an export that silently truncates is worse than a slow one. Memory stays flat because nothing holds the full result.\n- Failure mid-stream (headers already sent) can't become a JSON error, so the stream is aborted and the incident logged — a truncated file the merchant can notice, rather than a corrupt one that looks complete.\n\n### 5. Dashboard\n\nA **Download CSV** button next to \"Recent orders\", exporting the **same rolling 30-day window the cards show** (Q4, rev 3), so the CSV total and the revenue card always agree.\n\nOne wrinkle to settle, because \"same as the dashboard\" is currently ambiguous: the card sends `to = today` and `to` is **exclusive**, so today's orders are already missing from it — the frontend half of TD-07.\n\n- **Option A (recommended): both use `to` = tomorrow.** One line in `public/app.js`, applied to the card and the export together. They stay identical, and today's orders stop disappearing. It fixes the frontend half of TD-07 as a side effect; the backend half (the exclusive bound itself) stays as documented.\n- **Option B: both keep `to` = today.** Zero scope creep, but the export deliberately ships a file missing today's sales, which is a bad property for a record a merchant archives.\n\nThis plan assumes **Option A** and its single shared helper (`currentRange()`) used by both the cards and the export, so the two can't drift apart later.\n\nThe button is not a plain `<a download>`: if the 10-minute merchant token has expired the browser would download a file containing `{\"error\":\"session_expired\"}`. The handler mints a fresh token first (the existing re-mint path), then triggers the download.\n\n### 6. Commits\n\n| # | Content |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | `src/lib/csv.ts` (escaping, injection defense) + unit tests |\n| 2 | `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` + scope tests |\n| 3 | `GET /api/orders/export.csv` (registered before `/:id`) + HTTP tests |\n| 4 | Dashboard button |\n\n## Answers to the open questions\n\n- **Q1 — Three amount columns**: `amount_cents`, `signed_amount_cents`, `amount`.\n- **Q2 — `from`/`to` optional**; one without the other is a `400`.\n- **Q3 — BOM + formula-injection prefix**: both included.\n- **Q4 — Current calendar month to date** (not the rolling 30 days), with the range shown on the button. See §5 for the exclusive-`to` handling.\n\n## Scope\n\n- New: `src/lib/csv.ts`, `test/csv.test.ts`, `test/orders-export.test.ts`\n- Changed: `src/dal/base-repository.ts` (iterator helper), `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/routes/orders.ts`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`\n- `docs/api.md`, `docs/architecture.md` — after validation, with authorization (CLAUDE.md §6)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Other export formats, scheduled or emailed exports, background jobs.\n- A date-range picker in the UI.\n- The remaining Tier 1 debt (TD-10, TD-11, TD-12) — the injection defense here mitigates the export path but does not replace input validation.\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — CSV unit tests + endpoint tests.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. **Route ordering**: `GET /api/orders/export.csv` returns CSV, not `404 not_found` (the regression this plan predicts).\n4. **Scope**: an `m_acme` session's export contains no `m_bistro` row; an admin token gets `403`.\n5. **Money**: the sum of `signed_amount_cents` for a full range equals `/api/revenue`'s `revenue_cents` for the same range (327 108 for `m_acme` on the seeded data).\n6. **Escaping**: a customer email containing `,`, `\"` and a newline round-trips through a CSV parser; `=HYPERLINK(\"x\")` comes back prefixed with `'`.\n7. **Headers**: `Content-Disposition` names the file with merchant and range; body starts with the UTF-8 BOM.\n8. **Streaming**: exporting a few thousand seeded rows keeps memory flat (measured with `process.memoryUsage()` before/after) and the response is chunked.\n9. **Browser**: the button downloads a file that opens correctly, and still works after the merchant token has expired.\n10. **Month window**: an order created today appears in the export (the exclusive-`to` trap), and one created on the last day of the previous month does not.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits. Large result sets\n\nRows are **streamed**, not accumulated:\n\n- `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` returns an iterator built on `Statement.iterate()`, with the merchant scope applied by `BaseRepository` like any other query.\n- The route writes the header, then rows in batches, honoring backpressure (`res.write()` returning `false` → wait for `drain`).\n- No row cap: an export that silently truncates is worse than a slow one. Memory stays flat because nothing holds the full result.\n- Failure mid-stream (headers already sent) can't become a JSON error, so the stream is aborted and the incident logged — a truncated file the merchant can notice, rather than a corrupt one that looks complete.\n\n### 5. Dashboard\n\nA **Download CSV** button next to \"Recent orders\", exporting the **same rolling 30-day window the cards show** (Q4, rev 3), so the CSV total and the revenue card always agree.\n\nOne wrinkle to settle, because \"same as the dashboard\" is currently ambiguous: the card sends `to = today` and `to` is **exclusive**, so today's orders are already missing from it — the frontend half of TD-07.\n\n- **Option A (recommended): both use `to` = tomorrow.** One line in `public/app.js`, applied to the card and the export together. They stay identical, and today's orders stop disappearing. It fixes the frontend half of TD-07 as a side effect; the backend half (the exclusive bound itself) stays as documented.\n- **Option B: both keep `to` = today.** Zero scope creep, but the export deliberately ships a file missing today's sales, which is a bad property for a record a merchant archives.\n\nThis plan assumes **Option A** and its single shared helper (`currentRange()`) used by both the cards and the export, so the two can't drift apart later.\n\nThe button is not a plain `<a download>`: if the 10-minute merchant token has expired the browser would download a file containing `{\"error\":\"session_expired\"}`. The handler mints a fresh token first (the existing re-mint path), then triggers the download.\n\n### 6. Commits\n\n| # | Content |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | `src/lib/csv.ts` (escaping, injection defense) + unit tests |\n| 2 | `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` + scope tests |\n| 3 | `GET /api/orders/export.csv` (registered before `/:id`) + HTTP tests |\n| 4 | Dashboard button |\n\n## Answers to the open questions\n\n- **Q1 — Three amount columns**: `amount_cents`, `signed_amount_cents`, `amount`.\n- **Q2 — `from`/`to` optional**; one without the other is a `400`.\n- **Q3 — BOM + formula-injection prefix**: both included.\n- **Q4 (rev 3) — The rolling 30-day window the dashboard already uses**, shared with the cards through one helper so both always match. Pending your nod on Option A in §5 (both include today) versus Option B (both keep excluding it).\n\n## Scope\n\n- New: `src/lib/csv.ts`, `test/csv.test.ts`, `test/orders-export.test.ts`\n- Changed: `src/dal/base-repository.ts` (iterator helper), `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/routes/orders.ts`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`\n- `docs/api.md`, `docs/architecture.md` — after validation, with authorization (CLAUDE.md §6)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Other export formats, scheduled or emailed exports, background jobs.\n- A date-range picker in the UI.\n- The remaining Tier 1 debt (TD-10, TD-11, TD-12) — the injection defense here mitigates the export path but does not replace input validation.\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — CSV unit tests + endpoint tests.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. **Route ordering**: `GET /api/orders/export.csv` returns CSV, not `404 not_found` (the regression this plan predicts).\n4. **Scope**: an `m_acme` session's export contains no `m_bistro` row; an admin token gets `403`.\n5. **Money**: the sum of `signed_amount_cents` for a full range equals `/api/revenue`'s `revenue_cents` for the same range (327 108 for `m_acme` on the seeded data).\n6. **Escaping**: a customer email containing `,`, `\"` and a newline round-trips through a CSV parser; `=HYPERLINK(\"x\")` comes back prefixed with `'`.\n7. **Headers**: `Content-Disposition` names the file with merchant and range; body starts with the UTF-8 BOM.\n8. **Streaming**: exporting a few thousand seeded rows keeps memory flat (measured with `process.memoryUsage()` before/after) and the response is chunked.\n9. **Browser**: the button downloads a file that opens correctly, and still works after the merchant token has expired.\n10. **Month window**: an order created today appears in the export (the exclusive-`to` trap), and one created on the last day of the previous month does not.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits. The merchant filter is\n   * applied exactly as in {@link select}.\n   *\n   * @param columns - Column list or expressions.\n   * @param options - Extra condition, trailing clauses and their parameters.\n   */\n  protected iterate<T>(columns: string, options: QueryOptions = {}): IterableIterator<T> {\n    const where = options.where ? ` AND ${options.where}` : '';\n    const tail = options.tail ? ` ${options.tail}` : '';\n    const sql = `SELECT ${columns} FROM ${this.table} WHERE ${this.merchantColumn} = ?${where}${tail}`;\n    return db.prepare(sql).iterate(this.scope(), ...(options.params ?? [])) as IterableIterator<T>;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Inserts a row, forcing the merchant column to the caller's scope.\n   *\n   * @param values - Column values, excluding the merchant column.\n   */","originalFile":"/**\n * Repository base classes — the only place in the application that touches the database.\n *\n * `BaseRepository` applies the merchant scope itself, reading it from the request's\n * {@link getAuthContext}. Subclasses cannot opt out: they never see the raw connection and\n * never pass the merchant id in, so \"the repository forgot the tenancy filter\" stops being a\n * possible bug. `AdminRepository` covers the few tables that are not merchant-scoped and\n * requires an admin (mint-scoped) caller instead.\n *\n * `test/architecture.test.ts` enforces that no other module imports the database handle.\n *\n * @see plans/005-jwt-auth-and-scoped-repositories.md\n */\nimport { getAuthContext } from '../auth/context.js';\nimport { db } from '../db.js';\n\n/** Raised when the current caller isn't allowed to run a repository query. */\nexport class ScopeError extends Error {\n  constructor(message: string) {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = 'ScopeError';\n  }\n}\n\n/** Optional fragments appended to a generated query. */\nexport interface QueryOptions {\n  /** Extra condition, ANDed with the scope filter. */\n  where?: string;\n  /** Trailing clauses, e.g. `GROUP BY … ORDER BY … LIMIT ?`. */\n  tail?: string;\n  /** Parameters for `where` first, then `tail`. */\n  params?: unknown[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Base class for every merchant-scoped entity.\n */\nexport abstract class BaseRepository<TRow> {\n  /** Table backing this repository. */\n  protected abstract readonly table: string;\n\n  /** Column holding the merchant id. */\n  protected readonly merchantColumn: string = 'merchant_id';\n\n  /**\n   * Merchant id of the current caller.\n   *\n   * @throws ScopeError when the caller has no merchant scope (e.g. an admin token).\n   */\n  protected scope(): string {\n    const context = getAuthContext();\n    if (!context.merchantId) {\n      throw new ScopeError(`${context.role} caller has no merchant scope for ${this.table}`);\n    }\n    return context.merchantId;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Runs a scoped `SELECT`. `'${value}` : String(value);\n  if (NEEDS_QUOTING.test(text)) text = `\"${text.replace(/\"/g, '\"\"')}\"`;\n  return text;\n}\n\n/**\n * Renders one CSV record, terminated with CRLF as RFC 4180 requires.\n *\n * @param values - Field values, in column order.\n */\nexport function csvRow(values: readonly unknown[]): string {\n  return `${values.map(escapeCsvField).join(',')}\\r\\n`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Streams a CSV document into a writable, respecting backpressure so memory stays flat\n * regardless of how many rows are exported.\n *\n * @param stream - Destination (an HTTP response).\n * @param columns - Header row.\n * @param rows - Row source; iterated lazily.\n * @param toValues - Maps a row to its field values.\n */\nexport async function writeCsv<T>(\n  stream: Writable,\n  columns: readonly string[],\n  rows: Iterable<T>,\n  toValues: (row: T) => readonly unknown[],\n): Promise<void> {\n  await writeChunk(stream, UTF8_BOM + csvRow(columns));\n  for (const row of rows) {\n    await writeChunk(stream, csvRow(toValues(row)));\n  }\n  stream.end();\n}\n\n/**\n * Writes a chunk, waiting for `drain` when the buffer is full.\n */\nasync function writeChunk(stream: Writable, chunk: string): Promise<void> {\n  if (!stream.write(chunk)) await once(stream, 'drain');\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":16,"oldLines":8,"newStart":16,"newLines":7,"lines":[" /** Byte-order mark, so Excel on Windows reads the file as UTF-8. */"," export const UTF8_BOM = '﻿';"," ","-const NEEDS_QUOTING = /[\"","-,\\r\\n]/;","+const NEEDS_QUOTING = /[\",\\r\\n]/;"," const FORMULA_PREFIX = /^[=+\\-@\\t\\r]/;"," "," /**"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"ec327394-e3f2-47d0-b79e-75906795fd20","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}

'merchant';\n    res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/csv; charset=utf-8');\n    res.setHeader('X-Content-Type-Options', 'nosniff');\n    res.setHeader('Content-Disposition', `attachment; filename=\"${exportFilename(merchantId, from, to)}\"`);\n\n    try {\n      await writeCsv(res, EXPORT_COLUMNS, ordersRepository.iterateForExport({ from, to }), toExportValues);\n    } catch (error) {\n      // Headers are already sent, so this can't become a JSON error: abort the transfer instead\n      // of finishing a file that looks complete but isn't.\n      console.error('csv export failed mid-stream', error);\n      res.destroy();\n    }\n  }),\n);\n\n/**\n * `GET /api/orders` — the caller's orders, newest first.\n */\nordersRouter.get('/', (req, res) => {\n  const orders = ordersRepository.list({\n    from: typeof req.query.from === 'string' ? req.query.from : undefined,\n    to: typeof req.query.to === 'string' ? req.query.to : undefined,\n    limit: typeof req.query.limit === 'string' ? Number(req.query.limit) : undefined,\n  });\n  res.json({ orders });\n});\n\n/**\n * `GET /api/orders/:id` — one order, scoped to the caller's merchant: another merchant's\n * order is reported as missing rather than returned (TD-02).\n */\nordersRouter.get('/:id', (req, res) => {\n  const order = ordersRepository.getById(req.params.id);\n  if (!order) {\n    res.status(404).json({ error: 'not_found' });\n    return;\n  }\n  res.json({ order });\n});\n\n/**\n * `POST /api/orders` — creates an order for the caller's merchant.\n */\nordersRouter.post('/', (req, res) => {\n  const body = req.body as {\n    customer_email?: string;\n    total_amount?: number;\n    type?: 'sale' | 'refund';\n  };\n  if (!body.customer_email || typeof body.total_amount !== 'number') {\n    res.status(400).json({ error: 'invalid_body' });\n    return;\n  }\n  const order = ordersRepository.create({\n    id: randomUUID(),\n    customer_email: body.customer_email,\n    total_amount: body.total_amount,\n    type: body.type ?? document.getElementById('orders-tbody');\n\n// The session lives in HttpOnly cookies, so this page never holds a token.\n// Merchant tokens are short-lived: on a 401 we ask for a new one and retry once.\nlet selectedMerchantId = null;\n\nfunction request(path, options = {}) {\n  return fetch(path, { credentials: 'same-origin', ...options });\n}\n\nasync function mintMerchantToken(merchantId) {\n  const response = await request('/api/auth/token', {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n    body: JSON.stringify({ merchantId }),\n  });\n  return response.ok;\n}\n\nasync function api(path) {\n  let response = await request(path);\n  if (response.status === 401 && selectedMerchantId && (await mintMerchantToken(selectedMerchantId))) {\n    response = await request(path);\n  }\n  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`${path} responded ${response.status}`);\n  return response.json();\n}\n\nfunction money(cents) {\n  return (cents / 100).toLocaleString('en-US', { style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' });\n}\n\nfunction isoDate(d) {\n  return d.toISOString().slice(0, 10);\n}\n\nfunction setStatus(text) {\n  sessionLabel.textContent = text;\n}\n\nasync function refresh() {\n  const summary = await api('/api/metrics/summary');\n  salesOrdersEl.textContent = summary.sales_orders ?? '—';\n  refundOrdersEl.textContent = summary.refund_orders ?? '—';\n  avgOrderEl.textContent = money(summary.avg_order_value_cents ?? 0);\n  avgNetOrderEl.textContent = `${money(summary.avg_net_order_value_cents ?? 0)} net of refunds`;\n\n  const now = new Date();\n  const thirtyAgo = new Date(now.getTime() - 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);\n  const revenue = await api(`/api/revenue?from=${isoDate(thirtyAgo)}&to=${isoDate(now)}`);\n  revenue30dEl.textContent = money(revenue.revenue_cents ?? 0);\n  revenueBreakdownEl.textContent = `${money(revenue.gross_sales_cents ?? 0)} sales − ${money(revenue.refunds_cents ?? 0)} refunded`;\n\n  const ordersRes = await api('/api/orders?limit=10');\n  ordersTbody.innerHTML = '';\n  for (const o of ordersRes.orders ?? AddressInfo } from 'node:net';\nimport type { Server } from 'node:http';\nimport { createApp } from '../src/app.js';\nimport { ADMIN_COOKIE, MERCHANT_COOKIE } from '../src/auth/cookies.js';\nimport { issueAdminToken, issueMerchantToken } from '../src/auth/jwt.js';\nimport { initSchema, db } from '../src/db.js';\n\nconst RANGE = 'from=2000-01-01&to=2030-01-01';\n\nlet server: Server;\nlet baseUrl: string;\nlet acmeCookie: string;\nlet adminCookie: string;\n\nbefore(async () => {\n  initSchema();\n  db.prepare(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO merchants (id, name) VALUES ('m_acme', 'Acme'), ('m_bistro', 'Bistro')`).run();\n  db.exec('DELETE FROM orders');\n  const insert = db.prepare(\n    `INSERT INTO orders (id, merchant_id, customer_email, total_amount, type, status, created_at)\n     VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'completed', ?)`,\n  );\n  insert.run('exp-1', 'm_acme', 'ana@example.com', 10000, 'sale', '2026-06-01T10:00:00.000Z');\n  insert.run('exp-2', 'm_acme', 'Doe, \"Jane\"\\nsecond@example.com', 2500, 'sale', '2026-06-02T10:00:00.000Z');\n  insert.run('exp-3', 'm_acme', '=HYPERLINK(\"http://evil\",\"click\")', 4000, 'refund', '2026-06-03T10:00:00.000Z');\n  insert.run('exp-4', 'm_bistro', 'bruno@example.com', 7777, 'sale', '2026-06-04T10:00:00.000Z');\n\n  server = createApp({ enableDevAdminSession: false }).listen(0);\n  await new Promise((resolve) => server.once('listening', resolve));\n  baseUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${(server.address() as AddressInfo).port}`;\n\n  acmeCookie = `${MERCHANT_COOKIE}=${(await issueMerchantToken('m_acme', '5m')).token}`;\n  adminCookie = `${ADMIN_COOKIE}=${(await issueAdminToken('5m')).token}`;\n});\n\nafter(() => {\n  server.close();\n});\n\n/** Requests a path with an optional cookie. */\nfunction call(path: string, cookie?: string) {\n  return fetch(`${baseUrl}${path}`, { headers: cookie ? { Cookie: cookie } : {} });\n}\n\n/**\n * Reads a response body as CSV text. `Response.text()` strips a leading BOM while decoding,\n * so the marker is asserted separately on the raw bytes.\n */\nasync function csvText(response: Response): Promise<string> {\n  return (await response.text()).replace(/^﻿/, '');\n}\n\n/** Minimal RFC 4180 parser, enough to read back what the export writes. */\nfunction parseCsv(text: string): string[][] {\n  const rows: string[][] = [];\n  let row: string[] = [];\n  let field = '';\n  let quoted = false;\n\n  for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {\n    const char = text[i]!;\n    if (quoted) {\n      if (char === '\"' && text[i + 1] === '\"') {\n        field += '\"';\n        i++;\n      } else if (char === '\"') {\n        quoted = false;\n      } else {\n        field += char;\n      }\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (char === '\"') quoted = true;\n    else if (char === ',') {\n      row.push(field);\n      field = '';\n    } else if (char === '\\r' && text[i + 1] === '\\n') {\n      row.push(field);\n      rows.push(row);\n      row = [];\n      field = '';\n      i++;\n    } else field += char;\n  }\n  if (field || row.length > 0) {\n    row.push(field);\n    rows.push(row);\n  }\n  return rows;\n}\n\ntest('export: the route is not swallowed by GET /:id', async () => {\n  const response = await call(`/api/orders/export.csv?${RANGE}`, acmeCookie);\n  assert.equal(response.status, 200);\n  assert.match(response.headers.get('Content-Type') ?? '', /^text\\/csv/);\n});\n\ntest('export: requires a merchant session', async () => {\n  assert.equal((await call(`/api/orders/export.csv?${RANGE}`)).status, 401);\n\n  const asAdmin = await call(`/api/orders/export.csv?${RANGE}`, adminCookie);\n  assert.equal(asAdmin.status, 403);\n  assert.deepEqual(await asAdmin.json(), { error: 'token_not_scoped_for_data' });\n});\n\ntest('export: contains only the caller merchant rows', async () => {\n  const text = await (await call(`/api/orders/export.csv?${RANGE}`, acmeCookie)).text();\n  assert.ok(!text.includes('bruno@example.com'), \"another merchant's row leaked into the export\");\n  assert.ok(text.includes('ana@example.com'));\n});\n\ntest('export: starts with a BOM and the documented header', async () => {\n  const text = await (await call(`/api/orders/export.csv?${RANGE}`, acmeCookie)).text();\n  assert.ok(text.startsWith('﻿'));\n\n  const rows = parseCsv(text.slice(1));\n  assert.deepEqual(rows[0], [\n    'order_id',\n    'created_at',\n    'customer_email',\n    'type',\n    'status',\n    'amount_cents',\n    'signed_amount_cents',\n    'amount',\n  ]);\n});\n\ntest('export: rows are chronological and refunds carry a negative signed amount', async () => {\n  const text = await (await call(`/api/orders/export.csv?${RANGE}`, acmeCookie)).text();\n  const rows = parseCsv(text.slice(1)).slice(1);\n\n  assert.deepEqual(rows.map((r) => r[0]), ['exp-1', 'exp-2', 'exp-3']);\n  const refund = rows.find((r) => r[3] === 'refund')!;\n  assert.equal(refund[5], '4000');\n  assert.equal(refund[6], '-4000');\n  assert.equal(refund[7], '40.00');\n});\n\ntest('export: sums to the same net revenue the API reports', async () => {\n  const text = await (await call(`/api/orders/export.csv?${RANGE}`, acmeCookie)).text();\n  const rows = parseCsv(text.slice(1)).slice(1);\n  const csvNet = rows.reduce((total, row) => total + Number(row[6]), 0);\n\n  const revenue = (await (await call(`/api/revenue?${RANGE}`, acmeCookie)).json()) as { revenue_cents: number };\n  assert.equal(csvNet, revenue.revenue_cents);\n});\n\ntest('export: hostile field values survive a round-trip and cannot run as formulas', async () => {\n  const text = await (await call(`/api/orders/export.csv?${RANGE}`, acmeCookie)).text();\n  const rows = parseCsv(text.slice(1)).slice(1);\n\n  // Commas, quotes and newlines come back exactly as stored.\n  assert.equal(rows[1]![2], 'Doe, \"Jane\"\\nsecond@example.com');\n  // The formula is neutralised with a leading apostrophe.\n  assert.equal(rows[2]![2], '\\'=HYPERLINK(\"http://evil\",\"click\")');\n});\n\ntest('export: names the downloaded file after the merchant and range', async () => {\n  const response = await call('/api/orders/export.csv?from=2026-06-01&to=2026-06-04', acmeCookie);\n  assert.equal(\n    response.headers.get('Content-Disposition'),\n    'attachment; filename=\"orders-m_acme-2026-06-01_2026-06-04.csv\"',\n  );\n  assert.equal(response.headers.get('X-Content-Type-Options'), 'nosniff');\n});\n\ntest('export: honours the date range', async () => {\n {"parentUuid":"a51e0f08-b4ef-487f-ba72-d202db1160ad","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"81998312-a411-4069-97fb-8ef364aee3c0","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012UQT68Y8dqSe1CdUmgwgbd","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\008-csv-export-of-orders.md has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"0b4bbc9b-158d-41a9-89ee-df6baafdc19a","timestamp":"2026-09-12T09:08:51.268Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\plans\\008-csv-export-of-orders.md","oldString":"**Status:** draft (rev 3 — export window aligned with the dashboard)","newString":"**Status:** done (2026-09-12, rev 3 — Option A approved) — implemented and validated locally; `docs/` pending authorization","originalFile":"# 008 — Feature: CSV export of orders\n\n**Status:** draft (rev 3 — export window aligned with the dashboard)\n\nThe challenge's Feature A. Chosen because it reuses what we just fixed — merchant scoping (plan 005) and refund semantics (plan 006) — and because an export button is the thing merchants ask for first on a dashboard like this.\n\n## Context\n\nThe dashboard can show orders but not take them anywhere. A merchant's real workflow (reconciliation, accounting, sharing with a bookkeeper) ends in a spreadsheet.\n\nThe feature is under-specified on purpose. What we decide here: **column shape, auth model, format conventions, and behavior on large result sets.**\n\nFacts checked before writing this:\n\n- `better-sqlite3` exposes `Statement.iterate()`, so rows can be streamed instead of materialized (confirmed against the real database).\n- `ordersRouter` registers `GET /:id` at [src/routes/orders.ts:26](../src/routes/orders.ts). A later `GET /export.csv` would be swallowed by it and answer `404 not_found`, so **the export route must be registered before `/:id`** — with a test that would catch the ordering mistake.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Endpoint\n\n```\nGET /api/orders/export.csv?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD\n```\n\n- **Auth: the existing merchant session.** No new auth model: the same `requireAuth()` guard, the same `merchant_session` cookie, the same `BaseRepository` scope. An admin (mint-scoped) token gets `403` like on any data route — the export cannot become a way to read another merchant's rows.\n- `from`/`to` are **optional**; when both are present the same range rule as the orders list applies (`from` inclusive, `to` exclusive). One without the other is a `400`, instead of silently exporting everything (the list endpoint's silent-drop behavior is TD-09; the export won't copy it).\n- Rows are ordered **`created_at` ascending** — chronological, which is what a ledger export is for, unlike the dashboard's newest-first view.\n\n### 2. Columns\n\n| Column | Example | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| `order_id` | `e3684c1d-…` | Join key back to the API |\n| `created_at` | `2026-09-11T11:45:35.866Z` | ISO 8601, UTC, unambiguous |\n| `customer_email` | `ana@example.com` | |\n| `type` | `sale` / `refund` | |\n| `status` | `completed` | |\n| `amount_cents` | `11136` | As stored: positive integer, no locale or rounding issues |\n| `signed_amount_cents` | `-11136` for refunds | **Sums to net revenue** |\n| `amount` | `111.36` | Decimal with a dot, for humans |\n\n`signed_amount_cents` is the column that matters: it carries the refund semantics from `src/dal/money.ts` into the spreadsheet, so `=SUM(...)` gives net revenue. Without it, every merchant would recreate TD-05 in Excel on their own.\n\nNo `currency` column: the schema has no currency and inventing a constant would imply multi-currency support we don't have. Documented as USD in `docs/api.md`.\n\n### 3. Format conventions\n\n- **RFC 4180**: `CRLF` line endings, header row, fields quoted only when they contain `,` `\"` `CR` or `LF`, inner quotes doubled.\n- **UTF-8 with BOM**, so Excel on Windows doesn't mangle accented names.\n- **Formula-injection defense**: a field starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR is prefixed with `'`. This matters here specifically: `customer_email` is attacker-controlled and barely validated (TD-11 is still open), so `=HYPERLINK(...)` in an email field would execute when the merchant opens the file.\n- Response headers: `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"orders-<merchantId>-<from>_<to>.csv\"`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.\n\n### 4. Large result sets\n\nRows are **streamed**, not accumulated:\n\n- `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` returns an iterator built on `Statement.iterate()`, with the merchant scope applied by `BaseRepository` like any other query.\n- The route writes the header, then rows in batches, honoring backpressure (`res.write()` returning `false` → wait for `drain`).\n- No row cap: an export that silently truncates is worse than a slow one. Memory stays flat because nothing holds the full result.\n- Failure mid-stream (headers already sent) can't become a JSON error, so the stream is aborted and the incident logged — a truncated file the merchant can notice, rather than a corrupt one that looks complete.\n\n### 5. Dashboard\n\nA **Download CSV** button next to \"Recent orders\", exporting the **same rolling 30-day window the cards show** (Q4, rev 3), so the CSV total and the revenue card always agree.\n\nOne wrinkle to settle, because \"same as the dashboard\" is currently ambiguous: the card sends `to = today` and `to` is **exclusive**, so today's orders are already missing from it — the frontend half of TD-07.\n\n- **Option A (recommended): both use `to` = tomorrow.** One line in `public/app.js`, applied to the card and the export together. They stay identical, and today's orders stop disappearing. It fixes the frontend half of TD-07 as a side effect; the backend half (the exclusive bound itself) stays as documented.\n- **Option B: both keep `to` = today.** Zero scope creep, but the export deliberately ships a file missing today's sales, which is a bad property for a record a merchant archives.\n\nThis plan assumes **Option A** and its single shared helper (`currentRange()`) used by both the cards and the export, so the two can't drift apart later.\n\nThe button is not a plain `<a download>`: if the 10-minute merchant token has expired the browser would download a file containing `{\"error\":\"session_expired\"}`. The handler mints a fresh token first (the existing re-mint path), then triggers the download.\n\n### 6. Commits\n\n| # | Content |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | `src/lib/csv.ts` (escaping, injection defense) + unit tests |\n| 2 | `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` + scope tests |\n| 3 | `GET /api/orders/export.csv` (registered before `/:id`) + HTTP tests |\n| 4 | Dashboard button |\n\n## Answers to the open questions\n\n- **Q1 — Three amount columns**: `amount_cents`, `signed_amount_cents`, `amount`.\n- **Q2 — `from`/`to` optional**; one without the other is a `400`.\n- **Q3 — BOM + formula-injection prefix**: both included.\n- **Q4 (rev 3) — The rolling 30-day window the dashboard already uses**, shared with the cards through one helper so both always match. Pending your nod on Option A in §5 (both include today) versus Option B (both keep excluding it).\n\n## Scope\n\n- New: `src/lib/csv.ts`, `test/csv.test.ts`, `test/orders-export.test.ts`\n- Changed: `src/dal/base-repository.ts` (iterator helper), `src/dal/orders-repository.ts`, `src/routes/orders.ts`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`\n- `docs/api.md`, `docs/architecture.md` — after validation, with authorization (CLAUDE.md §6)\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Other export formats, scheduled or emailed exports, background jobs.\n- A date-range picker in the UI.\n- The remaining Tier 1 debt (TD-10, TD-11, TD-12) — the injection defense here mitigates the export path but does not replace input validation.\n\n## Validation\n\n1. `npm test` — CSV unit tests + endpoint tests.\n2. `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.\n3. **Route ordering**: `GET /api/orders/export.csv` returns CSV, not `404 not_found` (the regression this plan predicts).\n4. **Scope**: an `m_acme` session's export contains no `m_bistro` row; an admin token gets `403`.\n5. **Money**: the sum of `signed_amount_cents` for a full range equals `/api/revenue`'s `revenue_cents` for the same range (327 108 for `m_acme` on the seeded data).\n6. **Escaping**: a customer email containing `,`, `\"` and a newline round-trips through a CSV parser; `=HYPERLINK(\"x\")` comes back prefixed with `'`.\n7. **Headers**: `Content-Disposition` names the file with merchant and range; body starts with the UTF-8 BOM.\n8. **Streaming**: exporting a few thousand seeded rows keeps memory flat (measured with `process.memoryUsage()` before/after) and the response is chunked.\n9. **Browser**: the button downloads a file that opens correctly, and still works after the merchant token has expired.\n10. **Window**: the CSV row count and the sum of `signed_amount_cents` match the revenue card for the same window; with Option A, an order created today appears in both.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the commits. Chosen because it reuses what we just fixed — merchant scoping (plan 005) and refund semantics (plan 006) — and because an export button is the thing merchants ask for first on a dashboard like this.\n\n## Context\n\nThe dashboard can show orders but not take them anywhere. A merchant's real workflow (reconciliation, accounting, sharing with a bookkeeper) ends in a spreadsheet.\n\nThe feature is under-specified on purpose. What we decide here: **column shape, auth model, format conventions, and behavior on large result sets.**\n\nFacts checked before writing this:\n\n- `better-sqlite3` exposes `Statement.iterate()`, so rows can be streamed instead of materialized (confirmed against the real database).\n- `ordersRouter` registers `GET /:id` at [src/routes/orders.ts:26](../src/routes/orders.ts). A later `GET /export.csv` would be swallowed by it and answer `404 not_found`, so **the export route must be registered before `/:id`** — with a test that would catch the ordering mistake.\n\n## Decision\n\n### 1. Endpoint\n\n```\nGET /api/orders/export.csv?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD\n```\n\n- **Auth: the existing merchant session.** No new auth model: the same `requireAuth()` guard, the same `merchant_session` cookie, the same `BaseRepository` scope. An admin (mint-scoped) token gets `403` like on any data route — the export cannot become a way to read another merchant's rows.\n- `from`/`to` are **optional**; when both are present the same range rule as the orders list applies (`from` inclusive, `to` exclusive). One without the other is a `400`, instead of silently exporting everything (the list endpoint's silent-drop behavior is TD-09; the export won't copy it).\n- Rows are ordered **`created_at` ascending** — chronological, which is what a ledger export is for, unlike the dashboard's newest-first view.\n\n### 2. Columns\n\n| Column | Example | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| `order_id` | `e3684c1d-…` | Join key back to the API |\n| `created_at` | `2026-09-11T11:45:35.866Z` | ISO 8601, UTC, unambiguous |\n| `customer_email` | `ana@example.com` | |\n| `type` | `sale` / `refund` | |\n| `status` | `completed` | |\n| `amount_cents` | `11136` | As stored: positive integer, no locale or rounding issues |\n| `signed_amount_cents` | `-11136` for refunds | **Sums to net revenue** |\n| `amount` | `111.36` | Decimal with a dot, for humans |\n\n`signed_amount_cents` is the column that matters: it carries the refund semantics from `src/dal/money.ts` into the spreadsheet, so `=SUM(...)` gives net revenue. Without it, every merchant would recreate TD-05 in Excel on their own.\n\nNo `currency` column: the schema has no currency and inventing a constant would imply multi-currency support we don't have. Documented as USD in `docs/api.md`.\n\n### 3. Format conventions\n\n- **RFC 4180**: `CRLF` line endings, header row, fields quoted only when they contain `,` `\"` `CR` or `LF`, inner quotes doubled.\n- **UTF-8 with BOM**, so Excel on Windows doesn't mangle accented names.\n- **Formula-injection defense**: a field starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR is prefixed with `'`. This matters here specifically: `customer_email` is attacker-controlled and barely validated (TD-11 is still open), so `=HYPERLINK(...)` in an email field would execute when the merchant opens the file.\n- Response headers: `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"orders-<merchantId>-<from>_<to>.csv\"`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.\n\n### 4. Large result sets\n\nRows are **streamed**, not accumulated:\n\n- `OrdersRepository.iterateForExport()` returns an iterator built on `Statement.iterate()`, with the merchant scope applied by `BaseRepository` like any other query.\n- The route writes the header, then rows in batches, honoring backpressure (`res.write()` returning `false` → wait for `drain`).\n- No row cap: an export that silently truncates is worse than a slow one. Memory stays flat because nothing holds the full result.\n- Failure mid-stream (headers already sent) can't become a JSON error, so the stream is aborted and the incident logged — a truncated file the merchant can notice, rather than a corrupt one that looks complete.\n\n### 5. Dashboard\n\nA **Download CSV** button next to \"Recent orders\", exporting the **same rolling 30-day window the cards show** (Q4, rev 3), so the CSV total and the revenue card always agree.\n\nOne wrinkle to settle, because \"same as the dashboard\" is currently ambiguous: the card sends `to = today` and `to` is **exclusive**, so today's orders are already missing from it — the frontend half of TD-07.\n\n- **Option A (recommended): both use `to` = tomorrow.** One line in `public/app.js`, applied to the card and the export together. They stay identical, and today's orders stop disappearing. It fixes the frontend half of TD-07 as a side effect; the backend half (the exclusive bound itself) stays as documented.\n- **Option B: both keep `to` = today.** Zero scope creep, but the export deliberately ships a file missing today's sales, which is a bad property for a record a merchant archives.\n\nThis plan assumes **Option A** and its single shared helper (`currentRange()`) used by both the cards and the export, so the two can't drift apart later.\n\nThe button is not a plain `<a download>`: if the 10-minute merchant token has expired the browser would download a file containing `{\"error\":\"session_expired\"}`. {"type":"bridge-session","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","bridgeSessionId":"cse_01RevUBptTUx7nmRkHFj8baE","lastSequenceNum":0,"ownerAccountUuid":"fd7153db-c57a-4ed8-a587-cc63ddfe7824","ownerOrganizationUuid":"a0c86979-17db-43c0-bac4-2f5d900230e2"}
{"parentUuid":"efabe234-5b0f-4889-93a0-7d945b11b621","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"f5a5b594-9be1-474b-a873-495081ce0ec5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TH8SnFSZ2Uw6BuFz9ZF9f4","type":"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Findings\n\n### 1. Sequential awaits that should be concurrent\n\n**`public/app.js:62, 69, 73` — `refresh()` — medium**\nThree independent GETs (`/api/metrics/summary`, `/api/revenue?from&to`, `/api/orders?limit=10`) are awaited one after another. Nothing consumes the previous result, so this is a pure 3× serialization of round-trips. On a LAN/localhost it's ~15 ms wasted; over a 150 ms-RTT mobile link the dashboard takes ~450 ms instead of ~150 ms, and the wait is repeated on every merchant switch (`selectMerchant` → `refresh`).\n\n**`public/app.js:30-37` (`api`) combined with the above — medium**\nThe 401-retry is per call. When the 10-minute merchant token has expired (very common: leave the tab open, switch merchant), each of the three sequential calls independently 401s, mints a token, and retries. Worst case one refresh becomes 3 × (401 + POST /api/auth/token + retry) = 9 sequential round-trips where 4 would do (one mint + 3 parallel reads). Each mint also costs a server-side `merchantsRepository.exists` query plus a sign + verify.\n\n**`src/routes/auth.ts:114-115` — low**\n`readSession(merchant)` and `readSession(admin)` are two independent `jwtVerify` calls awaited sequentially. HS256 verification is ~50-100 µs, so this is real but small; it's a `Promise.all` on principle, not a hot spot.\n\n**Backend otherwise: clean.** Every other route is synchronous end-to-end (better-sqlite3), so there is no concurrency to recover — `orders`, `revenue`, `metrics` do exactly one query each. No sequential-await antipattern there.\n\n### 2. Repeated work per request\n\n**`src/dal/base-repository.ts:68, 94, 106, 142` — medium**\n`db.prepare(...)` is called on **every** repository call and the `Statement` is discarded. better-sqlite3 does not cache prepared statements internally, so each request re-parses the SQL text and re-runs the query planner. For the aggregate queries in `metrics-repository.ts` and `orders-repository.ts` the SQL is long (multiple `CASE WHEN` expressions), and compilation is ~20-80 µs. At the current 80-row dataset **compilation likely costs more than execution** — i.e. the summary endpoint may spend the majority of its DB time planning, not scanning. Because it's synchronous, that cost is charged directly to the event loop. Worth noting the SQL is constructed by string concatenation from a small fixed set of shapes, so it is inherently cacheable.\n\n**`src/auth/jwt.ts:137-139` — low**\n`secretKey()` allocates a new `TextEncoder` and re-encodes the secret on every sign and every verify. `getJwtSecret()` itself is memoized (`env.ts:56`), so there is **no repeated file read** — `loadEnv` is guarded by `envLoaded`, and `readEnvValue`/`existsSync` only run on the first-generation path. Config/file reads per request: **clean**. `getConfig()` does rebuild a fresh object per call (`env.ts:45`), but it's called at wiring time, not per request.\n\n**`src/auth/guard.ts:54` — low at this scale**\nThe same token is verified on every request, with no verification cache. For a dashboard doing 3-4 calls per refresh that is 3-4 HMACs, ~0.2-0.4 ms total. Real but minor; it only becomes interesting under load, where it is pure CPU on the single thread.\n\n**`src/auth/dev-session.ts:26-49` — medium in dev**\nThe middleware runs before `express.static`, on **every** request including `/app.js`, `/index.html` and favicon. For any local request without an admin cookie it mints a token, which via `jwt.ts:128-131` **signs and then immediately verifies** the token it just produced — two HMAC operations. Any non-browser or cookie-less client (curl loops, load test, health polling) triggers this on literally every request.\n\n**N+1 queries: clean.** No loop anywhere issues a query per item. `create()` (`orders-repository.ts:102-111`) does a write followed by a read-back, which is 2 statements instead of 1, but that's constant, not N+1.\n\n### 3. Query efficiency and indexing\n\nThis is the weakest area. There is no composite index; both existing indexes are single-column.\n\n**`src/dal/orders-repository.ts:71-84` (`list`) — high at scale**\n`WHERE merchant_id = ? [AND created_at >= ? AND < ?] ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?`. Neither index satisfies both the filter and the ordering. SQLite must pick one:\n- `idx_orders_merchant` → fetches every row of that merchant, then builds a temporary B-tree to sort by `created_at` (a filesort);\n- or `idx_orders_created` → scans the whole table in date order, discarding other merchants' rows.\n\nFor a merchant with **100k orders**, the default `limit=10` dashboard call sorts 100k rows to return 10 — tens of milliseconds of fully blocking CPU for a query that a `(merchant_id, created_at)` index would answer in microseconds. The second path is worse for a small tenant in a large table: a merchant with 100 orders in a 1M-row table scans a large fraction of the table.\n\n**`src/routes/orders.ts:63-70` — medium**\n`limit` is `Number(req.query.limit)` with **no upper bound and no validation**. `?limit=1000000` materializes the whole merchant history as row objects and then serializes it to JSON — an unbounded memory spike plus a multi-hundred-millisecond event-loop stall from a single unauthenticated-shaped query string. `NaN` (e.g. `?limit=abc`) is also passed straight to the binder. Same unbounded shape at `src/routes/metrics.ts:26` (`top-customers` limit).\n\n**`src/dal/orders-repository.ts:143-155` (`revenue`) — medium**\n`WHERE merchant_id = ? AND created_at >= ? AND < ?` with three `SUM(CASE …)` aggregates. Only one of the two columns can be indexed at a time; whichever is chosen, the other predicate is evaluated per row, and because the index is non-covering every qualifying row costs a random rowid lookup into the table B-tree. The dashboard's 30-day window over a merchant with 100k orders/year touches ~8k rows — acceptable. Over a multi-year merchant with 1M rows the 30-day window is still bounded, so this scales better than `summary`.\n\n**`src/dal/metrics-repository.ts:47-70` (`summary`) — high at scale**\nNo date filter at all: it aggregates the merchant's **entire history** on every dashboard load, including `COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN type='sale' THEN customer_email END)`, which requires a temporary B-tree over all distinct emails. For a merchant with 100k orders that's a full 100k-row scan plus a distinct structure holding every unique customer, every refresh, synchronously. At 1M orders it's a ~0.3-1 s hard stall. This is the single most expensive endpoint the dashboard calls automatically.\n\n**`src/dal/metrics-repository.ts:77-87` (`topCustomers`) — medium/high at scale**\n`GROUP BY customer_email ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT ?`. No index on `customer_email`, so grouping needs a temp B-tree/hash over the whole merchant partition, and the `ORDER BY` is on an aggregate expression, so it can never be index-satisfied — the full grouped result is always sorted before `LIMIT` applies. O(n) scan + O(k log k) sort where k = distinct customers. (Note: this endpoint isn't called by `public/app.js` at all — it's API-only surface.)\n\n**`src/dal/orders-repository.ts:120-132` (`iterateForExport`) — high, and the docstring overstates the benefit**\n`ORDER BY created_at ASC` over the merchant partition with no supporting composite index means SQLite builds a **sorter before it can yield the first row**. So the comment \"rows are produced lazily, so exporting a large history does not materialize it in memory\" is only half true: the JS side stays flat, but SQLite materializes and sorts the whole result set (in memory up to `cache_size`, spilling to a temp file beyond) before the first `.next()` returns. A 1M-row export pays a multi-second, completely uninterruptible sort up front while the response headers have already been sent.\n\n**`getById` (`orders-repository.ts:92-94`) — clean.** The generated SQL is `WHERE merchant_id = ? AND id = ?`; `id` is `TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, so SQLite's autoindex gives a unique lookup and the planner will use it regardless of clause order. Minor nit: it goes through `select().all()[0]` with no `LIMIT 1`, which is harmless for a unique key.\n\n**`merchants-repository.ts:27` (`list`, `ORDER BY name`)** sorts an unindexed column, but the merchants table is the tenant list — dozens of rows. **Theoretical only.**\n\n### 4. HIGH — `isLocalRequest` is half client-controlled, so the dev admin-session gate opens to remote callers behind a same-host proxy\n`C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\src\\auth\\local.ts:50` (with `src\\auth\\dev-session.ts:36` and `src\\config\\env.ts:52`)\n\nThe gate is `isLoopbackAddress(req.socket.remoteAddress) && isLocalHostname(req.headers.host)`. The second conjunct is attacker-supplied, and the first is satisfied automatically for *every* request once anything terminates TLS/HTTP in front of the app on the same host (nginx/caddy/Apache `proxy_pass`, a sidecar, an SSH tunnel) — `remoteAddress` is then always `127.0.0.1`. `devAdminSession` defaults to on (`process.env.DEV_ADMIN_SESSION ?? 'on'`), so the deployed default is vulnerable; the code comment claims the peer address \"a remote client cannot forge\", which stops being true the moment a local proxy exists.\n\nExploitation: app deployed at `https://dash.example.com` behind nginx with the common `proxy_set_header Host $host;`, `DEV_ADMIN_SESSION` never set. Attacker sends `GET / HTTP/1.1` with `Host: localhost` (curl `--resolve` / `-H \"Host: localhost\"` against the public IP, or any proxy that forwards the header verbatim). `attachAdminSession` sees loopback peer + localhost Host, mints an 8h `admin_session` cookie and returns it in `Set-Cookie`. The attacker then calls `GET /api/merchants` (mint scope) to enumerate every tenant, and `POST /api/auth/token {\"merchantId\":\"m_bistro\"}` for each one, receiving a merchant cookie per tenant — full cross-tenant read of orders, revenue, metrics and the CSV export, with no credential of any kind. (Reporting this because it is a new consequence: the known/by-design item is loopback-only access, and the point here is that \"loopback\" is partly forgeable and the switch defaults on in production.)\n\n### 2. MEDIUM — `Secure` attribute on session cookies is decided by the client's `Host` header\n`C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge\\src\\routes\\auth.ts:58` and `src\\routes\\auth.ts:98`\n\nBoth `Set-Cookie` calls use `secure: !isLocalRequest(req)`. As in finding 1, `isLocalRequest` can be forced true by a client-supplied `Host: localhost` whenever the peer address is loopback (proxy deployment). The session cookie is then written without `Secure`.\n\nExploitation: over HTTPS, the attacker gets a victim to load `https://dash.example.com` — no, more directly: an active network attacker (hostile Wi-Fi) who can influence one request, or the victim's own browser after a single request whose `Host` resolves to `localhost` in a proxied setup, ends up holding a `merchant_session`/`admin_session` cookie with no `Secure` flag. The attacker then triggers any plain-HTTP request to the same host (`http://dash.example.com/favicon.ico` injected into any HTTP page) and reads the JWT off the wire, replaying it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (`guard.ts:98` accepts bearer on both scopes) to read the tenant's data. Also note `serializeClearedCookie` (`cookies.ts:68`) omits `Secure` unconditionally, so the same downgrade happens on logout.\n\n### 3. The error handler returns a constant `{\"error\":\"internal_error\"}`, `ScopeError` messages (which name the role and table) never reach the client, and `getById` returns 404 rather than 403 for another merchant's order, so there is no cross-tenant existence oracle.\n- **CSV formula injection / header injection:** correctly handled. `FORMULA_PREFIX` covers `= + - @ \\t \\r` and is applied to every string field before quoting, numbers are deliberately left unprefixed, RFC 4180 quote-doubling is right, and `exportFilename` strips everything outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` so the `Content-Disposition` header cannot be injected."}],"resolvedModel":"claude-opus-5","totalDurationMs":247134,"totalTokens":83271,"totalToolUseCount":27,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5493,"cache_read_input_tokens":71609,"output_tokens":6167,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":806},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":5493},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":6167,"cache_read_input_tokens":71609,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5493,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":5493,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"toolStats":{"readCount":23,"searchCount":1,"bashCount":3,"editFileCount":0,"linesAdded":0,"linesRemoved":0,"otherToolCount":0}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"1a8bdf6d-2ea4-414a-8e83-2930155b156d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"C:\\Users\\carlo\\myapps\\recruiting-challenge","sessionId":"770d0b1e-848c-4be2-92c4-2bd59dc5c55d","version":"2.1.266","gitBranch":"feature/carlos-challenge"}
